title: continue_exoplasim never writes the hyperdiffusion namelist, so every segment after the first runs the model compiled defaults
description:
run_exoplasim.py writes TDISSQ, TDISST, TDISSZ, TDISSD, NHDIFF and NDEL into plasim_namelist (six references). continue_exoplasim.py writes NONE of them (zero references). The model reads them from the namelist on every invocation and they are not restart records, so a continued segment silently falls back to the values compiled into plasimmod and plasim.f90.

CONFIRMED ON THE PRODUCTION BASELINE. run_2b20e3324bb0 -- the T21 run the project climatology and every downstream component rests on -- has FIVE segments and its plasim_namelist contains no hyperdiffusion keys at all. So four of its five segments, and 84 of its 85 orbits, ran with the model defaults rather than the derived values.

WHAT THAT CHANGES AT T21. plasim.f90:1443 branches only on NTRU==42, so T21 falls through to plasimmod defaults: ndel 2, nhdiff 15, tdissd 0.20 d, tdissz 1.10 d, tdisst 5.60 d, tdissq 0.1 d. The configured values are ndel 4, nhdiff 16, divergence 0.4457, vorticity 2.2285, temperature 5.6449, humidity 0.7421.

  ndel 2 against 4 is the ORDER of the operator -- grad^4 instead of grad^8
  humidity   0.1  against 0.7421  -- 7.4x stronger damping
  divergence 0.20 against 0.4457  -- 2.2x
  vorticity  1.10 against 2.2285  -- 2.0x
  temperature 5.60 against 5.6449 -- negligible

A different operator order is not a tuning difference. The hyperdiffusion derivation in config/planet.yaml, the alpha=4 choice and the n*/N=0.381 confinement target all describe a model the continued segments were not running.

ALSO AFFECTS the T42 cold arm built for the ladder work (run_8102b89a08ac): one orbit at the configured values and 86 on defaults, so it is not usable as a resolution reference until re-run.

HOW IT SURFACED. A converted T21-to-T42 state crashes with SIGFPE in the radiation (world-bhs). Arm A does not crash in its own directory but DOES crash on the identical restart when run under a namelist that carries the hyperdiffusion keys -- which is what exposed that the two namelists differ.

check_consistency has a hyperdiffusion check but it validates config/planet.yaml against its own rule, not a run namelist against the config. That is the gap: nothing compares what a run INTEGRATED with against what was declared.

Source: exoplasim/scripts/continue_exoplasim.py, exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py, exoplasim/runs/run_2b20e3324bb0/plasim_namelist, vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasim.f90:1443, plasimmod.f90:201,444,877-880
close_reason:
Fixed by world-8bs in this fan-out (batch H). continue_exoplasim.py:587 now calls declare_hyperdiffusion(model, config), the same function the prepare path uses, so a continuation writes NDEL, NHDIFF and the four TDISS* into plasim_namelist instead of falling through to the compiled defaults. They are written as replicated '<layers>*<value>' text rather than as scalars, which also closes world-720's failure mode -- a Fortran namelist assignment of a scalar to an array sets element 1 only and leaves the rest at the compiled default, giving a mixed-unit array. expected_namelist_keys covers all six plus FILTERKAPPA and NFILTEREXP, and verify_staged_namelists compares the five replicated ones as text so a scalar cannot pass.

The CODE defect is closed. The consequence for the existing baseline -- run_2b20e3324bb0 having run 84 of its 85 orbits on compiled hyperdiffusion -- is a separate issue and stays open as world-hxm.

title: Every cold start builds an Earth Arctic sea-ice field and starts the ocean at freezing
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 1.

configure()'s `rm *.sra` correctly removes the shipped Earth boundary fields --
the diag confirms codes 169, 210, 211, 709 and 903 all print `Init ...
internally`. The model does not then fall back to anything neutral.

With code 169 absent, xclsst stays at its -999 sentinel (icemod.f90:119) and
icemod.f90:230 does `where (xclsst <= TFREEZE) xclicec = 1.0`, putting full ice
cover on every ocean cell. make_ice_thickness (icemod.f90:1929-1982) then shapes
it with hmaxn=3.0, hmaxs=0.50, cminn=0.1, cmins=0.25 and a fourteen-element
monthly modulation table credited in its own comment to "CCM3 report pp
127-129".

Separately oceanmod.f90:96 declares `real :: yclsst(NHOR,0:13)` with no
initialiser while its neighbours at :95, :97, :99 and :100 all have one.
oceanmod.f90:285 does `yclsst = MAX(yclsst,TFREEZE)` and :291-293 copies it into
the ocean temperature, so whatever was in memory is clipped up to freezing.
Note -finit-real=snan in the checked profile does NOT cover this: it covers
locals, not module-scope SAVE arrays.

Measured 2026-08-24, first output bin of run_2b20e3324bb0:
  ts   ocean: min=214.832  max=271.900  mean=258.860
  sic  ocean: min=0.000    max=0.000    mean=0.000
  sit  ocean: NH mean=2.533   SH mean=0.139
The ocean starts globally at TFREEZE, every ocean cell carries ice in an 18:1
north-south ratio -- Earth's Arctic-Antarctic contrast on a world with 32 deg
obliquity and unrelated geography -- and ice COVER is identically zero because
xicecc initialises to 0 (icemod.f90:97) and mkicec can only grow it. Thick ice
carrying no albedo is not a physical state, and neither is the field it
replaced.

Both are written to the restart (icemod.f90:995-997, oceanmod.f90:615) and read
back, so this persists through every continuation. yclsst is also emitted as
ocean code 990 "clim. sst", which is meaningless.

The exposure is sweep_flux_earth, which has not run: each arm would cold-start
from a fully iced ocean, so the warm branch is only approached from below and
the hysteresis is never probed from the ice-free side. An arm at 0.90 that fails
to melt out would read as a snowball bifurcation when it is an initial-condition
artifact.

Do: give the ice and ocean a declared cold-start state for this world rather
than a constructed Earth one. Blocks the flux sweep.
acceptance_criteria: A cold start produces a declared initial ice and SST state with no CCM3 field and no uninitialised read; sic and sit are mutually consistent in the first bin; the flux sweep can start from a defensible state.
close_reason: A cold start with no codes 169/210/211 now begins from a DECLARED profile or refuses to begin. read_ice_surface no longer constructs ice cover from the SST sentinel; make_ice_thickness's CCM3 relation is reachable only when a real cover was read, and warns that it is Earth-fitted and hemispherically asymmetric. ice_cold_start takes either the read climatology or icemod_nl's tsst_eq/tsst_pol/hice_ini profile, tsst_pol + (tsst_eq-tsst_pol)*cos(lat)**2, symmetric by construction, and aborts if neither exists. oceanmod's yclsst gains its -999 initialiser (module-scope SAVE, which -finit-real does not reach) and the ocean starts from the declared profile rather than from memory clipped to freezing. xicecc is set from the initial cover on BOTH paths, which is the fix for sic being identically zero beside a non-zero sit: mkicec only grows it and icestep copies it into xicec every step. config/planet.yaml declares ocean.cold_start and run_exoplasim writes TSST_EQ/TSST_POL/HICE_INI on a prepare and on every resume; expected_namelist_keys checks them. The declared cold start is ice-free, which is the side of the hysteresis the flux sweep could not reach; an arm that wants the iced side declares a sub-freezing pole or a non-zero thickness. WHAT DEPENDED ON THE OLD BEHAVIOUR: all 9 runs in exoplasim/runs cold-started from the constructed field and the ocean at freezing, and every restart carries it forward; per rule 7 the canonical climatology lineage does not exist, so all of it is disposable. NO RESTART RECORD ADDED OR CHANGED. Commit b5918b94.

title: pyburn cannot read raw output: pyfft extensions are built for CPython 3.12, venv is 3.14
description:
Every new climate run dies at postprocessing and ExoPlaSim reports 'crashed or begun producing garbage', which is false: the model integrates fine (T42 arm, 95 s/orbit, sensible MOST_DIAG fields, no NaN, complete MOST_REST). Only the postprocessor fails.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced on the surviving raw file: pyburn.readfile imports exoplasim.pyfft (pyburn.py:662), an f2py extension. The only built copies are pyfft.cpython-312-*.so and pyfft991.cpython-312-*.so; the venv is Python 3.14.7 since a1d37bf7. A cpython-312 extension is not importable from 3.14, so pyburn cannot read ANY raw output. The .so files are untracked build artifacts (git tracks only the .f90), so the interpreter upgrade silently invalidated them and no new run has been postprocessed since.

FIX: rebuild both extensions for 3.14. exoplasim.compile_pyfft() exists but wants meson, ninja, gfortran, gcc -- ninja/gfortran/gcc are present, MESON IS NOT, and numpy 2.5 f2py refuses the distutils backend on Python>=3.12.

DO NOT call compile_pyfft() blindly: it runs sysconfigure() when most_compiler/firstrun are absent, which is the pre-CMake build path replaced in 137c55a2. Drive numpy.f2py directly.

The error message is its own defect: __init__.py:1150 turns any postprocessing exception into _crash(), which moves the run to <run>_crashed/ and blames the model.

BLOCKS every run, so SPAT-11 and the physics-filter arms both wait on it.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified 2026-08-23. Every acceptance criterion met.

Both extensions rebuilt for the running interpreter and import: pyfft.cpython-314 and pyfft991.cpython-314. Verified against an identity that can fail rather than by the import alone -- inigau's Gaussian weights are the measure of [-1,1] and must sum to 2, and both give 2.0000000000 exactly.

A raw MOST file postprocesses: run_9d4f4a3ad847's MOST.00000 went to NetCDF, and four subsequent two-orbit runs completed with their postprocessing.

smoke_test carries the check and it was verified BY BREAKING IT: both .so deleted, the check reports the ModuleNotFoundError and exits non-zero, the build restores them, and it goes green. 19 checks 0 failed.

environment.md records that a new interpreter means a pyfft rebuild, with the two commands.

BEYOND THE ROW, because compile_pyfft() could not be the answer: it swallowed failure (the raise was commented out), it called sysconfigure() which calls back into it behind marker files this fork stopped writing -- constructing a Model creates firstrun, which disabled the rebuild permanently -- and it verified nothing. Rewritten to build through sys.executable so the ABI tag cannot disagree with the interpreter that will import the result, to raise with f2py's output on failure, and to verify what it produced. exoplasim/scripts/build_pyfft.py is the registered entry point with a --check arm. Commits 5bb81bb7 and be4e41b3.

Needs meson on the host, which is now installed.

title: The checked build profile justifies -finit-real=snan by an MPI arm that world-38b deleted
description:
config/planet.yaml's model.compile_flags.profiles.checked is ["-fcheck=all", "-finit-real=snan"], and the comment above it ends:

  It is usable in THIS profile because these are MPI binaries, which cannot run
  SHTns. On a threaded build snan traps inside the library before it can say
  anything about the model, which is CLIM-70.

world-38b removed the MPI and serial build paths and the parmode axis, so there are no MPI binaries and every build this project can make is threaded. By the comment's own argument -finit-real=snan in the checked profile now traps inside SHTns before it can say anything about the model, on every build. So either the profile is unusable as declared, or the argument is out of date -- and nothing on record says which.

That matters because the checked profile is not decorative. -finit-real=zero was moved OUT of production on the strength of this profile existing to hold it (exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md, worth 26.03% of T170), on the reasoning that a check which can FAIL beats a tax that hides what it protects against. If the checked profile cannot run, that trade was made against something that does not exist.

Second defect in the same sentence: the issue id is wrong. clim-70 is 'Make a per-cell staged surface field detectably per-cell AFTER a restart' and has nothing to do with snan or SHTns, so a reader following the citation lands somewhere unrelated.

Do: establish whether -finit-real=snan can run on a threaded SHTns build -- the question is whether SHTns reads uninitialised reals of its own, or whether the trap fires only on model arrays -- and then either keep the flag with a correct argument, replace it with something that works on the only build there is, or drop it and say what the checked profile is for without it. Fix the issue citation either way. If the flag goes, exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md's conclusion has to be re-read: it rests on the checked profile being the place the poison went.

Source: notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md finding 1, whose remedy this was.

title: The convergence window's noise costs 20 orbits, about eight hours at T170
description:
assess_convergence uses a ten-orbit window, and at that width the test is noise-dominated: the standard error of the fitted offset is 0.113 K against an allowance of 0.075 K. Swept over the re-run T21 baseline run_8044646ea7f0 with --through, the consequence is now priced rather than described. The temperature is stationary from orbit 58 -- 297.42 K, spread 0.07 K, no trend through orbit 85 -- but the verdict flips seven times after that and only becomes stable at orbit 78. The criterion that flips is always extrapolated_offset_lt_0.15_k, which tests |offset| + half_width; that statistic wanders between 0.031 and 0.255 on a state that is not moving.

Twenty orbits of difference is four minutes at T21. At T170, where an orbit costs about 128 times a T21 orbit, it is about eight hours -- spent proving something the run had already done.

The stated goal for the ladder is to reach a converged state at the highest resolution in the least real time, so this is not a tuning question. Fix the window before the T170 rung is run, not after.

Widening the window is the obvious move and it is not free: a wider window needs more orbits before it can return any verdict at all, so the two effects trade against each other and the crossover has to be measured rather than assumed. The measurement is cheap because it is post-processing -- sweep --through against --window over the existing T21 run and find the window that minimises the orbit at which the verdict becomes STABLE, not the orbit at which it first passes.
acceptance_criteria: A window chosen by sweeping --window against --through on run_8044646ea7f0 and on the T42 arms, reported as the orbit at which each window's verdict becomes stable, with the chosen value written into the script and its reasoning recorded in notes/audits/resolution-ladder.md. The threshold for 'stable' is fixed before the sweep is read.
notes: Raised while re-running the ladder after world-1nz. The related standing point is that a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion, so the stability threshold has to be declared first. window 15 was identified earlier as the shortest that discriminates, on a different and invalid pair of runs; that number needs re-taking on these.

title: The verification arms that pass --parmode, now an unrecognised argument
description:
world-38b removed --parmode from build_model.py. build_model refuses an argument it does not recognise rather than defaulting -- that is the whole point of the file -- so every caller below now exits non-zero having built nothing. Some are a one-token deletion; two are a gate losing its reference arm and are not.

MECHANICAL, drop the argument and the _omp from the name they then look for:
- exoplasim/scripts/thread_count_sweep.sh:25 --parmode omp, :27 names ..._p${n}_omp.x
- exoplasim/scripts/verify_shared_determinism.sh:80 --parmode omp, :58 names ..._p${threads}_omp.x
- exoplasim/scripts/verify_shtns_model.sh:160 --parmode omp (--no-publish --print-path, so :134's _omp name is the only rename)
- exoplasim/scripts/verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh:86 --parmode omp, :41 names ..._p${ranks}_omp.x

A DECISION, because the arm they build does not exist any more:
- exoplasim/scripts/verify_fold_exactness.sh:43,49 and verify_fold_indexing.sh:79 both build --parmode mpi. Their names at :28 and :33 are already the no-suffix ones, so dropping the flag silently retargets each gate onto the threaded binary. Say whether the gate still measures what it was written to measure on that binary before it is retargeted.
- exoplasim/scripts/verify_threaded_numerics.sh:150-159. Its reference arm is 'serial' by default and 'mpi' by argument, and NEITHER build exists now. Its header at :89-95 already anticipates this. A gate whose whole shape is threaded-against-an-independent-reference needs a new reference: a control patch, a standalone driver, or the gate goes.

docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md states the cost this issue is paying: the MPI arm caught the dv2uv planetary vorticity race, the weight pre-scaling bug and the mkdheat inertness result.
acceptance_criteria: Every caller of build_model.py runs. Each gate that lost its reference arm either has a new one or is deleted with a reason; none is left silently comparing a binary against itself.
notes:
Also left for this issue: exoplasim/scripts/verify_shtns_equivalence.sh:47 explains its two-line abort stub as standing in for mpimod_stub, which is deleted. The sentence is still true of mpimod_omp -- the parallel layer drags the restart I/O chain in behind mpabort -- so it is a rename of the module named, not a change to the probe. run_shtns_probe.sh carried the identical sentence and is already fixed under world-38b.

DONE in commit 3b18a2c0, EXCEPT the one decision this issue names. Mechanical four renamed and de-flagged: thread_count_sweep.sh, verify_shared_determinism.sh, verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh, verify_shtns_model.sh. The trap was real and is handled: the no-suffix name is the name the MPI builds published, so an existence test can now find a binary the script did not build; thread_count_sweep.sh and verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh gained the stamp-and-mtime check verify_shared_determinism.sh already had. verify_shtns_model.sh builds --no-publish --print-path and was immune; its _omp name was dead. _bed_guard.sh needed nothing: it globs whatever binary the bed carries and checks the rung prefix, never composing a name. verify_omp_collectives.sh's title and verify_shtns_equivalence.sh's comment renamed off the deleted modules. verify_fold_exactness.sh and verify_fold_indexing.sh are deleted under world-en0, so their MPI arms are moot.

STILL OPEN, and it is the whole of what is left: verify_threaded_numerics.sh has no reference build. It now REFUSES in build_arm's reference case rather than running, because dropping --parmode there would have made the mpi arm build the threaded binary under its own name and compare the thing under test against itself -- a pass that means nothing. Its threaded and control arms are renamed, so only the reference is left to write. THE QUESTION: what is the second side now? A control patch as the reference (the wrongband patch already exists and is deterministic), a standalone driver that computes the band decomposition independently, or the gate goes. This costs what vendored-upstreams.md records the MPI arm caught: the dv2uv planetary vorticity race, the weight pre-scaling bug, the mkdheat inertness result. Not a decision to take inside another issue.

title: Follow the parmode removal into the runner, the package and the config
description:
world-38b removed the parmode axis from the build: build_model.executable_name now writes most_plasim_<res>_l<levels>_p<ranks>.x with no _omp, and rebuild_binaries.expected and check_consistency's cycle-capability check agree with it. Three consumers still append _omp or read model.parmode, and after the next rebuild each will go looking for a file that is not there.

Sites, all re-located against the tree as it stands after world-38b:

- exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py:2567 sets exe_suffix = '_omp' if model.parmode == 'omp', used at :2569 to name the executable the run must find, and raises if it is absent. Drop the suffix.
- vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py:367-368 composes the same name from self.parmode. This is the one that actually opens the binary. :388 also prints a build command carrying --parmode, which build_model.py no longer accepts.
- exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py:1161 declare_parmode raises when model.parmode is absent and refuses anything but 'mpi' or 'omp'. With one parallel layer it decides nothing; :2374-2393 and prepare_thread_stack at :93-104 are its readers, and the thread stack must still be prepared unconditionally rather than behind a parmode test.
- config/planet.yaml model.parmode: omp is what declare_parmode reads. It cannot be deleted before declare_parmode goes, or every run raises.
- lib/provenance.py:278,315,359,398 list model.parmode among the config keys a stamped artifact is checked against. Remove it with the key.
- exoplasim/scripts/build_restart_template.py:180 names a template <res>_l<lev>_p<n>_<parmode>.rest from the run manifest's physical block. The templates on disk are T21_l10_p16_omp.rest and T42_l10_p16_omp.rest, so renaming the slot renames staged artifacts; decide whether the template keeps the parmode word or drops it with the executable.

TWO LATENT BUGS THE RENAME FIXES, which is evidence the no-suffix name is the right one: continue_exoplasim.py:692 and run_stellar_cycle.py:297 already compose the name WITHOUT the suffix, so both were looking for a binary the omp-only registry never built.
acceptance_criteria: No consumer composes an _omp suffix; declare_parmode and model.parmode are gone or justified; a run finds the binary rebuild_binaries.py builds. Rule 4 applies: rebuild and --verify.
close_reason: Every consumer that composed an _omp suffix or read model.parmode is fixed: vendor __init__.py (binary name, suggested build command, and the parmode/mpi_opts/hyperthreading constructor parameters), run_exoplasim.py (exe_suffix, declare_parmode, --mpi-opts, the manifest's physical.parmode, prepare_thread_stack now unconditional and argument-free), continue_exoplasim.py, run_stellar_cycle.py, lib/provenance.py, config/planet.yaml, build_restart_template.py. declare_parmode is gone: with one binary and one transform it decided nothing, and model.parmode could not go before it did. The template name drops the parmode word rather than becoming the literal 'x'. Not verified by rebuild: batch J's build change is on fanout-J and not in this worktree, and the batch prompt forbids compiling. Rule 4's rebuild-and---verify is the coordinator's after the merge. Commit bde2bd65.

title: Commission T21 afresh: run_2b20e3324bb0 is not a baseline, on its damping or on its surface
description:
run_2b20e3324bb0 is the T21 production baseline on disk -- 85 orbits, 11.42 GB,
status climatology_complete -- and it is not a baseline. Two independent
reasons, either sufficient on its own.

ITS DAMPING. Its plasim_namelist carries no NDEL, no NHDIFF and no TDISS* at
all, while its run_manifest.json records a hyperdiffusion block claiming T21's
derived values. The manifest's five segments say how it got there:
  seg 0  orbits  0-39  spinup, prepared by run_exoplasim
  seg 1  orbits 40-69  spinup, continuation
  seg 2  orbits 70-81  post_equilibrium_climatology, continuation
  seg 3  orbit  83     diagnostic, continuation
  seg 4  orbit  84     diagnostic, continuation
Under world-1nz a continuation wrote no hyperdiffusion at all, so 45 of the 85
orbits ran the model's compiled T21 defaults on every level: ndel 2 rather than
4, grad^4 rather than grad^8. Under world-720 the prepare path wrote the keys as
bare scalars, which in a Fortran namelist sets element 1 and leaves levels 2 to
10 at the compiled defaults, so the other 40 orbits ran the configured damping
on one level of ten. No orbit of this run integrated what it records.

ITS SURFACE. The run's physical fingerprint carries geography 3080098d. The T21
surface family currently staged under exoplasim/inputs/t21 digests to 93c5a2c9
by geography_tag's own rule, and every .sra there was regenerated at 13:42 on
2026-08-24, after this run finished at 12:46. The run is not on the surface this
build now has.

Nothing about this is a judgement call under rule 7: the canonical climatology
lineage does not exist yet, so the run is disposable and the only question is
what is now worthless. Its climatologies are, and so is the 70-orbit T21
convergence figure measured on it, which downstream components must not carry.

The ladder's arm A carried the same damping defect. run_8102b89a08ac is now 1
orbit, smoke_complete, and likewise has no hyperdiffusion keys.

The code defects are both closed -- continue_exoplasim.py:587 calls
declare_hyperdiffusion, both drivers write layer-count-replicated
`<layers>*<value>` lists, and verify_staged_namelists compares them as text and
raises so a scalar cannot pass -- so a fresh run is correct.

Do, in order: rebuild every binary (rule 4; this fan-out changed
vendor/exoplasim heavily), regenerate the T21 surface family against the merged
config (check_consistency currently FAILS "generated inputs vs their config" for
boundary_conditions, albedo, roughness and 0229), then commission T21 from cold.
Measure the convergence orbit with an assess_convergence --through sweep.
verify_staged_namelists is the guard that has to pass on every segment.
acceptance_criteria: Binaries rebuilt, the T21 surface family regenerated against the merged config, and a fresh T21 commissioning from cold whose plasim_namelist carries the configured NDEL, NHDIFF and the four TDISS* as layer-count-replicated lists in every segment -- verify_staged_namelists is what enforces that and raises. Its exact convergence orbit measured by an assess_convergence --through sweep. world-e6m's retrospective gate passing on it.
notes:
Found while re-running the resolution ladder's arm A, which carries the same defect (run_8102b89a08ac). The check that catches it is the 'runs vs the hyperdiffusion they declared' case in scripts/check_consistency.py, added with the world-1nz fix.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55), reading the run
directories rather than the note. VERDICT: CHANGED. The run is still not a
baseline; three things in the row are wrong and one of them is in the notes
above.

WHAT THE ARTIFACT SAYS. run_2b20e3324bb0 is on disk, 85 orbits, 11.42 GB,
status climatology_complete, and its plasim_namelist carries no NDEL, no
NHDIFF and no TDISS* of any kind. Confirmed by reading the file. Its
run_manifest.json records a `hyperdiffusion` block (T21, nhdiff 8, alpha 4,
tau_vorticity 2.2285 d), so the manifest claims damping the namelist does not
carry.

THE ORBIT COUNT IS WRONG, and in the direction that makes it worse. The
manifest's five segments are:
  seg 0  orbits  0-39  spinup, prepared by run_exoplasim
  seg 1  orbits 40-69  spinup, continuation
  seg 2  orbits 70-81  post_equilibrium_climatology, continuation
  seg 3  orbit  83     diagnostic, continuation
  seg 4  orbit  84     diagnostic, continuation
So world-1nz's defect (a continuation writing no hyperdiffusion at all) covers
45 of the 85 orbits, not 84. But world-720's defect covers ALL 85: segment 0
predates the replicated-list fix and every run on disk from that period writes
the keys as bare scalars (`TDISSQ = 0.7421`, `NDEL = 4`), which in Fortran sets
element 1 and leaves levels 2 to 10 at the compiled T21 defaults. So no orbit
of this run integrated the configured damping on more than one level of ten,
and 45 of them integrated it on none.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INVALIDATOR, which the row does not know about. The run's
physical fingerprint carries geography 3080098d. The T21 surface family
currently staged under exoplasim/inputs/t21 digests to 93c5a2c9 by
geography_tag's own rule, and those .sra files were regenerated at 13:42 on
2026-08-24, after this run finished at 12:46. The run is therefore not on the
surface this build now has, whatever its damping did. Its climatologies are
worthless twice over and the 70-orbit T21 convergence figure goes with them for
either reason on its own.

THE OTHER RUN THIS ROW'S NOTES NAME. run_8102b89a08ac, the ladder's arm A, is
now 1 orbit and smoke_complete with an empty climatologies block; the 86-orbit
T42 arm is gone. Its plasim_namelist likewise carries no hyperdiffusion keys.

THE CHECK NAMED IN THE NOTES DOES NOT EXIST. There is no "runs vs the
hyperdiffusion they declared" case in scripts/check_consistency.py; the only
gate of that shape over run directories is "runs vs the energy fixer they
claim". What world-8bs actually built is run_exoplasim.py's

title: Masked lanes are evaluated in radmod's where-blocks at -O3, and the arguments are out of domain there
description:
gfortran vectorises where-blocks at -O3 by evaluating BOTH branches and
selecting, so an expression that is only legal in the lanes its mask keeps is
computed in the lanes it masks out as well. radmod.f90 has at least six such
sites and they produce a real NaN in the longwave radiation on a state that is
otherwise sound.

THE SITES, all confirmed in the current source:
- lwr's clear-sky transmissivity where/elsewhere chain, radmod.f90:3319-3355:
    ALOG10(zsumwv(:)+0.01)   :3322   elsewhere-branch of zsumwv <= 0.01
    ALOG10(zsumco2(:))       :3336   elsewhere-branch of zsumco2 <= 1.0
    log(zsumwv(:)-0.6931)    :3344   elsewhere-branch of zsumwv <= 2.
    log10(zsumo3(:))         :3352   elsewhere-branch of zsumo3 <= 0.01
  Each argument is legitimate above its own threshold and zero or negative
  below it. This is the block the observed fault was in.
- the shortwave cloud block, where(losun .and. dcc>0), radmod.f90:2425-2450:
  SQRT(zmu0(:)) at :2441 and :2442. zmu0 is the cosine of the solar zenith
  angle and is NEGATIVE at night, which is exactly what losun masks out.
- the shortwave absorber block, where(losun), radmod.f90:2484.
Clamping one moves the fault to the next, which is what says it is a class
rather than an instance.

IT IS A REAL NaN AND THE TRAP IS DOING ITS JOB. Rebuilding the T42
configuration with -ffpe-trap dropped, the same orbit from the same restart
completed and wrote a restart in which 69 of 199 records were non-finite: the
whole spectral state, sz, sd, st, sq, sp and their leapfrog partners. The FPE
trap is the only thing standing between this and a silent NaN climatology, and
the production binary carries it while an arbitrary rebuild need not.

RULED OUT WHEN IT WAS OBSERVED: not a blow-up (the preceding orbits held 294.1
to 294.8 K, jets at 90-100 m/s, surface pressure steady), not a corrupt restart
(no negatives in humidity, cloud, soil water, snow or ice, nothing non-finite),
not disk or memory. The snan-poisoned checked build does not isolate it: it
trips earlier in shtnsmod on scratch.

WHY IT MATTERS. Arm A ran 86 orbits at T42 on the same executable without
hitting it. Reachable but not common is the worst kind: a long climate run dies,
or a build without the trap produces a NaN climatology.

DO. Clamp each unsafe argument at the six sites, to a value that is an exact
no-op in the lanes the mask keeps -- zmu0 > 0 in daylight, each sum above its
own threshold in the elsewhere branch. That is a check that can fail: the clamp
is an identity where the mask keeps the lane, so the restart must be bit
identical on any state that did not previously trap. The physics is not touched.
-fno-tree-vectorize removes the whole class instead but is a build flag paying
for a source defect, protects nothing on a build that drops it, and its cost was
measured badly (the base arm crashed mid-run); if it is wanted, re-measure with
traps dropped on both arms.

Source: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/radmod.f90.
exoplasim/runs/run_47459a115d06_crashed holds the state the fault was observed
on, but see the notes: that reproduction expires at the next mandatory rebuild
and the defect is a property of the source, not of that trajectory.
acceptance_criteria: The six unsafe masked arguments in radmod.f90 clamped to values that are exact no-ops in the lanes their masks keep, verified by a bit-identical restart on a state that did not previously trap, and the FPE trap kept in production.
notes:
Downgraded in importance by world-caz (the hyperdiffusion regression) but NOT explained away by it. The radiation SIGFPE is real and reproduces on arm A's own state too, so it is not conversion-specific.

MECHANISM ESTABLISHED: unsafe masked expressions in where-blocks that gfortran vectorises at -O3, evaluating BOTH branches. The clearest instance is radmod.f90:2464-2495, guarded on losun (daylight), containing SQRT(zmu0) -- and zmu0, the cosine of the solar zenith angle, is NEGATIVE at night in the masked-out lanes. There are at least three: the longwave ozone/water/CO2 transmissivity blocks near 3344-3384, the shortwave cloud block at 2464, and the shortwave absorber block at 2523. Clamping one moves the fault to the next.

-fno-tree-vectorize removes the whole class but costs performance (measured badly -- the base arm crashed mid-run so that timing is not usable; needs redoing with traps dropped on both arms).

The clamps are exact no-ops in the lanes the mask keeps -- zmu0 > 0 in daylight -- so the fix does not touch the physics.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT:
CHANGED. The mechanism survives in source and is unchanged; the reproduction
and the trajectory-specific evidence do not survive this fan-out.

THE MECHANISM IS INTACT, cites re-located by content. Unsafe expressions inside
where-blocks that gfortran evaluates in both branches when it vectorises at -O3:
- lwr's transmissivity where/elsewhere chain, radmod.f90:3319-3355:
    ALOG10(zsumwv(:)+0.01)          at :3322, elsewhere-branch of zsumwv<=0.01
    ALOG10(zsumco2(:))              at :3336, elsewhere-branch of zsumco2<=1.0
    log(zsumwv(:)-0.6931)           at :3344, elsewhere-branch of zsumwv<=2.
    log10(zsumo3(:))                at :3352, elsewhere-branch of zsumo3<=0.01
  Each is legitimate in the lanes its mask keeps and negative or zero in the
  lanes it masks out. This is the block the fault was in.
- the shortwave cloud block, where(losun .and. dcc>0), radmod.f90:2425-2450:
  SQRT(zmu0(:)) at :2441 and :2442, and zmu0 is negative at night.
CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE: it names radmod.f90:2464-2495 as "the clearest
instance ... containing SQRT(zmu0)". What is at :2464 now is the magnification
factor block, 35./SQRT(1.+1224.*zmu0*zmu0), which is safe for any real zmu0.
The bare SQRT(zmu0) is at :2441-2442, two dozen lines earlier. The count of at
least three unsafe blocks stands; the third is the shortwave absorber block, now
the where(losun) do-jlev loop at :2484.

THE REPRODUCTION IS EXPIRING, and after the mandatory rebuild it is gone.
- run_47459a115d06_crashed still holds MOST_REST.00000 through .00007 and its
  plasim_restart, and its manifest records T42, executable
  eae6b0e89357df58...; the T42 entry in exoplasim/binary_manifest.json is the
  same sha, so as the tree stands today the crashing binary still exists.
- But radmod.f90 changed on this branch in seven commits (world-9d1, world-bqb,
  world-ro6, world-5rq, world-sv7, world-qvu, and the batch H merge), and rule 4
  requires every binary rebuilt after a change under vendor/exoplasim. Once that
  happens the executable is different, and "exactly eight orbits, byte-identical,
  backtrace at radmod.f90:3374" is no longer a recipe. Line 3374 today is inside
  the CLIM-42 CH4/N2O block, not the fault site.
- The trajectory is gone independently anyway: the state was converted from a
  T21 run whose surface family has since been regenerated, and the calendar, the
  filter power, the hyperdiffusion write, the sea-ice cold start, the surface
  albedo bands and the saturation-over-ice branch all moved under it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE. The defect is a property of the source and the
compiler, not of that trajectory: masked lanes are still evaluated, the
arguments are still out of domain there, and the FPE trap is still the only
thing between this and a NaN climatology on a build without it. Arm A having run
86 orbits on the same executable without hitting it is what makes it dangerous
rather than what makes it rare.

DO, restated. Two routes, and the choice is not between them and doing nothing:
- clamp each unsafe argument at the four lwr sites and the two shortwave sites
  above, to a value that is an exact no-op in the lanes the mask keeps (zmu0 > 0
  in daylight; the sums positive above their own thresholds). Six clamps, and
  the physics is untouched.
- or -fno-tree-vectorize, which removes the class and costs performance. The
  cost was measured badly -- the base arm crashed mid-run -- and needs redoing
  with traps dropped on both arms.
Prefer the clamps: -fno-tree-vectorize is a build flag paying for a source
defect, and it silently protects nothing on a build that drops it.

The bisection the old NEXT paragraph proposes (-O1/-O2, -fno-tree-vectorize,
the probe directory) is no longer available at the granularity it assumes,
because the binary and the trajectory are both about to move. Verify the clamps
by construction instead: each is an identity in the kept lanes, which is a check
that can fail.

SETTLED IN PARALLEL, 2026-08-24, by another wave-2 batch, after the
re-verification above was written. The close reason is authoritative and
supersedes the DO paragraph: the production profile moved to -O2 (benchmarked at
the same speed), the probe orbit completes with a finite restart, and two real
source defects were fixed on the way -- radmod initialising its shortwave column
integrals only inside where(losun), and rainmod's unbounded Tetens exponents
under kuo's untested parcel iteration. The remaining 66 masked domain-sensitive
intrinsics are world-5a0; -O2 vectorises too, so the class is quieter rather
than gone.

The re-located cites above stand and are what world-5a0 inherits: the lwr
transmissivity chain at radmod.f90:3319-3355 and the shortwave cloud block at
:2425-2450, with the SQRT(zmu0) at :2441-2442 and NOT at :2464.
close_reason: Not a NaN in the longwave: -O3's loop transforms evaluating the masked-out lanes of the physics modules' where-blocks, which -ffpe-trap then reports. The production profile is -O2, benchmarked at the same speed (41.35 s against 41.23 s over four interleaved T42 rounds, inside the 1.37 s scatter), and the probe orbit that died eight orbits in now completes with a finite restart. Two real source defects were found on the way and are fixed: radmod initialised its shortwave column integrals only inside where(losun), so night lanes carried stack contents into an accumulation that reads them, and rainmod's eighteen Tetens exponents are unbounded because kuo iterates a parcel temperature with no convergence test. The remaining 66 masked domain-sensitive intrinsics are world-5a0 -- -O2 vectorises too, so the class is quieter rather than gone.

title: restart_schema.py needs a POLICY entry for the glacier persistence clock
description:
glaciermod.f90's glacierstop writes a new restart record, 'persistt', the seconds of continuous snow cover at or above GLACELIM that world-qpe's persistence criterion counts. exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py has no POLICY entry for it, so scripts/smoke_test.py's "the restart schema covers every record the model writes" check is RED.

The entry, to go beside 'dsnowz' in the land prognostic block:

    "persistt": Policy(PROGNOSTIC_GRID, REMAP, INTENSIVE, domain="land",
                       bounds=(0.0, None),
                       why="seconds of continuous snow cover at or above "
                           "glacelim; the glacier persistence clock. An "
                           "elapsed TIME per cell, so it remaps as an "
                           "intensity and not as an inventory"),

INTENSIVE rather than RESERVOIR: it is an elapsed time per cell, not a stock, so an area-weighted mean is the right operator and there is no global inventory to close. domain="land" because glacierstep zeroes it wherever dls <= 0.5. bounds lower-bounded at zero because the clock is reset to 0.0 and only ever incremented by deltsec.

It is not an accumulator in restart_schema's sense: outreset never touches it, and its clean value at a cold start is zero only because a cold start has no snow, not because something resets it.
acceptance_criteria: smoke_test's restart-schema check passes; persistt has a POLICY entry with a stated remap policy.
close_reason: Applied on the coordination branch: persistt entered in restart_schema.POLICY as PROGNOSTIC_GRID/REMAP/INTENSIVE, domain land, bounds (0.0, None). smoke_test 22/22.

title: The T42 hyperdiffusion null result was measured on a damping that reached one level
description:
exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md reports that applying the derived

tau_vorticity of 3.7x. world-720 establishes that the experiment wrote TDISS*
and NDEL as bare scalars, so levels 2 to 10 kept the compiled T42 branch's
values while level 1 held the derived ones: the arm did not apply what it
recorded. Confirmed against the artifacts -- every run directory on disk that
carries these keys writes them as scalars, none writes the replicated form.

The analytic filter-versus-diffusion comparison (world-6on) stands on its own
and is not in question. What is in question is the corroborating experiment.

IT IS NOT A REBUILD AND TWO ORBITS ANY MORE. The settled T42 restart the arms
started from is gone (run_8102b89a08ac is 1 orbit, smoke_complete, and no other
T42 run on disk has more than one). The T42 surface family has been regenerated
and fails check_consistency against the merged config. filter_power moved from 8
to 16, and since the whole point of the finding is that the filter dominates the
hyperdiffusion, "two arms differing only in tau" is a different experiment at
the current gamma. And rule 4 requires every binary rebuilt first.

the binaries are rebuilt, the surface family regenerated and a settled T42
restart exists, run the two arms at the CURRENT filter with layer-count-

Depends on the same commissioning world-hxm asks for.

title: Salinity reaches the model through four compiled constants, and CPS is fresh water's value
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 10.

config/planet.yaml's ocean block states salinity "reaches the model through one
number, the freezing point of sea water". Four Fortran parameters carry it and
three have no namelist key:

  TFREEZE        icemod.f90:54                  freezing point; handled, -0.04 to -0.36 K
  CRHOS = 1030.  icemod.f90:21, oceanmod.f90:20 density "at S=34.7"; 1016 to 1032
  CPS = 4180.    oceanmod.f90:22                labelled sea water, IS FRESH WATER'S; 4070 to 3950
  CLFI = 3.28E5  icemod.f90:30                  fusion, depressed by Earth brine

Two separable consequences.

The mixed-layer heat capacity CRHOS*CPS used at oceanmod.f90:401 and :816 is
4.305e6 J/m3/K against sea water's real 4.10e6 at the declared salinity, so 5.1
per cent too large: the DECLARED mixed_layer_depth_m 50.0 is thermally 52.5 m of
sea water, and scripts/error_budget.py carries that depth as a structural item
stated in metres.

The snow-ice flooding threshold at icemod.f90:1349-1352 is
`1.E3*xsnow > (CRHOS-CRHOI)*xiced`, a DIFFERENCE of 1030-920 = 110, so a 1 per
cent density error is a 10 per cent threshold error. Across S = 20 to 40 the
true margin runs 96 to 112, i.e. -13 to +2 per cent about the compiled value: a
fresher ocean floods and converts snow to ice substantially earlier, trading
insulating snow for conducting ice and accelerating basal growth. That is a
sea-ice feedback CLIM-17's bracket is meant to span and currently cannot.

Do: correct CPS; make the salinity-dependent constants reachable; correct the
"one number" claim in config/planet.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: CPS is sea water's value; the salinity-dependent constants are reachable or explicitly declared; CLIM-17's bracket moves the flooding threshold; the config block no longer says one number.
close_reason: CRHOS, CPS and CLFI are icemod_nl keys; icemod passes all four salinity constants into oceanini so the two modules cannot hold different sea water, and oceanmod's own parameter copies are gone. CONSUMERS ENUMERATED: CPS reaches (a) the mixed-layer heat capacity CRHOS*CPS in mksst, mkiflux, addfc, mkfc and the entropy diagnostics, and through mkiflux's residual flux it reaches ice growth as well as the SST tendency; icemod's own CPS was declared and never used, and is now the source of truth it passes down. CRHOS additionally is the snow-ice flooding threshold in subsnow as CRHOS-CRHOI. CLFI appears only as CRHOI*CLFI, latent heat per m3 of ice, in icestep, mkice, mkflukoi, addfci and oceanmod's addfc. CRHOF is declared in icemod and used nowhere. VALUES: CPS's compiled default corrected from 4180 (fresh water at about 25 C) to 3990.34 (sea water at S=34.7 and its freezing point); CRHOS and CLFI keep their compiled defaults and are only exposed. run_exoplasim derives CRHOS and CPS from config's salinity by EOS-80 and the UNESCO (1983) polynomial, each checked against published check values and against the constant CPS replaces; CLFI is declared in config because it depends on the ice's own salinity and temperature and the model has no such variable. All four go through configure_otherargs, so they survive a continuation, and through expected_namelist_keys. At the declared salinity the run configuration moves to CRHOS 1027.94 and CPS 3990.33: mixed-layer heat capacity down 5.1 per cent, so a declared 50 m mixed layer is 50 m of sea water rather than 52.5, and the flooding margin CRHOS-CRHOI from 110 to 107.94. Every run and climatology on disk is superseded (rule 7). Commit 9c952a18.

title: A 5 m snow cap makes the enabled glacier module unable to build an ice sheet
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 4.

landmod.f90:55 dsmax = 5.00 m water equivalent, applied at landmod.f90:842-861.
The cap is applied to dsnowz, which is the same accumulator glaciermod.f90:355-358
builds ice orography from, so glacieroro cannot exceed 5.0/0.85, about 5.9 m of
ice. The module's stated purpose, "capturing the effects of large ice sheets on
atmospheric circulation" (glaciermod.f90:1-8), is unreachable, and
glaciermod.f90:211's `where (dsnowz > 30.0) dglac = 1.0` is dead code.

5 m is PlaSim's Earth seasonal-snow ceiling, chosen for a model where perennial
ice arrives as a prescribed mask rather than being grown by this module.
NGLACIER=1 and GLACELIM=2.0 are staged, so the module is on.

Everything above the cap is diagnosed as snowmelt (landmod.f90:860) and pushed
into dwater, so into soil water and runoff. Any cell that would glaciate instead
manufactures perpetual meltwater at up to the full snowfall rate, inflating
runoff and latent cooling and suppressing the ice-albedo feedback at the margin.

Do: pass maxsnow, which configure() already exposes at __init__.py:2840-2841, at
a value that lets perennial accumulation run, and declare it. Bears on
notes/glacier-rough-pass.md and on clim-34.
acceptance_criteria: maxsnow is passed and declared; a cold high-latitude cell can accumulate past 5.9 m of ice; the glacier orography responds.
close_reason: DSMAX is now surface.glaciers.max_snow_depth_m in config/planet.yaml, declared as -1 (landmod's own no-limit), reaching the model both through configure(maxsnow=) and through configure_otherargs so a continuation cannot revert it. Verified the premise first: NGLACIER=1 comes from surface.glaciers.enabled, and glaciermod's own 'dsnowz > 30.0 -> dglac = 1.0' was unreachable under the 5 m cap. The cap was NOT the only gate. landini's 'dsnowz = AMAX1(dsmax,0.)' for cells that arrive as glacier reads the cap as an initial depth, so with no cap it gives zero; glacierini runs immediately after landini and raises such cells to GLACELIM, which is the glacier module's own initial depth, and the staged dglac field is all zeros on this build in any case. The soil column is not exposed to unbounded snow either: landmod blends at most zsnowmax = 1 m of physical snow into it. Both facts are recorded at the code.

title: Snow over forest is masked by one spectrum-blind factor applied to both bands
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 7.

landmod.f90:229-236 sets albsmaxf1 = 0.5*albsmax1, albsmaxf2 = 0.5*albsmax2 and
albsminf1 = 0.75*albsmaxf1 for both bands, used at :544-561 to set dsalb, which
is what the radiation reads at NSTARTEMP=1 (radmod.f90:2951-2952).

The endmembers albsmax1/2 are correctly derived from the k25v spectrum. The
canopy masking on top of them is not: 0.5 and 0.75 are Earth-Sun broadband
ratios, from upstream's albsmaxf=0.4 over albsmax=0.8 (landmod.f90:28-31),
applied identically either side of 0.75 micron.

Same class as notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md finding 1, which named
codes 175 and 176 over vegetated GROUND. This is the SNOW albedo and nothing has
corrected it. Distinct from world-9m5, which is build_surface_albedo.py's tree
and grass endmembers.

Live, not the uniform-land default. Measured 2026-08-24 from the staged
orogen_T21_surf_0212.sra: 2048 cells, max 0.4988, nonzero on 997 cells with mean
0.3120 over those.

With albsmax1 = 0.96819, albsmax2 = 0.58529 and band weights 0.38237/0.61763,
anchoring on band 1 with model.vegetation_albedo_bands implies a canopy cover of
0.542, giving a band-2 forested endmember of 0.390 against the code's 0.293, so
0.097 too dark at full canopy; anchoring on band 2 leaves band 1 about 0.16 too
bright. One factor cannot serve both. About 0.019 too dark broadband at the
land-mean forest fraction and 0.030 at the maximum, one-signed warm, with the
larger half of the error in the band this star puts 0.618 of surface shortwave
into. Not in landmod_nl.
acceptance_criteria: The forest masking factor differs per band and is derived from the spectrum; band 1 and band 2 forested endmembers are mutually consistent at a single canopy cover.
close_reason: albsmaxf1/2 and albsminf1/2 are now a mixture of the band's exposed snow with the band's canopy albedo at a masked fraction, not a broadband ratio reapplied per band. landmod_nl gains albforest(2), forcovmx and forcovmn. The two fractions are solved from upstream's own Earth triple: 0.6153846*0.15 + 0.3846154*0.8 = 0.4 = albsmaxf and 0.4*0.15 + 0.6*0.4 = 0.3 = albsminf, so an Earth configuration reproduces upstream exactly, which is the check that can fail. run_exoplasim passes ALBFOREST = model.vegetation_albedo_bands = 0.075, 0.225 through configure_otherargs, so both the prepare and the resume path carry it. At full canopy the forested maxima move from 0.4914/0.2926 to 0.4241/0.3636 and the minima from 0.3685/0.2195 to 0.3347/0.2536: band 1 darker by 0.067, band 2 brighter by 0.071, +0.018 broadband. The two fractions differ from each other because upstream's two observational pairs do; that is recorded at the declaration rather than averaged away.

title: The land roughness field is anchored through a reference height computed at Earth's gravity
description:
build_surface_roughness.py:19, 221 and 244 hardcode 141.6 m as 'this planet's lowest level', three times, with no config key and no derivation. hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py:217 DERIVES the same quantity as (GASCON * t_air / gravity) * ln(1/SIGMA_LOWEST).

Measured 2026-08-24 with GASCON 287.017, SIGMA_LOWEST 0.9828: at g = 12.81 the reference height is 108.46 m at 279 K; at Earth's 9.80665 it is 141.67 m. The hardcoded value is the Earth one, high by exactly the gravity ratio 1.306.

The builder bisects k_oro so the area-weighted land mean of the derived z0 hits a target through ce = 0.16/ln(141.6/z0)^2, so the anchor is 14% low: ce at the 2.0 m default is 0.00882 as coded against 0.01004 correct. The '7.7x too much exchange' claim in the docstring and in lake-representation.md:208-214 is really 8.4x. This reaches land evaporation and therefore the carve criterion.

Separately: 0.16 is an unstated von Karman squared.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: lib/lapse.py:reference_height_m is now the one derivation; build_surface_roughness.py and carve_verdict.py both call it, and 0.16 is named KARMAN**2. CORRECTION to the finding: 141.6 does not enter the k_oro bisection, which solves on the land mean of z0 against dz0land directly, so the written field is unchanged and nothing downstream is invalidated -- the Earth height reached only the report's exchange_coefficient block and the prose quoting it. The report now brackets ce over 273.15-313.15 K because the height is linear in the lowest-level air temperature and the step runs before any climatology exists. Playa contrast about 8x not 7.7x; lake-representation.md water-roughness contrast about 11x not 10.4x.

title: Surface longwave emissivity is 0.98 over non-land and exactly 1.0 over land, uncited anywhere
description:
radmod.f90:3237: zeps(:) = dls(:) + 0.98*(1.-dls(:)). Land emissivity is exactly 1.0 by construction, ocean and sea ice 0.98. No comment, no unit, no citation. Verified that grep for 'emissivity' across notes/, exoplasim/notes/, docs/src/ and bd search returns nothing: this is the only large radiative literal in the module with zero coverage anywhere in the tree.

It is used consistently (:3238 emission, :3547 the (1-eps) reflection of downward longwave), so it is not an energy-conservation defect. It is an unexamined number. The cost is (1-eps)*(sigma*Ts^4 - LW_down), identically zero over land at eps = 1.0. Measured broadband emissivity of bare rock and desert sand is 0.90 to 0.95, so on a world with a large barren land fraction that is roughly 3.5 to 7 W/m2 of overstated land emission over the driest surfaces, one-signed. Ocean at 0.98 against seawater's 0.985 to 0.99 is roughly 0.5 to 1.5 W/m2.

Derive a land emissivity from the lithology map, or DECLARE the current values with a bracket.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Fixed in 42c434f2 by the DECLARE branch of the two the issue offers. ELWLAND and ELWSEA are radmod_nl keys at the values the literal carried, declared in config/planet.yaml with the bracket (0.90 to 1.0 land, 0.98 to 0.99 non-land), written unconditionally into every run's namelist and checked there by verify_staged_namelists. Behaviour is bit-identical: the defaults in the Fortran, in derive() and in expected_namelist_keys are all 1.0 and 0.98. The DERIVE branch needs a per-cell field from the lithology map, which a scalar cannot carry; filed as world-38y. Needs a rebuild (rule 4).

title: The CO2 shortwave patch and its analysis artifact still carry the superseded Howard fit
description:
radmod.f90:2262-2265 runs the HITRAN2020 refit (zca1=3.0658E-4, zcb1=20.376, zca2=3.8193E-3, zcb2=3.9672E-3, PHYS-10). exoplasim/patches/exoplasim-3.4.2-co2-shortwave.patch:193-196 and exoplasim/analysis/shortwave_band_weights.json (co2.closed_form_fit) both still carry the Howard fit (3.8265E-4, 44.539, 2.2325E-3, 5.8954E-3), which is +7.7% in absorptance at this planet's CO2 path.

exoplasim/notes/shortwave-co2.md:163-165 asserts the two agree, and shortwave_band_weights.py:986-988 writes that claim into every regenerated JSON, where it is true of the patch and false of the model.

Two consequences: re-running the generator silently reasserts the superseded fit as the stored artifact, and rebuilding from the patch stack restores a CO2 shortwave term 7.2% too strong. patches/README.md:20-22 requires a superseded patch to say so; it does not, and it is upstream PR #62.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Fixed in 4b946a05. The generator now reads radmod.f90's four coefficients instead of asserting its own Howard fit is the model's, and prices every CO2 prediction on them; corrk_cross_check --fit reads them back and reports a mismatch; the patch header declares its fit superseded per patches/README.md. Re-derived from the correlated-k tables: the refit reproduces radmod's coefficients exactly and Howard is +7.7% at this planet's path. The stored artifact's climatology-derived numbers were left as they stand -- predict() needs a baseline climatology and config declares none, so it cannot be regenerated on this build, and prediction_co2 now records which fit priced it.

title: The transform-equivalence gate certifies filter_power 8, and the model has run 16 since 2026-08-23
description:
verify_shtns_equivalence.f90:72 sets nfilterexp = 8 under the comment 'as the beds run it', inside a block header asserting 'THE CONFIGURATION UNDER TEST IS THE ONE THE MODEL RUNS'. config/planet.yaml:388 declares filter_power: 16, derived (gamma >= 14.78 required at T21), with check_consistency.py enforcing it. filter_kappa still matches; only gamma is stale.

Direction matters: exp(-8x^8) damps the mid-band far harder than exp(-8x^16) (0.969 against 0.9999 at n/NTRU = 0.5), and the mid-to-high band is where the SHTns residual is largest. The gate therefore measures a SMALLER transform error than the shipped configuration produces.

Fix the literal, then re-run the gate and re-read world-y9m's verdict against the result.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Literal fixed to 16 in verify_shtns_equivalence.f90 and in both probe_shtns_*.f90, which carried the same stale value; smoke_test.py:check_gate_filter_matches_config now compares every filterkappa/nfilterexp literal under exoplasim/scripts against config/planet.yaml in both directions. Certification confirmed power-dependent: both arms carry the same skspgp(n) so the filter divides out of a per-mode ratio, but the gate's error is a field norm and exp(-k x^16)/exp(-k x^8) peaks at exp(k/4) = 7.39 at kappa 8, at n/NTRU = 0.917. NOT re-run: compiling and running the gates is out of scope for the worktree, so world-y9m's verdict still needs re-reading against a gate run at gamma 16.

title: t0 = 250.0 K on every level is undeclared, and the core energy sink scales with it
description:
plasimmod.f90:882 declares t0(NLEV) = 250.0, the semi-implicit reference temperature, isothermal on all ten levels. It is a plasim_nl key and no run sets it: every diag echoes T0= 10*250.0. Nothing in notes/, docs/src/ or bd asks why 250, though resolution-tuned-parameters.md cites it repeatedly as a given.

It ranks high because the project's own measurement makes the energy sink proportional to it: Phi0_k = Sum_j g(j,k) t0 is built from t0 alone, and the note's finding is that Phi0 weights the difference by up to 3.8 times t0, giving Cimp - Ct = -0.9588 W/m2 against a sink of -0.7938. The defect the fork's energy fixer exists to mask therefore scales with a number nobody chose, and 250 K is Earth's mass-weighted tropospheric mean rather than this atmosphere's.

It also sets the explicit gravity-wave limit nconvtime computes (plasim.f90:700) and the blow-up floor at plasim.f90:1338.

Derive t0 from this atmosphere's own profile, or DECLARE it with the argument for keeping Earth's.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Derived and declared, and the result is a null one. The rule: the mass-weighted mean of the setzt profile over the model's own ten sigma levels, weights dsigma, on the NEQSIG=4 grid every run is on. On Earth's constants and Earth's ISA profile it returns 248.45 K, which identifies where the inherited 250.0 came from and is what makes the rule checkable rather than merely plausible. On this atmosphere's gascon and ga with the cold-start profile world-wmw declares it returns 249.35, so config/planet.yaml carries model.semi_implicit_reference_temperature_k: 249.4 and run_exoplasim writes T0 as a per-level list. The two agree to 0.65 K, so the core energy sink moves 0.26%, 0.002 W/m2 on 0.79: the sink is NOT settled by this and the change is not a tuning. What changes is that t0 is this world's number and moves when the profile does. Derivation and the reason the two agree are in notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 3; re-derivation from a settled climatology is world-5g5. Commit 64906320.

title: Every damping timescale is nondimensionalised with day_24hr and applied 1/rotspd too long
description:
plasim.f90:1783, 1789, 1799, 1804, 1809, 1814 and 1628 divide by day_24hr (86400.0, plasimmod.f90:961) while the nondimensional time unit is 1/ww = sidereal_day/TWOPI (plasim.f90:1514). The applied timescale is therefore mtspd/ntspd = 32/40 of the namelist value, which is exactly rotspd: 1.0 on Earth and 0.8 here, so the damping acts over 1.25x the intended time.

Applies identically to restim, tfrc and dampsp. Verified against run_2b20e3324bb0's diag: new maxval(tdisst) = 487719.36 = 5.6449 * 86400, and 86400/(TWOPI*487719.36) = 0.0282 where the correct 108000/(TWOPI*487719.36) = 0.0353.

Bounded on the diffusion by world-6on's finding that the filter dominates it; NOT bounded on tfrc.

Note also that plasim.f90:1510-1512's upstream comment calling day_24hr 'purely used for time unit conversions' is false: it is the denominator of this nondimensionalisation, so changing it changes what the model integrates.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Fixed. restim, tfrc, tdissd/z/t/q and dampsp now nondimensionalise with sidereal_day, which is what ww is built from; the ratio was rotspd, so every damping timescale was applied 1.25x too long here and exactly right on Earth. The [days]-to-[sec] conversion in dayseccheck and in the dampsp guard deliberately STAYS on day_24hr: that is the unit config/planet.yaml's timescales_days is derived in and check_consistency.py recomputes it in. The upstream comment calling day_24hr 'purely used for time unit conversions' is replaced by a statement of the two roles. plasim.f90, commit 9c2f5137. Rule 4: every binary needs rebuilding.

title: Hyperdiffusion is written as a scalar, so the derived damping reaches one model level of ten
description:
run_exoplasim.py:1031-1034 and stability_probe.py:177-181 write TDISSD/TDISSZ/TDISST/TDISSQ and NDEL as bare scalars. Fortran namelist assignment of a scalar to an array sets element 1 only, so levels 2-10 keep the compiled module defaults. Verified in run_2b20e3324bb0/MOST_DIAG.00002: NDEL=4, 9*2 and TDISSD=0.4457, 9*0.2000.

At T42 it is worse: the if(NTRU==42) block in plasim.f90:1443-1450 has already filled levels 2-10 in SECONDS, so the array is mixed-unit. run_953ee807d32f echoes TDISST=2.8224, 9*65664.0. dayseccheck (plasim.f90:1649) discriminates on maxval, sees 65664 >> deltsec and converts nothing, so level 1's timescale is read as 2.82 seconds against level 2-10's 65664 -- of order 23,000x the damping on the top model level, with no 'assuming [days]' line in the diag.

ExoPlaSim's own wrapper does this correctly (__init__.py:2804 writes '%d*%f' % (layers, value)); the project's scripts bypass it and edit the namelist key directly.

Fix: write every TDISS* and NDEL as a layer-count-replicated list, and add a check that the echoed array is uniform in units. Then re-examine resolution-tuned-parameters.md's null result, whose T42 experiment did not apply what it recorded.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Fixed on three sides. run_exoplasim.py:declare_hyperdiffusion and stability_probe.py now write TDISSD/Z/T/Q and NDEL as layers*value, which is what ExoPlaSim's own wrapper does. dayseccheck refuses an array whose positive entries straddle the timestep, so a mixed-unit array cannot be integrated silently again -- that is a right answer rather than a comparison, and it is the guard the issue asked for. Commits 9c2f5137 and 64906320. The re-examination of resolution-tuned-parameters.md's T42 null result needs two orbits and a rebuild and is filed as world-ba0.

title: Continuation segments drop filterpower and every hyperdiffusion key
description: continue_exoplasim.py:463 passes physicsfilter but not filterkappa or filterpower, so configure() rewrites NFILTEREXP to its default 8 on every continuation while config/planet.yaml:388 declares filter_power: 16. It also never calls declare_hyperdiffusion, and configure() does not write those keys either, so NDEL, NHDIFF, TDISSD, TDISSZ, TDISST and TDISSQ are absent from the staged plasim_namelist entirely and a continuation integrates on plasim.f90's hard-coded T21/T42 damping rather than the derived values. Verified on disk in exoplasim/runs/run_2b20e3324bb0/plasim_namelist, which records NFILTEREXP = 8 and none of the damping keys. That run reached climatology_complete at 85 orbits. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 1a.
acceptance_criteria: continue_exoplasim.py passes filterkappa and filterpower and calls declare_hyperdiffusion; and expected_namelist_keys at run_exoplasim.py:1462 covers both sets, so verify_staged_namelists fails when they are missing. No output is owed: the affected runs are disposable.
notes:
The gate that should have caught this is expected_namelist_keys, which checks neither set. Fixing the writer without extending that check leaves the same class open.

Nothing is owed on the output side. The canonical climatology lineage is not declared, so by rule 7 every build, run and climatology is disposable whatever has consumed it, and run_2b20e3324bb0's 85 orbits cost nothing. This row is the writer and the gate, and only those. Confirmed 2026-08-24: there are no extant artifacts to preserve.

The reason to fix it now rather than when a lineage is declared is that the defect is silent -- the staged namelist simply lacks the keys, so a segment run after the lineage is declared would inherit the same default damping with nothing to say so.
close_reason: continue_exoplasim.py passes filterkappa and filterpower and calls declare_hyperdiffusion; expected_namelist_keys covers FILTERKAPPA, NFILTEREXP, NHDIFF, NDEL and the four TDISS* arrays, the last five compared as replicated text so a scalar cannot pass. No numeric changed.

title: pyburn selects its FFT extension on nlat against two nlon values, killing the interpreter at T63 and T106
description:
pyburn.py:649 sets nlat = min(header[4], header[5]), the latitude count. Six sites then branch on 'if nlat in [192,320]' to choose the extension: :654, :659, :736, :741, :1080, :1085. But 192 and 320 are the LONGITUDE counts of T63 and T106.

pyfft.f90:791 accepts 8,16,32,48,64,96,128,256,384,512,1024,2048,4096. Neither 192 nor 320 is in it, and pyfft.f90:1193-1199 ends in a bare Fortran stop, which from inside an f2py extension terminates the PYTHON PROCESS with status 0: no exception, no traceback, no output file. The driver sees a successful process that produced nothing.

T63 (nlat 96, nlon 192) and T106 (nlat 160, nlon 320) both select pyfft and die. T127 (nlat 192) selects pyfft991 and works for the wrong reason.

The model binary is unaffected: build_model.py:60 carries NEEDS_FFT991 = {T63, T106} and routes correctly. Only the postprocessor's selector is wrong.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 4.
acceptance_criteria: The selector tests the longitude count, or equivalently nlat in [96,160]. Postprocessing a T63 or T106 output file completes instead of terminating the interpreter.
close_reason: Fixed: pyburn._fftmodule derives the selection from the longitude count and fftmod's radix loop; six branch sites become one. lib/rungs.fft_module states the same rule for the model build and replaces build_model.NEEDS_FFT991. No rung changes module.

title: The restart carries its resolution and nothing reads it back
description:
plasim.f90:904-907 writes nlat, nlon, nlev and nrsp into the restart. No get_restart_integer call in plasim/src asks for any of the four; read_atmos_restart takes nstep and naccuout and stops.

The read is 'read (nreaunit) pa(1:k1,:)' at restartmod.f90:155 with no iostat. An unformatted sequential read consuming fewer values than the record holds is legal and advances. So a donor written at a HIGHER truncation is silently reinterpreted: the target takes the leading k1*k3 values of a longer record, a flat reslicing that runs out of level one into the donor's tail. A LOWER-truncation donor hits end of record and dies with no iostat to name why.

restart_schema.py:776-789 validates all four, but that is the converter. An unconverted restart from another rung passes every gate the run path has.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 2.
acceptance_criteria: read_atmos_restart reads the four stamped integers and refuses a mismatch by name, or the run path refuses an unconverted cross-rung restart before the model is reached.
close_reason: read_atmos_restart reads nlat, nlon, nlev and nrsp before any array read and refuses a mismatch by name, printing both geometries and pointing at convert_restart.py. Placed above the first get_restart_array because a mis-sized unformatted read has already done its damage by the time anything downstream could notice. An UNSTAMPED restart is not a MISMATCHED one: nexcheck is lowered for the four reads and a value that did not arrive stays at its -1 sentinel and passes, which is the accuvers pattern already in the file. The refusal is broadcast with mpbci and the stop is on every task, not only NROOT -- a root-only stop would leave the others waiting in the next collective. plasim.f90, commit 446698e0.

title: A filter-stripped control binary occupies the registry's own build directory
description:
build_model.py composes the build directory tag from resolution, layers, ranks, parmode, profile, frame pointers and the flag delta. The STATE OF THE MODEL SOURCE is not in that tag, so verify_shtns_model.sh's in-place patch of shtnsmod.f90 builds its control arm into the same directory the registry entry claims.

Measured 2026-08-24: build/t21_l10_p16_omp_production/plasim.x is sha 6523babd32fbb827 with ZERO filter sites in its preprocessed shtnsmod.f90-pp.f90, which carries the CONTROL PATCH IN PROGRESS marker, against 11 sites in the live source and sha e0830f776ecb9a4f in plasim/run/most_plasim_t21_l10_p16_omp.x. Still present on a re-check at 09:50.

--no-publish fixed the half that overwrote the shipped binary. The build directory half is untouched and --print-path hands its caller that exact path. The drop+extra hash in tag() exists to keep arms apart; a source patch is an arm the tag cannot see.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 1.
acceptance_criteria: Either the source state enters the build tag, or an arm that patches model source gets its own build root. A verification arm can no longer leave a binary under the registry's tag for any rung.
close_reason: Fixed: build_model.py detects the control-patch markers in plasim/src, builds under build/patched/<tag>_s<hash> instead of the registry's root, and refuses outright when the caller asked to publish. Registry tag unchanged for a clean tree. The existing stale binary is left as an artifact.

title: The dust intensity may be a tabulation bias, and soil texture is the lever that was never examined
description:
Menut et al. (2013), read after world-c8m closed, qualifies its answer in two
ways that the closure did not account for.

THE TABULATION ITSELF BIASES HIGH. Their finding, comparing the in-situ LISA
data set against the ERS satellite retrieval: "The LISA dust fluxes are, on
average, higher than the other model configurations. This is mainly due to the
distribution of z0 values: being TABULATED, values are more discrete and thus
less variable and realistic than those provided by ERS from satellite data."

world-c8m replaced one scalar with two tabulated per-lithology values, which is
LISA's approach and not ERS's. The central land-mean dust AOD moved from 0.0938
to 0.4133 in that change, and 0.41 is Saharan-everywhere. Menut gives a
mechanism for a high bias of exactly that shape, so the jump may be the
tabulation rather than the world.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Within a lithology the roughness is not one value: a playa
has smooth interior and rougher margins, and this project has the geometry to
say so -- the basin solution knows each basin's area, its sink and whether it
overflows. A distribution of z0 within a class, rather than one value per class,
is the ERS-like direction and is buildable from what is already on disk.

AND THE INTENSITY LEVER IS SOIL TEXTURE, NOT ROUGHNESS. Their decomposition: for
a given soil data set, two roughness data sets differ mainly in the SPATIAL
DISTRIBUTION of the flux; for a given roughness data set, two soil texture data
sets differ mainly in its INTENSITY. world-c8m treated roughness as the whole of
the uncertainty in the ANSWER, and on this evidence roughness mostly moves WHERE
the dust is. Nothing in this project has examined what its soil size
distribution does to the dust intensity, and `pedology` owns that field.

A third, smaller: using a drag partition at all lowers fluxes by a factor of 2
to 3 against not using one, which is worth knowing when comparing this project's
numbers to any model that omits it.
acceptance_criteria: Either the within-class roughness distribution is built and the central AOD retaken against it, or the tabulation bias is bounded by some other means and recorded. Separately, a soil-texture sensitivity is run on the dust intensity, so that the roughness bracket is not carrying uncertainty that belongs to the texture.
notes: references/menut2013.pdf, sections 4.2.1 and 5. Raised immediately after closing world-c8m, on reading the paper that issue's own notes had said to read.

title: The dust answer is set by one unconstrained parameter: the aeolian roughness of erodible ground
description:
With the quadrature and the bracket's low end both fixed (world-494), the dust
bracket over the T21 bootstrap still spans the reopening threshold:

    arm       z0 m       emission Tg/yr   land AOD
    low      3.3e-06        47984.90       1.7873
    central  1.0e-04         2479.89       0.0938
    high     1.0e-03            0.13       0.0000

    reopening test: land-mean AOD 0.0000 to 1.7873 against 0.10 -> CROSSES

That is a factor of 370,000 in emission across the bracket, and it is ONE
parameter: `drag_partition.aeolian_z0_m`, the roughness of the erodible patch
itself. Nothing else in the calculation is close to this in leverage. Emission
goes as roughly u* cubed above a threshold and u* goes as feff(z0)/ln(z_ref/z0),
so the two ways z0 enters compound rather than cancel.

WHY IT IS NOT CONSTRAINED HERE. `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` says the value is the
aeolian roughness of the erodible SURFACE and not the grid-cell roughness, and
that dust models in GCMs carry a separate aeolian roughness map for exactly this
reason. This project has no such map: it carries one scalar and a bracket, and
the bracket is honest about spanning a wet-smoothed clay pan to a playa carrying
pebbles, ripples and small dunes.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY NARROW IT. The erodible surface here is 17.49% of land and
is built from named lithologies -- `source_map.erodible_weights` gives
playa_clastic 1.0 and evaporite 0.1 -- so the question is answerable in the
project's own terms: what is the aeolian roughness of a playa, and of an
evaporite pan, and do those two want different values? That is a literature
question with a real answer, and it replaces one scalar with two keyed to
surfaces this world already classifies.

UNTIL THEN nothing may read a dust number as a value, and `ndustrad` should stay
off: switching the radiation onto a field whose magnitude is uncertain by five
orders of magnitude would put that uncertainty into the climate.
acceptance_criteria: drag_partition carries an aeolian roughness per erodible lithology, each sourced, and the reopening test is retaken. It may still cross; if it does, that is a statement about this world rather than about a missing measurement, and the dust radiative term is declared absent with that as the reason.
notes: Diagnosed on the first dust build over the converged T21 bootstrap, run_2b20e3324bb0, on 1463 high-cadence wind samples. aeolian/analysis/dust_baseline.json holds the run. references/INDEX.md has no aeolian roughness rows yet.
close_reason:
Sourced per lithology, and the bracket collapses from a factor of 370,000 to
10.6.

    class            z0 m      bracket m              source
    playa_clastic   3.0e-5   [1.0e-5, 1.0e-4]   prigent2005 T1 and 4.1
    evaporite       1.4e-4   [5.3e-5, 3.9e-4]   mackinnon2004 T1/T2 site 208

MARTICORENA ET AL. (1997) IS WHY THEY DIFFER, and it says so directly: Saharan
lakes fed by streams "loaded with detritic sediments became clayey plains with
SMOOTH SURFACES", while "paleolakes, fed by superficial gypseous water, became
EMBOSSED TOPOGRAPHY, sensitive to weathering", with sebkha surfaces varying
"depending on their salt content and on the experienced periods of drying and
moistening". A clastic playa and an evaporite pan are a smooth surface and a
rough, more variable one.

MACKINNON ET AL. (2004) MEASURED THE ROUGH ONE. Their site 208 is a playa
carrying `saltpush` -- "salt push-ups or ridges created by expanding salt and
clay crusts on playa surfaces", 2 cm high, 5 cm apart -- and it is the strongest
sheltering species there, threshold friction velocity ratio 0.75 against 0.98
and 0.99 for the bushes beside it. Its aerodynamically derived z0 is 0.014 cm
over a 0.0053 to 0.039 cm range. That is the evaporite central value and bracket
unchanged.

PRIGENT ET AL. (2005) CARRIES THE SMOOTH ONE. The Bodele and Chott Djerid
depressions, the Sahara's strongest dust sources, "could have been lakes during
former wet climate periods, allowing accumulation of sediments. For those
regions it can be expected that the surface is relatively smooth, with low
roughness parameters." Their convention for active dust sources is 0.001 cm and
their sand-desert boundary is 0.02 cm, which set the ends.

CELLS COMBINE THEM as an erodible-area-weighted GEOMETRIC mean, because the drag
goes as 1/ln(z/z0) and it is ln(z0) that averages. The arms are now fields, not
scalars, so a cell of pure playa and a cell of pure evaporite sit at different
roughnesses within one arm.

REBUILT:

    arm       emission Tg/yr   land AOD   z0 geo-mean m
    low          25718.22       0.9701      1.007e-5
    central      10838.66       0.4133      3.020e-5
    high          2418.14       0.0922      1.006e-4

    reopening test: 0.0922 to 0.9701 against 0.10 -> STILL CROSSES

AND THE CROSSING IS NOW MARGINAL RATHER THAN TOTAL. It used to span "dust is
absent" to "dust dominates"; it now spans 0.0922 to 0.9701, and the only arm
below the threshold misses it by eight percent. The honest reading is that dust
DOES matter radiatively on this world and the open question is how much, not
whether. That is a statement about Vesper -- it carries far more closed-basin
playa than Earth does, at 17.49% of land erodible, and clastic playa is the
smooth end of the roughness range -- rather than about a missing measurement.

THE CENTRAL ESTIMATE MOVED UP 4.4x, from 0.0938 to 0.4133 AOD, and that is the
sourcing rather than a bug: the dominant erodible class is playa_clastic at
weight 1.0, and 3.0e-5 m is 3.3 times smoother than the generic 1.0e-4 m scalar
it replaced. A land-mean dust AOD of 0.41 is Saharan-everywhere and 10838 Tg/yr
is four to ten times Earth's total emission. Both follow from this world having
more playa, and both are worth a second opinion before anything downstream
treats them as settled -- but they are now what the sourced parameters give
