- The message at :1035-1039 is the one every run directory prints.

DO, reduced to TWO's acceptance clause: report the jtune ordering upstream, or
move the block after the namelist read in the fork, and record which. Nothing
about ONE remains to decide -- the derived table is in config and enforced --
so the "decision on whether to supply resolution-appropriate hyperdiffusion
above T42" is answered: it is supplied, derived, and refuses a rung it has no
entry for. The ladder's stability ceilings still want re-reading, but against
the filter and the CFL limit rather than against the hyperdiffusion, which is
world-6on's territory and not this row's.

title: The physics filter is unbooked, and it biases the identity that found the adiabatic energy source
description:
TWO FINDINGS, and the second is the one that matters.

ONE: NO TERM BOOKS THE PHYSICS FILTER. mkdheat (plasim.f90:4337-4603) recomputes the wind field before and after Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, converts the kinetic-energy difference to a temperature tendency and books it as denergy23 and denergy25; fluxmod books surface friction and vertical-diffusion frictional heating as 21 and 22. Nothing does this for the physics filter. The filter preserves n=0 exactly -- f(0)=exp(0)=1 -- so it cannot change the global MEAN of a linear field, and global-mean enthalpy is safe. Kinetic energy is QUADRATIC in the winds, so damping high-n modes removes KE, and that removal is returned as heat nowhere.

TWO: THE 26-27 IDENTITY IS NOT FILTER-NEUTRAL. exoplasim/notes/water-and-energy-closure.md finds denergy26 - denergy27 = +0.3446 +/- 0.0129 W/m2 where it must be zero, calls the spectral core a net energy source worth 15.6% of the conversion it performs, and concludes the atmosphere is radiating away energy the numerics create. That identity is built at plasim.f90:3275-3325 from GRIDPOINT fields, and both are filtered:

  denergy27 takes winds from dv2uv(zsd,zsz,zugp,zvgp), and dv2uv applies fmu = znn1*m*skspgp and fmv = znn1*skspgp. KE is 0.5*(u^2+v^2), so it carries the filter SQUARED.
  denergy26 takes temperature from sp2fl -> sp2fc, which applies fsp = skspgp. Enthalpy is linear in T, so it carries the filter to the FIRST power.

The note already reasons that the Robert-Asselin time filter enters both terms the same way and so cannot be read out of their difference. The physics filter does NOT enter both the same way. f against f^2 does not cancel, so 26 - 27 cannot vanish under a nontrivial filter even for a dynamical core that conserves exactly. The difference is largest where f is near 0.5, which is n/NTRU = 0.737 by construction.

THE DECISIVE TEST, and it has a right answer: measure denergy26 - denergy27 on a short NENERGY=1, NLOWIO=0 window with NFILTER=0 and with NFILTER=2, identical otherwise. If the source collapses toward zero with the filter off, the +0.3446 is the filter -- either as diagnostic bias or as real unbooked dissipation, which the KE identity -denergy27 = denergy(21+22+23+25) then separates. If it is unchanged, the filter is innocent and the note's attribution to the semi-implicit scheme stands.

WHAT IS AT STAKE. If confirmed, a headline finding in the water-and-energy-closure note is wrong: the spectral core is not creating 0.3446 W/m2, the instrument is reporting it. NENERGY is 0 in the active configuration, so this costs a short diagnostic segment rather than a production run. It also bears on the physics-filter row, since it changes what turning the filter off would COST.

NOT A CANDIDATE FOR THE PLANETARY RESIDUAL: that closed as measurement under CLIM-11.
acceptance_criteria: denergy26-27 measured at NFILTER=0 and NFILTER=2 on one bed, both arms reported with their scatter; the water-and-energy-closure note updated to whichever answer the arms give; if the filter carries it, the KE identity re-read to say how much is diagnostic bias and how much is unbooked dissipation
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-23 by a five-arm grid; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md has it. THE BIAS HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and by the arm that makes the bias identically zero.

denergy26-27, two orbits each, common restart, same binary and surface:
  kappa 8, dt 45     0.3147 +/- 0.0150
  kappa 2, dt 45     0.4020 +/- 0.0528
  kappa 8, dt 22.5   0.1204 +/- 0.0114
  kappa 2, dt 22.5   0.1637 +/- 0.0153
  filter off, dt 22.5  0.5575 +/- 0.0503

With the filter off, f = 1 everywhere, denergy26 and denergy27 carry the same weight by construction, and the f-against-f^2 bias term is exactly nothing. The residual is then the LARGEST of the five -- 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. If bias were the cause, removing it would drive the residual toward zero; it raises it 4.6x.

Both dependences are the time-scheme signature instead. It SCALES WITH THE TIMESTEP: halving dt gives ratios of 0.38 at kappa 8 and 0.41 at kappa 2, between first and second order, which is truncation-error behaviour and not what a spatial weighting artifact does. And it GROWS AS THE FILTER WEAKENS, monotone at fixed dt -- 0.1204, 0.1637, 0.5575 for kappa 8, kappa 2, off -- because less filtering leaves more small-scale structure for the semi-implicit step to mishandle.

So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution stands and its number is not a constant of the model: the spectral core genuinely fails to conserve enthalpy plus kinetic energy, and the size is set by the timestep and by how much spectrum survives the filter. At the configuration this project runs it is 0.31 W/m2.

The kinetic-energy identity closes in all five arms against a ~2.1 W/m2 conversion, so the pairing holds throughout. The short-dt arms were checked per orbit against the dt-45 control for a leapfrog transient off a dt-45 restart and show none: 0.1284/0.1123 against the control's 0.3253/0.3042.

STILL OPEN, and the row stays open only for this: no term books what the filter removes. mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion alone.
close_reason:
Both halves resolved 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the evidence.

THE BIAS HALF IS REFUTED, by the arm built to test it. The claim was that denergy26 carries the filter to the first power and denergy27 carries it squared, so 26-27 could not vanish under a nontrivial filter however well the core conserves. With the filter OFF, f = 1, both terms carry the same weight by construction and the bias term is exactly zero -- and the residual is the LARGEST of the whole grid, 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. Removing the bias raises the residual 4.6x where the hypothesis needs it to fall to zero. Confirmed across nine further cells: the residual grows monotonically as the filter weakens at every timestep.

What the dependences say instead is truncation error. It scales with the timestep, ratios of 0.60 at dt 30 and 0.38-0.41 at dt 22.5 against linear's 0.667 and 0.500, consistent across kappa 8, 4 and 2. So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution to the semi-implicit step stands, and its number is not a constant of the model: 0.31 W/m2 is what this timestep and this filter cost. Eight-orbit arms confirm the short windows to within 2%.

THE UNBOOKED HALF IS BOUNDED, by an identity that runs the wrong way for it. Nothing books the filter's KE removal -- mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, fluxmod the surface and vertical-diffusion terms, neither knows the filter exists -- and the filter preserves n=0 exactly so only the quadratic quantity is exposed. The kinetic-energy steady-state identity is what would find it, and a stronger filter removes more, so the gap must WIDEN with kappa if the filter is the missing term. It NARROWS: -0.013 to -0.000 at kappa 8, rising through +0.007 at kappa 2 to +0.039 with the filter OFF, where the filter's dissipation is identically zero and there is nothing to book.

At the adopted kappa 8 the identity closes to within 0.013 W/m2 against a conversion of about 2.1, six tenths of a percent. The term is real in principle and below what this instrument can see at production settings, so the row closes on the bound rather than on an mkdheat implementation.

REOPEN IF: the identity stops closing at the adopted kappa, or a rung's KE conversion grows enough that six tenths of a percent is worth chasing.

title: Settle the physics filter before the timestep ladder: gp|exp|sp came from the tidally-locked presets
description:
config/planet.yaml declares physics_filter: "gp|exp|sp", which run_exoplasim.py, continue_exoplasim.py and run_stellar_cycle.py pass to ExoPlaSim's configure(). Confirmed in an actual run namelist rather than inferred from config: NFILTER=2, NGPTFILTER=1, NSPVFILTER=1, FILTERKAPPA=8.0, NFILTEREXP=8, MPSTEP=45.0.

WHERE IT CAME FROM, and this is the reason the row exists. The base Model.configure defaults physicsfilter="" -- OFF. Earthlike sets a 45-minute timestep and NO filter. The three tidally-locked classes, TLaquaplanet, TLlandplanet and TLmodel, set physicsfilter="gp|exp|sp" AND a 30-minute timestep. This project's config carries the timestep from one preset and the filter from the other, and Vesper is not tidally locked. It has been in config/planet.yaml since the initial commit 67ff46ba with no decision commit behind it, and exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md records only "We enable the filter but tune nothing".

UPSTREAM'S OWN GUIDANCE is that Earth-like models typically do not require filtering, that tidally-locked models do, and that filtering MAY be beneficial for Earth-like models at very high resolution or with sharp topography. Vesper is Earth-like in composition and unlike Earth in its star; it also has deliberately sharp topography, since preserving carved closed-basin floor below sea level is the entire point of the Orogen fork. So the setting is not obviously wrong -- it is UNDECIDED, and it is currently decided by inheritance.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, computed from legmod.f90:167-235. f(n) = exp(-8 (n/NTRU)^8), applied to skgpsp at gp->sp and skspgp at sp->gp, then folded into the per-mode factors fsp, fgp, fmu and fmv. The fork's own comment is explicit: every SP->GP weight carries skspgp and every GP->SP weight carries skgpsp, NO WEIGHT IS EVER USED UNFILTERED. So it reaches fc2sp, sp2fc, sp2fcdmu, dv2uv, uv2dv, qtend and mktend -- the nonlinear dynamical tendency transforms as well as the physics coupling -- and shtnsmod.f90 imports fsp from legmod so the SHTns path carries the identical filter.

IT IS SCALE-FREE IN n/N, which is what the vague "use at higher resolutions" guidance does not capture. The half-power point is n/N = 0.737 at EVERY rung: n=15.5 at T21, 30.9 at T42, 62.6 at T85, 93.5 at T127, 125.2 at T170. Per application f is 0.63 at n/N=0.7, 0.45 at 0.75, 0.26 at 0.8, 0.03 at 0.9; with both directions on, the round-trip transfer is 0.40, 0.20, 0.068 and 0.001. Every rung loses the same FRACTION of its spectrum, so the filter does not distort the ladder's relative comparison -- but the effective resolution of every rung is well under nominal, and T170's half-power wavenumber of 125 sits essentially at T127's truncation.

WHY IT GATES SPAT-11. The filter damps exactly the smallest scales that set the stability limit, so the largest scientifically acceptable timestep is a function of the filter setting. Measuring the ladder under one filter configuration and running production under another gives a number for a model nobody runs. Upstream pairs gp|exp|sp with 30 minutes and no filter with 45; this project runs the filter with 45.

DECIDE IT PER RUNG, because the reason upstream gives is resolution-dependent even though the filter is not: higher resolution resolves sharper gradients off the same topography, so Gibbs ringing gets worse while the filter cuts the same fraction. The decision procedure is arms with and without the filter at a rung, judged on the ringing signature near steep orography rather than on preference -- spectral overshoot around the carved basin rims, negative specific humidity, oscillatory precipitation downstream of sharp relief.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded per-rung decision with its evidence, in exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md; config/planet.yaml carries the chosen setting per rung rather than one global string; SPAT-11's timestep ladder runs at the chosen setting and says which one
notes:
THE FILTER BUYS TIMESTEP. Measured 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md.

The filter-off arm TRAPS at dt 45 and integrates two clean orbits at dt 22.5. So the earlier reading here -- that the filter is load-bearing full stop -- is too strong. It is load-bearing AT A 45-MINUTE STEP. Upstream pairs gp|exp|sp with 30 minutes; this configuration pairs it with 45 and would need roughly 22.5 without it.

That makes the filter and the timestep one decision rather than two, and it is the finding that reaches SPAT-11: the largest scientifically acceptable step is a FUNCTION of filter strength, so a ladder that fixes one and sweeps the other measures one arbitrary point on a trade.

There is a second axis to the trade, from the same grid. Weakening the filter raises the spectral core's non-conservation monotonically at fixed timestep -- 0.1204, 0.1637, 0.5575 W/m2 for kappa 8, kappa 2, off at dt 22.5 -- so a weaker filter costs spurious energy creation as well as timestep. A stronger filter costs spectrum: f is scale-free in n/NTRU with its half-power point at 0.737 for kappa 8 and 0.876 for kappa 2.

So the row's question is now three-cornered and per rung: kappa, timestep, and how much of the top of the spectrum each rung can afford to lose. The trap gives a hard floor to measure against at each rung -- the weakest filter that still runs at a given step.
close_reason:
Settled 2026-08-23. The provenance finding stood and its conclusion did not: gp|exp|sp did come from the tidally-locked presets while the 45-minute step came from Earthlike, and the setting is load-bearing rather than inherited cargo. exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md has the arms, exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md the argument.

THE FILTER BUYS TIMESTEP, so a filter strength and a timestep are one decision. Without the filter the model traps in the shortwave on the first radiation call at 45 minutes and runs at 22.5, and the requirement STRENGTHENS up the ladder: unfiltered, T42 runs at dt 30 and T170 needs dt 10. That is upstream's stated reason for filtering, measured rather than quoted -- a finer grid resolves sharper gradients off the same orography while a scale-free filter keeps cutting the same fraction.

KAPPA 8 AT EVERY RUNG, and it is not a compromise because it wins on both axes. Against kappa 4, 2, 1 and off it takes the longest stable step at every rung tested AND gives the smallest adiabatic non-conservation -- 0.3147 W/m2 at dt 45 against 0.3460, 0.4020, 0.6574 and a trap. What it costs is spectrum, which is the only reason not to go stronger: f is scale-free in n/NTRU with its half-power point at 0.737, so a stronger filter takes more of every rung's spectrum for a benefit nothing has measured. Nothing above kappa 8 was tested.

THE STEP IS THE PER-RUNG PART, and config/planet.yaml now carries it as model.resolution_timestep_minutes with check_consistency.py refusing a timestep_minutes that disagrees -- verified by making it disagree. Adopted: T21 45, T42 45, T85 45, T127 30, T170 22.5. Measured ceilings: T21 90+, T42 60, T85 45 untested above, T127 30 with dt 45 refusing outright, T170 22.5 with dt 30 blowing up after 3.8 minutes.

THE ADOPTED STEP IS BELOW THE CEILING AT T42 DELIBERATELY. A step that does not blow up is a stability floor and not a licence. T42 at 60 would be a third off every T42 run and is not adopted, because the roadmap's timestep experiment -- cold-start stability with traps armed, warm-start closure, climatological differences after settling, wall time per orbit -- has not been run. That is SPAT-11's, and this table is what it starts from rather than what it concludes.

CARRIED FORWARD to SPAT-11, which is the acceptance criterion this row cannot discharge itself: the ladder must run at the adopted setting and say which one. Two cells carry more risk and are labelled: T85 at 45 and T127 at 30 are at their tested ceiling on a single orbit, and T170 at 22.5 sits one step below a cell that fails LATE, which a short check cannot see.

title: Verify the prescribed ocean heat-transport channel end to end with a field whose answer
description:
Verify the prescribed ocean heat-transport channel end to end with a field whose answer is known, BEFORE anything computes a real one. `nfluko = 1` makes `oceanmod.f90` read surface code 903 as a monthly W/m2 field and `addfc` apply it under the header comment "prescribed advection"; `close_ocean_energy.py` already reads the same code out of the `ocean_output` stream and records it as identically zero today. Use a zero-global-integral ocean dipole; bind grid, calendar, interval, units, source hash and land/sea/ice mask; require the reported accumulation to reproduce the written field and its area-weighted global integral to remain zero

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` finding 2 and section 8a
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and instrumentation rather than physics, so it is a diagnostic segment and not an orbit. Cheapest row here and it is what makes OCN-3 legible: without it, an offline model's first field would arrive with no way to separate a wrong field from a wrong channel. It also converts the error budget's no-q-flux item from STRUCTURAL with "no cheap version exists" into something with a route, which `nhdiff` bounded but did not supply [step: bootstrap_run]. WHY THIS IS FIRST, made explicit 2026-08-22: the channel this row verifies is what makes OCN-5's loop possible at all. The atmosphere-ocean poleward transport partition cannot be got right in one pass, because a slab-forced climatology has the atmosphere carrying the entire load with no coefficient to reduce -- unlike cGENIE, which tunes `betaz`, `betam` and `diffamp` to make room for its ocean. The correction has to return to the NEXT atmospheric run, and code 903 under `nfluko = 1` is the only path for it. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28c CRITICAL PATH, 2026-08-24. Section 59 decides the coupling architecture as offline full-flux, which has exactly one structural weakness: the atmosphere-ocean transport partition is iterated rather than solved, because a slab-forced climatology hands the ocean a flux field computed on the assumption that the ocean does nothing. Surface code 903 under nfluko = 1 is the only channel that returns the correction to the next atmospheric run. So this row is no longer merely the cheapest ocean row -- it is the one the adopted architecture depends on, and raised to P1 to say so. Nothing else in the ocean set should be started ahead of it. SCOPE UNCHANGED BY THE SEA-ICE DECISION, 2026-08-24, recorded so it is not widened by mistake. Section 7b adds an ocean surface velocity to the return set, but that field has no channel in ExoPlaSim to verify: icemod has no advection at all, so the consumer does not exist until world-pt8 writes it. This row remains the heat channel alone, surface code 903 under oceanmod's nfluko = 1. Note that icemod carries its OWN nfluko in icemod_nl, a separate variable with a different meaning -- a flux correction toward a prescribed ice climatology -- so setting the ocean's does not activate the ice one, and neither is exposed by ExoPlaSim's Python API. The route is a namelist patch or a fork change either way.

title: T42 at dt 45 blows up in the 47th orbit from a state with no trend
description:
run_900548ae632e, T42, kappa 8, MPSTEP 45.0, -O2, cold start, 85 orbits asked for. It integrated 46 orbits of ordinary climate and took a SIGFPE inside the 47th, at vsqrtsd on 273./dt(jhor,2) in swr. Read out of the register at the trap, dt is -12.81 K: a gridpoint at a negative absolute temperature, at the second level from the top. dt is dt(NHOR,NLEP) in plasimmod and is temperature rather than a tendency, and the instruction is reached down the scalar losun branch past a cmpb/je that skips night lanes, so it is a daylight cell rather than a masked-lane artifact.

Nothing was building towards it. Level 2's coldest cell holds about 190 K with no trend across the whole run, and none of the four restarts before the failure carries a non-positive temperature anywhere. One cell went from roughly 190 K to below zero inside one orbit.

The linear stability boundary does not explain it. exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md fits the stable step as roughly 1/N and measures T127 at dt 30, which puts T42 near 90 minutes -- twice the step that failed here. So this is not the CFL boundary those probes found.

The practical consequence is already taken: the ladder runs T42 at dt 22.5. What is open is the mechanism. Candidates worth separating are a genuine nonlinear instability, which is not obliged to be monotone in the step; a single physics parameterisation producing an unbounded tendency at one cell, which the level-2 location and the suddenness both fit; and something specific to the second level from the top, where the note's earlier T127 blow-up also lived.

The reproducer is cheap and exists: MOST_REST.00046 of run_900548ae632e_crashed reaches the trap in one orbit, about 90 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: The mechanism named and demonstrated on the reproducer -- which term drives one cell's temperature below zero in a single orbit -- and either a fix or a stated stable-step rule for T42 that a 46-orbit run does not falsify.
notes: Found while re-running the resolution ladder's arm A after world-1nz. Distinct from world-bhs, which was optimisation-dependent: the world-bhs probe orbit completes at -O0, -O1, -O2 and -mno-avx512f and produces 69 non-finite restart records only at -O3. This one traps at -O2 on a genuinely negative temperature.

title: verify_latitude_pairing.py is a pipeline gate that tests a function deleted from the model
description:
exoplasim/scripts/verify_latitude_pairing.py lifts 'ilatperm' verbatim out of vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/plasimmod.f90 and compiles it inside a parameter module to check the paired latitude decomposition's index map. plasimmod.f90 no longer contains ilatperm.

Verified 2026-08-24 by running the script's own extraction regex against the current source: no match, so extract() reaches 'raise SystemExit("ilatperm not found in " + SRC)' and the gate exits non-zero having checked nothing.

The paired latitude decomposition was deleted in 2508bedb, 'Delete the paired latitude decomposition, 515 lines', because SHTns replaced legmod and cannot use the permuted layout, so there was nothing left to buy and two grid layouts to carry. That commit removed ilatperm, the LPAIRLAT parameter, seven paired branches in legmod, four in mpimod, three blocks each in utilities and utilities_omp, the un-permute in plasim.f90 and shtnsmod's refusal. It predates the wave-2 fan-out.

The gate is still declared: config/pipeline.yaml:677 lists it, exoplasim/README.md:321 has its row, and scripts/smoke_test.py:909 carries a named SPAT-2 exemption for it.

This is exactly the class world-en0 closed by DELETING verify_fold_indexing.sh and verify_fold_exactness.sh, on the reasoning that repointing them would have made them pass vacuously, which is worse than not running. The same applies here and more simply: there is no function to repoint at.

Do: ask whether the thing should exist before fixing it. The decomposition is gone, so the property the gate checks is not a property of anything in the tree. Delete verify_latitude_pairing.py with its pipeline.yaml row, its README row and its smoke_test RUNG_TABLE_EXEMPT entry, the way world-en0 did.

Check verify_symmetric_transform.py in the same pass but do NOT assume it goes with it: it lifts sp2fc and sp2fcdmu out of legmod.f90, both of which still exist, and checks them against an associated Legendre table from scipy, which is a test with a right answer independent of the decomposition. What it may no longer exercise is the MIRROR path, since 2508bedb removed the paired branches from legmod, and its PARAMOD still injects 'logical, parameter :: LPAIRLAT = .true.'. Establish whether that injection now does nothing before touching the file.

Source: exoplasim/notes/paired-latitude-decomposition.md, which described the decomposition as live and now records that it was retired.

title: config/planet.yaml's atmosphere preamble still says radmod has no CH4 and no N2O term
description:
config/planet.yaml lines 158-164, the paragraph immediately above the 'atmosphere:' key, reads:

  What this block CAN say is bounded by what the model reads. PlaSim's longwave
  is Sasamori (1968) over water vapour, CO2 and ozone, and the shortwave adds
  Rayleigh and the same three; radmod.f90 has no CH4 and no N2O term, so there
  is nothing here to set them to. Their absence is a property of the radiation
  scheme rather than a composition choice ... Adding either means adding a band,
  not a key.

Every clause of that is now false, and the block DIRECTLY BELOW IT contradicts it:

- radmod.f90:190-191 declares 'ch4' and 'n2o' as radmod_nl keys, broadcast at :1112-1113, in the namelist at :919.
- The longwave band that carries them is resident in radmod.f90 (CLIM-42), with zch4a0 at :3064 and the rest of the band constants beside it.
- config/planet.yaml:199-200 sets pCH4_bar: 0.0000016 and pN2O_bar: 0.0000003, MEASURED 2026-08-20 under CLIM-43 from Rugheimer et al. (2013), and run_exoplasim.py:171-172 converts both to the ppmv radmod_nl wants.
- The CH4/N2O block's own text prices the band: 'At these abundances against zero it lowers global mean outgoing longwave by 0.799 W/m2.'

So a reader grepping config/planet.yaml for CH4 lands on the reason it cannot be set, four lines above where it is set. CLAUDE.md: 'Rewrite superseded content; do not mark it.'

Do: rewrite that paragraph to say what the longwave now carries -- water vapour, CO2, ozone and the CLIM-42 trace-gas band -- and what it still does not, which is the honest bound the paragraph was written to state. Keep the one-signed direction argument for whatever absorbers remain absent. The pCO2 paragraph above it is unaffected and its 'currently unbacked' outgassing check is a separate matter.

Filed by the notes/audits sweep, from notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md finding 5, whose own text this supersedes in the same direction.

title: An absent surface field is not an error, and the compiled land mask default is all land
description:
surfmod.f90's get_surf_array handles an ABSENT surface file by writing '* Init <name> [code = NNNN] internally *' to the diagnostic unit, leaving kread at 0, and returning. mpsurfgp then leaves the array untouched, so the module default stands. There is no error path and no way to tell that line from the thirteen other codes a healthy run initialises internally.

The default that matters is plasimmod.f90's dls = 1., the land/sea mask, which is ALL LAND. With doro at 0.0 the model integrates a flat, entirely continental planet and produces a full set of numbers for it.

world-fuh closed the neighbouring half -- check_surf_header now refuses a file whose header words 5 and 6 disagree with NLON and NLAT, by name -- and its close reason records that the dls default was deliberately left: 'The dls=1. all-land default is in plasimmod.f90, batch A's file, and is untouched.' So the WRONG-GRID case refuses and the ABSENT case does not.

Why it matters here rather than upstream: upstream ships Earth boundary fields, so absent means the user removed them. This project supplies every field itself and deletes the shipped ones on purpose (configure()'s rm *.sra), so absent is the state a staging bug produces, and finding 9 of the audit records that T85, T127 and T170 have executables and no surface family at all.

Nothing integrates that way today: the project-side surface_field_report raises on a missing intended code and declare_hyperdiffusion raises on a rung with no table entry. This is about the model refusing for itself rather than relying on a driver that a direct invocation bypasses.

Do: decide which surface codes are REQUIRED for a run to be meaningful -- the land/sea mask 172 and the orography 129 at least -- and make surfini abort naming the code when one of those is absent, rather than falling back to a compiled default. Codes that are genuinely optional keep the internal-init line. Rule 4 applies: this is model source, and every binary needs rebuilding.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 3.

title: archive_builds.py's EXPECTED_GRIDS is a literal list that no build on disk satisfies
description:
scripts/archive_builds.py:56-57 declares

    EXPECTED_GRIDS = ["exoplasim-T21", "exoplasim-T42", "exoplasim-T63",
                      "exoplasim-T85", "grid-512x256"]

with the comment 'A build is these five exports. Fewer means it is still being generated.' It is used at :150 as a completeness gate: a build directory missing any of the five is printed as 'incomplete' and SKIPPED, so its payload is never archived.

Measured 2026-08-24 against the tree:
- source/precarve-craton-10m/ (the ACTIVE build) holds exoplasim-T21, T42, T85, T127, T170. It has neither exoplasim-T63 nor grid-512x256, so it can never be archived, whatever else is true of it.
- source/precarve-craton/ holds exoplasim-T21, T42, T63, T85, T127 and grid-512x256, so it passes.

The list is also the last ladder restatement world-ltc's SPAT-2 lint does not reach: it is rung names inside path strings with no dimensions beside them, so neither check_no_rung_literal_in_a_path nor check_no_rung_table_outside_rungs fires. world-ltc's own description names archive_builds.py:56-57 as one of the remaining copies and its close reason does not say what happened to it.

Do: decide what a COMPLETE build is, and derive the check rather than list it. The grids a build actually carries are a property of the export recipe in source/README.md, not of this script; if the set is meant to be the ladder it should come from lib/rungs.py, and if it is meant to be the grids that build was generated at it should come from the build's own manifest. Either way the gate must pass for a build that is finished, or it silently disables archiving.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 10.

title: run_2b20e3324bb0 integrated the physics filter at NFILTEREXP 8, not the declared 16
description:
Found by the retrospective gate added under world-e6m (scripts/check_consistency.py, 'runs vs the namelists they staged').

run_2b20e3324bb0/plasim_namelist carries NFILTEREXP = 8 while the run's own manifest source_config declares model.filter_power: 16. All 85 orbits of the T21 run the project's numbers rest on were integrated at gamma 8. The same is true of run_8102b89a08ac, which is already declared invalid by its directory name.

Every other run on disk carries NFILTEREXP = 16, so this is the same staging generation as world-1nz: the two runs that lack NDEL, NHDIFF and TDISS* entirely are exactly the two at gamma 8.

WHY IT IS NOT A DETAIL. check_consistency.py's 'filter confinement' case exists because the filter, not the hyperdiffusion, is this model's small-scale damping, and it derives gamma by requiring the crossover against the cascade to sit at or above 0.6 of the truncation. At gamma 8 the crossover is 0.41 -- most of the rung paid for and thrown away. filter_power is 16 for that reason (world-6on). So run_2b20e3324bb0 resolved less than its rung claims, and any spectral or timestep evidence read off it was taken at a gamma the config has since rejected.

world-hxm asks for T21 to be commissioned afresh on two grounds, its damping and its surface. This is a third and it is not named there. world-ba0 records the same gamma move for the T42 arms.

Do: name the filter exponent alongside the damping in world-hxm's re-commissioning, and re-check anything measured on run_2b20e3324bb0 that depends on the resolved spectrum.

title: verify_shtns_model.sh has not run against the energy diagnostics' new SHTns arm
description:
world-3ya routed eleven per-timestep legmod transforms in spectrala and spectrald through sh_sp2gp and sh_dv2uv, moving their destinations to full-globe arrays in pumamod with threadprivate band pointers. The change was written and reviewed statically. It was NOT compiled and NOT run: the batch that made it was forbidden to build, because .venv installs ExoPlaSim editable from the MAIN checkout and every worktree shares exoplasim/runs/ and source/ through symlinks.

What has to happen before any run consumes a binary carrying this:

1. python exoplasim/scripts/rebuild_binaries.py, then --verify. Rule 4: one executable per (resolution, layers, ranks, parmode), and a rebuild only refreshes the configuration it was asked for.
2. exoplasim/scripts/verify_shtns_model.sh. It builds one --parmode omp binary and runs NSHTNS=1 against NSHTNS=0 on it, which is exactly the axis these eleven sites now branch on. Before world-3ya the two arms computed the diagnostics the same way and the comparison could not see them; now it can.
3. The comparison must be read on denergy 24, 26 and 27 in particular, not only on the prognostic fields. Those three drive the energy fixer, which writes stt, so a difference there is a difference in what the model integrates rather than in what it reports.

WHAT WOULD MEAN WRONG. A deadlock or a hang says a barrier was placed where the team does not all arrive. A denergy26 - denergy27 that moves by more than the last bits between the two arms says a transform lands somewhere the arithmetic below it does not expect. 'ENERGY FIXER DIVERGED' says the diagnostics are grossly wrong, which is the loud failure the fixer's 100 W/m2 bound exists to produce.

Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 4.
notes:
world-olt landed in the same batch and needs the same rebuild for a different
reason: radmod.f90's four CO2 shortwave closed-form coefficients moved when the
correlated-k join was closed (zca1 3.1020E-4, zcb1 19.857, zca2 3.8291E-3,
zcb2 3.9587E-3), which changes what swr computes by +0.5% on the CO2 shortwave
absorptance, about +0.008 W/m2 of Earth-mean insolation. That is not visible in
the NSHTNS=1 against NSHTNS=0 comparison -- both arms carry it -- so it is a
rebuild requirement and not a gate.

title: No retrospective gate reads a run directory for the hyperdiffusion it declared
description:
world-hxm's notes say the check that catches a run integrating compiled
hyperdiffusion is a "runs vs the hyperdiffusion they declared" case in
scripts/check_consistency.py, added with the world-1nz fix. There is no such
case. The only gate of that shape over exoplasim/runs/ is "runs vs the energy
fixer they claim", which reads each run_manifest.json's `energy_fixer` and
compares it against NENERGYFIX in the run's own plasim_namelist.

What world-8bs and world-720 built instead is run_exoplasim.py's
expected_namelist_keys plus verify_staged_namelists: it covers FILTERKAPPA,
NFILTEREXP, NHDIFF, NDEL and the four TDISS*, compares the five array-valued
ones as replicated `<layers>*<value>` TEXT so a scalar cannot pass, and raises
rather than warns. Both run_exoplasim.py and continue_exoplasim.py call it. That
is the right guard and it holds going forward.

What it does not do is read a run that already exists. run_2b20e3324bb0 is on
disk with 85 orbits, climatology_complete, a `hyperdiffusion` block in its
manifest and no NDEL, NHDIFF or TDISS* in its plasim_namelist at all, and
nothing in the tree says so. A run prepared before the guard, or copied in, or
edited, is invisible.

The energy-fixer gate is the pattern and it is fifteen lines: for each
run_*/run_manifest.json with a `hyperdiffusion` block, read the sibling
plasim_namelist and compare NDEL, NHDIFF and the four TDISS* against what the
manifest recorded, as text for the replicated ones. A manifest that claims
damping its namelist does not carry is a run whose climatology is not what it
says it is.

Do: add the case to scripts/check_consistency.py beside "runs vs the energy
fixer they claim". Expect it to FAIL on the runs currently on disk; that is the
finding, not a reason to weaken it.

Source: world-hxm, re-verified 2026-08-24.
notes:
Done as three cases in scripts/check_consistency.py:audit_runs, beside 'runs vs the energy fixer they claim'.

1. 'runs vs the namelists they staged' -- expected_namelist_keys REUSED, driven from each manifest's own source_config, read back off the FILES (CONS-9). A wrong value fails. An absent key fails when the run's namelist_checks block claims it was staged, and WARNS when it does not, because the run predates the key and the model used its compiled value with nothing recording which.
2. 'runs vs the hyperdiffusion they declare' -- world-e6m as written: the manifest's hyperdiffusion block against plasim_namelist, both inside the run, NDEL and the four TDISS* as replicated <layers>*<value> text.
3. 'runs vs the surface fields they staged' -- per-code surface_field_sha256 against the .sra that code resolves to now.

Severity is the prepare-time guard's own: verify_staged_namelists raises on a wrong staged value, and run_exoplasim.py refuses to seed from a donor whose surface hashes moved.

WHAT IT FINDS ON DISK. Two runs carry a hyperdiffusion block and none of NHDIFF, NDEL, TDISSD, TDISSZ, TDISST, TDISSQ: run_2b20e3324bb0 and run_8102b89a08ac. Ten more carry them as bare scalars where the layer count is 10, so levels 2..10 kept readnl's compiled values (world-720). run_2b20e3324bb0 also carries NFILTEREXP = 8 against its own config's 16 (world-dkl), and is the only run whose staged surface has moved: codes 174, 175, 176 and 212 have been regenerated since it ran, and 129 and 172 have not.

--self-test gained eleven cases over a fixture run built to agree with itself, green first and one break per case. Four mutants of audit_runs -- array compared numerically, surface content ignored, a claimed absent key demoted to a warning, hyperdiffusion absence ignored -- were each caught by exactly the case that names them.

No run directory was written, moved or deleted.
close_reason: audit_runs added to scripts/check_consistency.py: staged namelists vs the config and manifest each run carries, staged namelists vs the declared hyperdiffusion block, and per-code surface_field_sha256 vs the .sra on disk. All three go red on real runs, which is the finding; --self-test proves each can pass on a run that agrees with itself.

title: reproducibility_matrix.py launches with mpiexec and there is no MPI build
description:
exoplasim/scripts/reproducibility_matrix.py:339 runs the model as mpiexec -np <ranks> ./most_plasim_t42_l10_p<ranks>.x, and :303 and :332 check that bed against binary_manifest.json by that name. world-38b removed the MPI build, so after the next rebuild the name it asks for will be the THREADED binary and mpiexec will launch <ranks> copies of a threaded executable that each believes it owns every latitude.

The matrix's subject is what a run's answer depends on across rank counts and output cadences. Under one runtime the rank axis is a thread axis, which is a different experiment: the threads share one address space and one spectral state. Decide whether the matrix is re-derived over thread counts, whether RANKS becomes a thread ladder run without mpiexec, or whether the artifact it produced stands as a record of a runtime that no longer exists and the script goes.

Do NOT retarget it by deleting mpiexec: it would then run <ranks> unrelated single processes in one directory over the same restart files.
acceptance_criteria: The script either measures a runtime this project has or is deleted with a reason. No arm launches the threaded binary under mpiexec.

title: 66 domain-sensitive intrinsics sit inside masked where-blocks in the physics
description:
Fortran evaluates BOTH sides of a where-block and masks only the assignment. The model's physics modules rely on that being harmless, and it is not: 66 calls to sqrt, log, log10, exp and their ALOG spellings sit inside where-blocks whose masked-out lanes hold arguments the function is undefined on. radmod has 50 of them, rainmod 3, and the rest are spread over the alternative convection schemes, seamod and oceanmod. The clearest case is SQRT(zmu0), the cosine of the solar zenith angle, inside a where(losun) that selects daylight -- zmu0 is negative at night by construction.

Scalar code never reaches those lanes. A vectorising compiler does, and with -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow in the build profile a discarded lane becomes SIGFPE. That is world-bhs: a T42 run died eight orbits in, and the fault moved to a new site each time one was clamped -- radmod's longwave, then kuo's Tetens exponent, then radmod's shortwave.

The profile is now -O2 rather than -O3, which removes the transforms that were firing at no measured cost. That is NOT a fix for this issue: -O2 vectorises too, so the class is quieter, not gone, and a different state or a different rung can wake it again.

The fix is to make each site's argument safe for any lane. Where the enclosing computation already caps the result the guard is provably free -- rainmod's eighteen Tetens exponents are all followed by AMIN1(zqs,rdbrv) on the next line, so clamping the exponent to +-80 cannot change a value that survives. Each of the 66 needs that argument made, and the ones where it cannot be made are the ones worth knowing about.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 66 sites is either guarded with a clamp that is argued to be a no-op on the values the model keeps, or recorded as unable to be, and the world-bhs probe completes at -O3 with -ffpe-trap on.
notes: Enumerated by walking where/endwhere nesting over plasim/src/*.f90 and matching sqrt|log|log10|alog|alog10|exp|asin|acos inside the blocks. Two are already done: radmod's shortwave column integrals were being initialised only inside where(losun) and are now unconditional, and rainmod's Tetens exponents are clamped.

title: Guard rainmod's 34 Tetens sites against the pole at ra4
description:
rainmod.f90 divides by (T - ra4) at 34 sites -- in the exp() argument of Tetens' saturation formula, in zdqsdt, and in the zcor Newton denominators. ra4 is 35.86 K and the formula is singular there. In kuo() the divisor is ztnew, a Newton-iterated PARCEL temperature with no bound of its own, so a lane whose iteration is not converging can pass through the pole; just below it the exp() argument reaches about +4800 and overflows, which the production profile's -ffpe-trap=overflow turns into SIGFPE.

Today the build works around this: plasim/CMakeLists.txt compiles rainmod.f90 with -fno-tree-vectorize, so the enclosing scalar 'if' actually skips the non-convecting lanes rather than computing and discarding them. That costs 2.4% of wall clock at T42, measured, and it does NOT make the scalar path safe -- it only removes the compiler's licence to evaluate lanes the source never meant to evaluate. A column that genuinely drives ztnew to the pole still traps.

The fix is to guard the divisor, not the temperature: replace each (X - ra4) DIVISOR with max(X - ra4, 1.0), which binds only below 36.86 K and sends the exp() argument to about -4700, underflowing to zero. Leave (TMELT - ra4) alone: it is a constant numerator equal to 237.3.

Verify by removing the CMakeLists block and running the world-bhs probe under -ffpe-trap. Then re-measure: the flag should be worth its 2.4% back.
acceptance_criteria: rainmod compiles vectorised, the world-bhs probe completes with a NaN-free restart under -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow, and the set_source_files_properties block is gone from plasim/CMakeLists.txt.
notes: Found while fixing world-bhs. radmod's sibling defect was fixed in source (clamps on SQRT/LOG arguments plus unconditional initialisation of the shortwave column accumulators, which where(losun) had left undefined on night lanes); rainmod was left to the build flag because it holds almost none of the model's vectorisation value -- 2.4% against radmod's share of 43%.

title: Thirteen legmod transforms still run per timestep inside live nenergy blocks
description:
world-dr8 routed mkdheat's two sp2fl calls through sh_sp2gp and found thirteen more of the same shape that it could not move. In plasim.f90's spectrala and spectrald, inside guards that are live at NENERGY = 1: six sp2fl and two dv2uv and one sp2fl (nenergy > 1) in spectrala, and one plus three plus two sp2fl in spectrald. Every one is outside any nshtns branch, so an NSHTNS=1 build does the Legendre transform twice per timestep -- once through the wrappers for the dynamics and once through legmod for the diagnostics.

They cannot be swapped in place, which is why mkdheat went first. sh_sp2gp uses an omp do and needs a shared full-globe destination; these write into arrays the routine ALLOCATES per thread (ztt, zttgp, zugp, zvgp, ztgp, zqgp, zpgp and the rest). mkdheat's could move because hddt_g and its per-thread pointer already existed from CLIM-57.

Do: give each of those scratch arrays the shared _g twin and per-thread pointer that exoplasim/notes/shared-spectral-state.md describes, then branch each site on nshtns the way mkdheat now does. Evidence and the per-site table: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 4.
assignee: Every legmod transform reachable at NENERGY = 1 goes through the SHTns wrappers under NSHTNS = 1, or is measured and declared as a deliberate legmod caller. verify_shtns_model.sh still passes.
close_reason:
Eleven live sites converted, two blocks left on legmod deliberately, in commit 69992036. spectrala: six sp2fl and two dv2uv; spectrald: three sp2fl. Each branches on nshtns with sh_sp2gp / sh_dv2uv and its barriers, and keeps the sp2fl + fc2gp arm otherwise. zttgp, ztgp, zqgp, zqmgp, zugp, zvgp, zpgp and zpmgp are full-globe arrays in pumamod with threadprivate band pointers, adding 6*NUGP*NLEV + 2*NUGP words of shared storage -- 496 KB at T21, 1.94 MB at T42, 7.75 MB at T85 -- against a team total that is unchanged.

Three corrections to the finding. (1) Eleven live, not thirteen: spectrald's three sp2fl are guarded by ndheat > 1, which defaults to 1 with nothing in this project raising it, and its block writes only to Fortran unit 9. (2) The one sp2fl under nenergy > 1 is six transforms a step inside a jterm loop, and nenergy > 1 is the world-0ov control, reached only from energy_diagnostics: 2. Both stay on legmod. (3) The obvious saving is NOT available and is a trap: assoc_spectral aliases sdp, spp, sqp and szp onto sd, sp, sq and sz, so spectrala's step 4 has already advanced the shared state by the time the diagnostics run. Those transforms are the state at t+dt, paired against apm, aqm and atm at t-dt, which is what makes denergy 26 and 27 a centred difference. gridpointa's dp, dq, gu and gv are the state at t and are a different quantity.

Nothing here is removable: denergy 24, 26 and 27 drive the energy fixer, which writes stt, and config/planet.yaml sets energy_fixer: true.

The acceptance criterion's second half is NOT met by this batch and is now world-klr: verify_shtns_model.sh was not run, because this batch was forbidden to compile. Rebuild and run it before any run consumes a binary carrying this.

Evidence rewritten into notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 4 (commit 92979bbe).

title: verify_staged_namelists reads one float per key, so every list-valued namelist key is unchecked
description:
exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py's verify_staged_namelists does float(namelist_value(path, key)) for every entry expected_namelist_keys returns. A list-valued key raises ValueError and is reported as 'is not a number', so no list-valued key can be placed under the gate at all.

Two are affected today and both are written unconditionally by configure_otherargs:
- ALBFOREST@landmod_namelist, the per-band canopy albedo (world-nfh). Not in expected_namelist_keys, and this is why.
- ACL2@radmod_namelist, the cloud absorption triplet. Also absent.

This matters for the same reason CONS-9 exists: the namelist in the run directory is what the model integrates, and class 22 is a key that was staged on prepare and dropped by every continuation with no guard noticing for a whole run. ALBFOREST is exactly that shape -- a fork-added key that reverts to landmod's compiled Earth-Sun broadband endmember in both bands if a continuation drops it.

Do: let expected_namelist_keys carry a sequence value and have verify_staged_namelists compare element-wise with the same 1e-9 tolerance, reporting which element differs. Then add ALBFOREST and ACL2. Keep the raise-rather-than-warn behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: ALBFOREST and ACL2 are in expected_namelist_keys and a deliberately corrupted element in a staged namelist makes verify_staged_namelists raise, naming the element.
close_reason: expected_namelist_keys now carries a sequence and verify_staged_namelists compares element-wise at 1e-9, naming the element; length is compared first, which subsumes the replicated-text branch, and the five hyperdiffusion keys moved onto the one path. ALBFOREST and ACL2 are under the gate, along with TSWR3 and oceanmod's NHDIFF and HDIFFK, which were unconditionally staged and equally unchecked. Corrupting element 2 of ALBFOREST and element 3 of ACL2 in a scratch copy staged by the real staging code raises naming that element; NDEL as a scalar raises on its length. Commit 858d5c0a.

title: clim-65 must declare its ocean diffusivity arms in true units, and clim-16's labels are 1.44x wrong
description:
Consequence of world-mll, recorded so the next reader of the horizontal-diffusion A/B does not take the old numbers at face value.

hdiffo used to divide the requested hdiffk by Earth's radius squared on an angular grid, so the realised diffusivity was (a_earth/a)**2 times the coefficient an arm declared. It now runs on this planet's radius and hdiffk means what it says.

Two consequences. clim-16 was closed on a MEASURED 300/1000/3000 m2/s bracket and those arms did reach this code, so what they actually ran was 432/1440/4320: the diffusivity labels on that result are wrong, though its conservation claim does not depend on the coefficient's value and is untouched. And clim-65's arms have to be declared in true units, which is now what config/planet.yaml's horizontal_diffusivity_m2_s means.

Do: state the corrected labels wherever clim-16's bracket is cited, and set clim-65's arms against the corrected meaning.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT: STILL
TRUE. world-mll landed the code fix and nothing corrected the labels.

The fix, cites re-located: oceanmod.f90's parameter(PLARAD=6.371E6) is gone.
hdiffo does `use pumamod, only: plarad` at oceanmod.f90:1376 and applies
`zfac=hdiffk(jlev)/plarad/plarad` at :1394; oceanini refuses nhdiff > 0 with no
radius and logs the radius it will use at :291-296; the module-level use is at
:170. So horizontal_diffusivity_m2_s means what it says from here on.

The consequence is untouched: every arm that ran under the old code applied
(a_earth/a)**2 = 1.4396 times its nominal coefficient, so the CLIM-16 bracket
labelled 300/1000/3000 was 432/1440/4320.

DONE IN THIS PASS. The three audits that stated the defect as live now record
the fix and point here for the part it does not repair:
- notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 3
- notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 10
- notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 12

STILL TO DO, and this is what keeps the row open. Every remaining site that
quotes the bracket at its nominal labels:
- exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md, the "Measured: the CLIM-16
  hdiffk bracket, 2026-08-20" section from line 88, the realisation table at
  :182 and the summary row at :427 (`nhdiff = 1`, `hdiffk = 1000`). The
  predicted rms heating table at :44 understates the model by the same 1.44 and
  model-earth-centrism.md finding 3 carries the corrected figures,
  0.75/2.51/7.53 becoming 1.08/3.61/10.84.
- exoplasim/scripts/predict_ocean_terms.py:92, whose --hdiffk default arms are
  [300, 1000, 3000]. The script builds its operator on Vesper's radius already
  (:99), so it was always predicting the true-unit answer and it is the LABELS
  on the measured arms that were wrong, not the prediction.
- clim-65's arms, which have to be declared against the fixed meaning. That
  half is not writable yet: clim-65 is a prescribed-SST run and there is no
  climatology on this build.

Left OPEN deliberately. The audits are corrected; the measurement note and
clim-65's arm declaration are not, and the latter waits on a climatology.

title: dsalb is not a restart record and nothing sets it before the first radstep of a continuation
description:
plasimmod.f90 declares `real :: dsalb(2,NHOR)` with NO initialiser. It is not written to the restart by any module -- grep 'dsalb' over the restart calls returns nothing -- and neither landini nor seaini sets it on the nrestart > 0 branch; both set it only in their cold-start branches.

The physics order inside makephysics is fluxstep, radstep, rainstep, surfstep. So on the FIRST timestep of every continuation segment, radstep reads dsalb before anything has written it. Under NSTARTEMP = 1 the shortwave reads dsalb and nothing else (radmod.f90's zra1/zra2 and zra1s/zra2s are dsalb*nstartemp + dalb*(1-nstartemp)), so that first step runs on whatever dsalb holds.

Module-scope arrays are static, so in practice it is a zero-filled .bss and the first radiation step of a continuation sees a perfectly black surface everywhere -- ice caps, glaciers, desert and ocean alike. One timestep per segment, one-signed, and it does not appear in the log. Under -finit-real or any build that does not zero-fill it is not even reproducible.

dalb IS restored (plasim.f90 mpputgp/mpgetgp 'dalb'), which is exactly why this was invisible: the broadband path a reader checks first is covered and the two-band path the model actually runs is not.

The fix is a restart record for dsalb, which means a mpputgp/mpgetgp pair in plasim.f90 beside dalb's and a POLICY entry in exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py. Both files belong to other owners, so nothing is changed here. Reconstructing it in landini and seaini instead would mean duplicating landstep's snow, forest and glacier blending at initialisation, which is the wrong shape: the state it is derived from is all restored, but so is dalb, and the record is one line.

Worth measuring before assuming it is negligible: the segment boundary is also where a bracket arm starts, and CLIM-17's lesson was that a per-segment revert measures as zero in an A/B that was designed to have a right answer.
acceptance_criteria: dsalb survives a restart, or the first radstep of a continuation demonstrably reads the same albedo the last radstep of the previous segment did.
close_reason:
Not a defect: the premise is false. dsalb IS a restart record and was one before this fan-out began -- 'dsalb1' and 'dsalb2' appear at the original base commit 05dd9453. plasim.f90 writes them at :957-958 as mpputgp('dsalb1',dsalb(1,:),NHOR,1) and mpputgp('dsalb2',dsalb(2,:),NHOR,1), reads them back unconditionally in the surface-grid block at :1288-1289 beside dalb's own read, and exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py carries a POLICY row for each (DERIVED_GRID, REMAP, INTENSIVE, bounds 0-1, rebuilt_by_model).

How the finding went wrong is worth keeping: it grepped for the record name 'dsalb' and found nothing, because the VARIABLE is dsalb and the two RECORDS are dsalb1 and dsalb2, one per band. restart_schema.py's own docstring warns about exactly this -- 'aasqsp is written from aasqout ... anything looking for the variable cannot look for the record name'. A restart-coverage question has to be asked of the record names, and smoke_test's 'the restart schema covers every record the model writes' check is what answers it; it was green throughout.

No black-planet timestep exists. The two-band path is covered exactly as the broadband one is.

title: verify_fold_indexing.sh and verify_fold_exactness.sh point at a worktree that no longer exists
description: Both gates hardcode a WT= absolute path to a .claude/worktrees/spectral-optimisation directory and derive PKG, SRC, KEEP and REF from it; verify_fold_indexing.sh also hardcodes SP as a session scratchpad under the system temp directory. That worktree is gone, so neither script can run: the first thing each does is copy from a path that does not exist. They also carry the rung as a literal, verify_fold_indexing.sh line 33 and line 88, which is what the SPAT-2 path lint exists to stop; they are exempted by name in scripts/smoke_test.py with a pointer here rather than silently fixed, because a script that cannot run should be decided about before it is repaired. Do: decide whether these two still earn their place now that the filter fold has shipped and verify_filter_fold.sh exists. If they do, anchor them in the repo the way every other gate does and remove the exemption; if they do not, delete them and the exemption together. Source: world-ltc
close_reason: Deleted both, with their SPAT-2 exemption, their pipeline.yaml rows and their README rows. Established first what they were meant to run against: both shipped in 52b96305, the same commit that committed the fold, and both recover their UNFOLDED arm from git (git show HEAD: and git checkout --). From that commit onward the unfolded arm IS the folded source, so they have never been able to produce a meaningful result from inside the repo -- broken since 2026-08-20, the day they were added, and depended on exactly once before that, in the development worktree, with the result recorded in exoplasim/notes/legendre-filter-fold.md. Repointing their paths would have made them pass vacuously, which is worse than not running. verify_filter_fold.sh survives because it takes both executables as arguments; the note's Reproducing section now carries the recipe and the test-filter method. build_model.py:226 still names verify_fold_exactness.sh and is filed separately: that file belongs to the MPI-removal batch. Commit d7e383ee.

title: build_surface_albedo.py --mode modelled writes one identical field to 174, 175 and 176
description:
SPEC-5 gave the vegetated paint a band pair: analysis/vegetation_albedo.py splits the same leaf integrals at 0.75 um and config carries model.vegetation_albedo_bands, and build_surface_albedo.py writes it to codes 175 and 176. That split is gated on `mode == "vegetated"` (the `band_grids` block). `--mode modelled` -- the mode the script's own docstring calls the only one that is not an assumption, and the mode that closes the loop with LPJ-GUESS -- falls through to `band_fields = {code: field for code in ALBEDO_CODES}`, so 174, 175 and 176 all receive the same broadband array.

That is exactly what the vegetation_albedo.py docstring says a canopy certainly does not do: reflect equally either side of 0.75 um. Under NSIMPLEALBEDO=0 the radiation reads 175 and 176 and not 174, so the production path stages a canopy asserted to be spectrally flat.

Two pieces are missing, and the second is the real one:

  1. the cover endmembers now have band values available in principle --
     analysis/vegetation_albedo.json's band_shape_from_leaf is [0.4535,
     1.3628] and applies to any canopy level -- so tree and grass could be
     split the same way model.vegetation_albedo was;
  2. the SUBSTRATE they are blended against has no band values at all.
     rock_albedo in the export is one broadband number per class, and
     analysis/rock_albedo.py derives a broadband star-weighted value. A
     modelled cell is cover*canopy + (1-cover)*substrate, so a band pair for
     the blend needs a band pair for the rock table, which is a re-run of
     rock_albedo.py split at 0.75 um.

Until (2) exists the honest options are to leave modelled writing a flat pair
and say so in the report it writes, or to split only the canopy term and hold
the substrate flat, which mixes a split quantity with an unsplit one. Neither
is chosen here.
acceptance_criteria: --mode modelled writes a band pair to 175/176 derived from split canopy AND substrate integrals, or the report it writes records that the pair is flat and why.

title: Soil thermal inertia is one scalar, and a quarter of this land is playa or evaporite
description:
Successor to world-sy9's third acceptance clause. world-sy9 made soildiff, soilcap, snowdiff, sicediff, snowcap, sicecap and rhosnow reachable as landmod_nl keys and recorded what the single value costs; it did not give the playa and evaporite classes their own thermal inertia, because they are SCALARS and the model has no per-cell slot for either.

landmod.f90's soilstep builds zcap and zdiff per layer as sicecap*dglac + soilcap*(1-dglac) and the same for the diffusivity. Both terms are scalars. Thermal inertia sqrt(k*rho*c) is 2078 J/m2/K/s^0.5 at the default pair against roughly 625 for a dry playa or salt crust, so the classes config/planet.yaml names as evaporite and playa clastics are damped by about 3.3x too much. That feeds the diurnal and seasonal surface temperature swing, which feeds evaporation, which feeds P - E, which is the numerator of the carve criterion, and it feeds the dust emission threshold.

What a per-class treatment needs, so the size is visible before anyone starts:

  - two new NHOR arrays in landmod for the conductivity and the heat capacity,
    replacing the scalars in the zcap/zdiff construction;
  - a staged surface field per array, so two new surface codes and two
    surfcode() rows in surfmod.f90, and the codes have to be chosen against
    the existing table AND against what pyburn names;
  - restart records for both, with POLICY entries in
    exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py -- they are STATIC_GRID/TARGET like
    dz0clim, not prognostic;
  - a generator that reads the lithology the same way
    exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_roughness.py does, its row in
    config/pipeline.yaml, its inert-key entries in lib/provenance.py, and its
    README line;
  - the k, rho and c values per rock class, which is the part that is not
    mechanical: the export carries albedo per class and not thermal
    properties, so this needs a literature table and a derivation script under
    analysis/ of the same shape as analysis/rock_albedo.py.

Not started here because it is a component rather than a fix, and because its
surface codes and restart policy cross two other owners.
acceptance_criteria: The playa and evaporite classes carry their own thermal conductivity and heat capacity; the values have a derivation; the field has a generator, a pipeline row and a restart policy.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT: STILL
TRUE, unchanged in substance. Nothing in wave 1 or wave 2 touched the per-cell
thermal inertia question; world-sy9 is still open and this is still its
successor.

Cites re-located by content:
- The seven scalars are landmod.f90:142-148 (rhosnow, soildiff, sicediff,
  snowdiff, soilcap, sicecap, snowcap), reachable in landmod_nl at :247-255 and
  broadcast at :376-382. That is world-sy9's half and it landed.
- soilstep still builds both fields from scalars:
    zcap(:,jlev)=sicecap*dglac(:)+soilcap*(1.-dglac(:))
    zdiff(:,jlev)=sicediff*dglac(:)+soildiff*(1.-dglac(:))
  at landmod.f90:835-836, and the snow blend that reads them at :872-883.
  There is still no NHOR array for either.
- config/planet.yaml:894 carries barren_rock_classes: [evaporite,
  playa_clastic], and :884-892 the playa albedo override, so the two classes
  the issue names are declared and are the ones the export distinguishes.
- The pattern the work would follow is intact: build_surface_roughness.py
  exists and is a {res} pipeline step, restart_schema.py:404 has dz0clim as
  STATIC_GRID/TARGET, lib/provenance.py carries the inert-key sets, and
  analysis/rock_albedo.py is the shape the derivation script would take.

So the size estimate in the description stands as written. The one part that is
not mechanical is unchanged too: the export carries albedo per lithology class
and no thermal properties, so k, rho and c per class still need a literature
table before anything else in the list is worth starting.

title: Remove the MPI build path: only the threaded OpenMP build is used
description:
The project builds and runs ONLY the threaded OpenMP parmode. The MPI path, the serial path and the parmode axis itself all go: the user has decided that killing serial, mpimod_stub and parmode is part of killing MPI, not a separate question.

DECIDED, so this is now a straight removal:
- serial/mpimod_stub goes with it. mpimod_stub is referenced from exactly one place, the CMakeLists parmode branch; nothing links it. plasim.x is the only CMake target, and buildice.x/newsnow.x are not built by CMake at all.
- parmode leaves the build tag and the executable name. There is one configuration, so the axis carries no information.

What carries it today:
- vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/CMakeLists.txt:35 declares the PLASIM_PARMODE cache variable, :50 requires it present, :59 require_one_of serial/mpi/omp, :120-127 the three-way _mpimod branch, :226 puts parmode in the build's own diagnostic string. The branch collapses to mpimod_omp.
- exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py: PARMODES, the --parmode argument, the mpif90 compiler branch and its PATH check, and parmode inside tag() and executable_name(). NOTE: batch E has just rewritten parts of this file (patched-build directories, the FFT selection moving to lib/rungs.py), so this work rebases onto that, it does not predate it.
- vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/mpimod.f90 and mpimod_multi.f90 delete. mpimod_omp.f90 is the survivor.

Renaming consequences, which are the real cost and must land in the same commit:
- Every build directory and executable name changes: most_plasim_t21_l10_p16_omp.x loses its _omp.
- scripts/check_consistency.py's 'cycle capability' check names that executable literally.
- exoplasim/scripts/rebuild_binaries.py enumerates configurations by parmode.
- CLAUDE.md rule 4 states the one-executable-per-(resolution, layers, ranks, parmode) fact and names both parmodes. It is a rule that bites and is true until this lands.
- docs/src/reference/builds.md carries the registry and the durable set.

NOT settled by this issue: world-ljj. Under the threaded build NPRO is the thread count, so the NLPP decomposition is still live and can still truncate.
acceptance_criteria: No mpi parmode in build_model.py; mpimod.f90 and mpimod_multi.f90 gone or justified; CMakeLists selects one variant; CLAUDE.md rule 4 and builds.md updated in the same commit; smoke_test and check_consistency pass.
notes:
VERIFIED BEFORE THE EDIT, both of the things the scope said to check rather than assume:

1. Nothing outside CMake links mpimod_stub. add_executable appears once in the whole of vendor/exoplasim, for plasim.x; the only other build file is vendor/exoplasim/docs/Makefile, which is sphinx. plasim/bin/buildice.x and newsnow.x are checked-in binaries with no CMake target. Outside CMakeLists the name appeared only in comments, in binary_manifest.json's hashed source set, and in vendor/cgenie's own separate copy of the file. No script compiles any mpimod variant except verify_omp_collectives.sh, which compiles mpimod_omp.f90 alone.

2. restart_schema.compiled_modules() does depend on the slot, and correctly. It expands every ${VAR} in the _sources list to every value require_one_of and set() admit, so the parmode branch was contributing mpimod.f90, mpimod_stub.f90, utilities.f90 and utilities_stub.f90 to the inventory and to rebuild_binaries.model_sources(). With the branch collapsed to literals it returns 35 .f90 modules, PLASIM_FFT is the one slot left and still expands to both fftmod and fft991mod, and smoke_test's 'the restart schema covers every record the model writes' stays green. No restart record was lost: the put_restart_array calls in the deleted files pass a variable name rather than a literal, so the record scanner never saw them.

CORRECTION TO THE SCOPE: docs/src/reference/builds.md needed no change. Its registry and durable set are the Orogen build registry; it contains no reference to a binary, an executable name, parmode or rule 4. The rule-4 restatements that did need rewriting are CLAUDE.md rule 4, docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md class 11, exoplasim/README.md, and reproducibility_matrix.py's refusal message.

THE NEW NAMES:
  build/t21_l10_p16_omp_production   -> build/t21_l10_p16_production
  most_plasim_t21_l10_p16_omp.x      -> most_plasim_t21_l10_p16.x
  most_plasim_t170_l10_p16_omp_fp.x  -> most_plasim_t170_l10_p16_fp.x
Sixteen build directories under vendor/exoplasim/build/ are orphaned by the rename: the eleven *_mpi_production ones by the deletion outright, and t21/t42/t85/t127/t170_l10_p16_omp_production because the tag lost its parmode. The fourteen t42_l10_p16_omp_production_x* flag-sweep arms are orphaned the same way. All five binaries in plasim/run are orphaned, and binary_manifest.json is invalid independently of the rename because it hashes the three deleted sources.

THE RENAME FIXES TWO LATENT BUGS: continue_exoplasim.py:692 and run_stellar_cycle.py:297 already composed the name without a suffix, so both were looking for a binary the omp-only registry never built.

FOLLOW-ON, filed rather than done because those files belong to other batches: world-8tq (run_exoplasim.py, __init__.py, config/planet.yaml, lib/provenance.py, build_restart_template.py), world-d5l (the eight build callers that still pass --parmode, two of which lose their reference arm), world-7b2 (reproducibility_matrix.py's mpiexec), world-f1l (a comparison build can no longer name its compiler). utilities.f90 and utilities_stub.f90 are now in no source list and are recorded on world-cmz.
Count correction: all 31 directories under vendor/exoplasim/build/ are orphaned by the rename, not sixteen -- 12 *_mpi_production, 5 *_omp_production, and 14 t42_l10_p16_omp_production_x* flag-sweep arms. Every one carries a parmode in its tag. There is no build/patched/ on disk. They are artifacts and were not deleted.
close_reason: The MPI and serial paths and the parmode axis are gone. mpimod.f90, mpimod_multi.f90 and mpimod_stub.f90 deleted; CMakeLists.txt names mpimod_omp.f90 and utilities_omp.f90 as literals and no longer declares PLASIM_PARMODE; build_model.py has no --parmode, always uses gfortran and always appends -fopenmp -DOMPSHARED. Parmode left the build tag and the executable name, and the three name constructions this issue owned -- build_model.executable_name, rebuild_binaries.expected, check_consistency's cycle-capability check -- agree on most_plasim_<res>_l<levels>_p<ranks>.x. CLAUDE.md rule 4 and failure-modes class 11 restated without parmode and still saying that a rebuild refreshes only the configuration you built. vendored-upstreams.md replaces the do-not-delete-yet paragraph with what the deletion costs. smoke_test 24/24; check_consistency unchanged from its pre-change state in this worktree, and its cycle-capability line now names the new executable. Not built and not run, per the batch brief. Consumers outside this issue's file set are world-8tq, world-d5l, world-7b2 and world-f1l.

title: Stage the surface families for the rungs that have binaries and none
description:
rebuild_binaries.MATRIX builds T21, T42, T85, T127 and T170, and
config/planet.yaml declares hyperdiffusion timescales and a timestep for exactly
those five, so all five are rungs the project intends to RUN. Three of them have
no surface family staged under exoplasim/inputs/, and T42's family is missing
the soil-water field 0229 that T21 has.

The grid exports the generators need already exist: source/precarve-craton-10m
carries exoplasim-T21, T42, T85, T127 and T170.

Nothing integrates on an unprovisioned rung today: surface_field_report raises
on a missing intended code and declare_hyperdiffusion raises on a rung with no
table entry. This is the provisioning that makes the three built rungs usable,
and it is what spat-11's short per-rung integration needs.

THREE OF THE FOUR GENERATORS ARE RUNNABLE NOW, and one is not:
- boundary_conditions (0129, 0172) and surface_roughness (0173) have needs: []
  in config/pipeline.yaml and read the export and the lithology only.
- surface_albedo (0174, 0175, 0176, 0212) needs lpj_run, but that edge is the
  loop-C BACK edge: its gate says the first pass runs --mode vegetated on
  terrain alone, which is what land_albedo_source: vegetated selects and what
  T21 and T42 were built with.
- surface_soil_water (0229) needs the `soil` step, which needs
  bootstrap_climatology. T21's 0229 provenance records it was cut from a
  bootstrap regular climatology through pedology's soil map, and
  config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null with no climatology on
  this build. So 0229 for T42 and for the three new rungs is BLOCKED on a
  bootstrap climatology, not on running a step. It is also not currently
  required: model.soil_water_source is `uniform`, so 229 is not in the surface
  set run_exoplasim demands and check_consistency reports T21 complete at seven
  codes without it.

Do: stage boundary_conditions, surface_albedo and surface_roughness for T85,
T127 and T170 now. Take 0229 for T42 and the three new rungs with the rest of
loop A's post-bootstrap steps, when there is a climatology to cut a soil map
from.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 9, and world-3oj.
acceptance_criteria: Every rung in rebuild_binaries.MATRIX has boundary_conditions, surface_albedo and surface_roughness staged, and scripts/pipeline.py --status reports those three surface steps present with that rung configured. 0229 for T42 and for T85/T127/T170 is a separate clause, blocked on a bootstrap climatology and taken with the rest of loop A's post-bootstrap steps.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged wave-1 and wave-2 tree (base
aaeaed55). VERDICT: CHANGED. Every claim in the description still holds; the
shape change is that one of the four families is blocked and three are not.

STILL TRUE, cites re-located:
- rebuild_binaries.py MATRIX is the five rows T21/T42/T85/T127/T170, all
  ("omp"), and the comment above it now states the three conditions for a
  runnable rung and which check refuses on each. world-3oj landed that.
- config/planet.yaml declares model.hyperdiffusion.timescales_days and
  model.resolution_timestep_minutes for exactly those five, and
  declare_hyperdiffusion raises on a rung the table does not name.
- source/precarve-craton-10m carries exoplasim-T21, T42, T85, T127 and T170.
- exoplasim/inputs/ holds t21, t42, stellarspectra and templates only. T85,
  T127 and T170 have nothing staged. T42 has 0129, 0172, 0173, 0174, 0175,
  0176 and 0212 and no 0229; T21 has 0229 as well.
- All four generators are {res}-parameterised pipeline steps:
  boundary_conditions, surface_albedo, surface_roughness, surface_soil_water.

WHAT THE DESCRIPTION MISSED, and it splits the acceptance criterion in two:
- boundary_conditions and surface_roughness have needs: [] and read the export
  and the lithology only. Runnable for the three unstaged rungs today.
- surface_albedo needs lpj_run, but that edge is the loop-C BACK edge and its
  gate says the first pass runs --mode vegetated on terrain alone, which is
  what land_albedo_source: vegetated selects and what T21 and T42 were built
  with. Runnable today.
- surface_soil_water (0229) needs the `soil` step, which needs
  bootstrap_climatology. T21's orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json records
  exactly that: it was cut from
  exoplasim/analysis/climatology/bootstrap_regular_climatology.nc through
  pedology/data/precarve-craton-10m/soilmap.txt. config/planet.yaml carries
  baseline_climatology: null and no climatology exists on this build, so
  "T42's 0229" is BLOCKED on a bootstrap climatology, not on running a step.
- Not urgent for the current rung either way: model.soil_water_source is
  `uniform`, so 229 is not in run_exoplasim's required surface set and
  check_consistency reports T21's family complete at seven codes without it.

DO, restated: stage boundary_conditions, surface_albedo and surface_roughness
for T85, T127 and T170 now; take 0229 for T42 and the three new rungs at the
same time as the rest of loop A's post-bootstrap steps.

title: Derive a per-cell surface longwave emissivity from the lithology map
description:
world-qvu declared `land_longwave_emissivity` and `sea_longwave_emissivity` in config/planet.yaml and named them ELWLAND and ELWSEA in radmod_nl, at the values the compiled literal carried. That makes the assumption visible and gives it an arm; it does not make it right.

Land emissivity is uniform, and this world's land is not. Bare rock, desert sand and salt crust run 0.90 to 0.95 broadband in the thermal window while vegetated and wet surfaces run 0.96 to 0.99, and config/planet.yaml names evaporite and playa clastics as barren classes over a large share of this land. A scalar cannot carry that.

Do: build a per-cell broadband thermal emissivity from the lithology map the way build_surface_albedo.py builds albedo, stage it as a surface field, and read it in lwr in place of the ELWLAND scalar. `zeps` at the head of lwr is already a per-cell array, so the model side is a field read rather than a scheme change. Needs an emissivity per lithology class with a source, which references/INDEX.md does not currently carry.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 6, notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 6.

title: Regenerate the dust forcing tables against the current surface albedos
description:
exoplasim/scripts/dust_optics.py has been regenerated and its warms_over list already changed: at the config's playa_clastic albedo the OPAC band-1 row no longer warms over playa fill, only over salt crust, because critical_surface_albedo is 0.3001.

analysis/dust_forcing.json and the tables in notes/dust.md could NOT be regenerated in the same pass: dust_forcing.py resolves the baseline climatology through lib/paths.py:climatology_path and config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null, so there is no climate to compute a forcing on.

What is at stake, from interpolating the note's own near-linear albedo dependence: the playa TOA net falls from about +4.3 to about +0.8 W/m2 and the land half of the global mean from about +2.05 to about +0.15. The land half of the SHORTWAVE-ONLY number moves further, and that is the one DUST-3 turns on and the one the 1.5 W/m2 reopening threshold at dust_forcing.py:472 is applied to. Whether the threshold verdict survives is not answerable by interpolation and must be re-measured.

Do: once a baseline climatology is declared, re-run exoplasim/scripts/dust_forcing.py, rewrite the three tables in notes/dust.md and the summary table at its DUST-12 section, and re-read the reopening verdict. Blocked until then.

Source: world-2bf, and notes/audits/opaque-constants.md

title: APART and RHOP are never written, so in-model dust would settle about 1790x too slowly
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md, dormant section.

aeromod.f90:43-44 declares apart = 50e-9 m and rhop = 1000 kg/m3, a 50 nm
photochemical haze grain at water density, and both are in aero_nl
(aeromod.f90:194). run_exoplasim.py:enable_dust_emission (1154-1252) writes
L_AERO, l_source, aerofile, l_aerorad and every key in prov["namelist_values"],
