and aeolian/scripts/build_dust_source_fields.py:98-129 builds that dict with the
fourteen DUST* keys and NEITHER APART NOR RHOP.

The correct values already exist, unread, in
exoplasim/data/dust/vesper_dust_aerosol.provenance.json as apart_m = 2.2068e-06
and rhop_kg_m3 = 2600.0 -- the burden-matched radius derived FOR THIS PLANET'S
GRAVITY by exoplasim/scripts/dust_aerofile.py:158.

Through vels at aerocore.f90:1185, v = 2*beta*apart^2*ga*(rhop-rhog)/(9*mu):
radius contributes (2.2068e-6/5e-8)^2 = 1948, density 2.602, and the Cunningham
factor 0.354 (beta 1.039 at 2.21 um against 2.936 at 50 nm, lambda 67.5 nm at
1 bar and 288 K). Net 1793. The compiled default gives about 1.2 um/s where the
intended grain falls at about 0.21 cm/s.

Sedimentation is the only removal term active by default, since ldepvel and
lwetdep are 0, so the burden would instead be set by the timestep-dependent
99-per-cent-per-step bottom-layer scrub at aerocore.f90:944. mmr2n
(aerocore.f90:1239) is off by 44.14^3 * 2.6 = 2.24e5 on number density, dormant
only because run_exoplasim.py:1242 pins l_aerorad = 0.

Dormant: L_AERO is set only inside enable_dust_emission, which returns early at
:1181 because model.dust_emission is absent from planet.yaml. One config key
away.

Also correct aeolian/notes/in-model-dust.md:528, which asserts the sidecar
carries APART and RHOP in namelist_values. The code does not do this.

A NEW instance of the class in notes/audits/aerosol-particle-radius.md, not the
audited one: that audit is about radmod's copy diverging from aeromod's (fixed
in this fork at aeromod.f90 by rad_apart = apart), and this is about neither
copy ever being set.
acceptance_criteria: APART and RHOP are written from the provenance sidecar; a dust run reproduces the intended settling velocity; in-model-dust.md matches the code.
close_reason: enable_dust_emission reads the AEROFILE's own provenance sidecar beside the .dat it already stages and writes APART and RHOP from it, refusing if the sidecar is missing or either value is not positive. Two provenance files reach that function and the distinction is load-bearing: the source-field sidecar carries the emission law, the aerofile sidecar carries the grain. in-model-dust.md corrected -- it asserted the sidecar was already the run's source of radius, and no code path opened it.

title: There is no saturation-over-ice branch, while the latent heat already switches
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 24.

p_earth.f90:44-46 sets ra1=610.78, ra2=17.2693882, ra4=35.86, the Magnus-Teten
coefficients over LIQUID water, and that single formula is used at every zqsat
site in rainmod.f90 (about fifteen) and at seamod.f90:254. Meanwhile the latent
heat correctly switches to ALS below TMELT (rainmod.f90:767, :886, :980, :1083;
fluxmod.f90:693-700) and the Clausius-Clapeyron derivative zdqsdt is the liquid
one multiplied by L_s/cp.

Saturation over ice is about 25 per cent below saturation over liquid at 250 K,
so cold-cloud condensation is systematically over-produced and the
thermodynamics is internally inconsistent with its own latent heat.

The ice coefficient set is already in the tree at p_mars.f90:48-50, as
610.66/21.875/7.65.

This CANNOT be fixed from config as the tree is built: p_exo.f90 exposes alv,
als and tmelt in planet_nl and p_earth.f90 does not, and p_earth is what
compiles (world-cwu, world-58v). It needs a second branch rather than a
different single set in any case, so it is a source change either way.
acceptance_criteria: Saturation vapour pressure branches on ice below the melting point; the branch is consistent with the latent heat already in use.
notes: world-58v changed the premise: alv, als and tmelt are now in planet_nl on p_earth.f90, the module that compiles, so the latent heats and the switching temperature ARE settable from config. What remains is exactly what the finding says is a source change: ra1/ra2/ra4 are a single liquid-water set and the fix is a second BRANCH below tmelt, not a different single set. p_mars.f90 was deleted under world-cmz; its ice coefficients were 610.66 / 21.875 / 7.65 and that is the whole of what it carried for this issue.
close_reason: ra1i/ra2i/ra4i added to pumamod and planet_nl in all three planet modules at 610.66/21.875/7.65; three elemental selectors ra1s/ra2s/ra4s branch per gridpoint. Thirty-two sites in rainmod, two in landmod and one in simba take the temperature in the expression. fluxmod's two take the phase from the where arm and seamod's two stay liquid, because fluxmod treats every cell with dls < 0.5 as evaporating liquid whatever its temperature. This is a physics change and moves the climate.

title: The glacier persistence test is one run segment, and persistflag is not in the restart
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 19.

glaciermod.f90:42 initialises persistflag(NHOR) = .TRUE., glacierstep (:588)
only ever clears it, and glacierstop (:614) converts whatever survives to
dglac = 1.0. persistflag is NOT written to the restart: glacierstop writes only
groundsg, dglacsg, doro and dglac (:622-628).

The module header says the criterion is "some snow cover continuously for an
entire year" (glaciermod.f90:10-11). What it is, is continuously for one
invocation of the model. This project runs one orbit per invocation
(N_RUN_YEARS=1, N_DAYS_PER_YEAR=146, N_RUN_STEPS=5850), so the persistence
evidence a modelled glacier needs is half what the module was written to
require, and it resets to a clean slate at every segment boundary.

The threshold GLACELIM is reachable and set to 2.0, which is ExoPlaSim's Earth
snowline default restated. The DURATION is not reachable at all, because it is
the segment length -- so the criterion silently changes meaning if anyone runs
multi-orbit segments.

Do: carry persistflag in the restart so the criterion means what it says, and
declare the intended duration rather than inheriting the segment length.
acceptance_criteria: persistflag survives a restart; the persistence duration is declared and independent of segment length.
close_reason: persistflag is replaced by persistt(NHOR), the seconds of continuous snow cover at or above GLACELIM, written to and read from the restart by glacierstop and glacierini. glacierstep resets it when cover breaks and converts the cell the moment it reaches glacpersec, so the conversion no longer waits for a segment boundary and no longer depends on where one falls. The duration is GLACPERSIST in glacier_nl, in ORBITS, converted by m_days_per_year * day_24hr -- the same conversion landini uses for tau_veg -- and declared in config/planet.yaml as surface.glaciers.persistence_orbits: 1.0, which is the duration a one-orbit-per-invocation caller was already enforcing, so the criterion is unchanged. It reaches both the prepare and the resume path through configure_otherargs. persistflag is DELETED rather than left set-and-never-read. NOT DONE HERE and filed as world-e1x: exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py needs a POLICY entry for persistt, and scripts/smoke_test.py's restart-schema check is red until it has one. That file belongs to another batch; the exact entry is in world-e1x.

title: The model's calendar is a 360-day Earth year that calini never updates
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 18.

calmod.f90:19-22 declares n_days_per_month=30, n_days_per_year=360,
m_days_per_year=360, m_days_per_month=30. calini (:44-99) copies
n_days_per_month, n_days_per_year, n_start_step, ntspd, solar_day and mpstep --
and NOT m_days_per_year or m_days_per_month, which plasim.f90:1506-1507 has just
set to 183 and 15.

So calmod's mtspd is 146*40/360 truncated to 16, and the calendar year is
360*16 = 5760 steps against the orbit's n_steps_per_year = 5850: the calendar
drifts 1.54 per cent per orbit against the season and is a full year out after
about 65 orbits. tcalday becomes 43200 s, so a "calendar day" is half a 24-hour
day and step2cal30 reports hours 0 to 11. cal2step and step2cal30 are not
inverses: plasim.f90:1585 encodes with mtspd=32, 146 and 15 and step2cal30
decodes with 16, 360 and 30, so year 1 month 1 day 1 encodes to step 4672 and
decodes as 23-Oct-0001. outmod.f90:119 and :147 pack ihead(3) from that while
ihead(8) reports 183, so one eight-word header carries two different days per
year.

Bounded today: pyburn.py:492 and :539 take the netCDF time axis from header[6],
the raw step counter, and radiation takes its orbital phase from n_steps_per_year
independently (radmod.f90:1848, :1979), so nothing this project reads goes
through it. It becomes live the moment anyone enables climatological ozone
(radmod.f90:1999), t-nudging or flux correction (miscmod.f90:264, :321), the
land surface annual cycle (landmod.f90:1490, :1519), or prescribed ice and SST
(icemod.f90:1883-1919, oceanmod.f90:745, :765) -- all of which interpolate
through step2cal30.

Related trap in the same machinery: n_days_per_year == 365 silently switches the
whole model to Earth's Gregorian calendar, with mondays, the 400/100/4 leap rule
and Jan..Dec names (calmod.f90:107, :138, :277, :387, :463). N_DAYS_PER_YEAR is
derived from the flux and the rotation period at run_exoplasim.py:238, so
nothing structurally prevents a future world landing on 365, and there is no
guard and no message.

Do: have calini copy both, and add the 365 guard.
acceptance_criteria: calmod's month and year lengths match pumamod's; cal2step and step2cal30 round-trip; a 365-rotation year raises rather than silently switching calendars.
close_reason: calini takes m_days_per_year, m_days_per_month and mtspd from the caller, so the calendar day is the 24-hour day and tcalday comes out at day_24hr by construction. readnl gains a setter for m_days_per_month, the year over twelve rounded up. cal2step uses m_days_* and kyea-1, making it the exact inverse of step2cal30 over three years of steps and making year 1 month 1 day 1 encode to step 0 -- which also moves every cold start's orbital phase from 0.799 to 0. Residual drift 0.10 per cent against 1.54. calini aborts on n_days_per_year == 365 with the reason.

title: The archived surface albedo is the Earth-Sun broadband value, not the one the radiation used
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 15.

landmod.f90:28-33 declares six non-spectral albedo scalars: albsmin=0.4,
albsmax=0.8, albsminf=0.3, albsmaxf=0.4, albgmin=0.6, albgmax=0.8. landini
re-derives only the banded copies from the spectrum (:225-236); those six are
never touched.

landstep computes dalb(jhor) from them (:544-557, and :601-603 for glacier), and
since radstep runs BEFORE surfstep in the timestep (plasim.f90:4048 then :4082),
radmod's correct overwrite of dalb at radmod.f90:2943 is discarded by landmod
every step. The landmod value is what outmod.f90:2641 accumulates and :695
writes as code 175, which is in both REGULAR_CODES and SNAPSHOT_CODES.

Radiation reads dsalb and is unaffected, so this is archival only. The stored
field reads +0.068 over cold snow, +0.057 over snowy forest and +0.061 to +0.068
over cold and melting glacier. Any future surface energy closure or map that
reads 175 will be wrong by that much, one-signed, only over the cryosphere.

Note also that code 175 collides with dalbcl1 on input (surfmod.f90:252), so the
same code means two different things in and out.

Do: derive the six scalars from the spectrum alongside the banded pair, or write
the flux-weighted combination of dsalb as 175 instead.
acceptance_criteria: Code 175 equals the albedo the radiation used; the input/output collision on 175 is documented or resolved.
close_reason: landstep and seastep now rebuild dalb from their own dsalb as zsolars(1)*dsalb(1,:) + zsolars(2)*dsalb(2,:) at nstartemp = 1, which is radmod.f90's own expression at the line that writes the diagnostic. Over land radmod's ocean direct-beam branch is gated on 1-dls, so dsalb is untouched there and code 175 now equals what the radiation used EXACTLY over snow, forested snow, glacier and the sea-ice fraction -- every surface the finding measured, where it read +0.057 to +0.068 high. One residual, named in the code and not left to be discovered: over the OPEN-WATER fraction radmod substitutes the ECHAM-3 zenith-angle direct-beam albedo when necham = 1 (the default, and this project does not override it), so 175 there is the flux-weighted doceanalb rather than the zenith-corrected value. Reproducing it would need radstep's local zmu0, which is not module state and is zonally averaged when ndcycle = 0. What replaced the Earth broadband albsea/albice pair is therefore a star-weighted ocean albedo rather than an exact one. Nothing the radiation reads changed: dsalb is untouched and at nstartemp = 0 both paths are unchanged. The six non-spectral scalars are left as they are rather than re-derived, because under two-band shortwave they now feed nothing but the nstartemp = 0 path. The 175 in/out collision is documented at surfmod.f90's surfcode rows -- staged background albedo per band in, dalb with the cryosphere blended into it out under pyburn's name alb/surface_albedo, and 176 not written out at all -- rather than renumbered, because staged .sra files and written output both depend on the numbering.

title: One Earth-average soil thermal pair, and the conductivity is in no namelist
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 14.

landmod.f90:73 soildiff = 1.8 W/m/K and :76 soilcap = 2.4E6 J/m3/K, applied
uniformly at :697-698. These are moist mineral soil, Earth's global average, on
a project that already derives albedo and roughness per cell from lithology.

Thermal inertia sqrt(k*rho*c) is 2078 J/m2/K/s^0.5 for the default against
roughly 625 for a dry playa or salt crust, so the quarter of this land that
config/planet.yaml names as evaporite and playa clastics carries about 3.3x too
much thermal inertia and its diurnal and seasonal surface temperature swing is
damped by roughly that factor. That feeds evaporation, which feeds P minus E,
the numerator of the carve criterion, and it feeds the dust emission threshold.

SOILCAP is a namelist scalar (landmod.f90:172) reachable through cpsoil and not
passed. soildiff is not in the namelist at all, and neither are snowdiff,
sicediff, snowcap, sicecap or rhosnow. Neither can be a field; both are scalars,
so a per-class treatment needs a source change.

Checked and not a finding, recorded so it is not re-derived: the soil layer
depths are adequate. At kappa = 7.5e-7 m2/s the annual damping depth is 1.94 m
here against Earth's 2.75, so the 12.4 m column is 6.4 damping depths against
Earth's 4.5 and the zero-flux bottom boundary is if anything better here.
dztop = 0.20 m against a 30-hour diurnal damping depth of 0.161 m is 1.25
against Earth's 1.39, so 11 per cent under-thick.
acceptance_criteria: soildiff is reachable; both constants are declared or derived from lithology; the playa and evaporite classes carry their own thermal inertia.
notes:
TWO OF THREE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES DONE, 2026-08-24. Left OPEN for the third.

Done. soildiff, snowdiff, sicediff, sicecap, snowcap and rhosnow are landmod_nl keys, values unchanged, so soildiff is reachable for the first time and the others are settable rather than compiled. soilcap was already a key and gained the mpbcr it never had -- without it every non-root rank kept the compiled default while root read the namelist, so a multi-rank run could disagree with itself about the soil's heat capacity. The declaration beside the block records what one scalar per planet costs: thermal inertia 2078 J/m2/K/s^0.5 against roughly 625 for a dry playa or salt crust, so the evaporite and playa classes are damped by about 3.3x too much, and that reaches evaporation, P - E and the dust emission threshold.

Also kept, from the issue and not re-derived: the soil layer depths are adequate. 12.4 m is 6.4 annual damping depths here against Earth's 4.5, and dztop is 11 per cent under-thick against the diurnal damping depth.

NOT DONE. 'the playa and evaporite classes carry their own thermal inertia' needs a per-cell FIELD, and the model has no slot for one: soilcap and soildiff are scalars in the zcap/zdiff construction. Filed as world-yip with the full shape -- two NHOR arrays, two new surface codes and surfcode rows, two restart POLICY entries, a generator with its pipeline row and inert-key entries, and a literature-derived k/rho/c table per rock class that this project does not have. It is a component rather than a fix and it crosses two other owners' files, so it was not started in this batch.

title: The sea-ice albedo ramp keeps an Earth broadband slope under star-derived endpoints
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 12.

seamod.f90:156-158 and :270-272 use
`dicec*AMIN1(dicealbmx(b), dicealbmn(b) + 0.025*(273.-dts))`.

dicealbmn and dicealbmx are star-weighted per band by radmod.f90:725-756 and
independently verified by analysis/ice_albedo.py. That work stopped at the
endpoints. The slope 0.025 per K is Earth's, tuned to Earth's broadband span
albice - 0.5 = 0.25, which is exactly 10 K, and neither it nor the 273.0 anchor
is a namelist key. landmod.f90:436-441 does the same job correctly with a
FRACTIONAL ramp, (albgmax-albgmin)*(dts-263.16)/(tmelt-263.16), which is the
structure this should have.

Band 1 spans 0.6203 to 0.8702, a span of 0.250, and saturates 10.0 K below
freezing; band 2 spans 0.3395 to 0.4729, a span of 0.133, and saturates 5.3 K
below. The two bands reach maximum albedo 4.7 K apart, a gap set entirely by how
far the re-weighting stretched each endpoint and by nothing about the modelled
ice. At 268 K band 2 reads 0.4645 against a consistently scaled 0.4062, so
+0.058 in band 2 and about +0.036 broadband.

Near zero in the global mean, because most modelled ice is colder than either
saturation point, and several W/m2 locally in the 263 to 273 K band where the
ice-albedo feedback lives.

One tell that 273.0 is a magic number rather than a physical anchor: it is
neither TMELT = 273.16 nor TFREEZE, so at the melting point the formula returns
0.004 BELOW its own declared minimum.
acceptance_criteria: The ramp is fractional and per band; both bands saturate at the same temperature; the anchor is TMELT or TFREEZE rather than 273.0.
close_reason: seamod's ramp is fractional and per band: zsicf = clamp((TMELT - dts)/dicealbdt, 0, 1), applied as dicealbmn(b) + zsicf*(dicealbmx(b) - dicealbmn(b)). Both bands now saturate at the same temperature, the anchor is TMELT rather than 273.0, and the formula returns exactly dicealbmn at the melting point instead of 0.004 below it. dicealbdt joins seamod_nl at 10.0 K, which is upstream's implied width at Earth's broadband span, so an Earth configuration keeps the same saturation temperature. albicemn replaces the literal 0.5 in the non-spectral copy, which is Earth's minimum sea-ice albedo. Measured against the staged endpoints: at 268 K band 2 goes 0.4645 -> 0.4083 and band 1 0.7608 -> 0.7679, -0.032 broadband; the largest broadband change over 263 to 273 K is -0.032 and the ends are within 0.004. Both call sites changed, seaini and seastep, and the calculation sits inside the where(dls < 0.5) block so it cannot read dts over land.

title: The ozone profile is placed at a fixed geometric height fitted to Earth's scale height
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 11.

radmod.f90:81-82, bo3 = 20000. and co3 = 5000., both in metres, applied at
:1987-1996. mko3 builds its height coordinate hypsometrically with the model's
own ga, correctly, and then places the profile against a fixed geometric 20 km.
This world's scale height is 0.766 of Earth's, so 20 km is 3.6 scale heights
here against 2.7 on Earth.

The modelled photochemical ozone maximum is set by pressure-like conditions --
ultraviolet optical depth and three-body recombination density -- not by
geometric altitude, so height is the wrong invariant. Holding pressure fixed
means bo3 about 15300 and co3 about 3830.

Reproducing the L10 sigma levels and the mko3 recursion with a 230 to 288 K
profile, the fraction of the modelled ozone column deposited in the top model
layer goes from 0.616 at Earth gravity to 0.794 here, and layer 2's share halves
from 0.202 to 0.105. This redistributes shortwave heating rather than changing
the column, so the budget effect is small and consistent with
exoplasim/notes/ozone.md calling it second-order for the surface; the top-layer
heating rate rises about 29 per cent, and that is the layer setting the modelled
tropopause temperature and static stability.

Distinct from the a1o3/aco3/toffo3 shape issue that note already records: this
one is about gravity.

Reachable with no rebuild but blocked by the driver: __init__.py:2927-2935
accepts ozone as a dict with height and spread and writes BO3/CO3, while
run_exoplasim.py:1894 passes ozone=bool(atmosphere["ozone"]), forcing the
boolean path. Both files need a line.
acceptance_criteria: run_exoplasim passes the ozone dict; BO3 and CO3 are set on a pressure-equivalent basis and declared in config; the top-layer column share is reported.
close_reason:
Fixed in a5c469f0. ozone_height_m and ozone_spread_m are declared in config/planet.yaml at upstream's 20000 and 5000 scaled by (gascon/ga) over Earth's own (0.765592 at gascon 287.017 from the declared composition, ga 12.81), and configure_otherargs writes BO3 and CO3 from them on prepare and on every resume, checked by verify_staged_namelists. Top-layer column share reported in exoplasim/notes/ozone.md, measured by reproducing mko3's recursion on the model's own ten sigma levels: 0.4184 at Earth gravity, 0.6718 here at 20 km, and the pressure-equivalent placement returns every layer to the Earth-gravity value to machine precision. No Fortran change was needed.

Correction to the issue: __init__.py did NOT need a line. Earthlike.configure forwards **kwargs, and configure(), loadconfig() and exportcfg() all handle the ozone dict already. The driver was routed away from that dict deliberately -- it also rewrites A0O3, A1O3, ACO3 and TOFFO3, which would turn four more Earth constants into transcriptions in run_exoplasim.py, and those four are the separate profile-SHAPE question the ozone note records.

title: The SHTns and threaded-numerics gates apply one tolerance at every rung, derived at an unnamed one
description:
exoplasim/scripts/verify_threaded_numerics.sh:68-71 and verify_shtns_model.sh:57-60 carry identical bounds with no rung in them: TOL=1e-10, STEPS='1 2 5 10 20 40', BIRTH=1e-11, JUMP=1e4. Both take res as argument 2 and apply these unchanged at every rung.

The derivation at verify_threaded_numerics.sh:22-27 is explicitly a MEASUREMENT -- 3.2e-13 at one step, 1.4e-13 at twenty, 3.0e-10 at sixty -- and THE RUNG IT WAS MEASURED AT IS NEVER STATED. verify_shtns_model.sh:33-36 then says the bounds are taken unchanged from that check.

The amplification these bounds encode is a property of the spectrum, so it is rung-dependent by construction: a T170 run has eight times the truncation of T21 and reaches a given norm in fewer steps for entirely sound reasons. The gate therefore silently changes strictness with rung, toward false failures at the top of the ladder and false passes at the bottom.

world-y9m closed the T21 instance on the structure of the verdict rather than on the bound. This is the remaining half: whether one bound is defensible across the ladder at all.

Companion defect: _bed_guard.sh:24-52 checks KICK and SEED but never that the bed's grid matches the requested res, so a T42 bed with 'res T85' fails on an SRA header and reports only 'an arm produced no restart'.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md, and the gate scripts named above.
acceptance_criteria: Either the bounds are derived per rung, or one bound is shown to hold across the ladder with the rung it was measured at named. The bed guard refuses a bed whose grid does not match the requested rung.
notes:
PARTIAL, 2026-08-24. Companion defect FIXED: _bed_guard.sh gains require_bed_grid, which reads the bed's grid off its N???_surf_*.sra names and refuses one that is not the requested rung (and cross-checks the bed's executable name). All four gates that source the guard call it. Verified: the T42 bed passes as T42 and is refused as T63 and T85.

BIRTH: the arithmetic half is now DERIVED per rung. Every spectral restart record is an fc2sp analysis, a sum over the whole grid, so the rigorous upper bound on a regrouped float64 version of it, in any association order, is NLAT*NLON*eps -- 4.6e-13 at T21 to 2.9e-11 at T170, a factor of 64 across the ladder. Both gates compute it and REFUSE to run where the declared BIRTH sits below it, which the flat 1e-11 does from T106 up: those rungs now say why instead of failing every sound change. The birth SCALE is larger than the floor by rainmod.f90:92's record gain, (2*NLEV)^2 = 400 on the linear sigma grid, which is why the two measurements on record differ by ten (3.2e-13 for the grid-band change, 3.35e-12 for SHTns on the baseline bed).

REMAINING, and the whole of what is left: TOL = 1e-10 and JUMP = 1e4 are NOT derivable from arithmetic. Both encode the rate at which the model amplifies a last-bit difference, which is a property of the flow, and it is rung-dependent by construction. Two further defects in JUMP's current form, both arithmetic and both fixable once a rate exists: it is a per-SAMPLE ratio applied to STEPS='1 2 5 10 20 40', whose gaps run from 1 to 20 steps, so it is 20x looser on the last gap than the first; and verify_threaded_numerics.sh's header says 'roughly three decades every twenty steps' while its own quoted numbers (3.2e-13 at 1, 1.4e-13 at 20, 3.0e-10 at 60) are three decades over SIXTY.

THE EXPERIMENT: run the growth curve unchanged at three rungs on the same terrain and fit the per-step factor at each. Then TOL = BIRTH * g^20 and JUMP over a d-step gap = g^d, with g per rung, and the rung each was measured at recorded.

title: Three verification gates have bounds several decades from anything ever observed
description:
Recorded together because the pattern is one thing: a gate whose bound cannot be reached is not a gate, and claims elsewhere lean on these having passed.

  verify_threaded_numerics.sh:70-71, copied verbatim to verify_shtns_model.sh:59-60 -- BIRTH=1e-11 and
  JUMP=1e4, both hard rc=1 gates. The 50-line docstring above them derives the run LENGTHS carefully and
  neither bound. BIRTH sits about 30x above the measured birth-scale difference; the observed jump in the
  only run on record is 5.4x, four decades below the gate. This matters because
  shtns-viability.md:907 leans on 'the jump bound already tests the growth's shape' to argue about the
  1e-10 bound that world-y9m is open on.

  transform_exactness.py:57 -- ROUNDOFF = 1e-10, 'a control above this means the apparatus is wrong'.
  Its neighbour STORAGE = 1e-6 is derived from float32 output; this is not, anywhere. Double-precision
  round-off on a global mean over 64x128 is of order 1e-14, four decades below the gate. It decides
  whether the world-bxr energy-sink measurement is declared valid or void.

  corrk_cross_check.py:206-234 -- run_checks contains no threshold, no comparison and no raise. It is
  documented as 'The three things that could have failed, before any number is quoted' and the docstring
  claims it proves the division works to 0.2%. The 0.2% is nowhere in the code, and --checks returns at
  :309 before any number is computed, so the checks never run before a quote. Its siblings
  co2_overlap_589.py, trace_gas_band_model.py and cloud_band_weight.py all raise SystemExit; this one
  prints. It is the script that produced h2o_sw_level 1.127.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Two of the three fixed. transform_exactness ROUNDOFF is now roundoff_bound(nlat_fine, nlon_fine) = N * float64 eps, derived at the run's own rung; the two recorded controls sit three decades inside it. corrk_cross_check's run_checks now returns failures and raises, its three bounds are inequalities with no tolerance in them, and the checks run BEFORE the quote on every invocation rather than only under --checks, which returned early. Check 2 found a real 25 cm-1 hole between the bundle's IR and VI band sets carrying 0.00017 of solar flux, now computed and named. The third part -- verify_threaded_numerics.sh and verify_shtns_model.sh's BIRTH and JUMP -- is moved to world-2ic, which is the issue about those bounds not being derived per rung: BIRTH's arithmetic floor is now derived per rung and refuses from T106 up, and JUMP is a growth rate that is not derivable from arithmetic.

title: assess_convergence carries its own radiative feedback, 11% off the canonical slope it never imports
description:
assess_convergence.py:69: FEEDBACK_W_M2_K = 1.31, commented 'measured, not assumed', with no pointer to where. Measured 2026-08-24: lib/sensitivity.py's SLOPE_K_PER_FLUX_RATIO = 202.0 gives kelvin_per_w_m2(alpha=0.3) = 0.84812, i.e. an implied radiative damping of 1.1791 W/m2/K, which is the 1.18 that exoplasim/notes/forcing-bundle-predictions.md:370-372 uses and attributes to that module.

CLAUDE.md names lib/sensitivity.py as the one flux-to-kelvin conversion. assess_convergence.py does not import it. FEEDBACK_W_M2_K sets tau_expected, which sets the fallback remaining-offset that is judged against OFFSET_TOLERANCE_K = 0.15, so it is an input to a pass/fail verdict.

Beside it at :68, SLAB_HEAT_CAPACITY = _MLD * 1025.0 * 3990.0 is uncited, where the model's own values, cited to source in close_state_energy.py:67-68 and close_ocean_energy.py:121-122, are CRHOS = 1030.0 and CPS = 4180.0, which is 5.3% higher. The slab is modelling the model's mixed layer, so the model's constants are the right ones.

Route both through lib/, and fix forcing-bundle-predictions.md:368 which carries the same 1025/3990 pair.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Routed both through lib/. lib/sensitivity.py gains radiative_damping_w_m2_per_k (the reciprocal of kelvin_per_w_m2) and planetary_albedo_from_fluxes; assess_convergence reads rst/rsut and evaluates the damping at THIS RUN's own window albedo rather than a declared one. Slab takes close_state_energy.CRHOS/CPS, cited to oceanmod.f90. Measured on run_2b20e3324bb0: alpha 0.2703, damping 1.229 W/m2/K against 1.31, tau_expected 11.09 orbits against 9.89 -- widening the fallback bound only, which can refuse a run and never pass one. forcing-bundle-predictions.md CLIM-33 corrected.

title: config/planet.yaml's derived radiation scalings are hand-transcribed from artifacts and nothing compares them
description:
The generators print a value ('h2o_sw_weight for config/planet.yaml: ...') and a human retypes it into config. scripts/check_consistency.py never opens shortwave_band_weights.json or cloud_band_weight.json, and lib/provenance.py only lists the keys as inert or active. The values agree today (h2o_sw_weight 1.346, co2_sw_weight 1.510, cloud_absorption_scale 1.192, verified against their JSONs).

That route has already drifted twice: once in the model source (the CO2 shortwave fit) and once in the dust notes, where dust_forcing.py:139-141 and dust_optics.py:88-91 now read vegetation_albedo 0.165 and playa_clastic 0.23 from config while notes/dust.md:224-227, :325-328, :396-400 and analysis/dust_optics.json still say 0.18 and 0.40. Interpolating the note's own near-linear table, playa TOA net falls from +4.3 to roughly +0.8 W/m2 and the land half of the global mean from about +2.05 to +0.15, roughly 13x, against the 1.5 W/m2 reopening threshold at dust_forcing.py:472. dust_optics.json's 'warms_over': ['playa fill', ...] becomes false at 0.23, its critical_surface_albedo being 0.3001.

Have check_consistency.py compare each config scaling against the artifact that generated it, and regenerate the dust tables.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: check_consistency.py now compares h2o_sw_weight, co2_sw_weight and cloud_absorption_scale against shortwave_band_weights.json and cloud_band_weight.json at the tolerance the config's own written precision implies (half a ulp of the last decimal), each row naming its generator. All three agree today. analysis/dust_optics.json regenerated; its OPAC band-1 warms_over drops 'playa fill' at the config's 0.23, as predicted. The dust FORCING tables could not be regenerated -- dust_forcing.py needs a baseline climatology and config carries baseline_climatology: null -- so that half is world-zz6, and notes/dust.md now states the albedo set its tables were measured at.

title: The diffuse aerosol two-stream is bit-identical to the direct one, and the fork's new branch entrenches it
description:
radmod.f90:2661-2664 (band 1) and :2693-2696 (band 2). Verified that zaertf1s and zaerd1s are assigned and NEVER READ anywhere in the file: the only occurrences are the declarations at :2354 and :2356 and the assignments at :2661-2662 and :2679-2680. zaerd1s is built from zaertf1, the direct-beam path, and zaert1s and zaerr1s then divide by zaerd1, the direct-beam denominator.

So the diffuse-beam aerosol transmission and reflection are bit-identical to the direct-beam ones, the '!using zmu00 not zmu0!' comment at :2661 describes something that does not happen, and the factor-of-2 diffusivity the scattered stream should carry is absent.

Inherited from upstream, but the fork rewrote these exact lines for the per-cell arrays and preserved it, then wrote the new conservative-scattering branch to set zaert1s = zaert1 and zaerr1s = zaerr1 explicitly at :2681-2682, which makes the defect now read as deliberate.

Latent: NDUSTRAD=0 and no run has ever had aerosol radiation on. This is the path clim-40 and dust-13 switch on, so fix it before either.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason:
Fixed in 87bf526f. Both bands and both branches: the exact branch now builds zaerd1s/zaerd2s from zaertf1s/zaertf2s and divides zaert*s and zaerr*s by them, and the conservative branch takes b*tau/zmu00 for the diffuse beam instead of copying the direct answer. zaeru and ztemp depend only on ssa and the backscatter ratio and are correctly shared. Latent: the block is inside if (iaeron == 1), naerosp is 0 in every run, so no existing result moves. Needs a rebuild (rule 4).

What this settles for dust-13 and clim-40, and what it does not: the diffuse leg of the aerosol two-stream is now a diffuse leg, so switching either path on no longer silently doubles the diffuse extinction toward a low sun. It settles nothing else. dust-13 is still blocked on dust-11's measurement and on world-24v's aeroqlw, which is the longwave half of the l_aerorad pin's rationale. clim-40 is still blocked on aeolian/analysis/sea_salt_baseline.nc. Sea salt takes the CONSERVATIVE branch (ssa within 1e-5 of 1 in a double build), which is the branch whose diffuse leg was a verbatim copy, so clim-40 is the consumer this repair matters most for.

title: The energy fixer's controller state is not in the restart, so no run shorter than 80 steps corrects at all
description:
denergyfix, denergyacc, nenergyacc and nenergywin appear in no put_restart_* call (plasim.f90:902-1012) and no get_restart_* call (:1163-1260). Every segment therefore begins with denergyfix = 0 AND discards its first window, so the first 2*ntspd = 80 steps of every segment run with no correction and then step to the full value.

At 5850 steps per orbit that is 1.4% of a segment, worth roughly 0.011 W/m2 on the segment mean against a 0.05 W/m2 convergence criterion: small but one-signed, and it makes each segment's first two model days non-comparable to the rest.

The sharper consequence: any run shorter than 80 steps never applies a correction at all, which includes the 20-step SHTns verification gate. Nothing in that gate exercises the fixer.

Adjacent to world-5qy (naccuout and the output boundary) but a different object.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason:
denergyfix is in the restart: put_restart_real in epilog, get_restart_real in read_atmos_restart under the lowered nexcheck so a restart written before this reads as zero. A segment now starts on the previous segment's converged correction instead of at zero, which ends both halves of the finding -- the 2*ntspd uncorrected steps at every segment boundary, and any run shorter than one window applying no correction at all, the 20-step transform gates included.

The three window accumulators (denergyacc, nenergyacc, nenergywin) are DELIBERATELY NOT saved, and this is the part that is a decision rather than a fix. The first step out of a restart carries a start-up transient of order 250 W/m2 and the design discards the first window for exactly that reason; splicing a partial window across a segment boundary would feed that transient into the previous segment's average, which is the failure the windowing exists to avoid. A segment therefore applies the carried correction from step one and measures its own clean window before changing it.

restart_schema.py gains a controller-state semantic class and the policy for denergyfix, action TARGET across a CONVERSION: the correction is a heating rate reached against one truncation's own conversion defect and that defect is resolution-dependent, so a T21 correction is not the T85 one.

This does not settle the dry adiabatic sink and is not a tuning of it: it makes the correction continuous across segment boundaries, and the size of the defect is still denergyfix itself, still reported. Commit 446698e0.

title: compare_albedo_bracket's classifier threshold no longer separates the endmembers, so the bracket collapses
description:
compare_albedo_bracket.py:119: name = 'lithology' if mean > 0.256 else 'vegetated'. The docstring cites 'bare rock at 0.315 land-mean albedo and vegetated at 0.223'. Measured 2026-08-24: inputs/t42/albedo_report.json gives land_mean_bare_rock = 0.2483, below the threshold.

So every --mode lithology run on the current build classifies as 'vegetated', and since temps is a dict keyed on that name (:163) the two arms of a bracket collapse to one entry and the script reports 'cannot bracket'. This decides the verdict on the experiment that establishes whether the vegetation feedback is first-order.

Classify on the mode that was requested rather than on a threshold over the result.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: albedo_mode now takes the endmember from source_config.model.land_albedo_source on the run's own manifest, with no fallback; the land-mean albedo is still measured from the run's staged SRA and reported beside it. Instrument-versus-effect: the endmembers' separation survived (0.0824 against the 0.092 the 0.256 cut was placed in) but both moved BELOW the cut -- 0.2483 bare rock, 0.1659 vegetated -- so the classifier kept its resolution and lost its placement, which is why the fix is not a better cut point. Added a check that fails when two arms at one flux were handed the same land-mean albedo. Verified: the old rule returns 'vegetated' for both of today's endmembers; the new one returns 'lithology' for a lithology manifest and raises where the declaration is absent. Every run on disk declares vegetated, so 'cannot bracket' is now a true statement about the run set.

title: T31 is unbuildable, and the resolution ladder is spelled four more times outside lib/rungs.py
description:
CMakeLists.txt:57 hardcodes require_one_of(PLASIM_NLAT ... 32 64 96 128 160 192 256) and the help string at :31 repeats it. lib/rungs.py has T31: 48. build_model.py --res T31 resolves cleanly through rungs.RUNGS and then dies at cmake with FATAL_ERROR. It fails loudly rather than silently, but T31 is unbuildable and nothing says so.

This is the defect lib/rungs.py's own docstring says it was created to end (SPAT-2: 'four scripts each carried their own copy of the mapping, and two of the four were missing rungs the others had'). Four more private copies survive:
  cache_budget.py:32-40   omits T63 and T106, invents T213 (213,320,640) which is on no ladder anywhere,
                          and its comment claims 'as build_model.py resolves them' where build_model.py:58
                          is RESOLUTIONS = dict(rungs.RUNGS). --res uses choices=sorted(RESOLUTIONS), so
                          T63 is refused and T213 prints a per-die budget for a rung with no binary.
  verify_transform_roundtrip.sh:30-31   missing T63 and T106; its two sibling scripts already shell out
                          to rungs.geometry()
  stability_probe.py:63
  filter_timestep_matrix.py:103-104   which cites SPAT-2 in the comment directly above its local copy

Add 48 to the CMake list and route the four scripts through lib/rungs.py.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md

title: OMP_STACKSIZE and the stack ulimit exist in every gate and in none of the production run path
description:
Nine gate and bench scripts set OMP_STACKSIZE=512M with ulimit -s unlimited: verify_shtns_model.sh:140, verify_threaded_numerics.sh:137, verify_shared_determinism.sh:106, verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh:103, verify_omp_collectives.sh:63, profile_transforms.sh:48, profile_memory.sh:64 and :70, attribute_barrier_wait.sh:41, bench_ab.py:62. bench_ab.py:74-79 records that without the ulimit, at T127 the master overruns a 16 MB limit and segfaults.

Verified that the production launcher sets neither: __init__.py:522-523 builds _exec as 'OMP_NUM_THREADS=%d OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./' and grep for OMP_STACKSIZE or ulimit across __init__.py, run_exoplasim.py and continue_exoplasim.py returns nothing.

So the one setting that decides whether a threaded T127 or T170 run survives at all exists only in the instruments and not in the thing being measured, and the threading work is headed at those rungs. 512 is also a round number with no derivation: threads-instead-of-ranks.md:61 says only that the largest spilled local is 14 MB so it must be 'well above the 8 MB default'.

Set it in the launcher, and derive the value from the measured spill.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: run_exoplasim.py:prepare_thread_stack sets OMP_STACKSIZE and RLIMIT_STACK on the launching process before the model is constructed; continue_exoplasim.py imports and calls it, so every segment gets the same stack the prepare does. Both are set because they size different stacks: OMP_STACKSIZE for the non-master threads, the rlimit for the master, which bench_ab.py measured segfaulting on a 16 MB limit at T127. No-op for any other parmode. Recorded on the run manifest and on each segment record. VALUE PRESERVED at 512M, carried from the gates unchanged; deriving it needs a high-water stack measurement, which is world-p4b.

title: rainmod's precipitation-evaporation gamma is 0.01 at T21 and the note records the T42 branch as live
description:
rainmod.f90:31 declares gamma = 0.01 and :88-90 sets gamma = 0.007 only when NTRU==42 .and. NLEV==10. config/planet.yaml reads resolution: T21, layers: 10 (verified), so the branch does not fire and gamma is 0.01. exoplasim/notes/resolution-tuned-parameters.md:88 states the T42 branch 'which this project's configuration does hit'. The documentation no longer matches the code.

gamma is the fraction of the sub-saturation deficit that falling precipitation evaporates per timestep (rainmod.f90:2244-2246; it is divided by deltsec2, so it is not a rate and carries no time unit). It controls re-evaporation before precipitation reaches the ground, i.e. P-E over land directly. The two branches differ by 43%.

This is not a one-off: the resolution has flipped between T21 and T42 five times and resolution_timestep_minutes gives both rungs the same 45-minute step, so nothing compensated. A precipitation-physics constant has been oscillating under a key nothing connects to precipitation. Neither branch has a derivation upstream either.

Correct the note, and decide whether gamma should be resolution-keyed at all.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: The NTRU==42 .and. NLEV==10 gamma override is removed rather than re-keyed: gamma is a fraction of the deficit per TIMESTEP, both rungs run the same step, and a 43 per cent jump on a rung change makes every cross-rung comparison carry a precipitation-physics change. Every run is T21 and integrated 0.01, unchanged. resolution-tuned-parameters.md corrected: the T42 branch was never hit.

title: The vertical grid and model top come from an ExoPlaSim subclass default, and the audit records the wrong mechanism
description:
run_exoplasim.py instantiates exo.Earthlike and passes neither vtype nor modeltop (verified: grep returns nothing). Earthlike.configure (__init__.py:4409) supplies vtype=4 and modeltop=50.0, so NEQSIG=4 and PTOP=5000.0 Pa reach the model from a library subclass default. Neither has a key in config/planet.yaml.

exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md:558 says 'modeltop None, giving PTOP 5000 Pa, appropriate for a 1 bar atmosphere'. The premise is false: if modeltop were None then 'if modeltop:' at __init__.py:2960 is false, PTOP is never written, and the model uses plasimmod.f90:315's compiled ptop = 7500.0 Pa. The number is right only because Earthlike supplies 50 hPa. The same document opens 'configure() takes 102 parameters. We set 26; the rest sit at defaults' -- two of those defaults are the subclass's, and vtype is not mentioned in that audit at all.

vtype is not cosmetic: plasim.f90:1716-1725 (neqsig==4) rescales the sigma polynomial so the top half-level sits at ptop/psurf, while the neqsig==0 fallback at :1752 runs it unrescaled at sigma 0.0766. The two put the model top at 5000 Pa against 7660 Pa.

Separately, the sigma distribution itself (plasim.f90:1720, 0.75*zsk + 1.75*zsk**3 - 1.5*zsk**4) has three coefficients with no comment, no citation and no derivation anywhere in the tree.

Set both explicitly from config, and correct parameter-decisions.md.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: model.vertical_grid and model.model_top_hpa declare NEQSIG 4 and PTOP 5000 Pa, both scripts pass them, expected_namelist_keys covers them. Values unchanged. parameter-decisions.md corrected: modeltop was NOT None -- at None, configure's truthiness test fails, PTOP is never written and the model uses plasimmod's compiled 7500 Pa; 5000 came from Earthlike's own 50 hPa pin. The quartic's coefficients are derived where they are written.

title: A fourth copy of Earth's lapse rate, plus a 255 K Earth clamp, inside the postprocessor
description:
pyburn.py:217: RLAPSE = 0.0065, used at :2001, :2004, :2841 and :2844 to build sea-level pressure, code 151 / psl, which is in both REGULAR_CODES and SNAPSHOT_CODES (run_exoplasim.py:31,41).

notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md finding 3 (PHYS-12) swept three copies of 6.5 K/km and built lib/lapse.py to measure the rate from the model's own profile (7.8 K/km, clim-34). This is a fourth copy the sweep did not reach, and it is the only one that writes a field into every climatology. 6.5 against 7.8 is 20% low and the reduction error grows with terrain height. Nothing downstream currently reads psl, which is the only reason this is not already wrong in a quoted number.

alpha = gascon*RLAPSE/gravity does use the correct gravity, so the lapse rate is the whole defect.

Beside it, pyburn.py:2003 and :2843: tstar[tstar<255.0] = 0.5*(255+tstar[tstar<255.0]), ECMWF's cold-surface guard for the reduction, calibrated on Earth's surface temperature distribution. It fires wherever the bottom-level temperature is below 255 K, which on a 32-degree-obliquity world is a large fraction of land for much of the orbit, and warms tstar by up to (255-T)/2, i.e. 10 K at 235 K. Neither the threshold nor the halving is derived and there is no config key.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
notes:
CORRECTION to the spec this was applied from. The spec stated that p_exo.f90 is 'the planet module this project actually compiles'. It is not, and never was: plasim/CMakeLists.txt admitted only p_earth | p_mars, defaulted to p_earth, and build_model.py never passed -DPLASIM_PLANET, so every binary in vendor/exoplasim/build compiled p_earth.f90.o. p_exo.f90 has since been deleted entirely under world-58v/world-cmz.

This does not change the fix that was applied here -- dropping code 151 and naming RLAPSE_EARTH and PSL_COLD_GUARD_K_EARTH stands on its own -- but it changes the count. The live copies of Earth's lapse rate were pyburn.py and p_earth.f90, not pyburn.py and p_exo.f90; p_exo.f90's copy was never reachable. After this issue the one live copy is lib/lapse.py, and p_earth.f90:42 is Earth's own module, correct where it is.
close_reason: Applied on the coordination branch to batch F's spec. Code 151 dropped from REGULAR_CODES and SNAPSHOT_CODES (this project's lists, not a vendored default); RLAPSE -> RLAPSE_EARTH and the bare 255.0 -> PSL_COLD_GUARD_K_EARTH in pyburn.py, both documented as Earth defaults reachable only by an explicit request for 151. Verified before acting that RLAPSE and the guard are used at four sites and all four are the psl reduction, and that nothing in any component reads psl. Live copies of Earth's lapse rate go from two to one; p_exo.f90:43 remains as finding 17.

title: oceanmod carries Earth's radius, and it goes live under the horizontal-diffusion A/B
description:
oceanmod.f90:24: parameter(PLARAD=6.371E6), used at :1344 as zfac = hdiffk(jlev)/plarad/plarad. oceanmod uses resmod rather than pumamod, so this is its own parameter and shadows nothing.

Dormant today: NHDIFF=0 in every run namelist. It is filed anyway because config/planet.yaml says of that key that 'the keys exist to be BRACKETED in an A/B, not tuned into the baseline', which is clim-65. When that runs, hdiffo divides the requested hdiffk by Earth's radius squared on a planet of 1.20 radii, making the effective diffusivity 1.44x whatever the arm declares, with nothing in the output to say so. The bracket would come back wrong.

notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md:95 catches the identical parameter(radea=6.371E6) in cpl.f90, which is genuinely dead; this live twin two files away was missed.

Blocks clim-65.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
notes:
MERGED 2026-08-24 with world-st4, the resolution-divergence audit's independent finding of the same defect. Unique evidence from that bead, kept because this one lacked it:
- The mechanism is the metric, not just a scale factor: oceanmod's grid is angular (dlam = 2*pi/NLON, cphi and dphi in radians), so zfac = hdiffk/plarad/plarad at :1344 is what supplies the metric. An arm labelled 1000 m2/s behaves as 1440.
- CONSEQUENCE ALREADY BANKED: clim-16 was closed on a MEASURED 300/1000/3000 bracket, and those arms DID reach this code. The diffusivity LABELS on that result are therefore wrong by 1.44x. Its conservation claim does not depend on the coefficient's value and is untouched.
- Verified independently: grep over oceanmod.f90 returns exactly two occurrences, the declaration and the use.
Sources: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 10 and notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md.
close_reason: hdiffo took the planet radius from planet_nl by way of pumamod; oceanmod's parameter(PLARAD=6.371E6) is gone, oceanini aborts if nhdiff>0 with no radius and logs the radius it will use. LABEL vs VALUE: hdiffk's meaning is unchanged and its effect changes. An arm declaring 1000 m2/s now diffuses at 1000 m2/s where it diffused at (a_earth/a)**2 * 1000. So clim-16's measured 300/1000/3000 bracket was really 432/1440/4320 and its diffusivity labels are wrong by 1.44x; its conservation claim does not depend on the coefficient's value and is untouched. clim-65 must declare its arms in true units. Dormant in every run to date, NHDIFF=0 everywhere. Commit 893dbb1e.

title: The entire boundary-layer scheme runs at compiled Earth defaults that no run has ever named
description:
Verified that every run's fluxmod_namelist, seamod_namelist and surfmod_namelist are empty (&fluxmod_nl /END). So fluxmod.f90:25-30's constants are all live and unexamined:
  vdiff_lamm = 160.  the asymptotic mixing length in metres, the single number setting free-tropospheric
                     vertical diffusivity; zlamh = vdiff_lamm*SQRT(3*vdiff_d*0.5) at :783 derives the
                     heat version from it
  vdiff_b = vdiff_c = vdiff_d = 5.   the Louis stability-function coefficients, cited to 'ECHAM REPORT
                     218' at :243, which is a citation to a report and not a derivation, and none of the
                     three is separately justified
  zumin = 1.         documented as m/s but applied at :204 as a floor on u^2+v^2 and at :816 as a floor
                     on a wind DIFFERENCE: one constant, two quantities, one wrong unit in the comment
  ztscal = 250. (:762)  a reference temperature converting sigma to metres, no comment at all

Also fluxmod.f90:254-255's 0.0016 free-convection coefficient (Miller et al. 1992), on the zri <= 0 and dls < 1 branch, i.e. unstable ocean, which is most of the ocean most of the time. In the convective limit the bracket collapses to 0.0016*dth^(1/3)/(|U|*C_N), which is the convective velocity scale with g and the inversion height folded into the coefficient, and there is no ga in the expression. At 12.81 against 9.81 the coefficient is low by 1.306^(1/3) = 1.093, so free-convection latent and sensible exchange over calm unstable ocean is about 9% weak, over the warm ocean where the evaporation is.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Each of fluxmod's constants carries a statement of what it is and that the ECHAM value is kept because nothing here has measured a replacement. ztscal joins fluxmod_nl at the same 250 K. zumin is squared at the mktcoe site so it means m/s at both of its uses; at the declared 1 m/s nothing moves. THE FREE-CONVECTION COEFFICIENT MOVES THE SURFACE FLUXES: 0.0016 is Miller's with Earth's g folded in and w* goes as g^(1/3), so it was low by 1.093 and free-convection exchange over calm unstable ocean was about 9 per cent weak. fluxini derives it from ga.

title: Cloud liquid water, and therefore cloud optical depth, rests on two uncited Earth literals
description:
rainmod.f90:2005-2009: zzh(:) = 700.*ALOG(1.+dqvi(:)) and dql = 0.00021*EXP(-zzf/zzh)*gascon*dt/(sigma*dp). Two literals, no unit, no citation beyond a comment pointing at 'CCM3 description' fifteen lines earlier.

dql is the only thing setting cloud optical depth: radmod.f90:2465-2466 builds zlwp = 1000*dql*dp/ga*dsigma then ztau = 2.0*ALOG10(zlwp+1.5)**3.9, and radmod.f90:3270 uses it again for the longwave.

700. is an e-folding depth in Earth metres and is the one term in the expression with no ga and no gascon in it. It should scale with the atmospheric scale height, which here is 0.766 of Earth's. Gravity cancels everywhere except in that length (dqvi already carries 1/g), so a 0.766 scaling at a representative LWP of 100 g/m2 takes ztau from 30.8 to 22.6: a 27% cut in cloud optical depth, toward a darker planet. 0.00021 is a 0.21 g/m3 reference in-cloud liquid density with the same standing.

notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md finding 2 (PHYS-11) covers how a cloud REFLECTS. How much water the cloud is GIVEN has never been looked at. The Stephens fit that consumes it is equally uncited.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-24, from batch A's world-aee/world-bmf work: the per-layer liquid-water table in notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 15 is computed on sigma 0.038, 0.12, 0.21, 0.32, 0.44, 0.57, 0.70, 0.82, 0.92, 0.98. That is plasim.f90's neqsig == 0 fallback. Every run on record carries NEQSIG = 4 and PTOP = 5000, and run_2b20e3324bb0/MOST_DIAG.00001's vertical table reads 0.02500, 0.09372, 0.18812, 0.29717, 0.42058, 0.55432, 0.69069, 0.81826, 0.92191, 0.98282. The two agree from level 3 down; levels 1 and 2 are out by a third and a fifth, which is where the ratio is largest. Recompute the table on the rescaled set before quoting the 7.2x figure.
close_reason: Fixed in 1b9aa183. Both literals are rainmod_nl keys. clwhsc, the e-folding length coefficient, DERIVES from the model's own gascon and ga (700*(gascon/ga)/(287.0/9.80665), returning 700 at Earth's values) because it is a length and the heights it is measured against are already built that way; a positive namelist value overrides. clwref, the reference in-cloud liquid density, is exposed UNCHANGED at Kiehl's value: it is a condensate concentration with no gravity dependence, so no consistency argument moves it, and its bracket is world-8h6. This CHANGES RESULTS -- thinner high cloud, slightly thicker low cloud, simulated mean down on both the longwave trap and the shortwave reflection -- and is recorded as an unpriced row in forcing-bundle-predictions.md, because pricing needs a baseline climatology and config declares none. Needs a rebuild (rule 4).

title: aeroqlw is fork-added with no writer, and it is why l_aerorad stays pinned
description: aeroqlw is declared at radmod.f90:906, defined at :305 with default 0.0, and described by the fork's own comment at :286-292 as the thermal-IR absorption ratio for the interactive aerosol, the twin of dustqlw. dustqlw is written from the dust provenance file at run_exoplasim.py:1143; aeroqlw is written by nothing anywhere in the project. The emitted-dust path therefore has no longwave term available at all, structurally. run_exoplasim.py:1236-1243 pins l_aerorad = 0 and gives two reasons, and the other one is now stale: it cites radmod's apart 'which aero_ini never populates from the namelist', but aeromod.f90:277 does rad_apart = apart with a comment block at :265-276 describing exactly that fix. So the shortwave half of the rationale is fixed and the longwave half is this row. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: aeroqlw gets a writer or the interactive aerosol's longwave absence is declared. The l_aerorad pin's stated rationale matches the source it cites.
close_reason: Fixed in 0869eaa1. AEROQLW is derived in build_surface_dust.py beside DUSTQLW and recorded in the same provenance file (same ratio, and the same number here because dust_aerofile.py holds the mass extinction efficiency invariant under the rescale to apart, checked to 1e-9). run_exoplasim.py's pin becomes model.dust_emission_radiative, default false, so no existing run changes; when on it writes AEROQLW into radmod_namelist and raises rather than default, matching radini's refusal. The pin's stale half is corrected: aero_ini does hand apart across as rad_apart at aeromod.f90:277. Also corrected aeolian/README.md's claim that ndustrad and iaerint cannot both be on, which CLIM-39 removed.

title: The high-cadence stream writes no scalar record: hcadencesc has no caller
description: outmod.f90:2178-2201 defines hcadencesc and nothing calls it, commented or otherwise. This is a gap rather than only waste. The ordinary output path calls outsc beside outgp at plasim.f90:820-822 and the snapshot path calls snapshotsc beside snapshotgp at :784-785, but the high-cadence path at :806 and :815-816 calls only hcadencegp and hcadencesp. continue_exoplasim.py:469,578 does enable that stream for DUST-5, so the stream in use writes no scalar or time record. Separately, hcadencediag at outmod.f90:2320-2427 has exactly one call site and it is commented out at plasim.f90:807-809. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 8.
acceptance_criteria: Either the high-cadence stream writes its scalar record or the absence is declared and hcadencesc goes. What DUST-5 needs from that stream is stated either way.
close_reason: hcadencesc and hcadencediag deleted with the commented-out call that was hcadencediag's only call site. The absence of a scalar record is the decision and is stated at the high-cadence output block: the stream exists for DUST-5's gust distribution, HIGH_CADENCE_CODES is the winds, its time axis comes from the code 139 record hcadencegp already writes, and one orbit is 15 GB before anything is added.

title: The baseline climatology has no rung, and its grid is never checked against the configured one
description:
lib/paths.py:44-83 resolves climatology_path() from config's baseline_climatology key with a require_clean_io guard and NO grid guard. Changing model.resolution neither renames, invalidates, nor refuses the declared climatology.

Seven consumers then take the grid from the file and compute on whatever rung it happens to carry: scripts/error_budget.py:459, derive_design_flux.py:177, predict_ocean_terms.py:108, dust_forcing.py:353, shortwave_band_weights.py:111, lib/sensitivity.py:144, check_consistency.py:99.

error_budget.py MIXES rungs inside one product: its albedo half resolves through rungs.model_grid(config) at :186 while its hydrology half reads the climatology's own dimensions at :459, with no cross-check.

check_consistency.py:99 is the same defect inside the gate: land_sea_mask() is built from climatology_path(), so the coupling convention check at :503-508 can pass a T21 coupling for a T42 run.

build_surface_dust.py:215-217 and build_surface_soil_water.py:130-133 already do the right check and raise. It belongs in climatology_path where all the other callers would inherit it.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 11.
acceptance_criteria: climatology_path refuses a climatology whose grid does not match the configured rung, and error_budget can no longer combine two rungs in one product.
close_reason: lib/paths.py:require_configured_grid compares the climatology's lat/lon dimensions against lib/rungs.py:model_grid, and climatology_path applies it so all callers inherit it. build_surface_dust.py and build_surface_soil_water.py now call the shared expression rather than their own copies, which still covers the --climatology override that bypasses the resolver. error_budget's two halves can no longer disagree on rung, and its hydrology product records the grid. Verified both directions on the 32x64 bootstrap climatology.

title: nfixer gates nothing: the moisture fixer is unconditionally on
description: nfixer is declared in miscmod_nl at miscmod.f90:41, defaults to 1 at :10, and is commented 'switch for negative humidity fix (1/0 : on/off)'. It is tested nowhere in the tree: miscstep calls fixer unconditionally at miscmod.f90:93. fixer at :132-198 borrows moisture between columns to remove negative humidity, so a mass redistribution term documented as optional is in fact always on, and setting NFIXER=0 is silently ignored. Not fork damage: the independently vendored PlaSim at vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim/src/fortran/miscmod.f90:91 has the same unconditional call. Bears on the closure work in exoplasim/scripts/close_*_energy.py, which accounts for mass and energy terms this one is not currently named in. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: Either nfixer gates the call or the key stops claiming to. Whichever way it goes, the fixer's mass redistribution is named in the closure accounting.
close_reason: nfixer removed rather than wired up: negative specific humidity is not a state the model may integrate, so 'off' was never a configuration. The fixer's mass redistribution is recorded at the routine -- it conserves the column integral except where the global deficit exceeds the global surplus, where it is a sink -- and close_state_energy.py names it against its vapour reservoir.

title: A per-timestep legmod call survived CLIM-64, inside mkdheat's energy block
description: CLIM-64 closed on the finding that mkdheat was the last hot legmod caller. mkdheat still calls legmod's sp2fl at plasim.f90:5092 and :5106, inside if(nenergy > 0) and outside every nshtns branch. The comment above that block describes it as off by default; config/planet.yaml:502 declares energy_diagnostics: true, and run_2b20e3324bb0/plasim_namelist:3 records NENERGY = 1. The block therefore runs every timestep of every production run and legmod's Legendre loops run with it, alongside dv2uv at plasim.f90:3578 and :3587 and the sp2fc that sp2fl calls. The rest of legmod is correctly retained: the axis is nshtns, a runtime key, not the parmode, and verify_shtns_model.sh runs NSHTNS=1 against NSHTNS=0 on one omp binary. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 4.
acceptance_criteria: The nenergy diagnostic path either goes through the SHTns wrappers or is measured and declared as a deliberate legmod caller. The misleading 'off by default' comment no longer stands. Any change here is rule 4.
close_reason: mkdheat's two sp2fl calls inside if(nenergy > 0) now take sh_sp2gp into hddt_g under nshtns == 1, with the wrapper's barriers, and the 'off by default' comment is gone. Filed world-3ya for the thirteen more live per-timestep legmod transforms in spectrala and spectrald that CLIM-64 also missed; they need shared _g destinations first, which is why mkdheat could move and they could not.

title: cpl_stub's signatures have drifted from the oceanmod call sites
description: cpl_stub.f90 is compiled (CMakeLists.txt:183) and cpl.f90 is not. cpl_stub.f90:5 declares clsgini with six arguments; cpl.f90:136 declares it with eight; oceanmod.f90:345 calls it with eight. The count is not the whole defect: the call passes the integers nlsg and ngui into positions four and five, where the stub declares pslm(kxa,kya), a real array. clsgstep is the same, ten passed at oceanmod.f90:466 against eight declared at cpl_stub.f90:19. These are non-module externals with no explicit interface, so nothing diagnoses it and the link succeeds. Setting NLSG=1 on this build corrupts the stack rather than coupling an ocean. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 1c.
acceptance_criteria: Either the stub matches the call sites, or the nlsg branch and the stub go together. A build in which NLSG=1 silently corrupts the stack is not left standing.
close_reason: cpl_stub.f90 rewritten: clsgini, clsgstep and clsgstop now declare exactly what cpl.f90 declares and what oceanmod.f90 and plasim_dummy.f90 pass, and each calls mpabort. A build linked against the stub has no LSG in it, so NLSG>0 on it is a configuration that cannot be honoured; the previous no-op also returned pfldo untouched, which oceanstep then scattered from an uninitialised local. Unchanged wherever NLSG=0, which is every run. Verified by grep over the whole tree: the only other call sites are plasim_dummy.f90 (not compiled), and they match too. Commit cb78c7cf.

title: configure(orography=) writes OROSCALE, which no namelist declares
description: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py:2739 and :3495 write OROSCALE into landmod_namelist. oroscale is a module variable at plasimmod.f90:965, used at glaciermod.f90:170,241,342 and surfmod.f90:429, but it appears in no namelist declaration in any of the 57 source files; landmod_nl at landmod.f90:168-173 does not carry it. landmod.f90:215 is a bare read(12,landmod_nl) with no iostat, so an unrecognised name aborts the run. The orography scaling knob is unreachable from any namelist and the documented API that sets it would stop the model. Latent only because this project's harness never passes orography=. NDESERT has the same shape on one branch: __init__.py:3719 writes it to plasim_namelist, which declares it at plasim.f90:1410, while :3729 writes it to landmod_namelist, which does not. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 1b.
acceptance_criteria: Either oroscale enters landmod_nl and the API works, or the API stops offering a knob the model cannot read. NDESERT is written to one group on both branches. Decided rather than left latent.
close_reason: oroscale enters planet_nl in all three planet modules and the API writes OROSCALE to planet_namelist. planet_nl is the only group that can hold it: every reader runs inside surface_ini and planet_ini is the only namelist read before that. NDESERT now goes to plasim_namelist on both branches; the desertplanet=False arm wrote landmod_namelist, which does not declare it, so turning it off aborted the run.

title: Extend the SPAT-2 rung lint to shell scripts and to rung-to-dimension tables
description:
The lint that closed SPAT-2 does not reach most of the surviving ladder copies.

scripts/smoke_test.py:995 builds its file list with d.glob('*.py'), so every shell offender is invisible: verify_transform_roundtrip.sh:29-33 (a case over six rungs, refusing T63 and T106 as unknown), verify_gauss_weights.sh:54 (five bare latitude counts), verify_fold_indexing.sh:33, verify_fold_exactness.sh:28, thread_count_sweep.sh:19-20.

Its path test at :867 recognises .sra, .nc, .json and .rest, so '.x' escapes it: most_plasim_t21_l10_p16.x would pass the lint even inside a .py file.

And check_no_rung_literal_in_a_path only fires on PATH-shaped strings, so a dict mapping rung to dimensions is out of scope by design. That is what the remaining copies are: stability_probe.py:63, filter_timestep_matrix.py:103, verify_latitude_pairing.py:44-48, archive_builds.py:56-57.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 10.
acceptance_criteria: The lint scans shell scripts, recognises .x as an artifact extension, and rejects a rung-to-dimension table outside lib/rungs.py. Every copy named above is either removed or exempted by name with its reason.
notes: MERGED 2026-08-24 with world-b3s, the opaque-constants audit's bundled version of the same work. That bead named four surviving ladder copies -- cache_budget.py:32-40, verify_transform_roundtrip.sh:30-31, stability_probe.py:63 and filter_timestep_matrix.py:103-104 -- and this bead plus world-qjq and world-ajx already cover all four with a finer decomposition, so b3s was superseded rather than kept. Note filter_timestep_matrix.py:103 cites SPAT-2 in the comment directly above its own local copy.
close_reason: Both rung lints now scan *.sh, the path lint recognises .x, and check_no_rung_table_outside_rungs is new: it catches a rung literal beside its own dimensions (twice in a file) and a line carrying three or more of the ladder's bare latitude counts. Fixed by routing through lib/rungs.py: verify_transform_roundtrip.sh, verify_gauss_weights.sh, filter_timestep_matrix.py; make_profile_bed.py's help string no longer names a rung. Exempted by name with reasons: verify_fold_indexing.sh and verify_fold_exactness.sh (unrunnable, paths point at a gone worktree -- world-en0), restart_convert_selftest.py (source-target grid pairs, no rung names). RUNG_OWNER became a mapping so every exemption states its reason. cache_budget.py's table is the one remaining hit and is NOT exempted: world-qjq already removed it in another fan-out worktree, so the lint goes green on merge.

title: cache_budget offers T213, which is not a ladder rung, and drops two that are
description:
exoplasim/scripts/cache_budget.py:33-39 carries a private RESOLUTIONS table of (NTRU, NLAT, NLON) whose header comment claims it is 'as build_model.py resolves them'. That is false: build_model.py:58 is 'RESOLUTIONS = dict(rungs.RUNGS)'.

It diverges from lib/rungs.py in both directions. It is MISSING T63 (96) and T106 (160), and it ADDS T213 (320, 640), which is not a rung and cannot be built. --res is choices=sorted(RESOLUTIONS) at :92, so '--res T213' is accepted and prints a plausible 32-MB-budget verdict for a configuration that cannot exist, quotable as a real one. '--res T63' errors as though T63 were invalid.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 10.
acceptance_criteria: cache_budget takes its geometry from lib/rungs.py. T213 is no longer offered and T63 and T106 are accepted.
close_reason: Fixed: cache_budget imports lib/rungs.py; --res choices are the eight ladder rungs, geometry comes from rungs.geometry. T213 gone, T63 and T106 accepted, T170 numbers unchanged.

title: The Lander-Hoskins filter's critical wavenumber is absolute and set for T21
description:
plasimmod.f90:452 is 'real :: landhoskn0 = 15.0', and its own comment states the assumption: the default gives 0.1 at n=N for T21. The filter at legmod.f90:184-186 applies exp(-(n(n+1)/(landhoskn0(landhoskn0+1)))^2), so it confines the tail at T21 and removes most of the RESOLVED spectrum at T85 and above.

The neighbouring exponential filter at legmod.f90:169-193 normalises by NTRU and has no such problem, which is what makes the omission legible rather than a judgement call. Cesaro and Riesz-2 likewise normalise by NTP1.

Distinct from world-ys9, which is the hyperdiffusion. This is the physics filter's critical wavenumber, and the filter is what actually damps this model.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 7.
acceptance_criteria: landhoskn0 is expressed as a fraction of the truncation the way cutoff_fraction already is, or its T21 anchoring is declared and its effect at each ladder rung is measured.
close_reason: Fixed: legini derives the critical wavenumber as landhoskn0 * NTRU / zhoskref, with zhoskref = 21.0 declared as the reference truncation. T21 unchanged bit for bit; no current run uses NFILTER 3. shtnsmod inherits it through legmod's fsp.

title: Global-mean diagnostics are unweighted arithmetic means over a Gaussian grid
description:
plasim.f90:2822-2830 forms mean 2m temperature, convective and large-scale precipitation, evaporation and outgoing longwave as sum(zgp)/(NLON*NLAT), with no Gaussian weight anywhere in the block.

On an unequally spaced Gaussian grid this over-weights high latitudes, and the size of the error is a function of NLAT. So the same simulated climate reports a different global mean T2m, precipitation, evaporation and OLR at two rungs from quadrature alone -- which makes these diagnostics unusable for exactly the resolution comparison SPAT-8 intends.

The convention exists and this path departs from it: icemod.f90:2002 uses xgw and utilities.f90:38 builds dglobe from the actual latitude bounds. Same class, diagnostic only: landmod.f90:144 reports land fraction as an unweighted cell count, and surfmod.f90:427 and glaciermod.f90:140 report means as sum(...)/NUGP.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 7.
acceptance_criteria: The global means in the status stream carry Gaussian weights, or every consumer of them is shown to be rung-internal so the quadrature error cannot enter a cross-rung comparison.
close_reason: The four global means in gridpointa are area-weighted, summed locally and reduced, which also drops four full-globe gathers per diagnostic step. Two helpers in plasim.f90 do the weighting in one place: gpareamean for a distributed field, ugpmean for a gathered one. ncountsea's land and sea percentages and the fifteen 'Mean:' orography and icesheet prints in glaciermod and surfmod follow. NO PUBLISHED NUMBER MOVES: the only reader of t2mean, precip, evap and olr is energy(), which passes them to guiput, and CMakeLists compiles guimod_stub.f90 whose guiput is a bodyless return.

title: Ocean horizontal diffusion uses Earth's radius, so its coefficient is 1.44x its label
description:
oceanmod.f90:24 is parameter(PLARAD=6.371E6). The module uses only resmod, NOT pumamod, so this is the ocean's only definition of the planet radius and the configured value never reaches it. Verified: grep over oceanmod.f90 returns exactly two occurrences, the declaration and the use.

The grid there is angular -- dlam is 2*pi/NLON, with cphi and dphi in radians -- so zfac = hdiffk/plarad/plarad at :1344 is what supplies the metric. At the declared 1.20 Earth radii the simulated ocean's horizontal heat diffusion runs 1.20^2 = 1.44 times stronger than the coefficient it is given: an arm labelled 1000 m2/s behaves as 1440.

nhdiff defaults to 0 in oceanmod and config/planet.yaml sets horizontal_diffusion: false, so no current run reaches it. clim-16 was closed on a MEASURED 300/1000/3000 bracket and those arms did reach it, so the diffusivity labels on that result are what is affected. Its conservation claim does not depend on the coefficient's value and is untouched.

Not a resolution finding. Found during the resolution sweep and belongs to the family in notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md, whose clean list does not cover oceanmod.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 12.
acceptance_criteria: The ocean's horizontal diffusion takes the configured planet radius. clim-16's bracket is restated against the corrected coefficient, or its labels are recorded as having been 1.44x.

title: get_surf_array reads the SRA header and discards it, and the default land mask is all land
description:
surfmod.f90:174-176 handles an absent surface file by writing '* Init <name> [code = NNNN] internally *', leaving kread at 0, and returning. mpsurfgp then leaves the array untouched and the module default stands. There is no error path.

The default that matters is plasimmod.f90:710, dls = 1.: the land/sea mask is ALL LAND. With doro at 0.0 the model integrates a flat, entirely continental planet, announced only in a line indistinguishable from the thirteen other codes a healthy run initialises internally.

The same routine reads the eight-word SRA header into ih(:) at :134 and :141 and never compares ih(5), ih(6) against NLON, NLAT. The header carrying the grid is read and thrown away, so an oversized file is silently truncated by the list-directed read.

surface_ini at :303-362 compounds it: any surface.sra is re-split and relabelled under the RUNNING model's NLAT, so a T21 field becomes N064_surf_*.sra with no check.

The project's read_sra compares the whole header and refuses, and surface_field_report raises on a missing intended code, which is what makes this latent rather than live.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 3.
acceptance_criteria: get_surf_array compares ih(5), ih(6) against NLON, NLAT and calls mpabort on a mismatch. A wrong-grid surface file is refused at startup rather than integrated on.
close_reason: Fixed: check_surf_header compares ih(5)/ih(6) against NLON/NLAT at both get_surf_array read sites and calls mpabort naming both grids. Also closes the surface_ini re-split path, whose output copies the donor header words. Every shipped and staged file passes. The dls=1. all-land default is in plasimmod.f90, batch A's file, and is untouched.

title: fft991mod's planner state is not threadprivate, and it is the module T63 and T106 select
description:
fftmod.f90:26 carries '!$omp threadprivate(lastn,nallowed,trigs)', added by this fork so a thread owns what a rank owned. fft991mod.f90 carries no threadprivate directive at all, while holding the same mutable planner state: lastn, ifax(10) and the allocatable trigs (fft991mod.f90:9-24).

fft991mod.f90:38-43 does its lazy init on that shared state, deallocating and reallocating trigs and rerunning set99 whenever n changes, while other threads are already inside fft991 reading it.

build_model.py:168 selects fft991mod for exactly T63 and T106, and this project builds parmode omp. So those two rungs, and only those two, put every thread into a race over the planner. Symptoms range from a wrong orography spectrum to a use-after-free.

Not currently reachable: neither rung is in rebuild_binaries.MATRIX. It is armed by the act of adding one.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 5.
acceptance_criteria: fft991mod carries the same threadprivate treatment as fftmod, or T63 and T106 are refused on the threaded build with a named error rather than racing.
close_reason: Fixed: !$omp threadprivate(lastn,nallowed,ifax,trigs) added to fft991mod, mirroring fftmod and extended to ifax. Per-thread footprint under 2.7 kB at T106, under 45 kB for 16 threads. Inert without -fopenmp.
