title: verify_shtns_model misses its 20-step tolerance on cloud cover, at four threads and at sixteen
description:
The model-level SHTns gate FAILS on this build. Run at T21 on a bed cut from run_2b20e3324bb0, at both thread counts:

  4 threads:  1 step PASS; 20 steps FAIL, dcc at 2.719e-10 against a 1e-10 tolerance
  16 threads: 1 step PASS; 20 steps FAIL, dcc at 3.936e-10

EXACTLY ONE RECORD of 199 misses, and it is dcc both times. Everything else is identical or at rounding scale.

EVERY OTHER DECLARED CRITERION PASSES. Born at 3.38e-12 against a birth bound of 1e-11, so the difference is at rounding scale where it starts. Largest jump between adjacent samples 5.4x against a bound of 1e4, so it grows smoothly rather than stepping. The SHTns arm is BIT IDENTICAL over four runs, so SHT_QUICK_INIT is doing its job and no timing race is involved. The filter control is rejected, so the check has teeth.

NOT A THREAD-COUNT EFFECT. The birth-scale difference is 3.380e-12 at four threads and 3.349e-12 at sixteen -- the same number. Reduction regrouping would scale with the count; this does not, so what is being seen is the transform difference itself rather than the sum order.

WHAT THE NUMBER IS PHYSICALLY. At 20 steps the worst dcc difference is 8.8e-11 in CLOUD FRACTION, a field that runs 0 to 1 with an RMS of 0.325. The gate divides by that RMS, which is what turns eleven significant figures of agreement into 2.7e-10 against a 1e-10 tolerance.

WHAT TO SETTLE, and it is not to loosen the tolerance after seeing the result -- a criterion chosen after the run it judges is not a criterion. Either the 1e-10 bound at 20 steps is wrong for a field whose RMS is a third and whose values saturate at 0 and 1, in which case the bound needs deriving rather than adjusting; or dcc genuinely amplifies faster than the other 198 records and the reason is worth knowing. exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md records an earlier run of this gate agreeing at rounding scale at 20 steps, on a different bed, so bed dependence is the first thing to separate out.

Found while validating that the threaded SHTns path is what runs, after a full rebuild from a cleared object cache reproduced all five binaries bit for bit.

Source: exoplasim/scripts/verify_shtns_model.sh, exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md
notes:
ANSWERED. Bed dependence is the whole of it, and dcc's gain is the mechanism.

MEASURED 2026-08-24, T21, on a full rebuild from a cleared object cache:
  bed from run_2b20e3324bb0 (85-orbit baseline): born 3.35e-12, 3.94e-10 at 20 steps -> FAIL
  bed from run_9df7ffa14256 (cold start, 1 orbit): born 5.88e-14, 2.00e-11 at 20 steps -> PASS
Same build, same thread count. Every other declared criterion passes on both beds: inside the 1e-11 birth bound, no jump above 5.4x against 1e4, SHTns bit-identical over four runs, filter control rejected.

ONE RECORD, AND IT HAS A GAIN. At 20 steps on the failing bed dcc is 3.94e-10 and the next record that is not its own accumulator is 47x below. rainmod.f90:1977 computes cloud fraction as zwfac*AMAX1(0,(zrh-rcrit)/(1-rcrit))**2 with rcrit = MAX(0.85, MAX(sigma,1-sigma)) at rainmod.f90:92, so d(cloud)/d(RH) carries 1/(1-rcrit)^2 -- 44 at the eight interior levels, 400 at top and bottom. Predicted from those constants: 1.7e-10 to 1.7e-9. Observed 3.94e-10.

The clamps matter: amplification acts only between AMAX1's zero and AMIN1's cap. The failing bed holds 32.1% of its cloud field between them, the passing bed 21.1% -- a factor of 1.5 of the 57x seed difference, the rest being an equilibrated state's small-scale structure.

WHAT THE BOUND IS. Not bed-independent. Taken unchanged from verify_threaded_numerics.sh, which calibrated it against a difference born at 3.2e-13; the baseline bed's is born ten times larger, so the same growth crosses the same bound sooner. It tests seed AND growth while the birth bound already tests the seed and the jump bound the growth's shape.

NOT IMPLICATED: the transform. At one step on the failing bed every spectral record is bit identical between the arms and the largest difference outside dcc is 1.5e-13.

WHAT REMAINS is one decision, and it must be taken before a run rather than after this one: whether the 20-step verdict should rest on decades-since-birth, which the script's own stated physics gives as three decades per twenty steps and which both beds pass (2.07 and 2.53). The gate now REPORTS that column; its verdict is unchanged.

Evidence: exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md, section 'The model gate's 20-step tolerance is bed-dependent, and dcc is why'.
close_reason: Option C: the verdict rests on integrated state, diagnostics are reported as advisory and not counted, the list comes from restart_schema. Both beds pass, control still rejected, worst counted record 5x inside the bound. The curve keeps every record so birth and jump keep the sensitive detector

title: A restart template's own state reaches every cell a moved coastline creates, and nothing says how far it may be from the donor
description:
A conversion across a resolution change leaves target cells with no source of their own class: at T21 to T42, 124 land and 132 ocean out of 8,192, which are the cells the coastline moved into. They take the target template's value by the converter's declared fallback, and that value is whatever state the template's run happened to be in.

MEASURED, and it is the dominant term. The T42 template used for the world-eyb measurement was a one-orbit cold start carrying 188 times the donor's sea-ice volume -- mean cover 0.114 against 0.0015 -- and 103% of the converted state's sea-ice volume residual is that template's ice arriving on those coastline cells. Soil water is 52% fallback-explained, land snow 104%.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE DERIVED-RECORD PROBLEM world-eyb refused. Those five records are rebuilt by the model in one timestep. A prognostic reservoir dropped onto a coastline cell is not: it is the state that cell integrates from.

WHAT TO SETTLE. Whether a template must be cut from a run within a declared distance of the donor's state, and what that distance is measured in; or whether the fallback should be something better than the template -- the nearest valid source cell of the same class is the alternative the specification names and the converter does not implement. Either way convert_restart should refuse or warn on a template whose state is far from the donor's, rather than reporting the consequence afterwards.

The report already carries the evidence per record: fallback_cells, cells_outside_domain, from_template_fallback and residual_explained_by_fallback.

Source: exoplasim/notes/restart-resolution-precision-converter.md, exoplasim/scripts/convert_restart.py, world-eyb

title: stability_probe takes its executable from a run directory, so a rebuild does not reach it
description:
exoplasim/scripts/stability_probe.py:96-107 selects its binary by globbing a TEMPLATE RUN DIRECTORY, and a run directory holds a snapshot taken when that run was staged. Nothing compares it against the build tree or against exoplasim/binary_manifest.json, so after any rebuild the probe silently integrates an older executable and reports its numbers as current.

OBSERVED 2026-08-24 and it cost a wasted cycle. rebuild_binaries.py had rebuilt all five configurations from patched radmod source and --verify reported 'all 5 binaries current'; the probe then ran the template's older copy and printed the pre-repair surface albedos, which read as the patch having failed to take. The stale executable's sha was 88d3ec09 against the manifest's e0830f77 for the same configuration name.

THIS IS THE NEIGHBOUR OF CLAUDE.md RULE 4 RATHER THAN AN INSTANCE OF IT. Rule 4 says a rebuild refreshes only the configuration you ran, so the others go stale silently. Here the rebuild was complete and correct and a CONSUMER read a copy the manifest does not track. Every other consumer that stages binaries from a run or template directory has the same exposure, so the audit is 'who copies an executable, and does any of them check its sha', not this one script.

The fix is cheap because the instrument exists: binary_manifest.json records a sha256 for every executable it builds, so a consumer can compare before running and refuse, or restage from the build tree.
design:
Prefer refusing to running stale. A probe that quietly reports the wrong model's numbers is worse than one that stops and says the binary is behind the manifest, because the numbers look ordinary either way -- which is failure-modes class 34's shape.

Decide whether the probe should restage from the build tree automatically or refuse and tell the caller to rebuild. Restaging is friendlier; refusing is more honest about what was measured. Do not do both silently.
acceptance_criteria: A probe run against a deliberately stale template stops with the two shas named, rather than producing numbers. And the sweep for other executable-copying consumers is done and recorded, so this closes a class rather than one script.

title: radmod normalises a low-resolution numerator by a high-resolution denominator, and band 1 is 1.47 percent dark
description:
radmod.f90's star-weighted surface albedos divide two integrals that do not cover the same interval, so the quotient is not a reflectance.

The numerator, a1 and a2, sums bb3(k)*blend(k) over 'wavelengths' -- the 965-point grid the ECOSTRESS blends live on, running 0.34 to 14.01 um. The denominator, z1 and z2 at radmod.f90:519-545, sums bb1 and bb2 over wv1 and wv2 -- the 2048-point hi-res grid, with band 1 running from the file's start and everything below minwavel zeroed, band 2 running to 100 um, and the band-edge interval added to z1. Line 609's zdenom1 = 0.01/z1 then divides the one by the other.

This is CLAUDE.md rule 3's class of defect on WAVELENGTH rather than longitude: two labellings of one axis combined without reconciliation. It is the same family as the Rayleigh reference grid mismatch already recorded in this module, which is the second instance in one file.

MEASURED, analysis/ice_albedo.json: band 1 is low by 1.47 percent RELATIVE on every affected surface, which is the signature of one wrong denominator rather than five separate faults. Absolute band-1 error runs -0.0144 on maximum snow, -0.0131 on maximum sea ice, -0.0112 on glacier ice, -0.0093 on minimum sea ice and -0.0075 on minimum snow; broadband -0.0057 to -0.0030. Band 2 escapes at 3.3e-4 because this star has little flux beyond the blend grid's 14.01 um, which is why the fault was invisible.

The sign matters and is the opposite of what was assumed: every surface is too DARK, so the simulation's ice-albedo feedback is slightly STRONGER than a consistent integration gives.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE ICE SURFACES. The same zdenom1 and zdenom2 normalise every surface radmod weights in that block, ground and ocean included, so this row covers all of them and analysis/ice_albedo.py measures only the five it was written for.
design:
Two self-consistent repairs, and the choice is not obvious. Compute z1 and z2 from bb3 on the 965 grid, which is minimal and matches the numerator but discards minwavel and the 0.316 to 0.34 um interval. Or interpolate the blends onto the 2048 grid and integrate the numerator there, which keeps minwavel and the full band-1 range but resamples measured reflectance. Price both and state which the model should carry; do not average them.

This is a change under vendor/exoplasim, so CLAUDE.md rule 4 applies: rebuild every binary in the matrix and verify against the source sha.

Physics is not a knob. The repair changes the simulation's albedos and therefore its climate, and the correct term is worth having whichever way the comparison moves.
acceptance_criteria: analysis/ice_albedo.py's model_bands column reproduces the repaired model's printed 'Finalized Albedos' to the same machine precision it currently reproduces the defective ones, and band1_error goes to zero by construction rather than by adjustment. The RECORDED block is updated from a post-repair run in the same commit, so the check keeps a right answer rather than being disabled.
notes: THE INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTS, 2026-08-24, so this row starts from a measurement rather than a survey. analysis/ice_albedo.py is registered as the ice_albedo step and reproduces radmod's current arithmetic to machine precision against the 'Finalized Albedos' block recorded from run_2b20e3324bb0. Its RECORDED table is the acceptance test for the repair: after the fix it must reproduce the NEW printed values to the same precision, with band1_error zero by construction, and the table updated from a post-repair run in the same commit so the check keeps a right answer instead of being disabled.
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-08-24. radmod.f90 now accumulates zout1 and zout2, the band flux lying outside the 965-point blend grid, and adds each blend's endpoint value across that gap before dividing by z1 and z2, so numerator and denominator cover one interval. All EIGHT surfaces the block weights are covered -- dsnowalb, dsnowalbmn, dsnowalbmx, dicealbmn, dicealbmx, dglacalbmn, dgroundalb and doceanalb -- because one zdenom pair normalises them all. THE REPAIR EXTENDS THE NUMERATOR rather than shrinking the denominator, and the reason is not arbitrary: an albedo multiplies the flux over a whole band, so it must be the reflectance averaged over that whole band. Normalising by the blend grid's own flux would average over a sub-interval and apply the result to all of it. The two self-consistent repairs differ by at most 0.001, on ground, where holding an endpoint value across the gap is least representative, and analysis/ice_albedo.json reports that residual so the choice stays priced. VERIFIED AGAINST THE COMPILED MODEL, not against the source: all five binaries rebuilt per rule 4 and --verify clean, then a two-step T21 integration read back for its own 'Finalized Albedos'. Sixteen numbers, every one matching the prediction to six decimals. Band 1 moves +0.0146 on maximum snow, +0.0133 on maximum sea ice, +0.0114 on glacier ice, +0.0095 on minimum sea ice, +0.0076 on minimum snow, +0.0019 on ground and +0.0011 on ocean; band 2 by at most 6e-5. EVERY SIMULATED SURFACE IS NOW BRIGHTER, so this WEAKENS the ice-albedo feedback rather than strengthening it -- the opposite direction to what the overturned PHYS-14 inferred. Physics is not a knob: the correct term is worth having whichever way it moves an agreement. analysis/ice_albedo.py's RECORDED block now holds the post-repair values and still refuses unless it reproduces them, so the check kept a right answer rather than being disabled. notes/external-model-survey.md section 11f.

title: A run does not end on an output boundary, so the energy diagnostics restart mid-window while naccuout does not
description:
outmod.f90:2543 justifies leaving adenergy and adener3d out of the restart with the claim that 'outreset runs immediately after the write and a run always ends on an output boundary, so an accumulation window never straddles a restart'. THE CLAIM IS FALSE and the artifact says so: with NSTPW = 160, run_9df7ffa14256's restart carries naccuout = 90 and run_2b20e3324bb0's carries 26. Eighty-two accumulator records in a freshly written restart are at neither zero nor their reset sentinel.

WHAT THAT COSTS. Every other accumulator IS carried across the restart and correctly continues its partial window. adenergy and adener3d are not, so on the first output record after every resume they hold what accumulated since the resume while naccuout counts from before it: the record is divided by 160 having summed maybe 70 steps. nenergy is on in this configuration -- denergy01 to denergy28 are in the output -- so this is live, not dormant.

It is CLIM-31's failure mode by another route. CLIM-31 was a seeded run opening on a donor's partial window and it was found the same way, on a field that cannot vary.

TWO ROUTES, and the choice is the work. Carry them in the restart, which the comment argues against because get_restart_array stops on a missing name when nexcheck = 1, so a rebuilt binary would refuse every restart written by the current one -- though that is what the accuvers marker at plasim.f90:1012 already exists to handle. Or make the claim true by ending a run on an output boundary, which is a change to how a block's step count is chosen and would also make the comment's argument sound.

Either way the comment has to stop asserting something the artifacts contradict.

Found while building the restart-template writer, whose whole subject is what a clean accumulation window looks like: convert_restart.py now refuses a template with dirty accumulators and named all 82.

title: Advect ExoPlaSim's own sea ice with the ocean's surface velocity
description:
Give icemod.f90 the advection term it does not have, driven by the circulation host's ocean surface velocity, so the simulation's sea ice moves while remaining prognostic in the atmosphere. This is the correction for the structural term OCN-21 declared and closed: icemod runs thermodynamics with no advection, transport, drift or dynamics anywhere in the file, so ice forms and melts in place, and the peer that runs this configuration reports excessive ice at a comparable resolution.

THE ARCHITECTURE IS ALREADY DECIDED and this row implements one half of it. notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 7b: ExoPlaSim's icemod stays AUTHORITATIVE for sea ice and the ocean returns a VELOCITY, not an ice state. So the ice fields stay prognostic and responsive to the atmosphere within a run, and what crosses the boundary is a transport agent -- the same shape as the heat decision, where code 903 carries convergence rather than a temperature.

WHAT THE SCHEME IS, and it is smaller than 'dynamic sea ice' implies. The EMIC-class reference is a second-order explicit transport on two prognostic fields using upper-ocean velocity, with a diffusion coefficient beside it and threshold parameters gating the doorway cases. There is NO ice momentum equation, no internal ice stress and no wind stress on the floe; a separate ice velocity field exists commented out at every use site. That is the tier to implement. The full dynamic-thermodynamic alternative is a momentum solve costing five new prognostic 2-D fields in the restart, a sixth promoted, five forcing fields in, a subcycle per sea-ice step, and numerical guards it cannot run without -- and it is not what this row is for.

DO NOT take the ice fields from the ocean instead. That option was considered and rejected on four grounds in section 7b, and icemod's read_ice_surface channel makes it available, so the rejection has to be respected rather than rediscovered.
design:
Scope: an advection term plus diffusion on the two prognostic ice fields, consuming an ocean surface velocity supplied on ExoPlaSim's grid. NOT in scope: any ice momentum equation, internal stress, or wind stress on the floe -- those are the EVP tier and a different decision. NOT in scope: taking ice cover, thickness or albedo from the ocean, which section 7b rejects.

This is a change under vendor/exoplasim, so CLAUDE.md rule 4 applies: rebuild every binary in the (resolution, layers, ranks, parmode) matrix and verify against the source sha, not just the configuration last run.

The velocity arrives on the ocean's grid and must be remapped to the atmosphere's, at every rung of the ladder. That is OCN-11's contract and a vector field rather than a scalar, so the support contract has to say what it does with direction under remapping -- state it there rather than improvising here.
acceptance_criteria: A conservation identity that can fail: total ice mass is unchanged by the advection operator alone, to a declared tolerance, on a field whose answer is known. Advection with a zero velocity field reproduces the thermodynamic-only result bit for bit. And the structural item 'sea ice does not move' is removed from scripts/error_budget.py in the same commit that lands the term, or restated with what it now covers.

title: ExoPlaSim's snow albedo has no zenith term, and the model applies one to open ocean in the same regime
description: ExoPlaSim's snow albedo is a linear ramp in SURFACE TEMPERATURE between 263.16 K and tmelt, landmod.f90:394-405, blended by forest fraction, with no solar zenith term anywhere. That is a missing predictor rather than a different parameterisation of the same one, and it is worth as much as the predictor the model does have. ClimaLand's form is min(1 - beta*(rho_snow/rho_liq - x0), 1) * (alpha_0 + d_alpha*exp(-k*cos_z)) -- zenith angle and snow density as a grain-size proxy, with no temperature term at all. Disjoint predictors for the same physics. At ClimaLand's calibrated alpha_0 = 0.59, d_alpha = 0.40, k = 1.96 and the density factor 0.874 at 330 kg/m3, the ZENITH TERM SPANS 0.565 TO 0.865, a range of 0.30, against this model's ENTIRE temperature range of 0.40 from dsnowalbmn to dsnowalbmx. Flux-weighted daily means at 32 degrees obliquity run 0.599 at the equator equinox to 0.783 at 60 degrees winter, an 0.18 swing that is absent from the simulation, largest in the winter hemisphere at high latitude where the snow is. THE INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IS THE ARGUMENT: radmod.f90:2892-2903 already applies a zenith-dependent albedo to OPEN OCEAN by default, so the same physical effect is present for one surface and absent for another inside one model, and both cases live in the same low-sun regime. Physics is not a knob: the term belongs in because it exists. ClimaLand's coefficients are Earth solar-spectrum calibrations and do NOT transfer; the form and the magnitude argument do. CLIMBER-X carries two implementations to read against it, references/climber-x/src/sic/surface_par_sic.f90:111-260, Warren-Wiscombe and Dang et al. (2015), both taking prognostic grain size AND dust concentration with grain size corrected for zenith angle. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a form, a Vesper-weighted coefficient derivation and a priced effect, not the change. Split out of PHYS-14 2026-08-24, which carries the ORTHOGONAL spectral reweighting and had been holding this in its notes untracked.
design: Out of scope: the spectral band split, which is PHYS-14. This row is the zenith dependence only, and the two compose rather than compete -- PHYS-14 fixes what the constants ARE, this fixes what modulates them. Snow density enters as the grain-size proxy, which is GRAV-8's constant, so that row is the prerequisite for the density half and not for the zenith half. Do not calibrate against ClimaLand's alpha_0 and d_alpha: they are Earth solar-spectrum fits and this project's undocumented-values rule makes them a test case rather than an anchor.
acceptance_criteria: A stated functional form with its provenance; coefficients derived against k25v rather than inherited; the effect priced in kelvin or declared unpriceable with the reason; and a statement of whether the open-ocean zenith formula already in radmod is the right form to reuse for snow or the wrong one, with the argument.
notes: REPARENTED 2026-08-24. This row was created blocked on PHYS-14, which has since been overturned and closed: radmod already star-weights the surface blends, so there is no spectral reweighting to wait for. The dependency moves to world-a0y, the normalisation defect in the same radmod block, because a zenith form should be derived against albedos whose band-1 values are right rather than 1.47 percent dark. The row's own argument is UNAFFECTED and gets stronger: PHYS-14's overturn showed radmod does carry the spectral half of surface albedo properly, which makes the total absence of a zenith term for snow the one real gap in that treatment rather than one of two.

title: Ingest the conversion report into run_exoplasim, and teach the --restart-from surface guard to read one
description:
convert_restart.py writes a report beside its output carrying the converter and schema hashes, both files' SHA-256 and geometry, every record's action and what it cost, and the donor's manifest. Nothing reads it.

WHAT HAS TO CONSUME IT: run_exoplasim.py should ingest the report into initial_state, validate the target surface hashes against the run's own staged fields, and record the donor as provenance rather than as lineage -- the converted state BEGINS a run lineage and is not evidence that source and target are the same experiment.

AND THE GUARD. restart_surface.py's --restart-from check today correctly refuses a donor restart whose embedded roughness, capacity or albedo would supersede newly staged surface files. A converted restart built on the exact target template resolves that problem, but only if the report's target surface hashes match the current run, so the guard has to recognise a valid report rather than refuse every converted state or wave them all through.

Blocked on the template writer, since no real conversion report exists until one can be made.

Source: exoplasim/notes/restart-resolution-precision-converter.md, exoplasim/scripts/convert_restart.py build_report, exoplasim/scripts/restart_surface.py
close_reason: run_exoplasim ingests the report, validates the template's surface against the run's staged files, records the donor as provenance, and now refuses a restart with no provenance at all -- which previously skipped the surface guard entirely

title: Add the model-owned converted-restart fixup path, for the state a converter must not rebuild
description:
A converted restart carries fields that are FUNCTIONS of other restart state: dalb, dsalb1, dsalb2, dz0 and dqsat. The converter cannot rebuild them -- reproducing the formulas in Python would be a second implementation of the model's physics -- so they arrive holding the target template's values, which are not consistent with the remapped soil water, snow and temperature beside them. convert_restart.py names all five in its report under expected_to_change_in_model_fixup.

WHAT THE PATH DOES, enabled explicitly through the namelist or the wrapper and running after every component's restart read: recompute grid areas and derived surface fields; enforce land/ocean/glacier consistency; rebuild humidity, albedo, roughness and the saturation caches through the model's own routines; perform documented bounds corrections; and reset every accumulation window through its own reset routines. The report's list is then the expected diff, so a target read/write smoke test can separate an intended fixup change from an unexplained one.

Touches vendored model source, so rule 4 applies: rebuild every binary and --verify.

Source: exoplasim/notes/restart-resolution-precision-converter.md, exoplasim/scripts/convert_restart.py
notes:
REOPENED AND RE-CLOSED ON A BETTER ANSWER, 2026-08-24. The refusal stands and the transient it would have removed is gone anyway.

dcc and dql turned out to be diagnostics -- rainmod.f90:1917-1918 zeroes both and mkclouds rebuilds them every timestep under NCLOUDS = 1 -- and the schema had them prognostic. Reclassifying them into the derived class would have regressed the converter, because that class took the TEMPLATE's values and the T42 template is a one-orbit cold start 0.39 in column cloud cover away from the donor. So the class was wrong, not its membership: all seven rebuilt records are now REMAPPED from the donor and merely named in the report.

dalb goes from 0.104 away from self-consistent to exactly zero, dz0 from 0.525. The 0.21 W/m2 first-record transient the model-owned fixup would have removed is therefore gone for free, without a model change or a rule-4 rebuild.

The measurement stands as the mechanism: 33.6 W/m2 instantaneous over 160 steps predicts 0.210 on the first record, measured 0.213.
close_reason: Refused on measurement: the derived records are rebuilt by the model in exactly one timestep (0.213 W/m2 measured on the first record against 0.210 predicted), worth 0.005 W/m2 over an orbit against an energy fixer at 0.42. first_record_tainted covers the transient; world-3e3 owns the fallback-state problem that turned out to dominate

title: reset_restart_accumulators zeroes 49 of the 114 accumulator records a restart carries
description:
CLIM-31's fix is incomplete. reset_restart_accumulators.py exists so that a run seeded with --restart-from does not open mid-window on the donor's partial accumulation, and its stated criterion is 'every record named below is one the model itself sets to zero at an interval boundary'. Its list names 50; the T21 restart on disk holds 114 records the schema classifies as accumulators, and 65 of them are not zeroed.

THE 65 INCLUDE THE ONES THE ORIGINAL SYMPTOM WAS MEASURED ON: aprl, aprc, aprs, aevap, assol, asthr, atsol, atthr, acc, azmuz, and the six spectral accumulators aasosp/aaspsp/aastsp/aasqsp/aasdsp/aaszsp, and the accumulated orbital scalars aorbnu/alambm/azdecl/ardist/arasc. outmod.f90:outreset zeroes every one of them at an interval boundary, so all 65 meet the module's own criterion for being safe to zero.

THREE MUST NOT BE ADDED BLINDLY, and this is why the fix is not simply widening the set. tempmin resets to 1.0e3, not zero (outmod.f90:2469): it is a running MINIMUM and a zeroed one reports 0 K for the rest of the run. asndch's reset is commented out on purpose (outmod.f90:2459, 'Let the net snow change keep accumulating'). aanrho appears in no reset at all. restart_schema.py already carries all three as model_reset sentinel/none with their reasons, so the fix is to take the set from the schema rather than maintain a second list, minus those whose model_reset is not 'zero'.

The tool is byte-for-byte unchanged by CLIM-52's reader consolidation; this is the defect that consolidation exposed, not one it introduced.

Source: exoplasim/scripts/reset_restart_accumulators.py, exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py, vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/outmod.f90 outreset, CLIM-31
close_reason: reset_restart_accumulators now reads restart_schema; 112 accumulators handled instead of 49, the reset column is derived from outreset and checked in smoke_test, and atsami was found in the process

title: Write the target restart template from the target build, and settle which of the two routes does it
description:
CLIM-52 built the restart converter and it requires a target template: a clean restart written by the EXACT target executable, supplying the record set and order, the precision, the target-resolution static surface fields, the compiler's seed shape and the accumulators' own reset values. Nothing in the tree writes one, so the converter cannot be run for real -- its self-test builds a synthetic template from the schema, which is a fixture device and is deliberately unreachable from the command line.

TWO ROUTES, and the decision cannot be taken by reading. (a) A target build run for ONE STEP with output cadence one, so the ordinary shutdown writer emits every enabled record after the model's own accumulator reset; it is available today and needs validating that every accumulation counter lands at its reset value. (b) A target-build template mode that runs normal initialisation, calls the model-owned reset routines and writes a complete restart without advancing the climate; it avoids maintaining cold defaults and sentinel values outside the model.

WHY THE SENTINELS ARE THE ARGUMENT FOR (b): outreset does not simply zero every accumulator. tempmin resets to 1.0e3 because it is a running minimum, asndch's reset is commented out on purpose, and aanrho appears in no reset at all. restart_schema.py records all three, and every one of them is a value a Python-side template writer would have to keep in step with the model by hand.

Needs a model run, so it needs permission.

Source: exoplasim/notes/restart-resolution-precision-converter.md, exoplasim/scripts/convert_restart.py
close_reason: Settled on the short-run route: build_restart_template.py cuts a template from a run of the target build and normalises the window with schema-derived reset values, so no model change is needed. Validated at T21 end to end -- the model loaded a converted restart and ran an orbit

title: Postprocessed vertical velocity wap is smaller than the divergence field implies by a factor of a few hundred
description:
The regular output's wap has an RMS of 2.6e-4 Pa/s. Computing omega from the model's own ua, va and ps by continuity gives 7e-2 Pa/s, a factor of 266, and a best-fit scale of 73 against a coarse finite-difference reference at one level. The divergence field itself is sane at 2.2e-6 s-1, so the flow is right and the diagnostic is not.

Measured on run_1987cc29e0f8 (T42, full physics) and consistent with run_329c5fa3fe73 (dry adiabatic). Both were written at NLOWIO=0, so wap is an instantaneous sample and not an interval mean.

WHY IT MATTERS: wap is the only route to the kinetic-thermal conversion term from the output, and world-bxr needed exactly that. The conversion had to be rebuilt from continuity instead. Anything downstream that reads wap as a vertical velocity -- a moisture flux, a cloud diagnostic, a convective mass flux comparison -- is reading a number that is two to three orders of magnitude wrong.

WHERE TO LOOK: the postprocessor. outmod.f90 already carries two known scaling defects in the same family, the real(8)->real(4) narrowing at line 130 and the 1.0/sqrt(eccf) at 250, and aroff is divided by naccuout at 611. The suspect is a missing or doubled factor of the model's non-dimensionalising time scale ww or of psurf.
acceptance_criteria: omega rebuilt from continuity and wap agree to within the derivative error of the reference, or the discrepancy is traced to a named line in the postprocessor and fixed.
notes:
FIXED AND VERIFIED. pyburn.py declared 'Pa s-1' for code 135 and then divided by
a hundred at both sites, with the comment saying so: '#transform to hPa/s'. ps
and psl are converted AND labelled hPa; this one was converted and not
labelled. The conversion is dropped so the artifact matches its own claim and
the CF canonical unit for lagrangian_tendency_of_air_pressure.

VERIFIED against the artifact, on run_3c1e54ecb7ff, by regressing wap against
omega rebuilt from continuity on a refined grid:

  lev    corr    scale reference/wap      before the fix
    2  +0.9531        0.975                   518
    4  +0.9820        0.937                   223
    6  +0.9726        0.963                   139
    8  +0.9668        0.898                    97
    9  +0.9795        0.933                    95

wap RMS 4.54e-2 Pa/s, against 7e-2 implied by continuity; it was 2.6e-4. The
residual six percent is the reference's own finite-difference error, stated
before the run.

Nothing in the project read wap, which is why this survived. It is now usable,
and it is the only route to the kinetic-thermal conversion from the output --
which is what world-bxr wanted it for and had to rebuild from continuity
instead.
close_reason: Conversion dropped at both sites; verified against the divergence field at a scale of 1 within the reference's own error.

title: Triage the rest of references/climber-x/src/ against the open task list ONCE
description:
Triage the rest of `references/climber-x/src/` against the open task list ONCE, with the rule declared first, so the tree is not re-surveyed piecemeal every time somebody remembers it exists. `src/lnd` and `src/smb` are read and their findings are in `notes/external-model-survey.md`; `atm`, `ocn`, `geo`, `bmb`, `lndvc`, `bnd` and `utils` are not, and together they are about 1.8 MB of Fortran. THE RULE: a module is a HIT when it implements a mechanism an open row already names, and it is recorded and dropped otherwise -- an interesting module with no row waiting on it is a distraction, and adding a row because a module exists is the tail wagging the dog. `src/geo` IS THE PRIORITY and its filenames say why: `drainage_basins.f90`, `runoff_routing.f90`, `lakes.f90` and `topo_fill.f90` sit on hydrography's ground, `hypso_topo.f90` and `hires_to_lowres.f90` on GRID-2's and SPAT's, and `coast_cells.f90`, `connect_ocn.f90` and `fill_ocean.f90` on OCN-11's ocean connectivity and bathymetry contract, which is the row BIG-MITgcm's delete-the-lakes step already justified. `src/bmb` is basal mass balance and is downstream of ice existing at all

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f, `references/INDEX.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. The hit list is `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 7, keyed to row ids as the rule required, with what was read and dropped named beside it. FIVE HITS: `src/ocn` shares GOLDSTEIN's lineage with cGENIE down to `invert.f90:70`'s `k = i + j*n`, and its `ubarsolv` has already been repacked for contiguous band storage while remaining two triangular sweeps, which splits OCN-19 from OCN-20 more cleanly than they were written; `src/geo/hypso_topo.f90` implements GRID-2's declared shape on ocean depth rather than land relief; `src/geo`'s lakes, topography filling and ocean connectivity sit on HYD's and OCN-11's ground; `src/ice_sico` is a third and heaviest route for CLIM-62; and `src/bnd/fake_*.f90` is the offline-driver pattern OCN-10 and EFOR-1 describe. title: The 400-750 nm photosynthetic window behind FRADPAR rests on four references and all four are
description:
The 400-750 nm photosynthetic window behind `FRADPAR` rests on four references and all four are marked `held`, including the one `references/INDEX.md` says the near-parity argument turns on and which the same table records as itself a secondhand use of another

Source: `notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md` finding 7
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19. All four read; all four rows flipped to read with dated findings; the window is CONFIRMED for this host with the one mismatch stated rather than hidden. Lehmer et al. (2021) Table 1 carries the K2V absorptance peaks exactly as used (675/711/746 nm), on Kiang et al. (2007b) surface spectra whose K2V is Segura's -- the same modeled star behind `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth`, a consistency nobody had noticed. The mismatch: Lehmer's K2V is 4620 K against this host's 4965; interpolating the peaks in temperature puts the reddest optimum near 720-725 nm here, so the 750 edge carries an Earth-like margin rather than the thin one a true 4620 K host would have. Kiang (2007b) says both quoted claims verbatim, including the anoxygenic caveat that caps the honest range. Marosvolgyi and van Gorkom (2010) validates the whole chain at the Sun: the optimization reproduces chlorophyll a's 670-680 nm before being asked about other stars, a check that could have failed. No bracket needed; FRADPAR's citation standing holds. title: Establish what each rung of the resolution ladder COSTS in wall clock
description:
Establish what each rung of the resolution ladder COSTS in wall clock, because SPAT-8 defers cost to "record cost separately" and nothing in this tree says what a rung is worth. That number is the justification for the whole optimisation workstream -- SHTns, the thread port and FP32 are aimed at the ladder rather than at T42 -- so it is currently the one term in that argument nobody has written down. THE INPUTS ARE MEASURED AND THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT THE PROBLEM: 77 to 93 s per orbit at T42 L10 on 16 ranks, a Legendre work ratio of 7.9x at T85 and 26.2x at T127 against grid work of 4.0x and 9.0x, transform shares of 5.5, 10.4 and 14.9 percent across those rungs, and a measured 39.7 percent from single precision. Composed naively those give roughly 240 local years a day at T85 against T42's thousand. THE MISSING TERM IS THE TIMESTEP and it is not small: `timestep_minutes` is 45 at T42 and a finer grid needs a shorter step for stability, so a factor of two there halves every projection and the composed number moves from 240 to about 120. `exoplasim/notes/non-mpi-performance-roadmap.md` already names measuring the largest scientifically acceptable timestep at each resolution as its first priority item, which is the same measurement

Source: `exoplasim/notes/spectral-transform-profile.md`, `exoplasim/notes/non-mpi-performance-roadmap.md`, `notes/audits/pyburn-postprocessing-cost.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a cost per rung with its timestep stated, and a BRACKET rather than a point wherever the timestep is assumed rather than measured, because a projection that hides an unmeasured factor of two is worse than a bracket that shows it. It needs no production run: the timestep question is answerable on a short integration per rung and the rest is arithmetic over numbers already recorded. ORDER IT BEFORE committing to a rung rather than after, since the point of knowing is to decide whether loop D can replay A, B and C at that support at all -- and SPAT-8 requires exactly that replay [step: rebuild_binaries]. A CONSERVATION IDENTITY THAT CAN FAIL, AND A DEFAULT WORTH INVERTING, 2026-08-22. ESMF states and tests itself against `sum(F_src*A_src*frac_src) == sum(F_dst*A_dst)` under destination-area normalisation, holding itself to about 1e-9 relative on analytic fields, with interpolation ACCURACY a separate and much looser 1e-2 test. THAT IS A CHECK WITH A RIGHT ANSWER and `lib/gridding.py` has never had one. Normalisation maps exactly onto this prefix's intensive/extensive split: destination-area for extensive totals, fraction-area for densities, and THE FRACTION FIELD MUST TRAVEL WITH THE RESULT because a fraction discarded is an identity that can no longer be evaluated -- the choice belongs to the FIELD, not to the call. THE DEFAULT WORTH INVERTING: ESMF errors on unmapped destination cells unless explicitly told to ignore them, checks the WEIGHT MATRIX rather than the intermediate search, and names the offending element id; the total-miss case has its own message so it cannot silently match zero cells. `lib/gridding.py:243-254` silently backfills empty cells from the nearest region centre and returns a count, with no threshold at which it refuses. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 55

McFadden, Wells and Jercinovich (1987) was held and unread; read, it states the clast source directly at p. 504, "mechanically weathered basaltic bedrock derived from topographic highs", so "consolidated bedrock rather than basin fill" is the paper's own criterion rather than a stand-in for one. It gives no clast flux and no minimum outcrop fraction and none is invented. Two things came free. The deposition UPPER bound is now sourced from the same paper rather than resting on Muhs alone: p. 505 has pavements buried under high loess rates, with "moderate eolian depositional rates ... critical for maintaining clasts at the land surface". And the clast supply is EXHAUSTIBLE, p. 505, "no new clasts are added to pavements once the bedrock topographic highs are reduced by erosion and buried", which a rule keyed on present substrate treats as permanent, so pavement area is an upper bound on an old surface -- a stated bound rather than a gap, since there is no time axis here. No lower bound on dust is carried, deliberately: no source gives a minimum rate and a strict-positivity guard on a continuous deposition field is a rule that can never fire [step: surface_classes]

description:
Nothing consumes the derived surface classes yet. Two consumers were the reason for building them and both are one field away: `build_dust.py` should read `pavement` as an emission SUPPRESSOR and a store of deposited dust, and `phosphorus_budget.py` should read `pavement` as a P sink and `diatomite` as the deflatable source

Source: `pedology/notes/derived-surface-classes.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the row's own point is the sign. Wells et al. (1995) dated pavement clasts with cosmogenic 3He and found them at the surface throughout, so a pavement is an accretionary surface UNDER A NON-ERODIBLE COVER: read as deflation armour the class would have been a product of emission and grown with it, and read correctly it suppresses emission and stores what falls. `build_dust.py --surface-classes` multiplies erodibility on paved regions by `dust.yaml:source.pavement_residual_erodibility`, DECLARED at 0.0 with a bracket to 0.25 because the paper gives a mechanism and no areal clast cover -- a mosaic is not a lid. `phosphorus_budget.py --surface-classes` reports both derived classes with their roles, which makes its own Sahara-to-Amazon caveat concrete: that comparison turns on a biogenic diatomite source rather than an evaporite one, and this world grows diatomite in its strandlines. NEITHER CONSUMER HARDCODES A CODE. `build_surface_classes.py` writes CF `flag_values`/`flag_meanings`, so `lib/surface_classes.py` resolves classes by NAME from the file's own legend and raises on an unknown one; verified by inserting a class ahead of `pavement` in a synthetic file, whose code moves 3 to 4 and whose mask follows, where a hardcoded 3 would have selected `bare`. title: Bracket the thermostat over WEATHERING SCHEME CHOICE
description:
Bracket the thermostat over WEATHERING SCHEME CHOICE, which currently carries no structural uncertainty at all. `pedology/scripts/thermostat_efficiency.py` returns a thermostat strength from one parameterisation and `config/planet.yaml` records that the outgassing plausibility check behind the prescribed pCO2 came from `weathering_fluxes.py`; neither has a bracket, and three published alternatives now sit on disk with their constants. `vendor/cgenie/genie-rokgem/data/input` ships Amiotte-Suchet 2003, Gibbs 1999 and GEM_CO2 as class lists plus constants tables, selected by `par_weathopt`. Amiotte and GEM_CO2 share base rates EXACTLY -- 1.586, 0.672, 0.152, 0.479, 0.095, then 0.272 against 0.222 -- and still disagree on the pair of columns that appear to carry the carbonate against silicate split of CO2 consumption, 0.93/0.07 against 1.00/0.00 for the carbonate class. Gibbs is a different formulation on different units. IF THAT COLUMN READING IS RIGHT THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE THERMOSTAT ITSELF, since silicate weathering is the long-term sink and carbonate weathering returns its CO2 on marine precipitation, so the silicate fraction is what sets thermostat strength

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 17, `pedology/analysis/thermostat_efficiency.json`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. CONFIRM THE COLUMN MEANING FIRST: it is inferred from position and the schemes' published form rather than from a header, and a bracket built on a misread column is worse than no bracket. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is what scheme choice costs the thermostat number, not an adoption -- rokgem's global-rate mode is coarser than this project's lithology map and is not a candidate. THE CLASS SYSTEMS DO NOT MAP and that is most of the work: rokgem uses carbonate, shale, sandstone, basalt, shield and acid volcanics, while this world's land is playa clastic at about a quarter, continental clastic, schist, granite, granodiorite, melange and evaporite. There is NO land carbonate class here, LITH-26 having placed carbonate on the shelf, and playa clastic and evaporite have no counterpart in any of the three. So each scheme has to be mapped onto the classes this world has, and the mapping is itself a declared assumption that belongs in the bracket rather than under it [step: weathering_fluxes, thermostat_efficiency]. PRECONDITION MET AND THE PREMISE CORRECTED, 2026-08-22, from the code that CONSUMES the table rather than from column position. The reading of columns 3 and 4 was RIGHT -- `rokgem_box.f90:1842` names them "fCa and fSi" outright and they partition `dum_calcium_flux` at 1848 and 1858. Column 1 is the base rate, column 2 the runoff exponent, 5 to 7 osmium. BUT THE DISAGREEMENT THIS ROW EXPECTED IS NOT THERE: the two files the code actually reads carry IDENTICAL fCa/fSi, 0.93/0.07 carbonate, 0.39/0.61 shale, 0.48/0.52 sandstone, 0.00/1.00 basalt. The 1.00/0.00 values quoted here are in the four-column `Amiotte_2003_consts.dat` and `Gibbs_1999_consts.dat`, which the seven-column reader cannot consume. THERE ARE TWO SELECTABLE 2D SCHEMES, NOT THREE, and `rokgem.f90:69,76` names them: `GKWM` IS Gibbs 1999 and `GEM_CO2` IS Amiotte-Suchet 2003, so the four-column files are archival vintages of the same two. Base rates are not comparable across schemes -- 32000 against 1.586 -- because the conversion factors carry different units. THE BRACKET THIS ROW WANTS IS THE RUNOFF FUNCTIONAL FORM, which is structural rather than a constant: GKWM is `runoff ** k` with per-lithology exponents 0.68 to 0.91, GEM_CO2 is strictly LINEAR in runoff. Both normalise through `r_avg_runoff`, so they agree at mean runoff by construction and diverge in the TAILS. The fSi-weighted effective exponent is 0.720, giving 1.57x at a fifth of mean runoff and 0.64x at five times it, and a thermostat about 30 PERCENT WEAKER under GKWM, flat at 29 to 32 percent across runoff responses of 1.05 to 1.50 -- so it is usable as one bracket number rather than a curve. That is the deliverable this row asked for, reached through the exponent instead of through fCa/fSi. The class-mapping work this row describes still stands and is still most of the effort. TRAP, currently inert: `sub_load_weath` reads seven values list-directed and would read a four-column file ACROSS line boundaries and desynchronise silently rather than failing; nothing can select those files today, but this row currently treats them as the scheme definitions. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 31

title: DECLARE the reduced wetland, peat and methane form and what taking each part COSTS IN CLAIMS
description:
DECLARE the reduced wetland, peat and methane form and what taking each part COSTS IN CLAIMS, so a fallback is a decision with a procedure rather than a retreat taken under pressure. WET-1 through WET-11 specify a target; nothing has yet shown that chain is implementable within this project, and it rests on SDEC-3's vertical coordinate, PLHY-4 and PLHY-5, PCAR-5's trait registry and BVOC-6's oxidant bracket, all wholly open. PALADYN is a design that works, is published and runs at this project's throughput, so it is the floor each part can fall back to. THE THREE PARTS ARE NOT EQUALLY VIABLE and that is the substance. EXTENT is genuinely supplied: wetland fraction is the TOPMODEL saturated fraction where the surface is snow free, from GW-26's index, and potential peatland is the fraction wet at least three months of the year; it forfeits only WET-2's mutual exclusivity, which is bookkeeping rather than physics. PEAT STOCK is supplied at a nameable cost: acrotelm and catotelm confined to the top soil layer, transfer at a critical acrotelm carbon, catotelm shifted down as density fills a layer, peat carbon vertical diffusivity zero, areal change capped at 1 percent a year with a minimum fraction seeding every cell; it forfeits WET-4's vertical resolution and with it every depth-resolved redox claim. METHANE is a bracket and never a measurement: a constant fraction of heterotrophic respiration wherever respiration is anaerobic, one fraction per surface type, which cannot separate production from oxidation and contains no transport, so WET-6's independent exposure and WET-7's diffusion, plant and ebullition pathways collapse into the constant

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3e, `biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and a DECLARATION rather than an implementation: the deliverable is the reduced form written down with its per-part cost and the condition for taking it, BEFORE anything is built to it, so the comparison is made while neither option is under schedule pressure. The condition is PER PART and not global -- a part falls back when a consumer needs the field and the dependency that part waits on does not exist -- and any fallback is labelled ON THE ARTIFACT, so nothing downstream can read a reduced field as a full one. ONE PROHIBITION SURVIVES INTACT: the methane part yields a surface FLUX under a transplanted-Earth assumption and never an abundance, so it may not move `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` on its own. The lifetime half that would convert the one into the other belongs to WET-10, and it has a reduced form of its own that WET-10 names [step: soil, groundwater, lpj_driver]

title: radstop saves the two solar constants through mpputgp
description:
`radstop` saves the two solar constants through `mpputgp`, which gathers `NHOR` per rank and writes `NUGP`, so the restart carries 8190 elements of buffer for a 2-element array and each rank reads 510 elements past the end of `zsolars`. Nothing reads the record back, so the cost is restart IDENTITY: `input_restart_sha256` and CLIM-31's `seed_copy_sha256` are stable only because `-finit-real=zero` holds the padding at zero

Source: `notes/audits/zsolars-restart-overread.md`, `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 18
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. `radmod.f90:1594` now uses `solarini`'s own idiom, `if (mypid == NROOT) call put_restart_array('zsolars',zsolars,2,2,1)`. The resume question was settled BEFORE the change rather than after: `reseek` locates records by NAME and skips data records WHOLE, so a record's size cannot dislodge another, and nothing reads `zsolars` in any case. Verified on three checks with right answers known in advance -- the record is 16 bytes where it was 65536 and still carries both solar constants; 397 of the restart's 398 records are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the stock build's, so the fix is physics-neutral by measurement rather than by argument; and restarts cross the change BOTH WAYS, the fixed binary resuming a stock restart and the stock binary resuming a fixed one, neither reporting a missing record. Found by the `-flto` arm of the build-flag benchmark returning five restart shas from five runs of one binary, which was not model non-determinism. A sweep of all 459 `mpputgp`/`mpgetgp` call sites against their declared shapes found this to be the ONLY genuine mismatch; the 24 in `simba.f90` are `allocatable` and allocated `NHOR`. CLIM-38 carries the second defect in the same nine lines [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Price the CH4 and N2O the radiation cannot carry
description:
Price the CH4 and N2O the radiation cannot carry, at THIS star's mixing ratios rather than Earth's, and report whether `derive_design_flux.py` is absorbing the difference

Source: `config/planet.yaml` atmosphere block, `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 5
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and it is the LARGEST item in the error budget by a wide margin: +2.25 to +5.26 W/m2, against mineral dust's +0.34 to +0.61 which stood second, and against 2.02 W/m2 for Earth's own CH4 and N2O by the same calculation. Etminan et al. (2016) could only bound it, being valid to 3500 ppb of CH4 and 525 ppb of N2O with this world above both ceilings; Byrne and Goldblatt (2014) cover 100 ppbv to 100 ppmv and settle it, and the two agree to 3.5% where both are valid. THE REMAINING WIDTH IS NOT THE RADIATIVE CALCULATION, which two independent methods fix to a few percent: it is a disagreement about whether tropospheric N2O is enhanced at all, and that is CLIM-43. THE MIXING RATIOS ARE THE FINDING. Segura et al. (2003) was already on disk and read, already supplying `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth` and `model.ozone_scale`, and its p. 701 says CH4 and N2O are "systematically higher for the K2V planet ... because of the difference in stellar UV fluxes", at the same modern-Earth surface fluxes: same biology, less near-UV, slower photolysis, longer lifetimes. Read off Fig. 12a at 1 PAL against Fig. 4 as calibration, a factor of 2 to 5 on both gases, with two independent checks that the figure reading is sound -- Fig. 4's Sun values reproduce modern Earth, and the text's "of the order of 20 ppm" at 0.1 PAL matches where Fig. 12a's peak reads. Gravity is applied and cuts the other way: 1 bar at 12.81 m/s2 makes a mixing ratio 0.756 of Earth's column, the same 23% the other absorbers already carry correctly. Two caveats pull opposite ways and are recorded rather than resolved: Segura's K2V is 4620 K against this host's 4965 K, and this star is DECLARED active where Segura's is a quiet modelled one, which puts near-UV back -- so `surface_uv_relative_to_earth` and this both rest on one assumption about the star's UV, and the activity declaration is in tension with it. AND THE DESIGN FLUX IS ABSORBING IT, by construction: `derive_design_flux.py` searches flux to meet thresholds on the modelled climate, so a missing greenhouse term is met with more starlight. The climate is not wrong; the ATTRIBUTION is, and the residual moves to everything keyed on insolation rather than temperature -- photosynthetically active flux, the shortwave band split, the aerosol forcings, the reported surface UV -- all with one sign. `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-absorbers.md` carries it; adding the band is CLIM-42
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and it is the LARGEST item in the error budget by a wide margin: +2.25 to +5.26 W/m2, against mineral dust's +0.34 to +0.61 which stood second, and against 2.02 W/m2 for Earth's own CH4 and N2O by the same calculation.

title: Add a CH4 and N2O band to the longwave. config/planet.yaml says the shape
description:
Add a CH4 and N2O band to the longwave. `config/planet.yaml` says the shape of it -- "adding either means adding a band, not a key" -- and CLIM-41 measured that the term outranks every other item in the budget

Source: `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-band.md`, `exoplasim/analysis/trace_gas_band_model.json`, `exoplasim/analysis/co2_overlap_589.json`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. Three bands on Donner and Ramanathan (1980) in `radmod.f90`: CH4 1306 and N2O 1285 overlapped by water vapour through the `zth2o` the routine already computes, N2O 589 overlapped by CO2 through a correlated-k fit cross-checked against Ramanathan (1976) Appendix A. Band intensities are a MATCHED TRIPLE with `A0` and `beta0`, so CH4's is recovered from the paper's own Table 2 and N2O's two from McClatchey, the compilation it cites. All four declared tests pass: the zero-abundance reduction identity is bit-identical on restart, output and snapshot over a segment crossing two writes; sign and monotonicity hold; 100 ppmv produces no NaN; and the term lowers global mean OLR by **0.799 W/m2**, which is 40% of the offline pricing and exactly what this scheme returns for CO2 against a line-by-line answer -- its whole CO2 greenhouse is 12.28 W/m2. **That comparison was later withdrawn**: the Earth figures it was held against were quoted from general knowledge, never sourced, and are an ATTRIBUTION with band overlap shared out rather than the REMOVAL measured here. Checked properly instead, every step of the chain is verified against a line list -- CH4's band absorptance within 7% of HITRAN 2020, the narrow-band Planck conversion to 1.004, and Sasamori's own CO2 absorptivity 0.175 against a line-list 0.165 -- so no defect is identified anywhere and what remains is two estimates of one quantity differing by 2.5x, priced as a disagreement in `analysis/error_budget.json`. **THE LAST DAY OF IT WAS ONE MISSING `mpbcr`.** `ch4` and `n2o` went into `radmod_nl` and not into `radini`'s broadcast block, so they kept their default of zero on every rank but the root and the band ran on eight polar latitude rows and nowhere else -- measuring 0.0175 instead of 0.799. Invisible: no warning, the run completes, `plasim_diag` echoes the values because that prints on NROOT too, and the symptom looks like weak physics. It was chased as physics through a Doppler-broadening hypothesis (Cess 1973 fetched, read, and it does not apply -- its branch is below Lorentz at every level here), a shortwave hypothesis, and a supposed 40x contradiction between two perturbations that were identical. What found it was dumping the flux PER RANK: exact zeros on seven of eight. Two things the false trails left standing: the band model is validated against HITRAN 2020 to better than 7% at every level, and the scheme's own CO2 calibration is measured. Failure-modes has the class; `config/planet.yaml` now declares the mixing ratios

title: Settle whether TROPOSPHERIC N2O is enhanced at this star
description:
Settle whether TROPOSPHERIC N2O is enhanced at this star, which is the whole width of the CH4/N2O budget item: read Rugheimer et al. (2013) Fig. 7's per-grid-star surface mixing ratios at its 5000 K point, which is this host to within 35 K

Source: `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-absorbers.md` section 3
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and it settles CH4 as well as N2O. The paper is a vector PDF, so Fig. 7 was extracted as PATH COORDINATES rather than read off a log axis: `analysis/trace_gas_forcing.py` parses the content stream, matches each curve to its legend colour and converts through the panel's own tick calibration. **The 5000 K grid point reads 1.600 ppmv of CH4 and 0.300 ppmv of N2O -- the Sun case's values on both gases.** Neither is enhanced. THE TWO SOURCES NEVER DISAGREED: the enhancement is real and turns on between 4750 K (1.600 ppmv CH4) and 4500 K (37.27), and Segura's K2V is 4620 K, INSIDE that transition, while this host at 4965 K is above it. The apparent conflict was a comparison between stars 345 K apart. It also closes the quiet-star caveat the estimate carried, because epsilon Eridani is Rugheimer's own 5000 K grid star and is what this world's activity is modelled on -- though `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth` still rests on the quiet-star calculation and now does so alone. Budget item goes from (2.25, 5.26) to (1.56, 1.98) W/m2 against 2.02 for Earth's own; it stays the largest single term, and is below Earth's only because 1 bar at 12.81 m/s2 is 0.756 of Earth's column. What outranks everything is now the TERM rather than the uncertainty in it, which is CLIM-42. Byrne and Goldblatt's fits are checked four ways and the script raises on each: branch continuity at 2.5 ppmv, the paper's 100 ppmv maxima, Earth's known industrial-era forcings, and the extracted Sun curve against Rugheimer's separately stated Sun-case numbers (1% on N2O, 8% on CH4)
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and it settles CH4 as well as N2O.

title: The model is not run-to-run reproducible, and nothing owns
description:
The model is not run-to-run reproducible, and nothing owns it: the SAME binary on identical inputs gives bit-identical output at 1 timestep and differs by 16, and `plasim_status` differs between two runs even at 1 timestep, so a bitwise restart diff reports nothing

Source: `notes/audits/model-reproducibility.md`, `exoplasim/analysis/reproducibility_matrix.json`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and the premise is REFUTED. A declared factorial -- 8 and 16 ranks, output off and at the production setting, segments crossing no write and two, three repeats each -- comes out bit-identical in `plasim_status`, `plasim_output`, `plasim_snapshot` and the model half of `plasim_diag` in every measurable cell. **The rank count is what is not free**: 8 against 16 ranks differ in 83 of 199 restart records, at round-off and growing, so an A/B must hold it fixed and a bracket at one rank count is not comparable to a control at another. The comfortable explanation was refuted by accident: the first pass ran on the binaries a run directory had frozen, which still carry the `zsolars` overread, and it reproduces THERE TOO -- so the overread is deterministic under `-finit-real=zero` and is a source of rank-dependence, not of run-to-run difference. What is left of the original observation is that its control could not have shown it: a gridpoint record is written on `mod(nstep, nafter) == 0` over the ABSOLUTE step count, and on the production restart neither a 1-step nor a 16-step segment reaches one. Two traps are now closed in code rather than in prose -- `plasim_diag`'s resource block is filtered from the source that writes it rather than from a diff, since every line of it is conditional on a non-zero counter; and the harness hashes a bed's executables against `binary_manifest.json`, because `--verify` answers whether the INSTALLED binaries are current and cannot answer whether the bed is running them. Consequence: bit-identity is available again, at a fixed rank count, and CLIM-39's reduction identity needs re-taking as CLIM-45
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and the premise is REFUTED.

title: Store the Legendre weights as P and Q alone. legini builds EIGHT NCSP x NLPP matrices
description:
Store the Legendre weights as P and Q alone. `legini` builds EIGHT `NCSP x NLPP` matrices and every one is touched every timestep, which is 48.4 MB a die at T127 and 114.9 MB at T170 against CCD0's 96 MB of L3 and CCD1's 32 MB -- and that footprint is the measured cause of a 10.5 point load imbalance that makes CCD1 the critical path at both resolutions. All eight are P or Q times a per-MODE factor and a per-LATITUDE factor, both separable and neither needing an `NCSP x NLPP` array, so storing two matrices instead of eight leaves 12.1 MB and 28.7 MB a die and both fit CCD1. It is the exact inverse of the filter fold, which moved a per-mode scalar INTO the matrices to save one multiply in three and returned 1.6% because those loops are bound by streaming the matrices rather than by the multiplier; the same sentence read backwards is the argument for this

Source: `exoplasim/notes/rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md`, `exoplasim/notes/legendre-filter-fold.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. It is a reassociation, so restart shas move and it needs `compare_restarts.py` at a declared tolerance with a control, as the symmetry work did. Two things to establish before believing the prize: whether the extra per-mode vector read costs the inner loops their vectorisation, and whether anything survives at T21 and T42 where the matrices already fit [step: rebuild_binaries, baseline_run] IN THE OPTIMISATION WORKTREE'S SCOPE, on CLIM-61's precedent: this is the same problem space that worktree is working in, so the reassociation may already be done or made moot there. The merging session owns reconciling this row.
close_reason:
Built, measured and refused, and the roadmap already carried the verdict this row did not. exoplasim/notes/non-mpi-performance-roadmap.md section 1: implemented in full, correct, four times smaller (114.9 MB a die to about 36 at T170, 15.1 MB a thread to 4.5, under the 32 MB target) and 1.56% SLOWER on the threaded build at T170 -- 80.57 s against 81.66 s, paired and interleaved, faster in 0 of 4 rounds, [-2.17, -0.74]. The code is reverted; verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh is kept and agreed with the eight-matrix build to 4.8e-13 at one step and 1.06e-11 at twenty against a 1e-10 bar declared before the arms ran.

THE PREMISE WAS BACKWARDS. The route was ranked first because the filter fold returned 1.6%, read as evidence these loops are bound by streaming the weight matrices. Undoing the fold costs the same 1.6% back, and the reading that fits both numbers is that they are bound by the MULTIPLY. A second measurement agrees: at NPRO=1 one thread streams 30 MB of pmat and 30 MB of qmat per transform against 1.88 MB at NPRO=16, and the two time the same, 1.45 ms against 1.48.

SHTns has since removed the matrices altogether, computing the Legendre functions on the fly and storing no NCSP x NLPP array, which takes pmat and qmat out of cache_budget.py entirely. The cache-boundary finding in rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md still stands; what no longer stands is that this is the way to act on it.

Closed WONTFIX. Reopen only if a resolution above T170 makes the memory headroom worth a small speed loss. The row stayed open because a71cc1bc pointed it at the merging worktree and the merge (85de8f85) never reconciled it.

title: Read the 103 implicitly SAVEd procedure-body declarations in plasim/src and classify each
description:
Read the 103 implicitly SAVEd procedure-body declarations in `plasim/src` and classify each as intended persistent state, harmless write-before-read, or a defect. The thread port tripped exactly one of them and the other 102 have never been examined. Under `-fopenmp` a SAVEd local is SHARED by every thread, demonstrated at seven of eight threads reading a value another thread wrote, while under MPI each rank is a process and its SAVEd locals are private by construction. So this class is reachable under threads and unreachable under ranks, and source that has only ever run under ranks has never exercised it. gfortran reports nothing at any warning level tried, so there is no flag that shortens this and it is reading

description:
Implement the schema-aware, target-template restart converter already specified for progressive T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 advancement: typed record inventory; precision conversion; triangular spectral projection with discarded/new-mode accounting; conservative Gaussian remapping of gridpoint state and extensive reservoirs; target-owned static fields, masks and accumulator resets; manifest/provenance binding; and fail-closed configuration compatibility.
