title: Evaluate the published ExoPlaSim-to-cGENIE forcing path before reusing
description:
Evaluate the published ExoPlaSim-to-cGENIE forcing path before reusing it, and resolve the scaling factor it ships with. `acapirala/exoplasim_genie_regrid` v1.2 (`10.5281/zenodo.10802839`) converts ExoPlaSim wind stress, wind velocity and planetary albedo onto cGENIE's grid and carries topography converters both ways, and its README instructs the user to set the wind-stress scaling `ea_11`/`go_13` to 2.0 for ExoPlaSim v3.0.6 and 2.6 for v3.3.0, moving `bg_par_gastransfer_a` from 0.715 to 1.1 alongside. Identify what physical quantity that multiplier stands in for, whether it corrects the atmosphere, the regridding or the ocean's drag closure, and whether it is documented anywhere but the README; then either derive it, bracket it, or declare it. `vendor/exoplasim` is a fork of neither release, so neither pair of numbers transfers unchecked. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is an explanation of the knob and a verdict on reuse, not a coupled run

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9b and 9f
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE, though the reading is worth doing either way because the same question would arise for any prescribed stress field. A tuning multiplier on a physical forcing is a knob under this project's conventions, and inheriting one silently is exactly the failure `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 16 names. Both published couplings are one-way, so this row supplies OCN-10's atmosphere-to-ocean half and leaves OCN-5's return path and exit predicate untouched [step: baseline_run]. A MECHANISM AND A PLACE TO LOOK, from `vendor/cgenie/` 2026-08-22. cGENIE's ocean expects wind stress at TWO STAGGERED LOCATIONS, and says so itself: `genie-main/genie_loop_wrappers.f90` lines 34 and 36 annotate `ocean_stressx2_ocn` as stress at the u point and `ocean_stressx3_ocn` as stress at the v point, and `genie.F:342-360` accumulates both over `kocn_loop` steps and divides, so what arrives is a time mean of a C-grid-staggered stress. A regridding route supplying one field where two are wanted, or missing that averaging, would need a compensating multiplier of about the size this row is asking about -- and the scaling being applied on BOTH the atmosphere and the ocean side, `ea_11` and `go_13`, is what an interpolation mismatch looks like rather than a physical correction. Check that FIRST. It is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not the explanation this row still owes. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10c. A SECOND PLACE TO LOOK, beside the staggering: muffingen itself writes `bg_par_gastransfer_a = 0.722` into the configurations it generates, and the published regrid path instructs moving that to 1.1 alongside the wind-stress scaling. So the gas transfer half of this row's knob has a generator DEFAULT to be compared against rather than only a README instruction. `references/muffingen/muffingen.m`, `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10f. A SECOND MECHANISM, and the likelier of the two, 2026-08-22. muffingen GENERATES a synthetic zonal wind stress: `source/make_grid_winds_zonal.m` says so in its own header, and `par_tauopt` selects the regime -- case 1 annotated modern Northern Hemisphere or paleo Eocene, case 2 a water world, case 3 automatic from a zonal gateway in the mask. THE SAME SWITCH ALSO WRITES `bg_par_gastransfer_a`, with the calibration in the comments reaching 0.722. So wind stress and gas transfer are COUPLED IN THE GENERATOR BY DESIGN, and the regrid path's instruction to set the stress scaling to 2.0 or 2.6 AND move gas transfer from 0.715 to 1.1 is not two independent corrections but one adjustment about wind made in the two places muffingen couples. It also explains the 0.715: muffingen's own default is 0.722, so the path starts at the generator's value and raises it. ASK FIRST WHAT THE EXOPLASIM STRESS IS BEING COMPARED AGAINST -- muffingen's synthetic profile, or an observational product -- because the multiplier is a ratio and its denominator has not been identified. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 18c. THE MULTIPLIER IS `scf`, THE WIND STRESS SCALING, 2026-08-22, and this supersedes the two earlier hypotheses rather than adding a third. `initialise_embm.F:1195` uses it in the stress non-dimensionalisation as `...*rh0sc*dsc*usc*fsc/(rhoair*cd*scf)`, beside the drag coefficient. It appears in BOTH `ini_embm_nml` and `ini_gold_nml`, and `initialise_goldstein.F:2110` passes it on as `go_scf` -- which is why the shipped configurations set `ea_11` and `go_13` to the SAME value, 1.531013488769531300, and why the README moves both together. So the answer to what physical quantity the multiplier stands in for is: it does not stand in for one. It is a scaling that reconciles a supplied stress product against the drag closure the components were tuned with, and 2.0 or 2.6 is that factor for an ExoPlaSim-derived stress against a default tuned for cGENIE's own wind product. The C-grid staggering of section 10c and the gas-transfer coupling of 18c are consequences of the same quantity rather than separate mechanisms. WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS ROW is whether the factor should be DERIVED -- from the ratio of the two stress products over a common grid -- or declared, and it cannot be inherited because `vendor/exoplasim` is a fork of neither release the README names. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28d. SCOPE CLARIFIED 2026-08-22: there are TWO published paths and this row tracks one. The offline `acapirala/exoplasim_genie_regrid` route moves wind stress, winds and albedo. cGENIE's in-tree `genie-plasim` is a different and fuller arrangement, handing over 17 fields including the latent and sensible transfer coefficients, both downward radiative streams and the moisture terms. Do not conflate them when resolving the scaling factor. Whether EMBM still runs under the in-tree arrangement is not settled by its declaration module and was not confirmed. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30b
close_reason: Verdict 2026-08-24: DO NOT INHERIT. Holden et al. (2016) states what scf is for -- the frictional-geostrophic ocean dissipates wind energy, so increased surface wind strengths are required to compensate and drive a reasonable circulation. Conventional ensemble range 1 to 3, widened to 2 to 4 for the T21 coupling in anticipation of understated Southern Ocean zonal wind stress, and varied as one of six subjectively tuned ocean parameters over a 50-member ensemble. So it is not a regridding artifact and not derivable from the ratio of two stress products over a common grid: it is a class-16 knob, and the README's 2.0 and 2.6 are two settings of it. If GOLDSTEIN is adopted, scf is DECLARED as a bracket and the bracket is reported -- that requirement moves to OCN-3. The row's other half is also resolved: the offline regrid path this row tracks belongs to the EMBM architecture, which section 59b eliminates, so there is no path to reuse and the dependency on OCN-3 was dropped as moot. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 59b and 59e.

title: Establish the usable resolution ceiling of the EMIC ocean before any adequacy claim rests
description:
Establish the usable resolution ceiling of the EMIC ocean before any adequacy claim rests on 36 x 36 x 16, and separate the model's limit from the connector's. MEASURE the wall clock of one short integration at 36 x 36 x 16, 48 x 40 x 16 and 36 x 36 x 32, which all ship as working configurations, and at one grid finer than any that does, to test the r^4-per-model-year estimate that section 9g reads off the `ubarsolv` loop structure rather than from a run; the component is serial, so cores cannot absorb the growth. Fix `nyear` by an explicit stability criterion rather than by the default 100, since `dt = sodaylen*yearlen/(nyear*tsc)` is a namelist consequence with no Courant check anywhere in the component. Then determine what muffingen's `.k1`, `.paths` and `.psiles` generation does above 36 x 36, whether the resolved island count exceeds the compile-time `GOLDSTEINMAXISLES` default of 10, and whether it runs under Octave at all. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a resolution/cost curve and a ceiling with its cause named

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9a, 9g and 8b
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE. It matters because the tier's entire attraction is its price and that price is a property of 36 x 36 rather than of the model, so an adequacy verdict at the shipped grid and a cost verdict at a usable one are not the same measurement. Section 8b's straits, sills and partial coasts are what a finer grid would buy, and with the resolved tier dropped they ride ENTIRELY on this row: resolution is now the only lever on connectivity, so if the grid that represents them is unaffordable the outcome is a declared unresolved-connectivity bracket rather than quiet acceptance of whatever the shipped grid represents. Edwards and Marsh's finding that errors reduce only moderately with a doubling of resolution is the reason to measure that benefit rather than assume it. This row sets the ocean's own support; OCN-11 still owns the map from the 10M export, and SPAT-8 replays loop A at whatever support is chosen [step: orogen, hydrography]. PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-08-22 from the vendored tree, and this row's island figure is CORRECTED: `genie-main/genie_control.f90:79` sets `#define GOLDSTEINMAXISLES 5`, not 10. Counting the maximum island index in all 294 shipped `.psiles` files gives a range of 1 to 8, with 89 of them -- about thirty percent -- above the default. So raising the macro is ROUTINE rather than exceptional, island count is a per-geography property driving a compile-time bound, and a new geography can need a rebuild before it runs at all. That bears on OCN-11 as much as here, since this world's island count is not knowable until a candidate configuration is generated. RESOLUTION: muffingen's settings annotate `par_max_i` and `par_max_j` as `[1-72]`, but of the shipped configurations 131 are 36 x 36, five are 18 and one is 12, and nothing is above 36 -- a declared range, not a demonstrated one, which is the distinction this row exists to draw. Shipped depth is `par_max_k=17` with one extra level, and `par_A_frac_threshold=0.50` matches this project's `geography_land_threshold` in convention. STILL NEEDS A DOWNLOAD: muffingen is a separate repository and `genie-paleo` holds only its outputs, settings and logs, so what it does above 36 x 36 and whether it runs under Octave are not answerable from here. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10d. OCTAVE REMAINS OPEN with the tree now local at `references/muffingen/`: it is MATLAB `.m` with a LaTeX manual under `DOCS/`, and a search finds no Octave statement either way. The manual is where to look. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10f THE CEILING NOW HAS A CONSTRAINT TO BE MEASURED AGAINST, 2026-08-24. Section 59 decides the coupling architecture as offline full-flux on exactly the property this row measures: that the ocean's grid is chosen for ocean adequacy and does NOT climb the T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 ladder with the atmosphere. So this row's resolution/cost curve is what the decision rests on, and it acquires a second deliverable beside the ceiling -- a statement of the ocean grid's independence from the atmosphere rung, since the published synchronous coupling gets its affordability from matching the three horizontal grids and this project deliberately does not. The eliminated architecture also supplies the negative datum: matching at T170 is a 512 x 256 ocean, eight times linear on a serial r^4 component, about 4000x. That is the number this row's curve should be read against.

title: Profile the EMIC ocean at the shipped grid BEFORE optimising either half
description:
Profile the EMIC ocean at the shipped grid BEFORE optimising either half of it, then parallelise the half that pays. There is no disabled parallelism to re-enable: the OpenMP in `tstepo.F:74-90` wraps duplicate-copy experiments and the block in `biogem.f90:718-735` calls `sub_wasteCPUcycles1`/`2`, so threading is new work. Attribute runtime between the barotropic solve, tracer advection and BIOGEM's tracer loops at 36 x 36 x 16; then decompose what threads, which is BIOGEM's `do n=1,n_vocn` sweep over vectorised columns and the 3D loops in `tstepo_flux`, and NOT `ubarsolv`, whose forward elimination and back substitution both carry loop-carried dependences. Delete the dead duplication at `tstepo.F:32-35` and `62-68` first: six arrays filled every ocean timestep and read by nothing. Validate against `genie-knowngood/`, which ships per-component reference output for four configurations

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9g and 9h
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE. The profile is the deliverable that orders everything after it, and it is cheap next to either piece of work: the barotropic solve dominates GROWTH with resolution while BIOGEM's tracers may dominate RUNTIME at the shipped grid, and those are different claims that this project has not separated. The dead-copy deletion is correctness-neutral and available immediately. Threading is what makes a finer grid affordable at all, since the component currently cannot spend a second core [step: any]. CITATIONS VERIFIED 2026-08-22 against the vendored tree, and two are stronger than written. `tstepo.F` declares the six arrays at lines 32 to 35 -- two full four-dimensional tracer arrays, two more tracer copies and two density copies -- and fills all six at lines 62 to 68 every ocean timestep, while the `tstepo_flux_t` calls that would consume them are COMMENTED OUT along with the whole OpenMP block, leaving `call tstepo_flux()` as the only live call. And `sub_wasteCPUcycles1` and `2` are real subroutines at `biogem_lib.f90:2267` and `:2289`, with the block that would call them commented out too: it was a scheduling experiment on deliberately wasted cycles, so there is not merely no parallelism to re-enable, there is none to read for intent either. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10a. THE VALIDATION SURFACE IS THINNER THAN THIS ROW IMPLIES, and it imposes an ORDER. `genie-knowngood/` is four netCDF files covering three components, not four: BIOGEM 3-D fields at 1.9 MB, an ENTS year-20 average, and GOLDSTEIN year-20 and year-10 averages, since two configurations cover the same component. Twenty and ten model years, so a short-run regression surface rather than an equilibrated comparison -- adequate for this row, worth knowing before it is asked to carry more. THE COMPARATOR IS BETTER THAN EXPECTED and already exists: `genie-main/src/c/compare.cpp` built as `nccompare.exe`, taking a relative tolerance IN ULPS and an absolute floor, which is the right measure for a reordering because it asks how far a result moved in representable numbers. THE ORDER: the GOLDSTEIN reference carries `opsi`, reported through `opsisc = dsc*usc*rsc*1e-6`, and `rsc` is Earth's radius hardcoded. So every number in the suite is a number at Earth's parameters, and the radius work under OCN-3 and OCN-12 destroys its applicability as its first act. This row is a correctness-preserving change at fixed physics, which is exactly what the suite is for -- so DO IT BEFORE the planet parameters move, or lose the validation surface. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 13. THE TWO THREADING TARGETS ARE NOT COMPARABLE, established by static analysis 2026-08-22, and this row treats them as one decomposition. BIOGEM'S SWEEP THREADS: every argument in the `do n=1,n_vocn` body is indexed by `n`, `loc_dtyr` is a read-only scalar, the reduction onto the grid happens after the loop, and both callees clear the three checks that would break it -- no `SAVE` or `DATA`, no writes to module-scope arrays since `bio_remin`, `bio_part`, `ocn` and `phys_ocn` are all reached through dummy arguments, and NO INITIALISED LOCALS anywhere in `biogem_box.f90`. That last is CLIM-51's implicit-SAVE class, which found 103 sites in `plasim/src` with no compiler flag that reveals them; across all of BIOGEM and ECOGEM the pattern appears 23 times and none is in the file holding this work. `tstepo_flux` DOES NOT: it includes `ocean.cmn` twice and that declares 44 COMMON BLOCKS, so GOLDSTEIN's state is global by construction and every variable the loop touches must be proved read-only or made private. In BIOGEM privacy is the default and sharing explicit; in GOLDSTEIN the reverse. THIS CHANGES WHAT THE PROFILE IS FOR: if it says `tstepo_flux` dominates, the answer is not "thread it" but that the threading route is expensive there and OCN-20's algorithmic route matters more, so the profile decides between two DIFFERENT KINDS of work rather than two candidates for the same kind. Caveats on the counts: they are an upper bound that does not separate module-scope declarations from procedure-body ones, and this is one level into the call tree. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 14

title: Replace the barotropic streamfunction solve with one that does not grow as r^3 per timestep
description:
Replace the barotropic streamfunction solve with one that does not grow as r^3 per timestep, and prove it against the existing reference output. `invert.f:32` orders the Psi points lexicographically as `k = i + j*n`, which is what fixes the bandwidth at `imax` and makes `ubarsolv`'s two triangular sweeps cost about `2*imax*(jmax+1)*(imax+1)` per ocean timestep with `gap(mpxi*mpxj, 2*mpxi+3)` in storage. Price a fill-reducing reordering against an iterative treatment of the elliptic streamfunction equation, and cost the island machinery FIRST, since `ratm`, `psisl`, `erisl` and `matinv_gold` all assume the present factorisation and `GOLDSTEINMAXISLES` bounds them. Any iterative scheme changes results to within a declared tolerance rather than exactly, so fix the tolerance and the acceptance comparison before choosing

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 9g and 9h
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and CONDITIONAL on OCN-3 selecting cGENIE and on OCN-19's profile showing this half is worth the work at a grid this project would actually run. It is the algorithmic complement to OCN-19 rather than an alternative: threads cannot help a sequential recurrence, and a reordering cannot help the tracer loops. Thresholds are fixed before results are seen, so the tolerance against `genie-knowngood/` is declared in the same commit as the implementation and not after the first comparison [step: any]. A CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT BESIDE THE COMPLEXITY ONE, found on verifying this row's citation. `invert.f:32` carries `k=i + j*n` exactly as quoted, and three lines above it sits an acknowledged and unresolved out-of-bounds: a comment saying gfortran will flag an array reference out of bounds, that it is all OK, and then "(I think ...)". So the routine this row proposes to replace has a defect its own authors recorded and did not settle. This project can settle it cheaply -- `-ffpe-trap` is in the production flag line and the checked profile carries `-fcheck=all`, which caught a real out-of-bounds during the CLIM-40 fold work -- and doing so before any replacement is designed says whether the reordering is a performance change or a repair. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10a. THE TOLERANCE INSTRUMENT EXISTS, so this row's requirement to fix it before choosing needs no new tooling: `genie-main/src/c/compare.cpp`, built as `nccompare.exe`, takes `-r` as a relative tolerance IN ULPS and `-a` as an absolute floor. Units in the last place is the right measure for an iterative scheme replacing a direct one, because it asks how far the answer moved in representable numbers rather than as a fraction. AND THE SAME ORDERING APPLIES AS OCN-19's: the reference fields are overturning streamfunctions scaled by `opsisc`, which carries Earth's hardcoded `rsc`, so this replacement must be validated BEFORE the radius work moves the parameters, or its acceptance comparison stops existing. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 13b and 13c

title: The sea ice is thermodynamic-only and that is an undeclared structural term rather
description:
The sea ice is thermodynamic-only and that is an undeclared structural term rather than a decision. `icemod.f90` runs thermodynamics with no ice dynamics and no transport, which is the same configuration BIG-MITgcm runs and names as a stated limitation, reporting excessive ice as its consequence at a comparable resolution. So the term is not negligible on peer evidence, and nothing here has priced it or written it down. `references/climber-x/src/sic` is the reference implementation in this model class, `sic_dyn.f90` and `transport_sic.f90`

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f, `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and BLOCKED, and the blocker is physical rather than a queue: sea ice dynamics is driven by wind stress and ocean currents, and this ocean is a slab with horizontal transport deliberately off under CLIM-16, so a dynamics scheme would be advecting ice across a motionless ocean. What is NOT blocked and is what this row asks for first: state the term in `analysis/error_budget.json` as a structural item beside no-q-flux, with the direction taken from the peer report rather than guessed, so the omission is declared where a reader of the budget will find it. The scheme itself follows the ocean and not this row [step: baseline_run]. SHAPE CORRECTED 2026-08-22, and the block confirmed. This row says sea ice dynamics is driven by wind stress and ocean currents; the EMIC-class answer needs only the second. `vendor/cgenie/genie-goldsteinseaice/tstepsic.f` announces itself as a "2nd order explicit transport code using upper level ocean velocities", and `tstipsic.f` builds its advective coefficients from `u(1,i,j)` and `u(2,i,j)` with `diffsic` beside them. There is NO ice momentum equation, no internal stress, no wind stress on the floe, and a separate `uice` field exists commented out at every use site. So the ladder runs: thermodynamic only here, advection by upper-ocean velocity in cGENIE, and a full dynamic-thermodynamic scheme in CLIMBER-X's `sic_dyn.f90`. THE BLOCK STANDS EXACTLY -- a slab ocean has no velocity field, so there is nothing to advect with -- BUT THE EVENTUAL FIX IS SMALLER than this row implies: an advection term on two prognostic fields using a velocity the ocean would already produce. That strengthens the case for declaring the term in the error budget NOW, since the declaration is not deferring an expensive decision. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 19. RELATED, 2026-08-22: in cGENIE's in-tree PlaSim coupling the sea-ice ALBEDO is supplied by the ocean model as `genie_alb_sic`, so PlaSim's own ice albedo pair does not set it. That is the pair which survives `radmod`'s open-ocean overwrite and which PHYS-14 owns, so a future coupling moves it out of this project's hands rather than needing it fixed first. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30b. PRICED, AND THE BLOCK IS SCHEME-DEPENDENT RATHER THAN ABSOLUTE, 2026-08-22 -- verified in source before acting on it. THE COST, from CLIMBER-X's EVP scheme (Hunke and Dukowicz 1997, elliptical yield curve, C-grid, from SIS2): FIVE new prognostic 2-D fields in the restart, `ui`, `vi` and the three stress-tensor components; ice concentration PROMOTED to prognostic and separately advected, a sixth; five forcing fields in; an EVP subcycle of 50 steps per sea-ice step against an SIS2 default of 432; one flux-corrected transport pass per advected field; and guards it cannot run without -- a velocity clamp at `cfl_fac*dx/dt` with `cfl_fac = 0.1` "for CFL stability near the Poles", a viscosity cap, and a stress limiter called every step. THE BLOCK: this row says a slab ocean has nothing to advect with, which is exactly right for cGENIE's advection-by-upper-ocean-velocity and NOT right for EVP, which is a MOMENTUM solve. `sic_dyn.f90:603` forms the forcing as `(Cor + PFu)*mi_u + (fxic_now + tauxa)` -- Coriolis, sea-surface tilt, internal ice stress and WIND STRESS -- with ocean velocity entering only as the drag reference at `:593`. With `uo = vo = ssh = 0` the tilt vanishes and drag becomes drag against still water, while wind stress, internal stress and Coriolis remain. Wind-driven ice over a motionless ocean is a reduced but coherent configuration, which is what free-drift approximations do. THE ROW'S CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED -- declare the term in the error budget first -- but restate the block as applying to one family of schemes rather than to sea-ice motion. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 43a-b DECLARED 2026-08-24, which closes this row's first and unblocked ask. scripts/error_budget.py now carries 'sea ice does not move' as a structural item with the peer's direction and no invented kelvin, beside no-q-flux. THE BLOCK LIFTS AS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE ARCHITECTURE DECISION rather than by its own work: offline full-flux adopts a circulation host that produces the ocean surface velocity this row said did not exist, so the remaining work is the advection term itself. AND THE AUTHORITY QUESTION IS SETTLED, notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 7b: ExoPlaSim's icemod stays authoritative and the ocean returns a VELOCITY, not an ice state. The alternative was available -- read_ice_surface already takes 14-month climatological ice cover and thickness, nice = 0 prescribes ice outright and nfluko = 1 diagnoses a correction against it -- and is rejected on four grounds, the first decisive: prescribed ice cannot respond to the atmosphere within a run, which severs the albedo feedback the design flux, the extreme-cold land fraction and the stellar cycle's grand minima all turn on. So this row's eventual scope is an advection term on ExoPlaSim's own prognostic ice, driven by the ocean's velocity: a change under vendor/exoplasim, so rule 4 applies. NOT INHERITED: the published synchronous coupling supplies ice temperature, height, fraction and albedo FROM the ocean, which is right without a lag and does not transfer to an offline arrangement.
close_reason: Declared 2026-08-24, which is what this row asked for. scripts/error_budget.py now carries 'sea ice does not move' as a structural item beside no-q-flux, with the direction taken from the peer report rather than guessed and no kelvin invented, since the correction requires an ocean surface velocity this slab does not have. The row's premise -- an undeclared structural term rather than a decision -- is resolved: it is now a declared term. Two things moved out rather than staying here. The AUTHORITY question is settled in notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md section 7b: ExoPlaSim's icemod stays authoritative and the ocean returns a velocity, not an ice state. The CORRECTION is world-pt8, blocked on OCN-3 and OCN-11, which implements the advection term against that decision. The albedo half was always PHYS-14's.

title: The two-band ocean albedo is collapsed to one value by the same default that computes it.
description:
The two-band ocean albedo is collapsed to one value by the same default that computes it. Section 29 established that `radmod.f90:2892-2903` overwrites the open-ocean albedo with a zenith formula under `necham = 1`; what it did not record is that **`dsalb(1,:)` and `dsalb(2,:)` receive the IDENTICAL expression**, so the band index -- a physical dimension -- holds one value. This project sets `two_band_albedo: true` specifically to obtain spectral surface albedo, and `solarini` duly computes 0.0744 and 0.0636 for the two ocean bands; over ice-free ocean, which is most of the planet, that is undone every radiation step for the direct beam. The diffuse component is read before the overwrite and does keep both bands

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 58c
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it is the SAME DECISION as OCN-7's remaining half rather than a separate one: the choice between ECHAM-3 and Briegleb, the choice of whether either should be spectral, and this collapse are one change to one expression. Fold this into whatever OCN-7 concludes rather than costing it twice [step: baseline_run]

title: Establish cGENIE's viability and MEASURED cost as the offline circulation host
description:
Establish cGENIE's viability and MEASURED cost as the offline circulation host, now that the resolved tier is off the board: whether it builds here; licence/version/provenance; how it consumes Vesper radius, gravity, rotation, calendar and pressure; what a candidate global configuration generated from the 10M bathymetry and mapped to the T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 atmosphere ladder looks like; what initial hydrography and boundary closures it requires; and what spin-up, restart and tracer costs are in wall clock and storage ON THIS MACHINE rather than quoted from a paper. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a viability verdict and a measured cost, not a run

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 6, 8b, 8c and 9
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. Offline is the only affordable coupling class, because equilibrating a deep ocean takes thousands of model years against orbits priced in wall-clock hours; the pattern to copy is aeolian, downstream of one climate and upstream of the next. That same argument removed MITgcm, since a primitive-equation host reaches equilibrium only at a resolution whose spin-up is unaffordable and a coarse one resolves no more than this candidate does. cGENIE remains a candidate rather than an adoption until OCN-10 through OCN-12 show that its forcing, support and Earth assumptions can be closed, and section 9c is the source read but not a licence to change what it found. Nothing has been built or measured yet, which is what this row is for. AMENDED 2026-08-22, and CORRECTED: an earlier version of this amendment claimed a three-dimensional ocean costs about four times, from BIG-MITgcm's 300 CPU-hours per 100 simulated years against this stack's 76. That ratio is a COUPLED SYSTEM against a BARE ATMOSPHERE and is not the price of an ocean; it is confounded on the atmosphere side too, since SPEEDY at five levels is much cheaper than ExoPlaSim at T42 with ten. What survives is narrower: BIG-MITgcm's own breakdown makes its 300 almost entirely the coupled fast system, so it is an atmosphere-plus-ocean figure against an atmosphere-plus-slab one, which bounds nothing tightly but is a real comparison. Report this row's cost in wall clock AND in whatever unit the coupling cadence makes meaningful, because CPU-hours per simulated year assumes every component advances on one clock and this pipeline is asynchronous: cost per PASS is the number that decides affordability at loop A's cadence, not cost per simulated year. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 2. THE TREE IS NOW LOCAL, vendored at `vendor/cgenie/` as a subtree from `derpycode/cgenie.muffin` master, MIT, so this row is workable rather than blocked on an acquisition. Two of its questions are already answered by the vendoring. WHETHER IT BUILDS HERE: not as it stands -- `genie-main/user.mak` sets `GENIE_ROOT = $(HOME)/cgenie.muffin` and `RUNTIME_ROOT = ../../cgenie.muffin`, so repointing those is the first fork change. LICENCE AND PROVENANCE: MIT, and the commit is a subtree merge in this repository's history rather than the state of a directory outside it. What remains is the measured cost and the Vesper-parameter question, which is the whole point of the row. NOTHING HERE IS AN ADOPTION: `vendor/cgenie` has no consumer, no pipeline row and no step, and it stays that way until this row returns a verdict. THE VESPER-PARAMETER QUESTION HAS A PARTIAL ANSWER, from reading the tree 2026-08-22: calendar and rotation are consumed, radius and gravity are NOT. `ini_gold_nml` carries `sodaylen`, `sidaylen`, `yearlen`, `nyear` and the depth scale, while `initialise_goldstein.F` hardcodes Earth's radius and gravity into the non-dimensionalisation and four derived scales carry them. Rotation is parameterised but fails open to Earth's rate when the two day lengths are set equal. OCN-12 owns the inventory; what this row takes from it is that the answer is not binary and the radius and gravity half is source work rather than configuration. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10e. AN ORDERING FALLS OUT OF THE VALIDATION SUITE and belongs here because this row owns the parameter change. `genie-knowngood/`'s GOLDSTEIN references are overturning streamfunctions reported through `opsisc`, which carries Earth's hardcoded `rsc`, so every number in the suite is a number at Earth's parameters. Moving radius and gravity for this planet destroys the suite's applicability as its first act. Either let OCN-19 and OCN-20 land first, since they are correctness-preserving changes at fixed physics and the suite is exactly what they need, or DECLARE a replacement acceptance test before the parameters move -- and it cannot be a comparison against those files. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 13c. THE SPIN-UP ARGUMENT WAS PROBED AND SURVIVES, 2026-08-22. cGENIE ships `genie-gemlite` beside `goldlite` and `ocnlite`, which looked like it might undercut the offline choice. It does not: `genie.F` cycles it as `mod(koverall, kgemlite*kocn_loop)`, running `gem_notyr` ordinary years and then entering a GEM cycle that copies tracer arrays AND climate state -- the comment says "here: sea-ice" -- into GEMlite and holds them. It is offline-tracer acceleration for carbonate chemistry once the circulation is settled, and does nothing for the circulation itself. Its own header also records that it cannot handle a CO2 pulse, since it needs ocean-surface to atmosphere disequilibrium to work. So the claim that equilibrating a deep ocean costs thousands of model years stands unmodified. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 26. THE COST MECHANISM IS IN THE TREE, 2026-08-22. `genie-plasim/src/fortran/plasim.f90:604-655` implements PlaSim-GOLDSTEIN gearing: with `ngear = 1` the atmosphere integrates for `ngear_years_plasim` years while accumulating daily means, then RETURNS IMMEDIATELY for the next `ngear_multiple - 1` blocks while the ocean is driven from the stored seasonal cycle, so the atmosphere runs one block in `ngear_multiple`. That is what makes a coupled ocean affordable and it should enter this row's cost model, not be rediscovered after it. The non-obvious part: the SST-dependent terms are recomputed live against `tstar_ocn` every geared step -- latent via saturation specific humidity, net longwave, sensible -- and only the coefficients and downward fields are replayed, because naive replay of net heat flux severs the feedback that holds SST. The source comment says "Needed for stability". Evaporation is deliberately not recomputed, for moisture conservation. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30c. ACCELERATOR INVENTORY, 2026-08-22: cost here is not one mechanism but two, controlled differently. Gearing skips the ATMOSPHERE on a fixed schedule with no adaptive guard, `ngear_multiple` being a plain integer. GEMlite skips the BIOLOGY AND CIRCULATION for geochemistry with the two-sided adaptive guard in section 35b. Price them separately; they compose, and only the second bounds its own error. Note also that GEMlite keeps a SECOND live copy of the ocean state -- its header says "there is an entirely seperate `ocn` for BIOGEM" -- which is the duplicate-state hazard rule 5 exists for and would need a provenance answer before adoption. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 35PORTING COST IS ASYMMETRIC AND SHOULD BE PRICED THAT WAY, 2026-08-22: the geochemistry is namelist-configurable while the calendar and the physical scaling constants are compile-time `PARAMETER`s stated in more than one place, so adoption cost sits in the physics core rather than spread evenly. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40. A PER-ITERATION ADOPTION COST THIS ROW SHOULD CARRY, 2026-08-22. `genie-paleo` is 286 pre-baked Earth geographies and no code, and the cost for a NEW geography is not the bathymetry -- that regrids -- it is the `.psiles` and `.paths` pair, which is TOPOLOGICAL: an integer island-label map and a HAND-ORDERED list of (direction, i, j) triples tracing a closed integration circuit around each island for the barotropic streamfunction solve. These cannot be produced by regridding a heightfield; muffingen generates them interactively. SO IT IS MANUAL WORK PER BUILD, AND IT INVALIDATES ON EVERY GENERATION THAT CHANGES CONTINENT CONNECTIVITY -- which is what a new Orogen generation does. Price it per iteration of loop A, not once. Also note the tuning infrastructure is inert here: three `errfn_*` programs and a HadCM3 target file compile to binaries that score the model against observed phosphate and alkalinity, and this world has nothing to tune against. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 46d ARCHITECTURE DECIDED 2026-08-24, and this row narrows to it: offline full-flux. The alternatives are eliminated in notes/external-model-survey.md section 59 and the audit's section 6 is rewritten to match, so this row no longer carries an open architecture question and its cost measurement is scoped to the offline case. THE COST ARGUMENT IS CORRECTED, and the correction matters to what this row measures. Holden et al. (2016) reports 75 simulated years a day coupled with PLASIM at 98 percent of the load and GOLDSTEIN essentially free, so a dynamic ocean does not cost what the ocean costs -- it costs being obliged to integrate the ATMOSPHERE for the ocean's thousands of years. Offline is chosen because it is the only class in which the ocean's cost does not climb the T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 ladder with the atmosphere. WHAT THIS ROW MUST NOW REPORT, beyond its existing questions: (1) the ocean's wall clock AT A FIXED GRID, stated as independent of the atmosphere rung, since that independence is the whole basis of the decision and an unmeasured claim is not one; (2) scf as a DECLARED BRACKET with the bracket reported, inherited from OCN-17's verdict -- it is a tuned parameter for GOLDSTEIN's wind-energy dissipation, conventional range 1 to 3, not derivable from a stress-product ratio; (3) whether the two Earth-fitted corrections of section 59d have Vesper analogues, which they do not, so any adequacy claim resting on the components' Earth behaviour inherits them. TWO CONFIGURATION QUESTIONS ADDED BY THE SEA-ICE DECISION, 2026-08-24. Section 7b makes ExoPlaSim's icemod authoritative for sea ice, so the candidate host must be configured so that its OWN sea-ice component does not also own it: establish whether genie-goldsteinseaice can be disabled or run diagnostically without breaking the ocean's surface heat and freshwater budgets, since brine rejection and the ice-covered fraction feed them. That is a viability question about this host, not an implementation, and it belongs in this row's verdict. Second, this row must report whether the host EXPORTS an ocean surface velocity in a usable form, because world-pt8's advection term consumes it and section 7b's whole argument is that the ocean returns a transport agent rather than an ice state. The published in-tree coupling never needed this, since it hands ice the other way, so it is not evidence that the field is available.

title: Scope ECOGEM as the ecosystem tier, with driver-agnostic MARBL as the named fallback
description:
Scope ECOGEM as the ecosystem tier, with driver-agnostic MARBL as the named fallback: licence/version/provenance; tracer and trait-count cost; restart and diagnostic state; required C-N-P-S-Fe-Si, alkalinity/DIC/O2 and optical inputs; absolute-time, K-star photon, gravity/sinking and temperature dependencies; what the covarying trait space must DECLARE; and every fixed Earth relation or inventory that survives. Darwin leaves the board with MITgcm, being an MITgcm package, and this costs nothing on the axis that mattered: trait-based ecology was never the discriminator between them, since both make community composition emerge from a declared trait space. Compare ECOGEM against MARBL on interface burden and on what each supplies as fixed Earth types. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a scoping note

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 12, 16 and 40d, `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and BOTH CANDIDATES ARE NOW LOCAL AND READ: ECOGEM inside `vendor/cgenie/genie-ecogem` from the vendoring, MARBL at `references/marbl/`, BSD-style from UCAR and in references rather than vendor because this row's deliverable is a scoping note. THE COMPARISON SPLITS SCIENTIFIC AGAINST ENGINEERING and should not be forced to a winner. ECOGEM WINS THE ECOLOGY, on the mechanism this row names: the cost is a FILE SWAP, verified at source: `par_ecogem_plankton_file` is a namelist string, `sub_init_populations` counts data lines and sets `npmax` from them, and every plankton-dimensioned array is ALLOCATABLE, so the ladder runs 1 / 8 / 9 / 11 / 16 / 18 / 64 populations across nine shipped `.eco` files with no recompilation. Sixteen is the reference configuration and not the price this row once quoted. TWO CORRECTIONS TO WHAT THAT LADDER MEANS: the 0.6 to 1900 um log spectrum is `8P8Z`'s, not the ladder's -- `32P32Z.eco` is a different grid, phyto 0.10 to 1224 and zoo 0.15 to 2800 with the offset not mirrored, so the sixty-four rung changes the size RANGE and not only the count; and the `3Diat4ZP_PiEu` against `NoDiat4ZP_PiEu` pair is not a free on/off pre-registration, since the diatom file carries 11 rows against 8, so it is a guild ADDED rather than a switch thrown. THE TRAIT SPACE THE ROW ASKS ABOUT IS NOT THE DATA FILE: it is 36 allometric `_a`/`_b` coefficient pairs in `ini_ecogem_nml`, applied as 39 `coef_a * volume ** coef_b` statements, so a population is a size and the traits follow. MARBL is the structural opposite and NOT because its count is locked -- `PFT_defaults` accepts `user-specified` and the shipped `+cocco` variant moves the count -- but because it has no allometric generator at all: 38 hand-set parameters per autotroph with a poison default of `1e34`. That, and not the file swap, is why ECOGEM wins the ecology. MARBL WINS THE ENGINEERING, and also not closely: regression tests, baselines, build tests, `code_consistency.py`, YAML settings with a JSON form carrying per-configuration defaults, declared dependencies, units and datatypes -- AND A STANDALONE DRIVER -- which is a TEST HARNESS and not an offline model: `marbl.F90` dispatches ten single-shot test names and `call_compute_subroutines` calls the compute routines once per column, with no time loop and no tracer update. It can answer a tendency-sensitivity question and cannot produce a spun-up state. ECOGEM has no entry in `genie-knowngood`, no test suite, no settings schema and no driver of any kind. STOICHIOMETRY IS NOT A WASH, and the earlier reading missed where ECOGEM keeps its: BIOGEM exposes `par_bio_red_POP_PON` and others in `ini_biogem_nml` with `bio_part_red` four-dimensional, but ECOGEM buries four Redfield literals in its own BIOGEM coupling arithmetic -- 138/106, two 16.0 and 6.625 -- none of them namelist-reachable. MARBL exposes three and derives seven from a fixed chain. THE PHOTON AXIS INVERTS TOO: MARBL's `f_qsw_par = 0.45_r8` is a Fortran `parameter` with no YAML entry and its six attenuation literals are hardcoded, while ECOGEM's `PARfrac`, `k_w` and `k_chl` are all namelist, so ECOGEM is the one correctable from a configuration file. A SECOND BURIED SOLAR CONSTANT, and it is this project's own recurring defect: `ecogem_box.f90:298` converts light as `E0 = PARlocal/0.2174`, which is 4.5998 umol/J and is the marine twin of the fixed 550 nm Earth coefficient BIO-25 found in LPJ photosynthesis. Read the two together. WHAT TO ACT ON WITHOUT DECIDING, restated now the driver is understood: what MARBL can be made to answer before an ocean host exists is a TENDENCY at a stated state, not a candidate, so the sequencing advantage is real but much narrower than it read. AND THE TWO ARE NOT INDEPENDENT CHOICES: ECOGEM cannot be extracted from cGENIE, so if OCN-3 selects cGENIE it is nearly free, and if OCN-3 does not, ECOGEM is unavailable at any price and MARBL's true cost is the tracer transport host underneath it. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 12, 13a and 16. A SPECTRAL PRECONDITION FOR ANY ECOSYSTEM TIER, 2026-08-22, which applies to ECOGEM and MARBL alike and not only to BIOGEM: marine light limitation is specified as an irradiance half-saturation in W m-2 and a SINGLE SCALAR light e-folding depth in metres, both solar calibrations. Water is transparent in the blue-green and strongly absorbing in the red and near-infrared, so a K dwarf's redder flux gives a SHALLOWER photic zone and production confined nearer the surface. The direction follows from the spectrum alone; the magnitude needs `k25v_hr.dat` integrated against water absorption, which is a desk calculation and should precede tier selection rather than follow it, since it changes the vertical structure any tier resolves. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40d. MAGNITUDE COMPUTED, 0.712, from artifacts already in the tree and with no new number. `exoplasim/data/water/hale_querry_1973_liquid_water.dat` gives water's absorption above 0.75 um, and the LONGEST e-folding depth anywhere in that range is 0.51 m, so all of shortwave band 2 is deposited in the top metre or two as heat and what reaches the photic zone is band 1 and nothing else. Band-1 flux fraction is 0.382 for k25v -- reproducing the project's canonical `flux_fraction_band1` exactly -- against 0.537 for a 5772 K Planck, which is `analysis/vegetation_albedo.py`'s own solar reference. THIS STAR DELIVERS 71 PERCENT AS MUCH LIGHT BELOW THE SURFACE LAYER. Limits, none of which change the sign: it is the flux reaching below the surface layer and not the photic DEPTH, which additionally needs visible attenuation that is not extracted here; and it is pure water, where productive water's chlorophyll and CDOM absorb more in the blue and partly offset it. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40e EVIDENCE POINTER, filed 2026-08-22: the comparison this row rests on is now `notes/audits/ecosystem-tier-ecogem-marbl.md`, read at source and carrying its own limits section; `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 12c and 16 are the earlier reading and have been corrected in place where that note contradicted them. WHAT REMAINS BEFORE THIS CLOSES is the SILICON axis and nothing else: the row asks for required C-N-P-S-Fe-Si inputs, and `squota` and the silicifier path were traced structurally only. `references/INDEX.md:516` records Naidoo-Bagwell et al. (2024), the EcoGEnIE 1.1 diatom extension, as `held` rather than read, and the note states that any silicon comparison between the tiers needs it first.

title: DECLARE the forcing procedure, provenance chain and exit predicate for the ocean-transport
description:
DECLARE the forcing procedure, provenance chain and exit predicate for the ocean-transport loop before its first pass, and add the loop and its OCN-2/OCN-10/OCN-11 steps to `config/pipeline.yaml` in the same commit. An ocean model forced by a climatology a zero-transport slab produced, and restored toward that climatology's own sea-surface temperature, returns a transport of zero by construction. Use flux forcing with no temperature restoring, retain weak salinity restoring only as an explicit control, and converge heat transport, SST/ice, global energy, freshwater/salt closure and the climate fields that drive the carve verdict

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 7, 8a and 8f
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and a DECISION rather than a measurement, which is why it is a task and the run is not. Ocean physics is inside loop A because transport can move design flux and the carve verdict; SPAT-8 must replay it at every candidate support. Ocean biology stays outside loop A while OCN-16 is closed, and opening carbon feedback creates a separate declared loop rather than silently extending this one. THE CANDIDATE SATISFIES HALF OF THIS ROW BY CONSTRUCTION AND CANNOT SATISFY THE OTHER HALF, 2026-08-22. cGENIE has NO sea-surface temperature or salinity restoring: `surf_ocn_sic.F` computes surface flux terms, `fx0o`, `evap`, `fxsen` and the sea-ice counterparts, and the ocean takes fluxes from whichever atmosphere it is coupled to. The one name that looks like restoring is not -- `rel` in `common /ocn_relax/` is used at `velc.f:103` as `u = rel*u1 + (1-rel)*u`, a numerical under-relaxation between solver iterates, so record it as a solver control lest somebody retire it as physics. The genuine explicit control is `get_hosing.F`, freshwater forcing with `hosing`, `hosing_trend` and `nyears_hosing` in `ini_gold_nml`, called UNCONDITIONALLY from `goldstein.F:259` and added to the freshwater flux at line 297 -- always in the path, inert only by parameter value, which is why a zero default is not the same as an absent term and it belongs in the provenance chain. THE SPLIT: this row's warning joins two failures with an "and" -- forced by a slab-derived climatology AND restored toward its SST. The candidate rules out the second by construction. Nothing in it rules out the first, because that defect is in what this project SUPPLIES. So read the requirement as two with different owners: no restoring is checkable once against cGENIE; flux forcing that does not encode the answer is this project's and is what the declared procedure is actually for. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 27. THE MECHANISM, DERIVED 2026-08-22, and it is sharper than this row's own statement. cGENIE tunes its atmosphere to make room for its ocean: `tstipa.f` moves heat and moisture as `betaz(l)*uatm(1,i,j)` and `betam(l)*uatm(2,i,j)` plus `diffa`, and `ini_embm_nml` exposes `diffamp(2)`, `diffwid`, `difflin`, `betaz(2)` and `betam(2)`, so the atmosphere-ocean transport PARTITION is a tuned quantity there. THIS PROJECT CANNOT DO THAT. On a slab with `nhdiff` off the ocean transports nothing, so ExoPlaSim's atmosphere carries the entire poleward load through resolved dynamics, with no coefficient to turn down. Hand those fluxes to a dynamic ocean and the total becomes an atmosphere already carrying everything plus an ocean carrying more. THE FLUX-FORCED FAILURE IS THE OPPOSITE SIGN FROM THE RESTORED ONE this row describes: not zero transport, but OVER-transport, because the flux field was computed under the assumption that the ocean does nothing. THIS APPLIES TO THE ARCHITECTURE OCN-10 SPECIFIES AND NOT TO THE PUBLISHED PATH, which keeps EMBM and lets it compute the heat fluxes with a tunable transport -- see OCN-10's fork. Under the no-EMBM architecture the loop is necessary rather than stylistic -- a single pass cannot converge the partition, because the atmosphere in the forcing climatology has not been told the ocean exists. And it is why OCN-2 comes first: the return path is `nfluko = 1` reading surface code 903 under the comment "prescribed advection", and verifying that channel with a known field is cheaper than discovering it is wrong once a circulation exists to blame. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28. A PEER EXIT PREDICATE WORTH COPYING, TWO-SIDED, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's GEMlite accelerator is controlled in `genie-main/genie.F` by ENTRY ON A RATE and EXTENSION ON AN ERROR INTEGRAL: `:621-638` extends the full-model phase whenever the year-on-year pCO2 change exceeds `gem_adapt_dpCO2dt`, default 0.1 ppm/yr, so the accelerator never engages while the system is moving fast; `:808-823` extends the accelerated phase only while cumulative drift from its starting pCO2 stays under `gem_adapt_DpCO2`, default 0.1 ppm. Unbounded extension is off by default with the reason recorded at the switch, and `gem_yr_min`/`gem_yr_max` bound the phase at 10 and 1000. THE PRECONDITION THAT MAKES IT WRITABLE is a single scalar summarising the accelerated subsystem's drift that is already computed; name that number for the ocean-transport loop when declaring this row's exit predicate, because without one the predicate can only be a fixed schedule. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 35 THE HAND-OVER RULE IS SUPPLIED, 2026-08-24, from the eliminated synchronous architecture where it is a working arrangement rather than an inference. Terms that depend on ocean temperature are recomputed LIVE against it -- saturation specific humidity and hence latent heat, net longwave, and sensible heat -- while only the transfer coefficients and the downward radiative and moisture fields are replayed. The source comment gives the reason: naive replay of net heat flux severs the negative feedback that holds sea surface temperature. Evaporation is deliberately NOT recomputed, for moisture conservation, with rescaling precipitation and runoff considered and rejected as no better. Adopt that split in this row's forcing procedure rather than deriving one. Section 59 also removes this row's architecture ambiguity: the loop is required, because offline full-flux is the decided class and it is the class in which nobody owns the partition. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 59f and 59g.

notes:

WHAT REMAINS IS THE SPATIAL HALF ONLY, and the two-band interface question, since `doceanalb(1:2)` is a band array holding one value in both elements like every other surface in the model. PHYS-14 owns that defect class; this row keeps the spatial variation. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 11c. THIS ROW'S PREMISE IS PARTLY WRONG AND ITS INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTS, 2026-08-22. `seamod.f90:155-158` does apply two namelist scalars, and then `radmod.f90:2895-2904` OVERWRITES the open-ocean part with a zenith-dependent formula, so in the default configuration those scalars survive only for the land and sea-ice fractions and `doceanalb` contributes nothing to open water. THERE ARE THREE BRANCHES, by `necham` and `necham6`: the default `necham=1` gives ECHAM-3, `min(0.05/(zmu0+0.15), 0.15)`; `necham6=1` gives Briegleb, which is the same formula cGENIE integrates in `ocean_alb.F`; both zero gives the constant. SO THE SPATIAL VARIATION THIS ROW ASKS TO COST IS ALREADY PRESENT AND ZENITH-DRIVEN, and what is available is a free A/B between two shipped parameterisations. Flux-weighted daily means: they agree within about ten percent at high sun -- 0.058 against 0.052 at the equator, 0.075 against 0.079 at 45 degrees equinox -- and diverge to 1.64x at 45 degrees solstice and 1.82x at 60 degrees winter, because ECHAM-3's cap binds above 79.5 degrees zenith and Briegleb has no ceiling. THE DIVERGENCE REGION IS LARGER HERE: at 32 degrees obliquity against Earth's 23.4 more of the year sits in the low-sun regime, and that is the winter hemisphere where sea ice forms. Both zenith branches are spectrally flat, which the source states in a comment rather than denying, so the negative spectral result above is unaffected. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 29 SECTION 11's OCEAN EXEMPTION SURVIVES ITS OWN CORRECTION, 2026-08-24, but for a different reason than stated. That is larger than the 0.002 spectral question this row was closing, and it is a different question -- a defect rather than a design choice. title: Orogen places the ice that carves this terrain by latitude and dimensionless elevation alone.
description:
Orogen places the ice that carves this terrain by latitude and dimensionless elevation alone. At the build's `glacialErosion` of 0.8 the ice line falls at 58 degrees latitude, positioned by the erosion slider and nothing else, and the altitude gate is in the model's elevation parameter so the snowline tracks maximum relief, which scales as 1/g, rather than a freezing altitude set by lapse rate and surface temperature. `glacIdx` consults no temperature at all: not the K2.5V spectrum, not the 32 degree obliquity, not the 30 hour rotation, and not even Orogen's own temperature field, which `computeTemperature` produces after `runPostProcessing` has already eroded. All three leading parameters point the same way, toward less polar ice than an Earth-tuned 58 degree threshold gives

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. The correction needs no new physics, but NOT the field first proposed here. `glac` is identically zero across all twelve bins and all 8,192 cells while the run manifest records `"glaciers": true`, and `snd` peaks at 0.29 m, which is seasonal snow. That zero is a fact about the grid, not the planet: the sub-grid peak excess `orog_max - orog_mean` on land averages 1.065 km and 2.969 km at the 90th percentile, so at the measured warm-season lapse rate of 7.372 K/km the model evaluates its own high ground about 7.8 K too warm on average and 21.9 K too warm in the top tenth, and no ice survives that. USE INSTEAD the warmest-month surface temperature, which is smooth and genuinely resolved at T42, corrected to each mesh region's own elevation through `lib/lapse.py`'s freezing-height criterion. `maps/build_basemap.py` lines 379-385 already implement exactly this for the basemap's ice shading. Measured that way, land below freezing in the warmest month goes from 0.002% on the model's orography to 1.657% on the 15.19 km mesh, and `analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py` is the registered computation. Raising the model truncation is not the alternative: T85 is about 150 km against a 7.59 km mesh, so the peak excess stays sub-grid at any resolution the model can afford. Drive `glacIdx` from that mask instead of `polarDist` and close it through loop A, which exists to feed a commissioned climate into the next generation; the terrain-before-climate ordering that blocks it inside one pass is not a constraint across iterations. SHAPE OF THE FIX, decided 2026-08-20: an ice mask consumed AT GENERATION like the carve list, `--ice-mask FILE`, not a post-hoc terrain alteration. Glacial, hydraulic and thermal erosion share one iteration loop and a mid-loop priority flood at `GLACIAL_MID_FLOOD_FRAC` exists to cut outlets through the depressions glaciation makes, so a separate later pass would leave them undrained and move the drainage network and the basin catalogue. Bootstrap with `--glacial 0`, an honest null, then commission and regenerate with the mask. Two constraints on it: mapping `glac` from the ExoPlaSim grid back to the mesh is a rule 3 crossing and must go by index or a shared coordinate source, and per `docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md` a current ice field can only say WHERE ice was, never how long, so the strength slider stays a declared choice rather than a measurement. Subsumes the mechanism half of GRAV-6 [step: orogen]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: this row is also upstream of any ice sheet mass balance, not only of the carve terrain. Every candidate scheme in this class drives ablation from surface temperature, which makes the 7.8 K mean and 21.9 K top-tenth warm bias measured here the single most damaging input error such a scheme can be given. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4 LADDER-PROOF, 2026-08-24, which upgrades this row from a correction to the permanent instrument. At 1.20 Earth radii the circumference is 48,090 km, so the ladder gives cell widths of 751 km at T21, 376 at T42, 188 at T85, 125 at T127 and 94 at T170 -- against a 7.60 km Orogen mesh. The top of the ladder is still twelve times coarser than the terrain the ice sits on, so the 1.065 km mean and 2.969 km 90th-percentile sub-grid peak excess stays sub-grid at EVERY rung this project will run. glac = 0 is therefore a permanent property of the model's orography rather than a statement about the world, and no resolution converts it into one. This row's mesh diagnostic is not a stopgap until the grid improves: it is the answer, and the model's glacier module is carried for its orographic feedback on cells it can resolve rather than as the instrument that locates ice. Same class of argument as the offline ocean decision -- the quantity wanted lives at a scale the atmosphere will not be run at. notes/glacier-rough-pass.md, extension 2026-08-24.

title: Snow, glacier ice and sea ice albedo are spectrally FLAT and solar-weighted
description:
Snow, glacier ice and sea ice albedo are spectrally FLAT and solar-weighted, and they are the only surface endmembers never re-derived for this star. `plasimmod.f90:428-432` declares `dsnowalbmx(2) = 0.8`, `dsnowalbmn(2) = 0.4` and `dglacalbmn(2) = 0.6` -- two-element BAND arrays initialised from a scalar, so the simulation's snow reflects identically either side of the 0.75 um split. That is the same defect `config/planet.yaml` records having fixed for vegetation, where "one identical field used to assert that a canopy reflects equally either side of the split". It also means the k25v spectrum fix did nothing for snow: the two-band machinery carries a star's shape by moving flux BETWEEN bands, and moving flux between two equal numbers changes nothing. THE DERIVATION IS DONE AND THE NUMBERS ARE IN THE NOTE. `exoplasim/surfacespecs.py` ships the ECOSTRESS blends the constants came from, `iceblendmax`, `iceblendmin`, `glacalbmin`, `seaicemax` and `seaicemin`, interpolated to the same 965 wavelengths `k25v.dat` uses, and only `pRT.py` reads them. Weighted by a 5772 K Planck they reproduce 0.8, 0.4 and 0.6 to within 0.016, WHICH IS THE CHECK THAT VALIDATES THE INTEGRAL before anything is concluded from the other column. SIX FOR SIX on that check, the worst by 0.016 and the ocean to three decimals. Weighted by `k25v` the band pairs are 0.983/0.585, 0.508/0.273, 0.764/0.406, 0.892/0.473 and 0.636/0.339, with broadbands 0.736, 0.362, 0.541, 0.631 and 0.451 -- so fresh snow is about 0.064 too bright, old snow 0.038, glacier ice 0.059, MAXIMUM SEA ICE 0.069 and minimum sea ice 0.049, every one in the direction that weakens the ice-albedo feedback at the cold end. Sea ice is the largest single error in the set and the one surface with no configuration key at all, so `dicealbmx` and `dicealbmn` are in this row's scope beside the land three. The OCEAN is exempt and that is a result rather than an omission: `oceanblend` moves 0.070 to 0.068 because water is nearly flat across the split, so it does not earn a key

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 11, `notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md`, `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 31
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and what is left is SHAPE rather than derivation: a provenance-stamped analysis product on `analysis/vegetation_albedo.py`'s pattern, an anchoring convention for the band pair like `vegetation_albedo_bands` so the flux-weighted combination reproduces the broadband value, keys in `config/planet.yaml`, and a decision on the sea ice pair, which belongs to `icemod` rather than `landmod` and has no config key at all today. `iceblendmax` against `iceblendmin` is already the grain and impurity bracket this row asked for, so that is answered too. HIGH LEVERAGE and unchanged: these drive the feedback that dominates the cold end, so this reaches the bare-rock endmember arm, PHYS-13's ice mask, the extreme-cold land fraction capping the design flux, and what the stellar cycle's grand minima are worth [step: surface_albedo, bootstrap_run]. THE SHAPE QUESTION IS SETTLED BY PRECEDENT ON BOTH SIDES, 2026-08-22. ExoCAM's modified CLM sets `albice(numrad) = (/ 0.80, 0.55 /)`, land ice albedo by waveband, under a header saying the CLM defaults are too high and citing Paterson (1994) p.59 for a FULL-SPECTRAL value of about 0.5 with CAM3 and Pritchard et al. (2008) as precedent. Two things follow. The two bands hold DIFFERENT numbers in an independent implementation, which confirms the flat arrays here are anomalous rather than conventional. And the values are anchored against a stated full-spectral target, which is the same convention `vegetation_albedo_bands` already uses -- so the anchoring rule this row needed is settled: the band pair reproduces the broadband value, and the broadband value is the one derived from the spectrum. As a sanity check the numbers line up the right way: section 11's `glacalbmin` gives 0.766/0.455 under the Sun against CLM's 0.80/0.55, lower because `glacalbmin` is the GLACIAL MINIMUM blend, old or dirty ice, while Paterson's 0.5 is a general glacier figure. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 22. A PREDICTOR THIS MODEL DOES NOT HAVE FOR SNOW, AND IT IS WORTH AS MUCH AS THE ONE IT DOES, 2026-08-22, and ORTHOGONAL to the spectral reweighting this row already settled. ExoPlaSim's snow albedo is a linear ramp in SURFACE TEMPERATURE between 263.16 K and `tmelt`, `landmod.f90:394-405`, blended by forest fraction, with no zenith term. ClimaLand's is `min(1 - beta*(rho_snow/rho_liq - x0), 1) * (alpha_0 + d_alpha*exp(-k*cos_z))` -- zenith angle and snow density as a grain-size proxy, with no temperature term. Disjoint predictors for the same physics. At ClimaLand's calibrated `alpha_0 = 0.59`, `d_alpha = 0.40`, `k = 1.96` and the density factor 0.874 at 330 kg/m3, the ZENITH TERM SPANS 0.565 TO 0.865, a range of 0.30, against this model's ENTIRE temperature range of 0.40 from `dsnowalbmn` to `dsnowalbmx`. Flux-weighted daily means at 32 degrees obliquity run 0.599 at the equator equinox to 0.783 at 60 degrees winter, an 0.18 swing that is absent, largest in the winter hemisphere at high latitude where the snow is. NOTE THE INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IT EXPOSES: section 29 established that ExoPlaSim applies a zenith-dependent albedo to open ocean BY DEFAULT, so the same physical effect is present for one surface and absent for another inside one model, and both cases live in the same low-sun regime. ClimaLand's values are Earth solar-spectrum calibrations and do not transfer; the form and the magnitude argument do. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 37b-c. THE MISSING PREDICTOR IMPLEMENTED, PLUS A DUST PATH, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/sic/surface_par_sic.f90:111-260` carries two snow-albedo schemes -- Warren-Wiscombe and Dang et al. (2015) -- BOTH taking prognostic grain size AND dust concentration, with grain size corrected for solar zenith angle. Snow grain size is a prognostic in the restart. That is section 37's missing zenith predictor implemented in an EMIC, with a second predictor beside it this project has no representation of at all. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 43f SCOPE MADE CONCRETE 2026-08-24. The derivation is done and validated; what this row delivers is four things and no new physics. (1) analysis/ice_albedo.py writing analysis/ice_albedo.json, on analysis/vegetation_albedo.py's pattern: re-weight iceblendmax, iceblendmin, glacalbmin, seaicemax and seaicemin from vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/surfacespecs.py against k25v, split at 0.75 um, provenance-stamped with spectrum sha256, library, spectra_used and a band recombination residual. The Sun-weighted column is the BUILT-IN test that can fail: it must reproduce 0.8, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7 and 0.5, six for six with the worst at 0.016. (2) The anchoring convention, matching vegetation_albedo_bands against vegetation_albedo: the band pair's star-flux-weighted combination reproduces the broadband value, and the broadband value is the one derived from the spectrum. (3) Keys in config/planet.yaml for all five. (4) The sea ice pair specifically, dicealbmx and dicealbmn, which live in icemod rather than landmod and have NO configuration key today -- that is scope this row ADDS rather than inherits. THE ROUTE IS NOT THE PYTHON API: exoplasim/__init__.py exposes only snowicealbedo, one scalar for all snow AND ice, which flattens the entire set. Namelist writes or a fork change. THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY LIVE, which is why this binds: the project sets two_band_albedo: true and runs at NSIMPLEALBEDO = 0, so the two-band path is on and does nothing for these surfaces because both bands hold one number. Landing values, K2.5V band1/band2 against the current constant: snow max 0.983/0.585 vs 0.8, snow min 0.508/0.273 vs 0.4, glacier 0.764/0.406 vs 0.6, sea ice max 0.892/0.473 vs 0.7, sea ice min 0.636/0.339 vs 0.5. Every one currently too bright, one-signed against the ice-albedo feedback at the cold end, and in the SAME direction as OCN-21's now-declared ice-motion term. THE ZENITH PREDICTOR IS OUT OF SCOPE and now has its own row, world-spd; this row is the spectral reweighting only.
close_reason: OVERTURNED 2026-08-24, and replaced by what checking it found. THE PREMISE IS FALSE: radmod.f90:600-790 already carries these five blends as Fortran arrays over the same 965 wavelengths, weights each by the configured stellar spectrum, splits at 0.75 um and assigns dsnowalb, dsnowalbmn, dsnowalbmx, dicealbmn, dicealbmx and dglacalbmn. radini runs at plasim.f90:513, BEFORE surfini reads any surface namelist, so the flat two-element declarations at plasimmod.f90:428-432 are defaults that are overwritten before they are used. The run says so: 'Finalized Albedos' in run_2b20e3324bb0 records snow max 0.968/0.585, sea ice max 0.879/0.473 and glacier 0.752/0.406. The bands hold different numbers and they are this star's, so the simulation's snow does NOT reflect identically either side of the split and the k25v fix DID reach it. What sections 11a-11c established is narrower than they claimed: it is surfacespecs.py, the PYTHON copy, that nothing weights. The error was reading declarations without checking a run. NO KEYS ARE ADDED, and that is the substantive half of this verdict rather than a saving. Writing config values for these would freeze the constants against the spectrum and override a computation that is correct in form -- so the shape work this row's scope described is not deferred, it is WRONG. WHAT REPLACED IT: analysis/ice_albedo.py, registered as the ice_albedo step, which reproduces radmod's arithmetic to machine precision and measures the one real fault it exposes -- a numerator on the 965-point grid divided by a denominator on the 2048-point grid, band 1 low by 1.47 percent relative on every surface, one-signed DARKER. That is world-a0y. The orthogonal zenith predictor is world-spd. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 11d and 11e.

title: Soil albedo carries no moisture dependence
description:
Soil albedo carries no moisture dependence, and the blocker is a missing state variable rather than a missing parameterisation. `dalbclim1` and `dalbclim2` at `landmod.f90:118-119` are PRESCRIBED STATIC fields on the same 0.75 um band split this project uses, and this project's own albedo products are moisture-blind too -- `analysis/rock_albedo.py`, `analysis/playa_albedo.py` and the surface-class builder all lack a wet/dry axis. Wet ground is darker than dry ground, so on land with a strong seasonal wetting cycle this is a seasonal albedo term with no representation. The parameterisation is standard: ClimaLand's `CLMTwoBandSoilAlbedo` after Lawrence and Chase (2007) is `alpha_band = alpha_dry*(1-S_e) + alpha_wet*S_e` on exactly that band pair, so it drops into the existing structure. WHAT IS ABSENT IS `S_e`: it is the effective saturation over the top 0.02 m, and ExoPlaSim's land is one scalar bucket with no depth, so there is nothing to evaluate it from

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 39
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and BLOCKED on LSHY-3, which is the only route to a near-surface saturation; nothing here is actionable before a land column exists, and this row is the reason to note that LSHY-3 enables a CLIMATE feedback and not only a hydrological one. WHEN UNBLOCKED the deliverable is the dry/wet endmember pair per surface class under this star, derived the way BIO-18 and PHYS-14 derive theirs, and NOT the Earth MODIS fields those references carry -- their values are spatially varying Earth calibrations and only the FORM transfers [step: vegetation_albedo, surface_albedo] IT SHARES DUST-17'S ARTIFACT AND MUST NOT DEFINE A SECOND. DUST-17 already specifies the top emitting-layer LIQUID water state this needs -- emitting depth, gravimetric conversion from LSHY-1 bulk density and texture, frozen water, capillary and groundwater wetting, inundation and wet/dry mosaic area -- and explicitly forbids "a second central hydrology". A near-surface saturation defined here would BE that second hydrology. So this row consumes DUST-17's state rather than deriving one, and the depth conversion is already stated once in `aeolian/config/dust.yaml:108-120` and reaches the model as the single namelist constant `dustwcv`. THE TWO ROWS DIFFER ONLY IN THE DEPTH THEY READ AT: Fecan's threshold correction and CLM's albedo saturation are both surface-skin quantities but need not share one number, so the emitting depth and the albedo depth are separate declarations off one profile. NOT A GAP, checked 2026-08-22: pedology takes RUNOFF rather than soil moisture for weathering and `build_soil.py:301-303` argues it -- leaching needs water to drain through the profile, and rain that falls and evaporates carries nothing -- so soil formation is a deliberate choice here and not an omission

title: Integrate Penman over the diurnal cycle rather than evaluating it at 12-bin means
description:
Integrate Penman over the diurnal cycle rather than evaluating it at 12-bin means

Source: `hydrography/scripts/carve_verdict.py`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17. Saturation vapour pressure is convex at about 6.7%/K, so the daily mean of e_s exceeds e_s of the daily mean and a bin-mean evaluation understates the deficit that drives Penman -- Jensen, and one-signed. The range is measured from the model's own `maxt` and `mint`, 8.08 K land-mean and 12.32 K at p90, and a sinusoid between them is integrated at 24 points; `delta` gets the same treatment, since a diurnal-mean e_s with a point-evaluated slope would be inconsistent in the flattering direction. Worth +0.59% on land-mean Penman, about half the +1.2% estimated, because the convexity is on the DEFICIT and Penman's radiative term dilutes it. Carve 1725 -> 1721. DIRECTION: the audit was right and I was wrong -- it raises E and closes basins, the SAME direction as PHYS-4, which only looked opposite while PHYS-4's stable premise still stood. Kept regardless of size: the diurnal cycle exists

title: Register standard LPJ-GUESS versus LPJ-GUESS-HYD as a no-retuning structural sensitivity
description:

Source: `biosphere/notes/plant-hydraulics-groundwater-audit.md` findings 1, 7 and 8
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; blocked on BIO-23, PLHY-2 through PLHY-4, GRAV-7, BIO-12/BIO-14, DEMO-4 and explicit permission for LPJ-GUESS runs; capacitance, turgor-limited growth, drought leaf shedding and biotic mortality remain declared omissions of the bracket [step: vesper_pfts, lpj_run, soil, surface_albedo]. A UNIT TRAP THIS PORT WILL HIT, AND A REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `plant_hydraulics.jl` is an independent implementation of what this row ports: the plant as a Darcy medium, `F = -K_eff*((psi2-psi1)/(z2-z1) + 1)` at `:197` with a harmonic-mean conductivity, and a Weibull vulnerability curve `K = K_sat*exp(-(psi/psi63)**c)` at `:256` after Liu (2020) and Sperry (2016), both per-PFT. THE TRAP IS THE UNIT. That gravitational term is written as a bare `+1`, which is right only because `psi` is in metres of HEAD, and head is `P/(rho*g)`, so the convention absorbs gravity and hides it. `toml/default_parameters.toml:49-53` stores `psi_63 = -408.163...` whose own description reads "Computed by -4 / 0.0098. Holtzman's original parameter value is -4 MPa" -- 0.0098 MPa/m being `rho*g` at EARTH gravity. So the stored number is a plant property times Earth. The same -4 MPa here is -312.26 m of head, exactly `1/1.306` of it. AND THE USE SITE MAKES IT WORSE: `soil_moisture_stress.jl:82` converts back with `psi*rho_water*grav`, so carrying `psi_63 = -408.16` forward while setting `grav` to 12.81 commits the error TWICE and presents the stress function with -5.22 MPa where the literature says -4. THE RULE TO CARRY: any plant-hydraulics parameter published as a PRESSURE and stored as a HEAD carries the gravity of whoever stored it, and nothing in the stored value says so. Failure-mode class 32 in its unit form. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 41. AND AN INDEPENDENT MODEL PUTS THE SAME CEILING IN A MORTALITY TERM, 2026-08-22. FATES uses `grav_earth` in exactly two places and one is plant hydraulics, as the gravitational head of the plant water column. At 12.81 m/s2 that head term rises 30.7 percent, raising the fractional loss of conductivity at a given soil water potential and therefore raising hydraulic-failure mortality -- **effectively capping tree height through a mortality rate rather than an allometric limit**. That is section 41c's hydraulic ceiling arriving by a second route in a second model, which strengthens the case for treating it as physics rather than as an allometric convention. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 54d

title: The no-soilmap fallback reads uninitialised memory into per-layer soil thermal properties.
description:
The no-soilmap fallback reads uninitialised memory into per-layer soil thermal properties. `modules/soilinput.cpp:696-772` `soil_parameters()` -- the path taken when `file_soilmap` is unset -- never writes `porosity_gridcell[]`, `org_frac_gridcell[]` or `min_frac_gridcell[]`, and `Soiltype()` does not initialise them. With `iforganicsoilproperties 1` and any soilcode other than 8, `modules/soil.cpp:3319-3321` reads those arrays into the per-layer heat capacity and thermal conductivity. Separately at `:735`, `soiltype.wtot` indexes `data[soilcode - 1][1]`, an out-of-bounds read at soilcode 0

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 57
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NOT EXERCISED in the live configuration, which passes `file_soilmap` -- so this is a latent trap on a documented and reachable fallback rather than a live defect. Fix or fail closed: an unset soilmap should refuse rather than proceed on uninitialised thermal properties [step: lpj_run] SOURCE CHANGE LANDED 2026-08-22 AND NOT COMPILED, so this row is blocked on a build rather than on effort. Fixed AND fail-closed. `soilinput.cpp:736` rewrites `wtot` as `gawc[0]+gawc[1]+gwp[0]+gwp[1]`, which is an identity rather than a guess -- `SoilInput::get_soil` computes it exactly that way at `:651` -- so the out-of-bounds index is gone rather than corrected. `:764-780` fills the three per-layer arrays from the same table entries the scalar `organic_frac`, `porosity` and `mineral_frac` two lines above already use, which is the degenerate case of what `get_soil` derives from a `SoilC` column and invents nothing. `guess.h` gains `UNSET_SOIL_FRAC = -1.0` and both read sites in `soil.cpp` refuse on the sentinel, a zero default having been a different silent-wrong. Every input path was checked so the guard cannot fire on a valid configuration. CORRECTION 2026-08-22: this is NOT clearable by a recompile. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree at all -- `framework/vesper.h` is a GENERATED header, and `pipeline.py --plan vesper_header` runs the chain to it through `baseline_run` and `baseline_climatology`, neither of which exists. So this row sits behind the same baseline run as CLIM-71, not behind a compile, and nothing here is verified by execution. Do not fit the header against the bootstrap climatology to make a build succeed; BIO-19 owns that ambiguity and choosing a climatology to serve a compile is not a way to settle it.
