title: Close accepted seasonal methane fluxes, including any separately conserved OCN-13 marine
description:
Close accepted seasonal methane fluxes, including any separately conserved OCN-13 marine source, through BVOC-6's Vesper oxidant/transport bracket: solve lifetime, OH feedback, atmospheric imbalance and global/latitudinal CH4, feed only a converged provenance-bound abundance to ExoPlaSim's radiative band, and prohibit combining modelled sources with the fixed-modern-Earth-flux 1.6 ppmv state

Source: `biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md` finding 10, `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8d
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; reduced chemistry interface follows WET-8/BVOC-6 and admits OCN-13 only as a named source, not a second atmospheric owner; replacement of `pCH4_bar` and every chemistry/climate response experiment require accepted closure and explicit permission [step: lpj_run, baseline_climatology, baseline_run]. A reduced form of the LIFETIME half exists and this row should be costed against it: `references/climber-x/src/ch4/ch4_model.f90` is a partitioned-lifetime box, tropospheric OH against separate chlorine, soil and stratospheric sinks, with an OH temperature sensitivity and OH sensitivities to CO, NOx and VOC precursors. The STRUCTURE transfers and the calibration does not: the precursor sensitivities are fitted to anthropogenic Earth emissions read from a file, the chlorine term is Earth stratospheric chemistry, and the OH field is a photochemical product of the host's ultraviolet -- which for this star is not an open question, since `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` already records that Rugheimer et al. (2013) computed the photochemical steady state at this effective temperature. A constant respiration fraction still yields a flux and never an abundance, so `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` stays this row's alone. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f. A ROUTE, NOT JUST A FLOOR, 2026-08-22. `vendor/cgenie/genie-atchem/atchem_box.f90` carries six methane oxidation schemes. The default is Osborn and Wigley (1994), `tau = tau0*(CH4/C0)**N`, with the comment "omitting [OH], [NOx] etc etc" and a clamp at half the reference concentration where the calibration curve ends. **`sub_calc_oxidize_CH4_schmidt03` is the same functional form with the constants EXPOSED** as `par_pCH4_oxidation_tau0`, `C0` and `N` rather than hardcoded, and its header names its calibration: a fit to the 2-D photochemistry model of Schmidt and Shindell (2003). So this row's oxidant and lifetime half reduces to DERIVING THREE NUMBERS from a photochemistry calculation for this host -- and `atmosphere.pCH4_bar` already records that Rugheimer et al. (2013) computed the photochemical steady state at this effective temperature, which is the same class of calculation. The conservation structure comes with it and is what this row wants: `O2 -= 2*fracdecay*CH4`, `CO2 += fracdecay*CH4` with 13C and 14C carried, `CH4 *= (1-fracdecay)`, per grid cell rather than as a global box. LEAVE THE `claire06` AND `goldblatt06` FAMILIES ALONE: they take a whole-atmosphere conversion factor with no grid indices and are Archean anoxic-atmosphere formulations, built for a kind of planet this one is not. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 20a. THE MASS-TO-CONCENTRATION CONVERSION IS A PLANET PROPERTY AND MUST BE DERIVED, NOT INHERITED, 2026-08-22. Any box-model methane budget needs a Tg-to-ppb factor, and CLIMBER-X's `src/ch4/ch4_model.f90:40` derives its 2.7476 Tg CH4 per ppb from EARTH's atmospheric mass of 5.1480e18 kg (IPCC, Prather et al. 2012). Column mass is `P/g` over `4*pi*R^2`, so with this world's 1 bar summed from `planet.yaml`'s partial pressures, 1.20 Earth radii and 12.81 m/s2, the atmosphere is 1.088x Earth's and the factor becomes 2.990 Tg CH4 per ppb: A GIVEN SOURCE IN Tg/yr PRODUCES ABOUT 92 PERCENT OF THE ppb IT WOULD ON EARTH. The same rescaling applies to any N2O or CO2 budget. ALSO A SPIN-UP CONSTRAINT for the seasonal budget this row closes: CLIMBER-X derives peat potential from a THIRTY-YEAR inundation memory, a 360-month ring buffer at `src/lnd/lnd_params.f90:379`, so a peat fraction cannot be established from one model year. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42b and 42d. THE LIFETIME IS COMPUTABLE AND THE DOOR IS NAMED, 2026-08-22. CAABA/MECCA carries the sink as real chemistry -- `CH4 + OH` with a modified-Arrhenius rate, OH from `H2O + O1D`, O1D from ozone photolysis -- and carries NO prescribed lifetime anywhere, so it must be derived offline as `1/(k*[OH])`. THE BLOCKING QUESTION IS ANSWERED NEGATIVELY FOR JVAL: its fitted cross-section coefficients were generated with a hardcoded 176-element ATLAS-2 SOLAR spectrum as the integration weight, so a different star needs that array replaced and the preprocessor re-run over a 19,393-line generated file. THE TRACTABLE DOOR IS CLOUDJ: `input/cloudj/FJX_spec.txt` holds the solar photon flux as EIGHTEEN NUMBERS in a text file, and CAABA accepts `photrat_channel='cloudj'`. CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: whether CLOUDJ has ever been exercised in this release is NOT determined -- there is no `caaba_cloudj.nml` and no testsuite entry where RADJIMT and TRAJECT both have one. Build-check before planning around it. SEPARATELY, `messy_jval.f90:1544` converts pressure to overhead column as `N_A/(M_air*g)` with Earth gravity, making every O2 and O3 slant column 1.306x too large here regardless of spectrum. AND THE SCOPE LIMIT: a box model gives a LOCAL chemical destruction rate, not a global lifetime -- that needs the local rate weighted over the atmosphere's mass and OH distribution, an offline integration over an ExoPlaSim climatology using a grid of box results. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 48

description:
Derive one mutually exclusive native-mesh wetness classification and seasonal area artifact: persistent peat-forming land, saturated non-inundated mineral soil, seasonal inundation, open lake/river/playa water and dry mineral soil; use hydrography, native groundwater state and sub-grid topography, aggregate fractions rather than thresholds, close against BIO-11's rootable surface and forbid latitude selection or double counting

notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; interface/area-closure work extends PLHY-5 and can proceed without LPJ-GUESS, while the groundwater driver must preserve persistence and seasonality rather than expose mean coarse-cell depth alone [step: hydrography, groundwater, soil, lpj_driver]. WET-12 names the reduced form of this classification, which is the TOPMODEL saturated fraction from GW-26's index; it is the part of the fallback that forfeits least, and mutual exclusivity is what it gives up. WHY THE LATITUDE PROHIBITION BITES, PRICED 2026-08-22. The fork's decomposition already selects by latitude and the step is large: `somdynam.cpp` gives a saturated mineral soil a moisture modifier of 0.360 on every pool, against 0.025 on the slow and passive pools for a high-latitude peatland stand, a factor of 14.4 on the long-lived carbon, switched at `PEATLAND_WETLAND_LATITUDE_LIMIT = 40.0`. NOTE ALSO that the general curve, Friend et al. (1997) Eqn 53 after Parton et al. (1993), BOTTOMS OUT AT 0.360 at full saturation rather than falling to zero -- so on that curve alone saturation does not preserve carbon, and the classification this row derives is doing all the work. THE MECHANISTIC ALTERNATIVE that needs no category: ClimaLand's DAMM implementation limits respiration by oxygen as `theta_a**(4/3)` through a Michaelis-Menten factor, so anoxia is a computed consequence of air-filled porosity rather than a stand type. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 34. THE INUNDATION SCHEME IS SMALLER THAN EXPECTED AND ITS COST IS PREPROCESSING, 2026-08-22. CaMa-Flood's ENTIRE floodplain representation is one precomputed array per cell -- a TEN-BIN CDF OF HEIGHT ABOVE NEAREST DRAINAGE, stored at each decile of flooded AREA -- turned at init into a storage-versus-level curve of ten nested prisms. The runtime prognostic state is TWO SCALARS, channel and floodplain storage; depth, flooded fraction and area are all diagnostic, recovered by walking the storage bins. The closure making it work is that channel and floodplain share one water surface elevation. THE COST IS NOT THE PHYSICS: `fldhgt` is not generated anywhere in the CaMa tree -- it comes from an external DEM upscaling package -- so adopting this means writing the HAND-CDF preprocessor against the region mesh ourselves. AND HAND DOES NOT EXIST HERE: `build_hydrography.py` computes level/area/volume curves at 128 levels but PER CLOSED BASIN from the priority-flood ordering, which is a lake curve. CaMa's is per routing cell keyed on height above the channel. Different quantity, same word. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 52a

title: Separate methane production and oxidation from the fork's globally tuned respiration ratios
description:
Separate methane production and oxidation from the fork's globally tuned respiration ratios: consume vertically resolved substrate, temperature, saturation/redox and electron-acceptor state from SDEC-3/SDEC-8, preserve the existing carbon subtraction/checks, expose production and oxidation independently, and retain the detailed 0.085 and simple 0.027 ratio models only as named Earth structural bounds rather than latitude regimes

Source: `biosphere/notes/wetlands-peat-methane-audit.md` finding 6
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; reduced operator and conservation fixtures follow WET-4/SDEC-3/SDEC-8; parameter-response experiments require accepted hydrology/vegetation and explicit permission [step: soil, groundwater, lpj_run]. WET-12 names the reduced form, a constant anaerobic respiration fraction, and records that it forfeits exactly what this row exists to expose: production and oxidation cease to be separable. SUBSTRATE AND REDOX HAVE A MECHANISTIC REFERENCE FORM, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand implements DAMM, Davidson et al. (2012), in `Soil/Biogeochemistry/co2_parameterizations.jl`: respiration is `Vmax(T) * MM_sx * MM_o2` with substrate `Sx = p_sx*Csom*D_liq*theta_l**3` and oxygen availability `D_oa*O2_f*theta_a**(4/3)` on Millington-Quirk tortuosity, each entering through its own Michaelis-Menten factor. That gives limitation at BOTH ends of the moisture range from two separate mechanisms, against this fork's single empirical humped curve plus a categorical override. It is the shape this row's vertically-resolved substrate/saturation/redox consumption would take. CANOPY ALBEDO DEPENDS ON THE SINGLE-SCATTERING ALBEDO `alpha + tau`, NOT ON REFLECTANCE ALONE: a leaf transmitting strongly in the near-infrared raises omega_NIR without raising omega_PAR, so the canopy keeps more of its NIR albedo relative to PAR than the leaf does, and since a K dwarf moves flux INTO the near-infrared that AMPLIFIES the correction rather than diluting it. ClimaLand's `pfts.jl` carries the missing column, CLM5.0 Table 2.3.1 giving `tau_NIR/alpha_NIR` of 0.286 needleleaf, 0.556 broadleaf tree and 0.971 GRASS. Running this project's own band pair through the semi-infinite similarity result gives canopy k25v/sun ratios of 1.1379, 1.1848 and 1.2226 against the leaf-level 1.1501 -- SO THE STATED BOUND HOLDS FOR ONE OF THREE CLASSES AND FAILS FOR THE OTHER TWO, grass included, which is where this project's per-class table already shows the largest shift at 0.303 to 0.333. THIS DOES NOT GIVE A CANOPY RATIO and must not be used as one: the similarity result carries no leaf angle distribution, no clumping, no soil background, no finite LAI and no direct/diffuse split, and the transmittances are an Earth calibration. It establishes only that the SIGN is not determined by leaf reflectance alone, so the bracket's upper end may not be an upper end. Settling it needs leaf TRANSMITTANCE, which a reflectance library does not carry -- a data gap rather than a derivation gap. THE CLASS DEPENDENCE RUNS ALONG THIS ROW'S OWN TREE/GRASS SPLIT, which makes the separate endmembers more necessary than the row currently argues. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 38

title: The calendar port left climate.mtemp on a hardcoded 31-day window
description:
The calendar port left `climate.mtemp` on a hardcoded 31-day window, and the ported form is two lines below it. `framework/guess.h:956` declares `Historic<double,31> dtemp_31` and `modules/driver.cpp:660` sets `climate.mtemp = climate.dtemp_31.mean()` -- a 31-day mean -- while `:718` reads THE SAME BUFFER the ported way, `dtemp_31.periodicmean(date.ndaymonth[date.month])`. So "month" exists twice in one function, 31 compile-time and 15 runtime. `mtemp` feeds `mtemp_min`/`mtemp_max`, then `mtemp_min20`/`mtemp_max20`, which are the PFT ESTABLISHMENT AND SURVIVAL criteria, and it gates the GDD5 and chilldays reset. THE SIGN IS OPPOSITE TO WHAT THE PORTING AUDIT PREDICTS: that note expects the coldest-month mean to read more extreme because the month is shorter, but the code never uses the month, so a 31-day window over a 183-day orbit DAMPS the seasonal cycle by about 3.55 percent of half-amplitude more than a ported month would -- roughly 1.4 C off the `mtemp_max20 - mtemp_min20` range on a cell with a 40 C annual swing

title: leaflong is read as Vesper orbits in one file and as Earth months in another
description:

(1992) specific leaf area as `sla = 0.2*pow(10, 2.41 - 0.38*log10(12.0*leaflong))`, where the `12.0` converts EARTH YEARS TO EARTH MONTHS. The same `12.0*leaflong` appears at `:2161` for `cton_leaf_min`, and `ctop_leaf_min` derives from that `sla` at `:2175-2178`. At `leaflong 0.5`, which is every summergreen and grass PFT, SLA comes out about 23 to 24 percent low and `cton_leaf_min` about 26 percent high. SLA sets leaf area per kgC, so it propagates into LAI, FPAR, APAR and GPP; the C:N and C:P minima set the whole nutrient limitation cascade

notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, and VERIFIED in the vendored ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 source rather than asserted. Land evaporation is `mkevap`, and its whole dependence on the land surface is `zkdiff = drhs * zkonst1 * dtransh / dt` at `fluxmod.f90:658`: `dtransh` carries roughness, so that channel is real, and `drhs` at `NVEG = 0` is one bucket, `min(1, dwatc/(0.4*dwmax))`, with the five `dsoilz` layers holding temperature rather than water. No root, canopy, interception or stomatal term exists in `landmod.f90`, `fluxmod.f90` or `surfmod.f90`. Two refinements to the claim as written. Forest fraction is NARROWER than it sounded: at `NVEG = 0` it only mixes the snow albedo's forested and unforested endpoints, so it is radiative and reaches evaporation not at all. And there is a FOURTH channel one step removed, `dwmax` from pedology carrying LPJ-GUESS soil carbon, already bounded near-inert at 1.06x on runoff for a 3.75-fold bucket change, so the word "only" needed it. The finding worth more than the task: switching SIMBA on would NOT supply the missing physics. It does couple back at `nveg == 2`, but `dsc`, its "stomatal conductance", is prescribed -- allocated to `rinidsc` at `simba.f90:157`, optionally read as surface code 1606, and never assigned again -- and `dlai` is computed and used nowhere but output. So the absence is a property of the model, not of this project's configuration

title: Define a reduced Vesper oxidant/trace-gas bracket before any central SOA yield
description:
Define a reduced Vesper oxidant/trace-gas bracket before any central SOA yield: drive OH/O3/NO3 chemistry from the K-star UV, water vapour, temperature and adopted soil/fire NOx, return precursor loss plus O3, OH/oxidizing-capacity, CO and methane-lifetime changes, and expose the inconsistency between biosphere-derived BVOC and the current fixed-Earth-flux ozone/CH4 state rather than silently combining them

Source: `biosphere/notes/bvoc-soa-atmospheric-coupling-audit.md` finding 6
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; start with a documented box/reduced-chemistry interface and fixed-yield screening bounds; a closed photochemical state may require machinery outside ExoPlaSim and any model experiment requires explicit permission [step: baseline_climatology, lpj_run]. A REUSABLE SHAPE FOR THE OXIDANT BRACKET, AND ITS LIMIT, 2026-08-22. CLIMBER-X has NO atmospheric chemistry, but `src/ch4/ch4_model.f90:179-183` carries a reduced form this row can take the STRUCTURE of: reciprocal lifetimes added over four sinks -- OH, tropospheric chlorine, soil and stratosphere -- with OH represented by a fitted log-linear surrogate in the methane burden plus NOx, CO and VOC emissions and a linear temperature term. IT IS A SURROGATE FOR OH, NOT OH, and its anchors are two independent Earth baselines, 1056 ppb and 286.83 K. Take the reciprocal-addition shape and the sink decomposition; re-fit or bracket every coefficient. NOTE WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPLY: the VOC term is a prescribed anthropogenic emission series read from file, so this gives a consumption interface and no producer, and ozone there is a prescribed radiative boundary condition that is never an oxidant. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42a. A SECOND REUSABLE FORM, BETTER CONDITIONED, AND ONE FAMILY TO REFUSE, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's `genie-atchem` has six CH4 sink schemes and NONE is photolysis -- one well-mixed box, no OH, the source saying "omitting [OH], [NOx] etc etc". TAKE THE POWER LAWS IN PARTIAL PRESSURE: `tau = tau0*(pCH4/C0)**N`, with `schmidt03` the better-conditioned variant, namelist-settable and calibrated over 1x to 200x C0 against the default's 8x. REFUSE THE POLYNOMIAL EMULATORS: `claire06` and `goldblatt06` fit photochemical output as polynomials in log10 of ABSOLUTE MOLE INVENTORIES in Tmol, not mixing ratios, which anchors them to Earth's atmospheric mass -- 1.088x here per section 42b -- and the source itself warns "neither O2 nor CH4 are truncated at edge of training values here, so USE CAUTION". A TRAP EVEN IF ADOPTING THE DEFAULT: `par_atm_CH4_photochem` defaults to a scheme that reads only compile-time constants, so the three namelist `par_pCH4_oxidation_*` values are SILENTLY IGNORED unless the scheme string is also changed, while the run log prints them as though in force. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 46a. AND A THIRD MODEL, THIS ONE WITH ACTUAL CHEMISTRY, 2026-08-22. Where cGENIE and CLIMBER-X offer parametric lifetimes to take the SHAPE of, CAABA/MECCA offers 2,323 gas-phase reactions of which 414 are photolysis, with OH, O1D and the quenching competition explicit. That makes it the instrument for deriving this row's oxidant bracket rather than another source to fit one from. Its photolysis door and the gravity correction it needs are in `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 48

THE SOURCE IS THE ADIABATIC SPECTRAL STEP, creating +0.345 +/- 0.013 W/m2 where enthalpy and kinetic energy must cancel, 15.6% of the conversion it performs, stable across four window choices. Three identities each with a right answer of zero, and the third is what makes the second mean anything: had the kinetic-energy budget not closed at -0.007, `denergy27` would not be the adiabatic generation. With the term counted the atmospheric budget closes to -0.104 +/- 0.107 against the model's own column enthalpy trend of -0.007, from -0.853 on the flux route alone; -0.20 W/m2 of the planetary residual remains unattributed. The four-run flux leverage is EXHAUSTED and was reported as such rather than read: every fixed-fraction hypothesis predicts a shift below the 0.035 W/m2 run-to-run scatter. No criterion was retrofitted, deliberately: the quantity is resolution- and timestep-dependent by nature, so it stays recorded raw and `close_term_energy.py` must be re-run on the first low-I/O-off block of any T85 run before a T42 number is carried into loop D [step: assess_convergence]

title: The -0.29 W/m2 slab residual is NOT the model
description:
The -0.29 W/m2 slab residual is NOT the model

Source: `exoplasim/notes/water-and-energy-closure.md`, `exoplasim/scripts/close_ocean_energy.py`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the row's own title turns out to be right for a reason nobody had reached: the residual was MEASUREMENT, all of it, in four layers each hiding the next. Three were the instrument. `align` floored `nrec // nbin` when the year is not a whole number of write intervals, worth 13.102 to 0.353. It then used EQUAL-WIDTH bins where pyburn's hold different record counts, 0.353 to 0.191. And the identities took the atmosphere side with `.mean(0)` while the stream side was a record mean, which is CLIM-13 committed two hundred lines below the block that diagnoses it -- D1 0.2016 to 0.0534. The fourth was the DATA. The model writes one record per 24.00 h and this planet's day is 30.00 h, exactly 40 timesteps against 32, so the regular output samples the diurnal cycle at FIVE PHASES forever while the ocean and ice streams accumulate every step and are a true integral. Predicted before the run: raise the sampling and the bias collapses. At NWPD = 8, ten phases and 1462 raw records an orbit against 182, D1 goes +0.0534 to +0.0079 -- a factor of 6.8 against the 2.8 that random noise would give, which is aliasing rather than variance. So the atmosphere and the streams agree to 0.008 W/m2 and the model's surface energy budget closes. D2 through D5 were at machine zero throughout. Found on the way and guarded: the streams follow their own counters and ignore NWPD, so the two sides only share a clock at NWPD = 1 and the closure now refuses any other case rather than tiling bins it does not share a clock with [step: bootstrap_convergence, baseline_convergence]
close_reason: done 2026-08-19, and the row's own title turns out to be right for a reason nobody had reached: the residual was MEASUREMENT, all of it, in four layers each hiding the next.

title: ExoPlaSim DEADLOCKS at NLOWIO = 0 on more than one rank once
description:
ExoPlaSim DEADLOCKS at `NLOWIO = 0` on more than one rank once `exoplasim-3.4.2-lowio-first-record.patch` is resident. `nlowio` is read from `plasim_nl` on NROOT and never broadcast, so the other ranks keep the compiled default of 1; the patch puts `nlowio` into a PER-TIMESTEP condition in `gridpointd` that guards `call mpsum(sqout,NLEV)`, so the non-root ranks take it every step and NROOT every `nafter`, and the ranks desynchronise on step one

Source: `notes/audits/nlowio-collective-deadlock.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Fixed by `exoplasim-3.4.2-nlowio-broadcast.patch`, which broadcasts `nlowio` and `nstpw` in `prolog` beside the `mpbci(nafter)` already there; the low-I/O patch is resident again on top of it and all binaries plus the cycle executable are rebuilt. A full T42 p16 orbit at `NLOWIO = 0` goes from never finishing to 89.7 s, which REPRODUCES the 90 s that `run_manifest.json` recorded for the 2026-08-17 segment -- the check that the fix restores behaviour rather than merely stopping a hang. NEITHER HALF BITES ALONE, which is why it hid: `NLOWIO = 0` was first set at 15:21 and the patch became resident at 22:50 on 2026-08-17, the 23:56 climatology ran `NLOWIO = 0` fine on a binary built before the patch, and the first run carrying both was on 08-18. It was diagnosed as a gcc regression because the system update landed at 01:59 in between, and a private gcc 16.1.1 prefix was built to escape a pessimisation that does not exist -- the three compilers give 77.7, 78.2 and 78.0 s on the same orbit, and the pre-update binary deadlocks identically. The low-I/O patch's real cost is 84.0 s against 78.0 s at `NLOWIO = 1`, about 8%, from the per-timestep humidity transform it deliberately adds. The test that separates all of it is to run the OLD binary under the NEW conditions and takes 78 seconds [step: rebuild_binaries, baseline_run]

title: Ocean horizontal heat diffusion has a namelist switch, nhdiff with hdiffk
description:
Ocean horizontal heat diffusion has a namelist switch, `nhdiff` with `hdiffk`, and the error budget records no-q-flux as STRUCTURAL with "no cheap version exists"

Source: `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 1, `analysis/error_budget.json` other_items
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. The declared 300/1000/3000 bracket ran against a length-matched control, one restart, one binary, fifteen diagnostic orbits each. CONSERVATION HOLDS, which was the prediction's primary claim: every arm's global net TOA difference is consistent with zero and inside the declared 0.3 W/m2, so the term redistributes and cannot be argued for or against on a global-mean flux. The poleward redistribution is confirmed at all three points, 0-20 losing and 40-60 gaining, each 15 of 15 orbits one-signed. The ice-edge term is measured through AREA rather than flux, which is where the signal-to-noise is: at 3000 the arm loses 0.00124 of the planet in sea ice and CLIM-17's conversion puts that at +0.079 to +0.127 K, while at the default the ice change is nothing and the predicted +0.03 to +0.12 K is not resolved and not claimed. THE SPREAD, which is what this row asked for: 40-60 ocean warming +0.13 to +0.19 K at the default and +0.36 to +0.57 K at 3000, each end a separate REALISATION of the same key, and sea ice 0 to -0.00124 of the planet. The realisation-to-realisation span is 35 to 37%, so a single realisation's error bar understates the uncertainty on one of these means by about a third. The method note worth keeping is that the differences must be read PAIRED per orbit -- combining each run's spread in quadrature double-counts the variability both inherit from one restart and inflates the error bars sixfold, which left only the top point resolved. The declared linearity falsifier appeared to fire and DID NOT: CLIM-19's replicate from a different restart put the 300 point below 1000 instead of above it, so the excess was an ice-state draw and linearity holds, 3000 over 1000 coming out 2.99 and 2.89 against a diffusivity ratio of 3.00 [step: baseline_run]

The polynomial is CHECKED against the constant it replaces rather than trusted, and that guard earned itself immediately: written at a 0.005 K tolerance it failed, because the polynomial gives 271.2449 and 271.25 is that rounded, so the tolerance is now the two decimals the model states. Direction carried in the error budget with its bracket: most land here is endorheic, so the exorheic share per unit ocean area is under half Earth's, a fresher ocean freezes WARMER, and the 20-to-34.7 psu span is about 1.1 K on the freezing point. title: The first output bin of every orbit has corrupted WIND and HUMIDITY only
description:
The first output bin of every orbit has corrupted WIND and HUMIDITY only, worsening downward from 1.02 at the model top

Source: `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 14
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, mechanism PINNED to six figures and now class 18. Three defects in the `NLOWIO = 1` path, and the counter was NOT the cause. `plasim.f90:857` and `:1086` save six SPECTRAL accumulators through `mpputgp`/`mpgetgp`, whose dummy is declared `pp(NHOR,klev)`; Fortran reinterprets the `(NESP,NLEV)` array and moves 5,120 of 19,040 elements at T42/L10/p16, so levels 4-10 are restored as ZERO while `naccuout` survives intact at 90 and the first write of each call divides 159 samples by 249. `outmod.f90:394` then subtracts the whole `plavor` from an accumulator holding only 0.638554 of it, leaving `-(1-delta)*plavor` in the (n=1,m=0) vorticity mode -- solid-body rotation, a retrograde 160.8*cos(phi) m/s on levels 4-10. That is the entire wind signature, and it explains every part of it: `ua` only because plavor lives in vorticity, worsening downward because the spurious wind is level-independent while the real one falls, and temperature escaping because `aast` holds the deviation from `t0`. Humidity is separate: `sqout` is recomputed only at output steps but summed every step and is not in the restart, and since 5850 mod 160 = 90 its phase walks with a 16-orbit period, measured at 0.946 correlation over 90 orbits. PREDICTIONS STATED BEFORE MEASURING, which is what makes this a mechanism rather than a story: the surviving coefficients must show no anomaly and the truncated ones must all show the same one, giving delta = 159/249 to six figures with a relative residual of 3e-7; a 6018-step run must give a DIFFERENT constant, predicted -0.127108 and measured -0.127108; orbit 0 of every run must be clean, and it is; and the wind anomaly must be a level-independent `cos(phi)` solid body of -53.59 m/s with nothing fitted, measured -53.44 to -53.56 on levels 3-9. The trap named in the task, `naccuout` persisting while the accumulators do not, was ELIMINATED with evidence: it is restored correctly, and the gridpoint accumulators share the same counter and are clean
close_reason: done 2026-08-17, mechanism PINNED to six figures and now class 18.

title: pyburn's reader was QUADRATIC in record count
description:
pyburn's reader was QUADRATIC in record count: `readallvariables` grew every variable with `variables[kcode] = np.append(variables[kcode],field)` once per record, and np.append reallocates and copies the whole accumulated array each call

Source: `notes/audits/pyburn-postprocessing-cost.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Records are collected per code and joined once with np.concatenate; `readvariablecode` had the same pattern and is fixed with it. One T42 orbit at `NLOWIO = 0`, 2.4 GB raw, driven with the exact kwargs `Model.run()` forwards and unprofiled both ways: 304.0 s to 29.4 s, 10.3x, np.append calls 3,062,749 to 1, and all 123 output variables BITWISE IDENTICAL. It reproduces the pipeline's own history -- `continue_exoplasim.py` records 387 s an orbit and this bench gives 81 s model + 304 s pyburn = 385 s; the same orbit is now 110 s. The triple loops over (time, lat, lon) in the omega/wa/streamfunction branches were vectorised in the same patch and are the smaller half. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG TWICE AND THAT IS THE DURABLE PART: cProfile charged 246 s to 6.0e6 tiny np.append calls in the loops, which is what a profiler costs for six million call events rather than what numpy spends, and the same 246 s actually belonged to the ~81k LARGE appends in the reader -- one function, two callers, call counts three orders of magnitude apart and opposite per-call costs. The ratio was the tell, not the tottime column. Separately, a claim that `example.nl`'s 216 duplicated codes were being processed was an artefact of the measuring harness: pyburn ignores `variables` when a `namelist` is passed, and the pipeline passes none. Consequences: the `NLOWIO = 0` penalty in `continue_exoplasim.py` is much smaller, and the 1.09x for two concurrent 8-rank runs was a workaround for this defect -- run at 16 ranks [step: rebuild_binaries, climatology]

title: Price the interior moisture source: the water a catchment delivers to a closed basin
description:
Price the interior moisture source: the water a catchment delivers to a closed basin evaporates over land in the world `hydrography/` describes and is exported to the ocean in the model, which has no lake, so the moisture source moves off the continent. It is 5.6 to 6.6% of land precipitation, sited in the arid interiors, on a planet whose land is 76.2% endorheic

Source: `notes/audits/unpriced-terms.md` finding 1, `exoplasim/notes/lake-representation.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the measurement DEFLATED it and flipped its sign. `carve_verdict.py` now computes the area-weighted integral every run into `runoff_source.endorheic_inflow`, with an identity that closes to 0.00% -- inflow equals lake net evaporation plus the runoff generated over the lake bed plus what spills to the ocean, those being the only doors out of the endorheic system. Endorheic catchments deliver 69% of land runoff off 76% of the land, credible where the 97% that prompted this was not, and the cause was multiplying an UNWEIGHTED per-basin mean by the total catchment area rather than the clamp, which is worth 4.2%. The substantive correction is that gross lake evaporation is the wrong quantity: what the atmosphere gains from a lake is its evaporation against what the model already evaporates on that ground, and this world's land is several times rougher than open water, so the model's own evaporation exceeds Penman on 2,484 of 4,105 land cells. The term is -2,374 km3/Earth-yr, -0.9% of land precipitation, and NEGATIVE, so the intuitive direction was wrong as well as the size. The estimator uses catchment means rather than lake-footprint values and is biased against the lake; it would have to be wrong by a factor of six to reach what was first claimed. Not a dust-scale item
close_reason: done 2026-08-19, and the measurement DEFLATED it and flipped its sign.

title: Mineral dust is the only aerosol this project has ever considered. No sea salt over an ocean
description:
Mineral dust is the only aerosol this project has ever considered. No sea salt over an ocean that is 57% of the surface, no volcanic sulfate beside the arc classes the pedology treats as continuing, and no mention of either anywhere in the repository

Source: `notes/audits/unpriced-terms.md` finding 2
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the answer is that sea salt is the SAME SIZE as mineral dust and the OPPOSITE SIGN: -0.16 to -0.89 W/m2 of global-mean top-of-atmosphere shortwave forcing across every declared bracket end, against dust's +0.34 to +0.61, and `analysis/error_budget.json` now carries both. Built as a component rather than an estimate: `aeolian/scripts/sea_salt_source.py` (Grythe et al. 2014 eq. 7), `sea_salt_optics.py` (OPAC indices and growth at ambient humidity, Mie on the k25v spectrum) and `build_sea_salt.py` (emission, transport, burden, optical depth, forcing), registered as steps `sea_salt_optics` and `sea_salt`. The EARTH CHECK is a ratio between two published source functions through one machinery, so our wind treatment divides out: Monahan 1986 and G13T come out at 0.705 and 0.680 of Grythe's Table 2 values and those agree to 3.5%. Three optics checks pass, including inverting OPAC's volume mixing to recover water's refractive index at 1.3328 against 1.333. Two results are reported and neither corrects the other, because Grythe's 30 um spume mode's lower tail dominates the mass below the 10 um cut and their own reported production excludes it. COST was correctly estimated as a model change for putting it IN the climate, and that half is not done: the fork refuses two aerosol paths at once on purpose. Two defects found on the way are recorded in the audit -- `hur` is in percent while its units attribute says otherwise, and the shared transport solver is in advective rather than flux form. CLIM-28 carries what is left
close_reason: done 2026-08-19, and the answer is that sea salt is the SAME SIZE as mineral dust and the OPPOSITE SIGN: -0.16 to -0.89 W/m2 of global-mean top-of-atmosphere shortwave forcing across every declared bracket end, against dust's +0.34 to +0.61, and `analysis/error_budget.json` now carries both.

title: Sulfate and volcanic aerosol are still untouched
description:
Sulfate and volcanic aerosol are still untouched, and the arc classes are the one place this pipeline treats volcanism as continuing. Sea salt turned out to be the same size as mineral dust and the opposite sign, so the prior that a second aerosol is negligible is now measured to be wrong once

Source: `notes/audits/unpriced-terms.md` finding 2
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19. Volcanic sulfate is BUILT and MEASURED SMALL: -0.013 to -0.032 W/m2 across every declared bracket end, one to two orders of magnitude below dust and sea salt, from a global-mean optical depth of 0.0035. `aeolian/scripts/build_volcanic_sulfate.py`, step `volcanic_sulfate`, with OPAC's sulfate tables in `exoplasim/data/sulfate/`. The SOURCE IS A COUPLING rather than a scaling and that is the point: Carn et al. (2017)'s satellite-measured passive volcanic SO2 flux scaled by `weathering_fluxes.py`'s own implied outgassing requirement, 1.10x Earth's, distributed over the arc classes the fork places about the volcanic front; the step refuses to run without the weathering artifact rather than falling back to a literal. The scale-height bracket moves the answer not at all, which confirms settling is irrelevant at 0.1 um and wet removal sets it. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT IS MOSTLY WORTH IS THE BOUND: the sulfate pathway here is weak, so reaching sea salt's forcing would need a sulfur flux over ten times Earth's, and that covers both sulfur sources this project cannot compute -- explosive eruptions, which need the eruption history `docs/src/reference/no-time-axis.md` says does not exist, and marine biogenic sulfur, which is Earth's LARGEST natural sulfur source and has no counterpart here because LPJ-GUESS is terrestrial and this project has no marine biosphere at all. `analysis/error_budget.json` carries the item for that reason rather than for its size. CLIM-29 carries what the bound does not reach

title: Decide whether the convergence criterion should test the REPORTED top-of-atmosphere net
description:
Decide whether the convergence criterion should test the REPORTED top-of-atmosphere net or the storage the model state actually shows

Source: `exoplasim/notes/baseline-equilibration.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17 as a DECISION, taken by the user after the evidence was laid out rather than by whoever found it, because choosing a quantity immediately after measuring that the new quantity passes is what `docs/src/practice/conventions.md` forbids. The criterion now tests state storage and the threshold is DERIVED: 0.15 K / (0.128 K per orbit per W/m2 * 9.9 orbits) = 0.118 from the temperature tolerance already committed to, against an estimator that resolves 0.111 to 0.116 W/m2 between 10-orbit and 20-orbit windows of the same run. The two agree to 6% and 0.12 is where they meet, four times tighter than the 0.5 it replaces -- which was itself picked early, never revisited, and applied to two different quantities. The threshold was committed BEFORE re-assessing, in its own commit, so the ordering is in the history rather than asserted. Outcome: the baseline stores -0.0547 and passes, three of four runs pass, and `run_b014469b8091` still fails, on the temperature-offset criterion rather than on energy. THE CHECK ON THE CHANGE: the old criterion passed the run FURTHER from equilibrium, `run_524fbed77a9a` at TOA -0.483 while its heat content rose at +0.084, against the baseline failing at -0.600 while storing -0.055. On storage the two rank the right way round. Reported TOA and its difference from storage stay recorded in every assessment, because that gap is CLIM-1 and a criterion that stopped reading the number would stop anyone noticing it move

`continue_exoplasim.py` labels every seasonal segment `post_equilibrium_climatology`, including a `--low-io` one; and `assess_convergence.py` takes the trailing `--window` orbits with no regard to what a segment was FOR

notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Purpose is DECLARED: `--purpose` is required with no default, because a default is the inference again with fewer places to notice it. `spinup` and `post_equilibrium_climatology` are the run's trajectory; `diagnostic` measures the model, not the planet, and does not move the run's status. THE TWO DEFAULTS RUN OPPOSITE WAYS AND BOTH ARE RIGHT: an unlabelled orbit counts as production, because defaulting it out would refuse to assess every run made before purposes existed, while an unlabelled `low_io` counts as tainted, because there the unlabelled case silently corrupts a field. `segments.py` is now the one reader of the segment list. title: Two comments justify a live rule by a build file the CMake rework deleted
description:
Both are correct rules resting on a stale reason, which is the shape CLAUDE.md's "rewrite superseded content" exists for: a reader checking the justification finds nothing.

1. scripts/smoke_test.py:737, check_omp_directive_line_length:

     The bar is 132, which is what `most_compiler_omp` passes as
     `-ffixed-line-length-132`

   most_compiler_omp was deleted with the make-based build on 2026-08-22, and -ffixed-line-length-132 is not in config/planet.yaml's f90_opts either -- notes/audits/model-build-flags.md measured it and found the executable byte-identical without it, so it left the line. THE BAR IS STILL 132 AND STILL RIGHT, for a better reason than the one stated: these are .f90 files, gfortran compiles them as FREE form, and 132 columns is gfortran's free-form default. That is also why the flag was a no-op. Restate the reason as the language default rather than as a flag nobody passes, so the check does not read as depending on something that could be dropped again.

2. vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/aeromod.f90:275:

     The two variables stay separate because radmod cannot use aeromod: aeromod
     already uses radmod, and make_plasim compiles it second.

   The circular-use argument is right and is the reason `rad_apart => apart` is aliased in rather than the two being merged. make_plasim is gone; the compile order now comes from the _sources list in plasim/CMakeLists.txt, and Ninja scans the use statements. Name that instead. Rule 4 applies to this one: it is model source, so touching it means rebuilding every binary, and it is a comment-only change -- worth batching with the next aeromod edit rather than doing alone.

Not in this issue, because they are deliberate historical explanations and read correctly in the past tense: build_model.py's "WHAT THIS REPLACED" block, rebuild_binaries.py:387, restart_schema.py:72, vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py:72-73, sweep_compiler_flags.py:47 and aerocore.f90:1408.

The escape hatch still earns its place -- the flag sweep uses it, and any re-check of the Legendre filter fold needs -ffp-contract=off on both arms -- so this is the comment and not the mechanism. Do: name the flag sweep and the fold re-check recipe in exoplasim/notes/legendre-filter-fold.md rather than a deleted file. Held out of world-en0's commit because build_model.py belongs to the MPI-removal batch. Source: world-en0

title: A comparison build has no way to name its compiler
description:
exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py:236 sets compiler = 'gfortran' and hands CMake the bare name, so a build takes whichever gfortran is first on PATH. The private toolchain prefix at ~/toolchains/gcc-16.1.1 exists for exactly one purpose, a deliberate compiler comparison, and docs/src/reference/external-data.md states as a standing rule that it is not to go on PATH.

Before world-38b the route was OMPI_FC, read by the MPI wrappers the build invoked. The MPI build is gone, so that route is gone with it, and the prefix currently serves only the standalone probes that take their compiler on the command line.

The build directory tag names every input that changes a byte of the executable, and the compiler is one -- so a --compiler argument has to reach tag() the way --extra-flag does, or two toolchains will land in one directory and reuse each other's objects. binary_manifest.json already records compiler_versions per build, which is the check that the argument took.
acceptance_criteria: A comparison build can name an absolute compiler without putting the prefix on PATH, and two toolchains cannot share a build directory.

title: The cGENIE candidate's genie-plasim carries the fftmod NLON 48 defect world-78e fixed in plasim
description:
vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim/src/fortran/fftmod.f90:9 lists nallowed = (8,16,32,48,64,96,128,256,384,512,1024,2048,4096) and its gp2fc at :44-60 is the same 8 - 4 - (3 or 2) chain the plasim copy has: radix 8, then radix 4 while four or more remain, then ONE radix-3 or radix-2 tail. That is 8 * 4**k * r with r in 1, 2, 3. For n = 48 the tail count is 6, the radix-4 pass fires on it and leaves 1, and neither tail runs, so 32 of the required 48 is applied and fc2gp overshoots the other way. No error either way. The comment at :13 claims 8-3-2, which is not what the loop does.

This is the same defect world-78e fixed in vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/fftmod.f90 and world-clb found in the puma and sam trees before world-6ak deleted those.

Nothing acts on this today. CLAUDE.md's layout records vendor/cgenie as the CANDIDATE offline ocean under OCN-3, not an adopted component: nothing reads it, and it does not build where it stands. genie-plasim is cGENIE's own atmosphere, which is not what the candidate would be adopted for, and T15 is not a rung this project uses. So this is filed to keep the finding rather than to schedule work.

Do: if cGENIE is ever adopted, or if genie-plasim is ever compiled, remove 48 from that table and add the comment world-78e wrote, before any T15 run.

title: vendor/exoplasim/docs documents an install path and functions this fork does not have
description:
vendor/exoplasim/docs is upstream's sphinx documentation for the pip-installable ExoPlaSim package. It describes a configure-and-compile-on-demand install this fork replaced with CMake and build_model.py, and index.rst:149, :188, :273 and :285 tell the reader to call sysconfigure() and printsysconfig(ncpus=...), both of which world-phg deleted along with the most_compiler files they read. index.rst:78 and :113 also advertise randomcontinents and the petitRADTRANS bridge, both deleted under world-569; docs/source/exoplasim.rst was corrected in that commit, index.rst was not.

Ask whether the tree should exist before correcting it. Nothing in this project builds these docs, and a fork whose build, install path and module set all differ has no upstream doc to keep current. Deleting is a fix.

Do: delete vendor/exoplasim/docs, or rewrite index.rst to describe the fork's install and use and say in the tree who builds it.
close_reason: Deleted vendor/exoplasim/docs and .readthedocs.yaml, its only builder. Premise re-verified: index.rst still calls sysconfigure() and printsysconfig() (deleted under world-phg) and advertises randomcontinents and the petitRADTRANS bridge (deleted under world-569), and nothing in this project builds the tree. Deletion rather than rewrite, because a fork whose build, install path and module set all differ has no upstream doc to keep current. One citation depended on it -- a biosphere audit note cited aeromod.rst for the cloud-free-fraction aerosol claim -- and it now cites radmod.f90:2763 and :2827, which is where (1 - dcc) weights every aerosol reflectivity. vendored-upstreams.md records the removal beside the build-system one. Commit 861521b0.

title: The correlated-k bundle's IR and VI band sets do not meet, and 0.00017 of the star's flux falls in the gap
description:
Found by world-134's rewrite of exoplasim/scripts/corrk_cross_check.py, which now computes and names the gap rather than letting it appear as a summation error (corrk_cross_check.py:272-292).

Measured on the 376 ppm table: the IR band set ends at 1974.95 cm-1 and the VI band set begins at 2000 cm-1. The two halves are joined without overlap and do not meet, so a 25.05 cm-1 window sits inside the table span and inside no band. Integrating this star's spectrum over it gives 0.00017 of the flux in the span.

Why this is a finding and not just bookkeeping: flux in the gap is flux the correlated-k tables carry no absorption coefficient for. Wherever the bundle is used to price a band-resolved scheme, that sliver is implicitly treated as transparent in both gas sets. 1.7e-4 is small against the band weights it would perturb, but it is a structural hole rather than a rounding term, and it is at 5 um, between the shortwave and thermal halves, where the two schemes hand over.

Do: establish whether the gap is an artifact of how the bundle was assembled here or is present upstream in the source tables; then either close the two sets against each other, or record the gap as a declared property of the bundle with its flux, so a consumer prices it rather than inheriting it silently. Decide BEFORE clim-61 uses the bundle to price a band-resolved shortwave and longwave.

Do NOT close the gap by widening a band edge to make the arithmetic tidy: the check that found this telescopes exactly for a contiguous partition, and moving an edge to silence it removes the only instrument that can see it.
acceptance_criteria: The gap is either closed in the bundle or declared with its flux fraction in the bundle's own metadata, and corrk_cross_check reports which. clim-61 is not run against an undeclared gap.
close_reason:
Closed by closing the join, in commit f1dbe00d. The gap is NOT a property of the bundle: upstream the two sets OVERLAP -- narrowbands_IR.in runs 10-3000 cm-1 in 40 bands, narrowbands_VI.in 2000-30000 in 38, each contiguous inside itself to the bit, sharing 2000-3000 -- and the Generic PCM never concatenates them, rad_correlatedk_read_opacity_tables.F90:361 setting IR_VI_wnlimit = 3000. and handing WNOI and WNOV to two independent solvers. Both band files are byte-identical between the 376 and 1000 ppm tables. corrk_cross_check.py makes the join itself because it needs one flux-weighted partition, and its cut at a round 2000 was what opened the hole: the IR grid has no edge at 2000, its nearest below being 1974.952011, so dropping every IR band reaching past 2000 dropped the sliver with them.

The join is now the VI set's own first edge, read from the data, and the straddling IR band is truncated to it rather than dropped, keeping its own k-distribution -- the only opacity the bundle carries over that sliver. No edge is widened. The hole detector stays and now RAISES rather than folding the hole into the sum, each half is checked for internal contiguity on load, and the run reports the join and the truncation by name. It reads 0.97204 in 76 bands + 0.00000 in 0 gaps = 0.97204 in one piece.

Two corrections to the issue as filed: 0.00017 is the SOLAR fraction, not this star's, which is 0.00025 because the gap sits at 5 um where the cooler host's boost is about 1.5; and the joined set was 75 bands, not 78, 78 being the two raw sets before the cut.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this took a model edit. --fit reads radmod.f90's four coefficients back out of the source, so the join change showed there as a disagreement. The refit was re-landed: zca1 3.1020E-4, zcb1 19.857, zca2 3.8291E-3, zcb2 3.9587E-3. Absorptance at this planet's CO2 path 0.005027 -> 0.005051, +0.5% and +0.008 W/m2 of Earth-mean insolation, against the fit's own 3.3% rms. Binaries must be rebuilt (world-klr).

clim-61 is unblocked, with one thing to carry: it must NOT inherit this script's join. The two sets are meant to be used separately over their own spans by two solvers, and the 2000-3000 cm-1 overlap the join throws away is real data a thermal scheme wants. Recorded in exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md, section 'The join between the IR and VI sets, and the hole it used to leave'.

title: Derive lake_dwmax_m from the seasonal water balance of the lake cells
description:
world-vus put model.lake_dwmax_m into config/planet.yaml and removed the hardcoded 0.2 m fallback from build_surface_soil_water.py, carrying the value unchanged. The DIRECTION is derived and stated in the config comment -- drhs reaches 1 above 40 percent of dwmax at landmod.f90:52-53, so a shallower bucket saturates the wetness factor on less water, and this planet's lakes sit in arid cells where the water to fill a deep bucket is not there. The VALUE is not.

The derivation: the depth at which a lake cell's own seasonal precipitation keeps its soil water above 0.4 * dwmax through its driest output bin. That needs per-cell seasonal precipitation and evaporation over the lake cells, so it needs a baseline climatology; config/planet.yaml carries baseline_climatology: null.

Note the ceiling the builder already records: a cell's annual evaporation is capped by its own precipitation plus storage however dwmax is set, because routed river water accumulates into driver (landmod.f90:1390) and never reaches dwatc. So the quantity being derived is a SEASONAL partition, not a sustained rate.

Do: once a baseline climatology is declared, take the per-cell driest-bin soil water over cells with a non-zero lake fraction and solve for the largest dwmax that keeps drhs at 1 through it. Report the spread across lake cells, because one number for all of them is itself an approximation.

Source: world-vus
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT:
BLOCKED, on config/planet.yaml's `baseline_climatology: null`. The finding is
unchanged; only its line cites moved.

Confirmed in the current tree:
- config/planet.yaml carries model.lake_dwmax_m: 0.2 with the direction argued
  and the value marked underived, and build_surface_soil_water.py:192-198 reads
  it with no fallback and refuses without the key. world-vus landed.
- The mechanism: drhsland = 0.25 and drhsfull = 0.4 are declared at
  landmod.f90:103-104 (the issue and the config comment both said :52-53, which
  is now the snow and glacier albedo block; corrected in this pass), and the
  application is
    drhs(jhor)=AMIN1(1.,dwatc(jhor)/(drhsfull*dwmax(jhor)))
  at landmod.f90:516-517. So drhs still reaches 1 above 40 per cent of dwmax.
- The ceiling the builder records is intact: routed river water accumulates
  into driver at landmod.f90:1527 (the issue said :1390) and never reaches
  dwatc, so what is being derived is still a SEASONAL partition.
- exoplasim/inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json records
  mean_lake_fraction_of_land_cells 0.171 and the land-mean dwmax before and
  after the lake write, so the cells the derivation ranges over are identified.

What blocks it: the derivation needs per-cell seasonal precipitation and
evaporation over the lake cells through the driest output bin, and there is no
climatology on this build. check_consistency reports the same.

title: The staged soil-water field needs one re-run: four new ocean and surface keys drifted its config stamp
description:
check_consistency.py FAILs 'generated inputs vs their config' on orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json: ocean.cold_start, ocean.sea_ice_fusion_j_kg, surface.sea_ice_lead_closing_m and surface.sea_ice_max_thickness_m are all new since it was built.

None of the four reaches soil water. The drift is by design: lib/provenance.py's _SURFACE_BLOCKS deliberately leaves 'surface' and 'ocean' OUT of surface_soil_water's inert set, on the stated argument that over-detecting a read costs a regeneration that runs in seconds and under-detecting one costs a climate run. So the remedy is the re-run and not an inert-set entry.

Not done here because it rewrites a tracked artifact from a parallel worktree, and because a stale derived artifact is the resting state of the tree rather than a work list.

Do: python exoplasim/scripts/build_surface_soil_water.py, then check_consistency.
notes:
Scope is SIX keys, not four. Batch D's two glacier keys drifted the same artifact in the same way and belong in the same single re-run:
  surface.glaciers.max_snow_depth_m
  surface.glaciers.persistence_orbits
alongside batch C's four:
  ocean.cold_start, ocean.sea_ice_fusion_j_kg,
  surface.sea_ice_lead_closing_m, surface.sea_ice_max_thickness_m

Coordinator note: the glacier pair was briefly marked inert for the three staged surface fields (commit 8ba17a8c) and that was reverted in ec3cc16c. No build_surface_*.py mentions a glacier, so the trace really does reach nothing -- but _SURFACE_BLOCKS deliberately leaves the 'surface' and 'ocean' blocks OUT of surface_soil_water's inert set, arguing that the textual trace over-detects a read, that over-detecting costs a regeneration measured in seconds and under-detecting costs a climate run. Inerting individual surface.* keys for that consumer reverses that decision one key at a time. Regenerating is the intended answer.

Do this AFTER every batch has merged, so the artifact is not regenerated against a config that is still moving. It rewrites a tracked artifact, so it must be run from the main checkout, not a parallel worktree.

Also still open on the same gate and NOT part of this issue: albedo_report.json drifted on model.tree_albedo and model.grass_albedo. That drift is honest -- build_surface_albedo.py really reads both.

title: Two dead declarations in icemod.f90: CRHOF and mkicecf
description:
Found while working world-9hb and world-12c, and left alone because neither is in either issue's scope.

icemod.f90 declares parameter(CRHOF = 1003.8) with the comment "DENSITY OF 'FRESH' WATER AT S=5". grep over vendor/exoplasim returns the declaration and nothing else: no consumer in any file, compiled or not. It reads as a fourth salinity constant beside the three world-9hb made reachable, and it is not one.

subroutine mkicecf(picedc,piced,picec) computes ice compactness from a climatological thickness. grep returns its own definition and nothing else; it is never called. It reads xclicec2 directly rather than through its arguments, and it uses hlead, so it looks live to a reader following world-12c's key.

Do: delete both, or say in the source why they are kept.
close_reason: Both removed under world-ro6, commit fad2a2fa. mkicecf and the CRHOF parameter each had exactly one occurrence in the tree - their own declaration - checked against every .f90 and .c in plasim/src with comments stripped and against the repository outside it, with vendor/cgenie's own PlaSim copy excluded.

title: icemod_template.f90 is a stale pre-fork copy that now diverges from icemod.f90 in five places
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/icemod_template.f90 is not in CMakeLists.txt's source list and nothing generates icemod.f90 from it: notes/audits/dormant-exoplasim-modules.md and notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md both already record it as dead in the tree, and notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md line 870 records it as a stale pre-fork copy.

It has now diverged further. It still calls oceanini with the pre-world-9hb argument list, still declares CRHOS, CPS and CLFI as parameters with CPS at fresh water's 4180, still carries zh0 as a local in mkicec and mkicecf, still calls getiflx (which it also still defines), and still constructs ice cover from the SST sentinel in read_ice_surface.

Ask whether it should exist before updating it. A 1900-line file that compiles nowhere and reads as a maintained variant of the module beside it is a trap for the next reader; deleting it is a fix. If it is kept, it needs the same five changes so that a reader cannot take it for the current model.

Do: delete it, or bring it level with icemod.f90 and say in it what it is for.
close_reason: Deleted under world-cmz, commit 2332dd76. It was in no _sources list and in no variant slot, and the five divergences from icemod.f90 were the argument for removing it rather than for levelling a file that compiles nowhere.

title: Bracket clwref, the CCM3 reference in-cloud liquid water density
description:
world-ofn exposed rainmod's two CCM3 cloud-water literals as namelist keys. `clwhsc`, the e-folding length coefficient, is now derived from the model's own gascon and ga because it is a length. `clwref` = 0.00021 kg/m3, the reference in-cloud liquid water density, was exposed at Kiehl et al. (1996)'s own value and NOT scaled: it is a condensate concentration set by microphysics and carries no gravity dependence, so there is no consistency argument that moves it.

What is missing is a bracket. It multiplies dql linearly, dql sets shortwave cloud optical depth through radmod's zlwp and ztau and longwave cloud emissivity through acllwr, and ztau goes as log10(zlwp+1.5)**3.9, so the response is strongly sublinear but not small. Nothing in this project has asked what range of in-cloud liquid density is defensible for a simulated atmosphere at this gravity and this condensation rate, nor whether the Stephens (1978) ztau fit that consumes it is valid outside the range it was fitted over -- that fit is equally uncited.

Do: state a bracket with a source, and run it as arms the way PHYS-11's cloud absorption bracket is run. Do not tune it against a comparison; physics is not a knob.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 8, notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 5.

title: ExoPlaSim's modify() raises NameError on maxsnow, physicsfilter's neighbours are worth the same grep
acceptance_criteria: modify(maxsnow=...) sets DSMAX; every other branch of modify() has been checked for a bare-name test.
close_reason: Fixed, and the grep the issue asked for was run as three AST sweeps over the whole class: free names in every method, %-format literals with no conversion, and self.<name>(...) that is neither a method nor an assigned attribute. modify() held five hits, not one: maxsnow, soildepth, nstorms (also self.int, which does not exist), and aerofile twice. All five now read self.<attr>. DSMAX is tested against None rather than truthiness so a declared cap of zero sets a zero cap; configure()'s live truthiness test at its own DSMAX site is left alone and configure_otherargs writes DSMAX unconditionally after it. Commit 6f84e164.

title: puma and sam carry the same fftmod NLON 48 defect the plasim copy had
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/puma/src/fftmod.f90:7 and the sam tree beside it list NLON 48 in nallowed, and their radix loop is the same 8-4-3-2 chain that cannot do it: la = 6 satisfies the la >= 4 test, one dfft4 pass leaves la = 1, and neither the radix-3 nor the radix-2 tail fires, so 32 of the required 48 is applied and the inverse overshoots. No error either way.

world-78e fixed exactly this in plasim/src/fftmod.f90 and in pyfft.f90. The puma, sam and cat trees were deliberately outside notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md's scope and nothing in this project builds them, which is why they were left rather than swept.

Decide whether these trees are kept at all before fixing them: they are upstream models beside plasim that this fork does not compile, and deleting them from the subtree may be the fix. Note that puma/src/fft991mod.f90 and sam/src/fft991mod.f90 already carry 512 in their tables, which is the external corroboration world-78e used for adding it to the plasim copy.
acceptance_criteria: Either the puma and sam FFT tables match what their radix loops can transform, or those trees are removed from the subtree with the reason recorded in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md.
close_reason: Moot: wave 1's world-6ak (commit 1bbdf63c) deleted puma/, sam/ and cat/ from the subtree entirely, and docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md:97-112 records the reason and what was kept instead. Both arms of the acceptance criterion are satisfied by that deletion. Re-verified on this base: the only fftmod.f90 left under vendor/exoplasim is plasim/src/fftmod.f90, which world-78e already fixed (48 removed, 8 added, and a comment at :19-25 saying what the radix loop can actually factor). Two corrections to this issue's description for the record: sam/src/fftmod.f90 did NOT carry 48 -- its table was (64,96,128,256,384,512,768,1024) and its defective entry was 768 (8*96 -> 24 -> 6 -> one dfft4 -> la=1, no tail), the same class at a different n; and this project never edited a file inside those trees, the only two commits touching them being the subtree import 28abfadd and the deletion. A surviving instance of the same table defect is vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim/src/fortran/fftmod.f90:9, filed separately.

title: Derive OMP_STACKSIZE from the deepest concurrent set of live locals
description:
world-3nk put OMP_STACKSIZE and the stack rlimit into the production launcher, carrying 512M unchanged from the nine gate and bench scripts that already set it. 512 is not derived.

What is known: exoplasim/notes/threads-instead-of-ranks.md measured 463.1 MB of spilled locals across 724 symbols at T170 at 16 ranks, the largest single one 14 MB, and says only that OMP_STACKSIZE must be 'well above the 8 MB default'. bench_ab.py:74-79 measured a T127 MASTER overrunning a 16 MB process-stack limit and segfaulting; the master runs on the rlimit and not on OMP_STACKSIZE, so the two need separate answers.

What 512M is worth: about 49 full-globe (NLON*NLAT*NLEV) float64 locals live at once at T170. The requirement scales with NLON*NLAT, so a rung-derived value is the right shape.

What is missing: the deepest CONCURRENT set of live locals in a parallel region, which is a call-graph-plus-frame-size measurement nothing in this tree makes. The largest single local is a lower bound and the total spill is an unusably conservative upper one.

Do: measure the high-water stack per thread at two rungs (valgrind --tool=drd, or a guard-page probe, or gfortran -fstack-usage summed along the deepest chain from the parallel region), then set OMP_STACKSIZE per rung from it with the margin stated.

Source: world-3nk
notes:
PARTLY DONE in commit 3fce31f8, left OPEN for the measurement it names.

Derived: exoplasim/scripts/stack_floor.py walks the model's call graph out of plasim.f90's single parallel region and sums the declared local arrays along the heaviest chain, which is the deepest CONCURRENT set of declared locals. The chain is master -> gridpointd -> aero_main -> prepare_uvps at every rung and the weight rises as NLAT squared. Validated against a built binary's BSS symbols, which hold the same declarations when -frecursive is absent: 0.3 per cent against the T170 figure in threads-instead-of-ranks.md, 4.8 per cent against the T85 binary, and one-signed 57 per cent low at T42 because gfortran spills above a size threshold. exoplasim/notes/thread-stack-floor.md has the numbers.

512M preserved unchanged and now bounded and checked rather than derived: prepare_thread_stack refuses a stack below the floor at the configured rung and names the chain, so a T170 run at the 8 MB OpenMP default is refused instead of segfaulting inside the model. Proven able to fail at 1M/T21 and 8M/T170.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the original Do: the floor counts declared locals only. The physics is whole-array notation, 169 where statements, and gfortran's temporaries for those live on the same stack. No source fact fixes their size. The measurement that closes this is gfortran -fstack-usage summed along the SAME chain the floor already names -- so it is now a targeted measurement on four routines rather than an open call-graph question -- at two rungs, with the margin then stated. This batch may not compile, so it was not taken.

Two findings for whoever does: the requirement is per thread and only partly divides by the team size, because NUGP-shaped locals are the whole globe (4.7x from one thread to sixteen at T170, not 16x), so more threads is not a way out of a stack bound. And the 32 MB per-die working-set convention is exceeded by the declared locals on this chain from T42 up; that is not a regression to fix by shrinking the stack, because a stack reservation is address space and the convention governs the hot working set. The master thread runs the same chain on the rlimit and is a separate answer: the soft limit is raised to the hard one, and a host whose hard limit is finite and below the floor has no check yet.

title: ExoPlaSim's top_restoretime setter writes a broken format string
description:
vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py:3995:

    self._edit_namelist("plasim_namelist","DAMPSP","%"%self._top_restoretime)

'%' is not a format specifier, so this raises ValueError: incomplete format the moment the setter runs. Its twin at :2687 inside configure() is correct ('%f'). Found while sweeping DAMPSP for world-rt1.

Latent: this project never sets top_restoretime, so the setter is not reached. It is upstream's file and the fork carries it.

Do: fix to '%f' and offer it upstream, or record it as an upstream defect the fork does not carry a fix for.
close_reason: Fixed to '%f'%self.top_restoretime; the line also read self._top_restoretime, an attribute bound nowhere, so it raised AttributeError before the format could. An AST sweep for %-format literals with no conversion over every .py in vendor/exoplasim found this one and no other. Commit 6f84e164.

title: Re-derive t0 from the baseline climatology's own mass-weighted mean
description:
config/planet.yaml declares model.semi_implicit_reference_temperature_k at 249.4, derived as the mass-weighted mean of the setzt profile over the model's ten sigma levels. That profile is the COLD-START first guess, which is the best estimate available while no settled climatology exists.

Once the canonical climatology lineage is declared, the same quantity is measurable directly: the dsigma-weighted, area-weighted global mean of the climatology's own temperature field. Re-derive it from that and update the config key.

Bounded: the cold-start derivation is within 0.65 K of the inherited 250.0 and the core energy sink scales with t0 at 0.26% per that difference, so this is a tightening rather than a defect. See notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 3.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the merged tree (base aaeaed55). VERDICT:
BLOCKED, on config/planet.yaml's `baseline_climatology: null`. The finding is
otherwise unchanged and correct.

What is confirmed in the current tree:
- config/planet.yaml declares model.semi_implicit_reference_temperature_k at
  249.4 with the derivation in its comment, and the block says in terms to
  re-derive it from the baseline climatology when the lineage is declared.
- notes/audits/opaque-constants.md finding 3 is still finding 3 and still
  carries the derivation and the null result. Its cite is now
  plasimmod.f90:879 for `real :: t0(NLEV) = 250.0`, corrected in this pass.
- declare_dry_constants in run_exoplasim.py writes T0 as a per-level list, so
  the config value is what integrates.
- check_consistency.py reports `baseline climatology: none named in config;
  anything needing a climate will raise`, and climatology_path() raises rather
  than falling back. There is nothing to measure the mass-weighted mean from.

Nothing else stands in the way: the rule is stated, the sigma set is the one
every run is on, and the quantity is a dsigma-weighted, area-weighted global
mean of the climatology's temperature field. Unblocks the moment a canonical
climatology lineage is declared.

Size is unchanged and still small: the cold-start derivation is within 0.65 K
of the inherited 250.0 and the core energy sink moves 0.26% under that, 0.002
W/m2 on a sink of 0.79.

title: Flux correction relaxes toward the constructed Earth Arctic ice field
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md, dormant section.

nfluko is the model's actual q-flux mechanism, and both its branches read Earth
artefacts. nfluko=1 reads code 709 (icemod.f90:436) and 903 (oceanmod.f90:324),
which do not exist here so they stay zero. nfluko=2 (mkflukoi, icemod.f90:1582)
relaxes ice toward xcliced2 -- the constructed CCM3 field -- and addfci
(:1653-1654) compares SST against xclssto, the interpolation of the -999
xclsst.

config/planet.yaml explicitly wants a q-flux bracket and
analysis/error_budget.json carries no-q-flux as a structural term, so this sits
directly on the path of work already planned: anyone reaching for nfluko would
silently relax this world toward an Earth Arctic ice field.

Depends on the cold-start initialisation issue for the underlying field. Do:
guard nfluko against the sentinel state, or record the hazard where CLIM-16's
successor would be read.
acceptance_criteria: nfluko cannot silently relax toward a constructed Earth field, or the hazard is recorded against the q-flux work.
close_reason: nfluko cannot relax toward a constructed field: it is refused outright when there is no read climatology, on the -999 sentinel in xclsst/yclsst, which is a restart record so a continuation that switches nfluko on is refused the same way a cold start is. nfluko=1's two correction fields, codes 709 and 903, get sentinels of their own so 'absent' is not read as 'zero everywhere'. The same refusal covers the three other branches that prescribe rather than integrate a surface: nice=0, ntskin=0 and oceanmod's nocean=0. VERIFIED, not assumed: every consumer of the constructed field enumerated by grep over icemod.f90 and oceanmod.f90. Guarded by the abort - icestep's nice==0 block, its nfluko==1 block (xicec from xclicec2, and the xmaxd clause), mkflukoi, addfci, oceanmod's addfc, mkfc, getflxco and the nocean==0 block. Clamped harmless - iceget's AMAX1 makes xclicec2/xcliced2 zero, which is what iceout codes 790/791 and oceanstep's pcliced argument then see; xflxice2 and yfsst2 are set to zero on the nfluko==0 branch. Diagnostic only - the nprint==2 blocks, and ocean output code 990 which emits the sentinel and is in no pyburn code table and read by no script here. Dead - mkicecf is never called. Nothing else reads them. scripts/error_budget.py's no-q-flux item now records that a q-flux is not available on this world at any price. analysis/error_budget.json is absent from this tree and needs a baseline climatology, so it picks the text up on its next run. Commits b5918b94, 3a368340.

title: SIMBA is Earth-fitted throughout and carries two traps that fire on enabling it
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md, dormant section.

Unreachable at NVEG = 0 -- surfmod.f90:481, :510 and landmod.f90:595 skip every
SIMBA call -- and one namelist key away, since configure(vegetation=...) is a
supported argument. This project has its own biosphere, so ask first whether
SIMBA should ever be on: deleting is a fix.

rlue = 3.4E-10 kg C/J (landmod.f90:63) is applied to dfd(jhor,NLEP)
(simba.f90:387), the BROADBAND downward shortwave, rather than to the
photosynthetically active fraction, which under this star is roughly 0.30 to
0.33 against about 0.45 for the Sun -- so light-limited modelled GPP would be
overstated about 1.4x. The code says so itself at simba.f90:456-459.
ct_crit = 5.0 (simba.f90:383) ramps linearly from 273.16 K then flat forever,
with no temperature optimum and no high-temperature cutoff at all. q10 = 2.0
(simba.f90:20, :418) is referenced to 283.16 K. co2_ref = 360 ppm and
co2_sens = 0.3 (simba.f90:44-46) are Harvey (1989)'s Earth beta factor.
zlaimax = 9.0, cveg_k = 0.5, cveg_l = 0.25, cveg_a = 2.9, cveg_f = 3.0
(simba.f90:24-38) are Earth biome fits. valb_min = 0.12, valb_max = 0.30 and
vsalb_min = 0.20 (simba.f90:26-28) are Earth-Sun broadband albedos, and
vsalb_min is a THIRD independent forest-snow albedo constant, inconsistent both
with the landmod masking factor and with anything derived from this star.

tau_veg = 10 and tau_soil = 42 years (landmod.f90:65-66) are scaled correctly
and planet-aware at landmod.f90:296-297 by m_days_per_year * day_24hr. That is
the trap in the other direction: it converts Earth-calibrated turnover times
into VESPER years, so 10 and 42 become 5 and 21 Earth years of physical
turnover.

Two latent traps:
  simba.f90:484 does dwmax(jhor) = zwmax, overwriting the soil water bucket
  every timestep with SIMBA's Earth range vwmax_min 0.05 to vwmax_max 0.5
  (simba.f90:29-30, :464) and SILENTLY DISCARDING the pedology-derived code-229
  field the whole bootstrap-to-baseline sequence exists to produce.

  simba.f90:486 sets dalb but NOT dsalb. Under two_band_albedo: true the
  radiation reads dsalb only, so SIMBA's vegetation albedo would have no
  radiative effect whatsoever while its roughness and bucket would. nveg=2 and
  twobandalbedo=True are incompatible and nothing says so.

At minimum, record the incompatibility and the dwmax overwrite where someone
would read them before enabling SIMBA.
acceptance_criteria: The nveg=2 / twobandalbedo incompatibility and the dwmax overwrite are documented where they would be read before enabling SIMBA, or SIMBA is removed.
close_reason: SIMBA stays OFF -- nothing enables it and nveg is untouched. Both traps are disarmed rather than recorded. Trap 1: vegini now REFUSES nveg = 2 with nstartemp = 1 and stops, because vegstep sets dalb and not dsalb, so under a two-band shortwave SIMBA's vegetation albedo would reach the radiation nowhere while its roughness and its soil water bucket reached it everywhere. The positive form is a per-band vegetation albedo and there is no derivation for one, so the refusal is the decision procedure until there is. Trap 2: 'dwmax(jhor) = zwmax' is gated on NVEGWMAX, a new vegmod_nl key, and vegini states at initialisation which field owns the soil water bucket. The default is 1 -- SIMBA, upstream's behaviour, preserved exactly -- so nothing changes for anyone running it today, but a run can now keep the pedology-derived staged code-229 field instead of having it silently overwritten every timestep. The module header carries both items and, separately, the Earth calibrations that are approximate rather than broken: rlue against dfd(:,NLEP), the BROADBAND downward shortwave, rather than the photosynthetically active fraction; ct_crit's linear ramp from TMELT with no optimum and no high-temperature cutoff; q10's 283.16 K reference; Harvey's beta factor; the biome fits; and vsalb_min as a THIRD independent forested-snow albedo constant, now inconsistent with landmod's albforest masking as well as with the spectrum. Deletion was considered as the alternative and not taken: surfmod, plasimmod, the restart records and the output code table all reference the module, so removing it is a cross-batch change rather than a fix.

title: The lead-closing scale is unreachable and the ice thickness clamp redistributes heat non-locally
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 26.

icemod.f90:1152, zh0 = 0.5 in mkicec, credited to "Hippler '79" at :1163, with
the same 0.5 m in mkicecf at :1205. It is the whole of the model's lead
parameterisation: a cell's compactness closes with an e-folding of 0.5 m of new
ice growth, and icemod.f90:746-750 then thresholds it at thicec = 0.5 into a
hard 0/1 mask. So zh0 alone sets how much modelled ice must grow before a cell
flips to iced for albedo and roughness, roughly 0.35 m. On a world whose year is
half Earth's the ice grown per season differs, and this Arctic-calibrated growth
scale is what converts it into cover. thicec is an icemod_nl key and unset; zh0
is not a key at all.

Beside it, xmaxd = 9.0 m (icemod.f90:58, icemod_nl-reachable, unset; the run
diag shows XMAXD= 9.0) is Earth's Arctic multi-year maximum, and its enforcement
is worse than a clamp: icemod.f90:705-718 melts the excess and getiflx
(:1988-2020) takes the GLOBAL area-weighted sum of that heat and redistributes
it onto every other cell with ice below 9 m. That is a non-local heat transport
with no physical carrier.

Dormant at the current climate -- thickness peaked at 4.46 m in spin-up and
0.78 m at equilibrium, so `zsum(1) > 0.` never fires -- and live in any cold
sweep arm.

Do: expose zh0; decide what xmaxd means here, and replace or bound the
redistribution before running a cold arm.
acceptance_criteria: zh0 is reachable and declared; the xmaxd redistribution is removed, bounded, or shown never to fire in the sweep arms.
close_reason: zh0 is now icemod_nl's HLEAD, declared in config at ExoPlaSim's value: exposed, not changed, and it reproduces the compiled 0.5 exactly. It was a local in both mkicec (live) and mkicecf (dead) and both now read the module value. getiflx is DELETED.
