The thickness limit's melt is paid out of the same cell's conductive flux to the ocean instead of a global area-weighted sum spread over every other cell with ice below the limit; the old form was a heat transport with no carrier and it also dropped the remainder silently whenever demand exceeded capacity, since xcfluxr is reset at the top of every icestep. xmaxd is DECLARED OFF (-1.0) in config/planet.yaml and written to the namelist, so the branch cannot fire in any arm. The argument: 9 m is Earth's Arctic multi-year maximum standing in for ice export, which this model does not have and which the error budget already carries as a declared structural term; and xmaxd is not only a clamp, because mkcflux and skintemp zero the conductive flux once ice reaches it, so a positive value stops basal growth outright. Conductive growth goes as the square root of time, so switching it off leaves nothing unbounded. Dormant at the current climate, so the baseline is unchanged. XMAXD and HLEAD are both in configure_otherargs and expected_namelist_keys. Commit 9e6372e1.

title: Runoff velocity constants are Earth-fitted, with gravity entering through the geopotential
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 27.

landmod.f90:1185-1186 and the identical pair at glaciermod.f90:303-304,
zcvel = 4.2 and zcexp = 0.18, used at landmod.f90:1328-1347 and
glaciermod.f90:541-561 as u = zcvel/zdx * |dh/dx|^0.18.

zoro there is GEOPOTENTIAL, not elevation, so the slope term carries ga: the
same topographic slope gives 1.306x the value here, worth 1.306^0.18 = 1.049 on
the velocity. Separately, open-channel velocity scales as sqrt(g), so a
physically consistent zcvel would be about 1.14x larger. The pit-filling
increment zoron = 1. + MIN(...) (landmod.f90:1231, glaciermod.f90:444) is
likewise 1 m2/s2, so 0.078 m of elevation here against 0.102 m on Earth.

oroini runs after roffini in surfini (surfmod.f90:479-480), so the glaciermod
copy is the one that survives.

A few per cent on river transit. Recorded because it is the only routing
timescale in the model and it is unreachable.
acceptance_criteria: The routing velocity constants are gravity-consistent, or declared as inherited with the magnitude reported.
close_reason: zcvel and the pit-filling increment were parameter(4.2) and a literal 1.0 in two copies, landmod's roffini and glaciermod's oroini, of which oroini is the one that survives. Both now derive from landmod_nl keys: zcvel = roffvel*ga**(0.5-roffexp) and zoroinc = roffpit*ga. Because zoro is geopotential, that makes the velocity proportional to sqrt(ga) once the slope is divided back to a topographic one, which is the open-channel scaling; the exponent is written as (0.5-roffexp) so the two cannot drift apart. roffvel = 2.022845 reproduces 4.200 at ga = 9.80665, and roffpit = 0.101972 m reproduces 1.000 m2/s2, so an Earth configuration is unchanged -- an identity that can fail. At this planet's gravity the effective zcvel is 4.575, 1.0893x upstream's, which is the 1.14x from sqrt(g) less the 1.049x the geopotential slope was already supplying.

title: Snow and glacier densities are Earth compaction values on a 1.31 g planet
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 25.

landmod.f90:72 rhosnow = 330 kg/m3 and glaciermod.f90:47 rhoglac = 850 kg/m3.

rhosnow converts water equivalent to physical snow thickness for the top-layer
heat capacity blend (landmod.f90:734, :741, :784, :791), so it decides how much
the modelled snowpack insulates the soil. rhoglac converts water equivalent to
ice thickness for the orography (glaciermod.f90:355).

Both are settled densities set by overburden compaction, which scales with
gravity, and this world's is 1.306x Earth's, so settled snow would be denser and
firn would densify faster.

The fork got the GRAVITY right at glaciermod.f90:344-351, with a comment
explaining why, and then multiplies it by an Earth-compacted density. Worth
roughly 10 to 20 per cent on snow insulation thickness and on glacier relief.
Neither is in any namelist.
acceptance_criteria: Snow and glacier densities carry a gravity-consistent compaction, or are declared as inherited with the bracket reported.
close_reason: Both densities are DECLARED AS INHERITED with the bracket reported, which is the second arm of the acceptance criterion. rhosnow joins landmod_nl and rhoglac joins glacier_nl, values unchanged at 330 and 850 kg/m3, so the bracket can now be RUN rather than only stated. The declaration beside each says what the constant does -- rhosnow converts water equivalent to the physical snow thickness that insulates the soil column, rhoglac to the ice thickness that enters the orography -- and that both are settled densities set by overburden compaction, which scales with gravity, so both are low on a planet whose surface gravity is 1.306x the one they were measured on. Not rescaled: firn densification is not a closed-form function of gravity that can be evaluated here, and this project brackets an estimate it cannot verify rather than guessing it. The bracket is the issue's own, roughly 10 to 20 per cent on snow insulation thickness and on glacier relief. glaciermod already had the GRAVITY right in the orography conversion, with its own comment; the density beside it is the half that is inherited, and that is now said where the two meet.

title: An undeclared Rayleigh sponge of 20 and 100 days sits on the top two layers
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 20.

plasim.f90:1437-1439, run BEFORE the namelist read:
  tfrc(1) = 20.0*day_24hr*frcmod
  tfrc(2) = 100.0*day_24hr*frcmod

TFRC and FRCMOD are in plasim_nl and this project sets neither. Note the
asymmetry: the NLEV=20 equivalent (plasim.f90:1459-1469) requires nrdrag = 1 to
switch on, while the NLEV=10 case -- the configuration this project runs -- is
unconditional.

By the day_24hr cancellation that world-rt1 records, these are 20 and 100
SIDEREAL days, so 25 and 125 Earth days. The sponge sits on sigma 0.038 and
0.119, roughly 25 to 40 hPa, so it is a stratospheric sponge rather than
boundary-layer drag.

An inherited Earth-tuned top-of-model damping, live in every run, appearing in
none of this project's declared parameters -- unlike the filter, the
hyperdiffusion and the timestep, which are all argued in config/planet.yaml.

Do: decide whether 20 days suits a 30-hour rotator at 1.31 g, and declare the
answer either way.
acceptance_criteria: The sponge timescales are declared in config/planet.yaml with an argument, whatever value they take.
close_reason: Declared, in ROTATIONS, as model.rayleigh_sponge_rotations in config/planet.yaml, and written by run_exoplasim.py as a full per-level TFRC in seconds rather than left to readnl's unconditional NLEV==10 branch. The answer to 'does 20 days suit a 30-hour rotator': 20 ROTATIONS does, and days does not. The sponge absorbs a wave field whose timescales are set by the rotation rate and the model's whole nondimensionalisation is in 1/Omega, so Earth's 20 days carries across as 20 rotations. It is also what the model was delivering before world-rt1 -- the day_24hr nondimensionalisation gave exactly 20 and 100 sidereal days -- so the resolution ladder's stability boundary was measured under the same sponge it keeps. Also corrected in the audit: the sponge sits at sigma 0.025 and 0.094, not 0.038 and 0.119; the note used the neqsig==0 fallback set and every run carries NEQSIG=4. Commit 64906320.

title: Earth's lapse rate and a 288 K surface set every cold start's initial profile
description:
notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 17.

CORRECTS world-cwu, which records alr as inert and "never consumed anywhere in
the live source". It is consumed. ALR is used at plasim.f90:2219-2224 inside
setzt, which builds the restoration and initial temperature profile, and setzt
is reached through initfd, gated at plasim.f90:487-491 on nrestart == 0. So it
is live on the cold-start path. A lowercase grep misses it; the uses are
uppercase.

setzt (plasim.f90:2202-2259) builds the profile from tgr = 288.0
(plasimmod.f90:314), ALR = 0.0065 (p_earth.f90:42) and dtrop = 12000.0
(plasimmod.f90:312). All three are namelist-reachable -- TGR and DTROP through
plasim_nl at plasim.f90:1426-1428, ALR through planet_nl -- and this project
sets none of them; confirmed absent from run_2c42c68fe9ca's staged namelists.

restim = 0 so damp = 0 and sr is an initial state rather than a restoration, and
dtep = dtns = 0 so the latitudinal structure is null. This world's dry adiabat
is 12.76 K/km against Earth's 9.76 and its scale height is 0.77x, so a 6.5 K/km
profile with a 12 km tropopause is a poorer first guess here than on Earth.

It washes out, so this costs spin-up rather than an answer. It is worth setting
because config/planet.yaml records that the resolution-ladder stability boundary
was measured entirely on cold starts, and that boundary is the ceiling for
exactly this transient.

Second and smaller use: plasim.f90:569 does zdlnp = zmeanoro/gascon/tgr followed
by psurf = exp(log(psurf)-zdlnp), so the declared 1 bar is reduced for mean
orography using Earth's 288 K -- about 200 Pa, 0.2 per cent of surface pressure,
but it means the realised global-mean surface pressure depends on an undeclared
Earth number.
acceptance_criteria: ALR, TGR and DTROP are set from config and declared; world-cwu's inert-alr claim is corrected; the realised mean surface pressure no longer depends on an undeclared value.
close_reason: ALR, TGR and DTROP are declared as model.cold_start_profile in config/planet.yaml and staged by run_exoplasim.py:declare_dry_constants, re-applied on every continuation and checked against the staged FILE by verify_staged_namelists. Values and their arguments: TGR 289.03 K, this model's own converged global-mean surface temperature at the declared baseline flux (lib/sensitivity.py SLOPE_BRACKET_RUNS warm arm, flux ratio 0.945, run_524fbed77a9a); ALR 0.008489 K/m, the same fraction of the DRY ADIABAT that Earth's 6.5 K/km is of Earth's, this atmosphere's g/cp being 12.75 against 9.76; DTROP 9220 m, the same number of pressure scale heights as Earth's 12 km, this atmosphere's scale height being 0.768 of Earth's. The realised mean surface pressure no longer depends on an undeclared value: TGR reaches the orographic reduction at plasim.f90 on every start, restart included, which is why it is re-applied on continuations too. world-cwu's inert-alr claim is corrected in p_earth.f90 itself, beside the assignment. Commit 64906320.

title: Remove the unreferenced procedures the sweep confirmed, about 485 lines
description: Zero callers anywhere in the tree, established by a comment-stripped sweep of every procedure name across all 58 files in plasim/src rather than only the compiled set, with external statements, procedure pointers and C-side symbols checked separately; the only such reachers in the tree are mpimod_omp.f90:554 for the OpenMP intrinsics and nresources in pumax_stub.c. In the model: fyppm, cosa, cosc, n2mmr, orb_print, mkicecf, surfname, check_equality, dtodat, nweekday, ndayofyear, writecolumn, guistep_puma, guihorlsg, sp3fc (legmod.f90:465-476), shtns_teardown (shtnsmod.f90:563-573, so SHTns is never torn down and the process exits holding its plans). In pyburn: readvariablecode, _getknownwordlength, _getmarkerlength, f2py_compile. Note that notes/audits/pyburn-postprocessing-cost.md:181-186 records fork effort spent repairing readvariablecode and _gettimevar, both of which remain unreachable. Also earthveg at specblock.f90:1426-1747, 322 lines of spectral data referenced by no file while the other thirteen arrays in that module are read by radmod.f90. In the omp parallel layer, 205 lines with no caller in the compiled set: mpgallgp, mpsumr, mpgathersp, the four mpread/mpwrite routines superseded by restartmod, mrsum, mrbci, mpgadn and four finish variants; mpsumscp, mpgallspp and mpgallsp all survived the SHTns migration and are live, so this is not transform fallout. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md sections 7 and 8.
acceptance_criteria: The procedures are gone. The MPI and serial reference builds still build and compare, since docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md keeps them as the correctness reference. Rule 4 applies.
close_reason: About 1,400 lines removed, list re-derived by a comment-stripped token sweep of every .f90 and .c in plasim/src plus the repository outside it, excluding vendor/cgenie (which ships its own PlaSim, so every name appears there) and excluding prose. INTERFACE blocks counted as references and caught ndayofyear, which radmod.f90 declared twice while both call sites were commented out. Removed: check_equality, cosa, cosc, fyppm, dtodat, ndayofyear, surfname, orb_print, n2mmr, writecolumn, sp3fc, shtns_teardown, planet_stop, guistep_puma, guihorlsg, mkicecf + CRHOF, earthveg (322 lines), and in the omp layer mrsum, mrbci, mpgallgp, mpgathersp, mpreadgp, mpreadsp, mpwritegp, mpwritesp, mpgadn and the four finish variants (from all three utilities files). From pyburn: readvariablecode, _getknownwordlength, _getmarkerlength, f2py_compile and _gettimevar. KEPT with reader named: mpsumr (verify_omp_collectives.f90 calls it - the issue was wrong), mpwritegph (37 call sites), nweekday (tools/caltest.f90). The mpimod.f90/mpimod_multi.f90/mpimod_stub.f90 copies of the dead collectives left to world-38b, which deletes those files whole. Rule 4: all five binaries need rebuild and --verify. Commit fad2a2fa.

title: zsolars is written to the restart, read by nothing, and still REQUIRE_EQUAL
description: radmod.f90:1799 writes zsolars into the restart and its only read is commented out at :1144. That is deliberate residue of the CLIM-38 repair recorded in notes/audits/zsolars-restart-overread.md: solarini is now unconditional and the arrays are recomputed from the namelist at every start. The record nonetheless still carries a Policy(OPAQUE, REQUIRE_EQUAL) at exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py:311, so a converter can refuse a restart over two values nothing consumes. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 8.
acceptance_criteria: Either the write and the policy row go together, or the record is kept as a configuration fingerprint and its why says so and its policy stops blocking conversion.
notes:
2026-08-24, batch B. Half done and the other half belongs to batch A.

DONE, in 386be59f: radstop's comment in radmod.f90 now states that the write is a CONFIGURATION FINGERPRINT and not checkpointed state, that nothing reads it back because CLIM-38 made solarini unconditional, and why it is kept.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ISSUE, verified against the source.
1. zsolars is NOT read by nothing. radmod.f90 forms the band-weighted surface albedo from zsolars(1) and zsolars(2) at nstartemp = 1, in swr, every timestep. It is live model state. What nothing reads is the RESTART copy: the get_restart_array block in radini is commented out.
2. The write is in radstop, not at the line the issue cites.

DECISION TAKEN: keep the record, per the second branch of the acceptance criteria. It is the only place a restart handed on without its run directory records which two-band split of the stellar constant the orbits were integrated with, and removing it changes the restart layout, which costs the schema, the converter, the template and every existing restart's layout for a 16-byte record.

STILL TO DO, in exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py, which batch A owns. One row, at the zsolars entry in the OPAQUE block:

    "zsolars": Policy(OPAQUE, TARGET,
                      why="a configuration fingerprint: the two-band split of "
                          "the stellar constant the run integrated with. "
                          "Nothing reads it back -- radini's get_restart_array "
                          "block is commented out and solarini rebuilds the "
                          "pair from the namelist and the spectrum at every "
                          "start (CLIM-38) -- so a converter must not refuse a "
                          "restart over it. The target template's own value is "
                          "what the target model will recompute anyway."),

REQUIRE_EQUAL becomes TARGET, and TARGET is already used with OPAQUE for accuvers, so the combination needs no new converter support. Do NOT delete the row: the write stays, and smoke_test's 'the restart schema covers every record the model writes' would go red.
close_reason: Applied on the coordination branch. Batch B's half (radstop's comment recording why the write is kept and that nothing reads it back) merged with the batch; the schema row is now OPAQUE/TARGET per B's decision, so a converter no longer refuses over a value radstart recomputes. smoke_test 22/22.

title: Two planet modules are accepted build values that cannot be built
description: CMakeLists.txt:61 admits p_earth and p_mars for PLASIM_PLANET. p_mars.f90:13-14 has a doubled comma inside the planet_nl continuation, so -DPLASIM_PLANET=p_mars is a validated, documented option that fails the build. p_exo.f90 is not admitted at all, and build_model.py never passes -DPLASIM_PLANET, so the CMake cache default p_earth always wins. p_exo.f90 is the only planet module exposing alv, als and tmelt in planet_nl: the latent heat of vaporisation, the latent heat of sublimation, and the melting point. On this fork the module that would make the modelled water thermodynamics settable is the one the build refuses, and writing any of those three keys today aborts the run against p_earth's namelist. Deciding this is upstream of world-cmz, which would otherwise delete both files. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md sections 2a and 5.
acceptance_criteria: Either the three thermodynamic keys reach planet_nl on the module that is built, or p_exo goes and the absence is recorded. p_mars is fixed or removed rather than left as an accepted option that cannot compile.
close_reason: alv, als and tmelt are in planet_nl on p_earth.f90, the module that compiles, at the values plasimmod.f90 already declared, and plasim.f90 broadcasts all three because they are threadprivate and only NROOT reads the namelist. The PLASIM_PLANET axis is removed from CMakeLists.txt and p_earth.f90 is a literal source: it admitted only a module that could not compile as its alternative, build_model.py never set it, and this build has one planet. p_mars.f90 and p_exo.f90 are deleted under world-cmz. Commit 3098acef.

title: Retire the namelist keys that gate nothing
description: Of 368 namelist variables the compiled model declares, 167 have no writer. Most are ordinary unused knobs. These are different: declared, sometimes written into every run, and read by no code at all. nflux (plasim.f90:1412, documented 'vertical diffusion 1/0'), npackgp and npacksp (:1415, naming a packing that is gone from outmod.f90), nguidbg (:1413, and written NGUIDBG = 0 in all nine runs), nsurf (surfmod.f90:377), zeta (carbonmod_nl, whose own declaration at carbonmod.f90:48 says 'not used' and which the shipped template writes into every carbonmod_namelist), and ngpitrigger (hurricanemod.f90:177, whose only non-declaration occurrence is inside a commented-out continuation). sellon is used only by the four GUI stub calls at plasim.f90:2854-2857, so it is a knob with no effect in any buildable configuration. nfixer is the same class but has its own row, world-bsp, because the term it claims to gate is a mass redistribution that is always on. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: Each key either gates what it says it gates or is gone, including out of the shipped templates. A reader can no longer set one and believe it did something.
close_reason: nflux, npackgp, npacksp, nsurf, zeta and ngpitrigger are gone from their groups, declarations, broadcasts and the shipped templates. nguidbg and sellon leave plasim_nl and the template but keep their module declarations, because their only reader is the uncompiled guimod.f90 and the compiled build passes sellon to bodyless column routines. nguidbg's second declaration in carbonmod's private plasim_nl had to go with it: that group WRITES a namelist plasim_nl no longer declares the name in.

title: Decide the entropy diagnostics: 452 lines nothing can switch on
description: Three separately declared switches named nentropy, in plasim_nl (plasim.f90:1412), icemod_nl (icemod.f90:288) and oceanmod_nl (oceanmod.f90:160), plus nentro3d. Nothing writes any of them and none appears in any run namelist. 381 lines over 42 sites are gated on nentropy > 0 and 71 lines over 31 sites on nentro3d > 0, across plasim.f90, outmod.f90, miscmod.f90, rainmod.f90, fluxmod.f90, landmod.f90, icemod.f90 and oceanmod.f90. This is the largest namelist-gated block in the model and notes/audits/dormant-exoplasim-modules.md does not cover it. The question is the one that row's section 2 asks of every dormant module: is this a decision somebody made, or a default nobody has read. Relevant that this project already runs NENERGY=1 and has an open interest in where the model loses energy. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 3.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict: enabled and consumed, or declared off with the reason, or deleted. Not left as 452 lines nobody has read.
close_reason: VERDICT: DELETED, 447 lines across ten modules. 'Enabled and consumed' was not available -- the blocks write codes 320-355 and 420-442, and 320/321 are already tempmin/tempmax on the same stream, in REGULAR_CODES, mapped by pyburn as mint/maxt, while 322-329 collide with the hurricane diagnostics; pyburn has no entry for any entropy code. Enabling them needed a renumbering nobody had asked for, so the switch was a trap. Deleting cannot change the climate: every assignment inside the guards is to a diagnostic accumulator or a block-local, none read outside a guard, and they share no storage with nenergy. Verified statically: no entropy symbol survives and every subroutine's block balance is unchanged against HEAD.

title: NLPP truncates, and the build gate is the only thing that catches it
description:
plasimmod.f90:102 is 'parameter(NLPP = NLAT / NPRO)', integer division, restated verbatim in oceanmod.f90:17, icemod.f90:15, icemod_template.f90:15 and plasim_dummy.f90:10.

mpstart checks only that the runtime rank or thread count equals the compiled NPRO (mpimod.f90:492-496, mpimod_omp.f90:583-589). Nothing in the Fortran checks that NPRO divides NLAT.

When it does not, NPRO*NLPP < NLAT and every consequence is silent: the scatters and gathers at mpimod.f90:145,171 cover only part of the globe; utilities.f90:24-36 makeareas reads cell areas from latitude slots the gather never filled; and under OMPSHARED the pointer association at plasimmod.f90:1099 leaves the top of the globe owned by no thread, so the forward transform analyses a polar band that is whatever the array was initialised to.

The only guard is CMakeLists.txt:72-77, added by this fork, with build_model.py:138-142 repeating it. That is the right place for it. This row exists because it is the ONLY place: a hand-edited resmod.f90 or a direct cmake invocation bypasses both, and nothing at runtime would say so.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 8.
acceptance_criteria: A runtime check refuses mod(NLAT,NPRO) /= 0 with a named error, so the invariant does not rest solely on the build system.
close_reason: Fixed on the threaded path: mpstart in mpimod_omp.f90 refuses mod(NLAT,NPRO) /= 0 with a named mpabort before assoc_grid, naming NLAT, NPRO, NLPP and the unowned latitude count. Build-time gates in CMakeLists.txt and build_model.py kept. mpimod.f90 left alone: MPI is dead, world-38b.

title: Two of the three vegetation albedo endmembers were left at Earth-Sun values when the third was re-weighted
description:
build_surface_albedo.py:163-167 carries --tree-albedo 0.13 and --grass-albedo 0.19. These are two of the three constants notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md finding 1 named in one sentence. The third, --vegetation-albedo 0.15, was re-weighted to this star and moved to model.vegetation_albedo: 0.165; these two were left as Earth-Sun values with a helptext for a source.

They are what --mode modelled blends, which is the mode the docstring calls 'the only one that is not an assumption'. Tracked as bio-18 for the biosphere side; the finding here is the swept-fix asymmetry, which is the same shape as the pyburn lapse rate: a sweep closed on the instance that blocked it and left its neighbours.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: The two endmembers are re-weighted by the same derivation the third went through and moved to the same place. analysis/vegetation_albedo.py gains COVER_ENDMEMBERS and writes cover_albedo, cover_albedo_earth_sun and cover_albedo_bracket; config/planet.yaml gains model.tree_albedo 0.143 (from 0.13) and model.grass_albedo 0.209 (from 0.19) with brackets [0.130, 0.148] and [0.190, 0.217]; and build_surface_albedo.py's two flags default to the config with no silent Earth-Sun fallback, which is the rule --vegetation-albedo already followed. The POPULATION leaf ratio 1.1002 rather than the per-class one: tree and grass differ by 0.006 in ratio and 0.001 in albedo, and the grass class has four spectra in it, so a per-class ratio would not resolve the effect it claims to separate. lib/provenance.py: the two keys and their brackets join the inert sets of the three builders that never read them, and are deliberately absent from surface_albedo's, which does; check_consistency's re-grep confirms both halves. Discovered and filed as world-36g rather than fixed here: --mode modelled still writes ONE identical field to codes 174, 175 and 176, because the band split SPEC-5 added is gated on --mode vegetated, and splitting the modelled blend needs a band pair for the rock table that does not exist.

title: akap is live and was not re-derived beside gascon, and two planet constants are inert
description:
akap = 0.286 (p_earth.f90:41) is LIVE and feeds acpd = gascon/akap at plasim.f90:1514, so it sets the specific heat of dry air. GASCON is derived from config/planet.yaml's declared composition; akap was not re-derived with it.

Measured 2026-08-24 from that composition (0.78025 N2, 0.21 O2, 0.0093 Ar, 450 ppm CO2): mean molar mass 28.9688 g/mol, R = 287.014 J/kg/K reproducing the namelist GASCON 287.0171 to five figures, cp = 1004.898, so the correct akap is 0.28562 against the model's 0.286. That implies cp 1003.56 rather than 1004.90, i.e. 0.13% low, worth 0.017 K/km on the dry adiabat (12.765 against 12.748). Small, and nothing records that it was checked; close_state_energy.py:74 only notes in passing that it is not overridden.

Fix: derive akap beside gascon from the same composition, or DECLARE it.

Two constants beside it ARE inert, checked case-insensitively: tropical_year = 31556956.0 and nplanet = 3 are set, MPI-broadcast, and consumed nowhere in the live source. Recorded because a reader auditing the planet configuration cannot tell that from the file.

CORRECTED 2026-08-24 by world-wmw: this issue originally listed alr = 0.0065 as a third inert. That was wrong. ALR is consumed eleven times in setzt (plasim.f90:2219-2259) and four times in guimod.f90, so it is live on the cold-start path. The error was a case-sensitive grep against uppercase uses. The cold-start profile constants are world-wmw's subject, not this one's.

The p_exo/p_mars selectability question -- CMakeLists.txt:61 admits only p_earth and p_mars, and p_exo is the only module exposing alv, als and tmelt in planet_nl -- is world-58v's and is not restated here.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-24, from notes/audits/model-earth-centrism.md finding 17: alr is NOT inert. ALR is consumed at plasim.f90:2219-2224 inside setzt, which builds the restoration and initial temperature profile, and setzt is reached through initfd, gated at plasim.f90:487-491 on nrestart == 0. So Earth's 6.5 K/km sets the initial atmosphere on every COLD START, on a world whose dry adiabat is 12.76 K/km. A lowercase grep for alr misses it; the uses are uppercase. tgr = 288.0 and dtrop = 12000.0 feed the same routine, and tgr additionally sets the orographic surface-pressure reduction at plasim.f90:569. Tracked as world-wmw. tropical_year and nplanet remain inert as this row states.
close_reason: AKAP is derived beside GASCON. run_exoplasim.py:declare_dry_constants takes (R, cp) from lib/lapse.py:gas_properties -- the one place in this tree that turns the declared composition into gas properties -- writes AKAP = R/cp into planet_namelist, and CHECKS the R it derived against the GASCON ExoPlaSim was actually configured with rather than assuming they agree. Measured 0.285618 against the inherited 0.286, so acpd = gascon/akap goes from 1003.56 to 1004.90 J/kg/K, 0.13%, 0.017 K/km on the dry adiabat. Re-applied on every continuation and checked against the staged file by verify_staged_namelists. tropical_year and nplanet are marked INERT where they are set in p_earth.f90, re-verified case-insensitively across plasim/src; akap, alr and gascon are marked LIVE and overridden from config in the same place. The alr correction the notes carry is now in the source itself. Commits 64906320 and 446698e0.

title: lake_dwmax_m is read from config with a hardcoded fallback and is not in config
description:
build_surface_soil_water.py:188: float(model.get('lake_dwmax_m', 0.2)). Verified that lake_dwmax_m is not in config/planet.yaml at all, so the hardcoded 0.2 m is what runs, confirmed in inputs/t21/orogen_T21_surf_0229_provenance.json.

It is the field capacity written into every run's dwmax over lake cells, with no config entry and no derivation. The .get() with a default reads as though config supplies it.

Either add the key with its derivation or make the absence an error.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: model.lake_dwmax_m declared in config/planet.yaml and the builder's .get(..., 0.2) fallback removed: it now refuses without the key. Value preserved at 0.2 m, so no staged field changes. The direction IS derived (drhs reaches 1 above 40% of dwmax, landmod.f90:52-53, so a shallower bucket saturates the wetness factor on less water, and the lakes sit in arid cells); the value is not, and world-kvr is that derivation, blocked on a baseline climatology. lib/provenance.py marks the key inert for surface_albedo, surface_roughness and boundary_conditions, traced by the same grep the other entries use; live for surface_soil_water, whose provenance record now correctly reads stale against config. Deliberately NOT added to continue_exoplasim's resume allowlist, because it changes a staged field; no run is spinup_in_progress, so nothing in flight is blocked.

title: Three rungs have binaries and no surface data anywhere
description:
Provisioning as it stands. Binaries from rebuild_binaries.MATRIX, data from plasim/dat and exoplasim/inputs:

T21   binary yes, dat 15 codes, inputs 8 codes
T31   binary no (build refuses), dat 15 codes, inputs none
T42   binary yes, dat 15 codes, inputs 7 codes -- 0229 missing, which t21 has
T63   binary no, no data
T85   binary YES, NO DATA
T106  binary no, no data
T127  binary YES, NO DATA
T170  binary YES, NO DATA

Combined with the silent fallback in world-fuh, a run at T85, T127 or T170 would integrate a flat all-land planet under T21's damping. It does not, because declare_hyperdiffusion (run_exoplasim.py:1005-1030) and surface_field_report both refuse before the model is reached -- but the refusal comes from the driver, not from the model, and nothing states that these three rungs are executable-only.

The question to answer before generating anything: are T85, T127 and T170 binaries kept for the cost ladder in spat-11 alone, in which case say so, or are they meant to be runnable, in which case the surface families are missing.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 9.
acceptance_criteria: Each built rung is recorded as either runnable, with its surface family present, or cost-ladder-only, with that stated where the matrix is declared. The t42 0229 gap is closed or declared.
close_reason: Recorded: every rebuild_binaries.MATRIX row is a rung meant to be run, which config/planet.yaml's hyperdiffusion and timestep tables independently state; none is cost-ladder-only. The comment at MATRIX now names the three conditions for runnable and the check that refuses on each. Staging T85/T127/T170 and T42's 0229 is filed as world-89v.

title: clim-68's line citations are stale and its TSWR3 sub-claim is inverted
description:
clim-68 states 'TSWR3 is live -- but only at :2382, four lines ABOVE the branch; its second use at :2445 is inside it and equally dead.'

The branch structure in the current radmod.f90 is if (nswrcl == 0) at :2424, else at :2456, endif at :2498. The issue's :2445 maps to the current :2482, zom0(:) = min(0.9999,1.-tswr3*zmu0*zmu0*zlog), which is in the ELSE branch: the computed-cloud path that nswrcl=1 selects. It is live, not dead. So TSWR3 acts in both of its uses, and only ACL2 is dead.

The 'applied at half strength' conclusion survives as a statement about which KEY acts. The line-level claim does not, and the issue's ten line citations are all about 37 lines stale after the fork's multi-species aerosol work. Anyone reopening clim-68 on those citations lands in the wrong branch.

Also: cloud_band_weight.py's docstring is framed entirely around re-weighting acl2 and never mentions that acl2 is the dead half.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Fixed in 289bbe1a. Verified against the current radmod.f90: the inverted sub-claim is confirmed. tswr3's second use is at :2482, inside the ELSE of if (nswrcl == 0) at :2424 -- the computed-cloud branch nswrcl=1 selects -- so it is live; its first use feeds zb5 at :2419, consumed at :2470 in the same branch. acl2's only uses are :2430-2452 in the prescribed branch and are dead. clim-68 rewritten with current citations; cloud_band_weight.py's docstring names which key its weight reaches the model through.

title: Every run log's planet table reports Earth's mass, density and albedo, and two rows computed before the rotation is applied
description:
p_earth.f90:89-135's print_planet is called from plasim.f90:196. The table in every MOST_DIAG mixes this world's values with Earth's under the header 'Simulating: Earth'. From run_2b20e3324bb0/MOST_DIAG.00001: Mass 5.9736e24 kg (this world is 1.881 Earth masses), Volume 108.321e10 km3, Equatorial radius 6378 km and Polar radius 6356 km one row above a correct Mean radius of 7645.464 km, Ellipticity 0.0034, Mean density 5520 kg/m3, Bond albedo 0.385, Black-body temperature 247.3 K, Perihelion 147.1 and Aphelion 152.1 e6 km. Surface gravity, solar irradiance, obliquity, eccentricity, rotation factor and gas constant are correct.

Two DERIVED rows are computed from stale state: Sidereal rotation period 23.9345 h and Sidereal orbit period 183.3019 days. Call order inside prolog is planet_ini (:194), print_planet (:196), then readnl, and sidereal_day is not recomputed from rotspd until plasim.f90:1490-1503. The model then integrates a 30 h rotation and a 146-day orbit.

Diagnostic only, no physics reads these. Filed because config/planet.yaml states the project's own position on exactly this hazard: a plausible number from the wrong world is worse than an error.

Move the call after readnl and replace the Earth block with this world's values or with nothing.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: print_planet is called after readnl, so the sidereal rotation and orbit rows report the rotation the model integrates instead of the one planet_ini set. It writes and reads nothing else, so the ordering changes nothing but the numbers' truth. The Earth block is gone: Mass, Volume and Mean density are DERIVED from ga and plarad through g = GM/a^2 on a sphere, and run on Earth's own ga and plarad the same expressions return 5.964, 108.34 and 5505 against the measured 5.972, 108.32 and 5514 -- the residual being the oblateness and rotation this model does not have, which is the check that the derivation is the right one. Equatorial radius, polar radius, ellipticity, Bond albedo, black-body temperature, perihelion and aphelion are DROPPED, because the model holds nothing they follow from. Same treatment applied to p_exo.f90, which carried Earth's table verbatim under a name that is not Earth's; p_mars.f90 keeps its own Mars values and gains the corrected call order. The 'Simulating:' header still prints yplanet, which is reachable through planet_nl and which this project does not set -- left reachable rather than hardcoded. Commit 446698e0.

title: The solar/sidereal timestep inconsistency is annulled by integer truncation, and stops being below dt 12.4 min
description:
ntspd = nint(solar_day)/nint(mpstep*60) (plasim.f90:1546) is per SOLAR day while ww = TWOPI/sidereal_day (:1514) sets the scaled time unit, so delt = TWOPI/ntspd (:673) should exceed deltsec*ww by n_days_per_year/(n_days_per_year-1) = 1.0069 here.

It does not, at any timestep this project runs, because the division truncates. At dt 45/30/22.5/15 min ntspd truncates to exactly sidereal_day/deltsec and delt/ww == deltsec to the digit; the run's own diag agrees, with solar day 108744.8, sidereal day 108000.0, 40 timesteps per day and 40*2700 = 108000.

The truncation stops annulling it once there are more than n_days_per_year - 1 = 145 steps per day, i.e. below dt = 12.4 min: at dt 10 ntspd is 181 against 180 (0.55%) and at dt 7.5 it is 241 against 240 (0.41%). So it is latent exactly where the T127 and T170 rungs are headed, and the current agreement is accidental: nothing in the code notices the coincidence.

File as a known-latent item to settle before the ladder goes above T85.

Evidence: notes/audits/opaque-constants.md
close_reason: Fixed rather than filed as latent. delt is deltsec*ww, which is what plasimmod.f90's own declaration of delt says it is; it was TWOPI/ntspd, and ntspd counts steps per SOLAR day while ww is built from the sidereal one. Identical at every timestep on the current rung table, where ntspd's integer division truncates to exactly sidereal_day/deltsec -- so nothing on the ladder up to T85 changes -- and correct at every timestep instead of at the ones where a truncation happens to agree. That removes the latency the issue asked to be settled before the ladder goes above T85. plasim.f90 (both the nkits block and the main one), commit 9c2f5137.

title: pyproject.toml's extras table is spelled [projection...] and is silently ignored
description: vendor/exoplasim/pyproject.toml:36 reads [projection.optional-dependencies], a typo for project, so hatchling ignores the whole extras table: h5, nc, mpl and pRT. pip install exoplasim[pRT] therefore installs nothing and reports no error, which is one reason pRT.py's dependency can never arrive through packaging. Small, self-contained, and it makes a documented install path a no-op. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 2d.
acceptance_criteria: Either the table is spelled project and the extras resolve, or the extras go with the modules they serve.
close_reason: [projection.optional-dependencies] renamed to [project.optional-dependencies], so the extras resolve. pRT dropped with the module it served; basemap dropped because its only appearance is in commented-out code in gcmt.py. h5, nc and mpl all still have live readers. Verified by tomllib parse.

title: Finish the build-system removal: make_most, most.c, sysconfigure and three stale claims
description: docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md records the CMake rework as the fork's largest deliberate divergence and lists what it deleted. Two tracked files that belong on that list survived: make_most, which builds most.x, and most.c itself, 125 KB of X11 launcher. Their only remaining reference is vendored LaTeX at Puma_UG_17/install.tex:58 reading 'Used by configure script', and that script is gone. sysconfigure() at __init__.py:139-214 is now a chdir round trip with every real statement commented out, and its except Exception handler prints result.stderr where result is never bound, so it raises NameError over whatever it caught; Model.__init__:464 still calls it and touches a firstrun marker into the installed package directory, dormant here because the marker exists untracked and live on a fresh clone. Three stale claims: config/planet.yaml:289 says rebuild_binaries.py writes line 3 of most_compiler_mpi and that script has no reference to most_compiler; vendor/exoplasim/.gitignore explains its every rule in terms of what configure.sh and compile.sh write into the source tree; and setup.py never runs because pyproject.toml declares hatchling, while the two disagree on version and dependencies and MANIFEST.in is a setuptools input hatchling ignores. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 2d.
acceptance_criteria: make_most, most.c and the dead sysconfigure path are gone; planet.yaml:289 and the fork .gitignore describe the build that exists; setup.py and MANIFEST.in are removed or made authoritative.
close_reason: make_most, most.c, setup.py and MANIFEST.in deleted; sysconfigure(), printsysconfig() and the firstrun block in Model.__init__ removed. The firstrun block was not merely dormant: on a fresh clone it set recompile=True and the recompile branch REFUSES rather than builds, so the first Model constructed would have aborted with SystemExit even with its executable present. config/planet.yaml's most_compiler_mpi claim and the fork .gitignore's configure.sh/compile.sh framing both now describe the CMake build; docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md names all of it in the fork's deletion list. Commit e9870295. NOT done and separate: vendor/exoplasim/docs/index.rst still documents upstream's configure/compile install path and references sysconfigure and printsysconfig - filed separately.

title: Delete the Python modules nothing imports, four of which cannot import
description: The world repo reaches the package through six names only, and dynamic access was ruled out first: getattr, setattr, eval, exec, globals, __dict__ and vars return zero hits across all eleven top-level modules. Whole modules with no caller: hpc/ 2180 lines over 11 files, of which seven fail to import on Python 2 implicit relative imports and two of the modules they import, identity.py and crawldefs.py, exist nowhere in the tree, while launcher.py:8 imports sets, removed in Python 3.0; pRT.py 2091, whose petitRADTRANS is absent from the environment and from requirements.txt and whose import failure is swallowed by a bare try/except at __init__.py:19-21; surfacespecs.py 1471 with zero definitions, referenced only by pRT.py, yet imported unconditionally at __init__.py:16 and globbing and loading every basespecs/*.npy at import time on every import exoplasim in this project; randomcontinents.py 577; colormatch.py 361; quickprocess.py 39, which hardcodes another planet's radius and gravity and a path under someone else's home directory. There is no cluster anywhere in this project's configuration or documentation. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 2c.
acceptance_criteria: The modules are gone and importing the package no longer loads spectra for a bridge that cannot import. smoke_test passes.
close_reason: Deleted: hpc/ (11 files), pRT.py, colormatch.py, randomcontinents.py, quickprocess.py, plus Model.transit, Model.image and the pRTopts option surface that existed only for pRT. surfacespecs.py is NOT dead and the issue's premise on it was wrong: analysis/ice_albedo.py, the ice_albedo step in config/pipeline.yaml, loads it by file path and reads its eight named reflectance arrays. What was fixed instead is the unconditional import in __init__.py, so importing the package no longer globs and loads every basespecs/*.npy. basespecs/ retained as the ECOSTRESS component spectra any re-blend of this world's surface albedos would start from. Commit 08ce9ce7.

title: Delete the vendored trees nothing builds, reads or ships
description: About 120 MB under vendor/exoplasim: plasim/bld/ 34 MB of staged sources and objects from the deleted build, already called non-authoritative at exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py:66; lsg/ 25 MB, whose real lsgmod.f90 is 9313 lines with no build rule while the compiled plasim/src/lsgmod.f90 is a 4-line empty return; plasim/dat/ 17 MB of Earth and Mars boundary sets the staging path never reads; and the sibling models and utilities puma/, sam/, cat/, octave/, cat_tools/, images/, tools/, basespecs/, hazeconstants/, exoplasim_testers/. postprocessor/ belongs with them and it ships: every burn7 call site in __init__.py is commented out, yet .gitignore:39 re-includes plasim/run/burn7.x by name and __init__.py:604 copies the whole of plasim/run/ into every model working directory. The LaTeX and PDF manuals, about 66 MB, are vendored documentation and are a separate judgement. Source: notes/audits/dead-code-and-unreachable-paths.md section 2b.
acceptance_criteria: The trees are gone or explicitly retained with a reason. burn7.x stops being staged into every run directory. The manuals are decided separately and the decision is recorded.
close_reason: vendor/exoplasim falls 171 MB -> 47 MB. Deleted lsg/, puma/, sam/, cat/, cat_tools/, octave/, images/, exoplasim_testers/, glacier/, postprocessor/ + plasim/run/burn7.x, plasim/dat/, the CAT manuals, Plasim_Report/, the configure-era compiler probes and the sibling-model scripts, plus four stray probe run logs at exoplasim/exoplasim/bench/. plasim/bld/ was already gone. burn7.x no longer reaches a run directory and its .gitignore re-include is removed. KEPT against the list, each with a named reader: basespecs/ (analysis/ice_albedo.py via surfacespecs), hazeconstants/ (Model.configure stages an aerofile from it), tools/ (the restart-converter note names pusca.f90's convert_restart_array as its base). Manuals decided and recorded in docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md: PlaSim RM, PlaSim UG and PUMA UG stay; the CAT manuals and the climate report go. Commit 1bbdf63c.

title: Delete the fifteen source files no build configuration compiles
description: Fifteen files in plasim/src, about 14,560 lines, are in no build configuration: cpl.f90 1998, icemod_template.f90 1934, rainmod_bm.f90 1424, rainmod_kuo_old.f90 1324, rainmod_mca.f90 1015, plasim_dummy.f90 817, pumax.c 4721, mpimod_multi.f90 463, guimod.f90 422, p_mars.f90 175, p_exo.f90 170, outdiag.f90 72, readdat.f90 34, resmod_def.f90 30, plus newsnow.f90 113 and buildice.f90 30. The last pair is the exception and must NOT go: it is the offline glacier accelerator and CLIM-53 owns the verdict. The three convection schemes have no build knob at all, since CMakeLists.txt:152 names rainmod.f90 as a literal with no variant slot. outdiag.f90 duplicates the live outdiag at outmod.f90:1096 and would be a duplicate-symbol error if added. title: Absolute per-cell thresholds in the physics encode a cell size with no NLAT term
description:
Each of these compares a gridcell mean, or a raw cell count, against a constant chosen for one cell size. None carries an NLAT term, and none is flagged.

hurricanemod.f90:71 SIZETHRESH = 30, an UNWEIGHTED count of flagged gridpoints used at :335-337. That is 1.46% of the globe at T21 (NUGP 2048) and 0.37% at T42 (8192), and a different area at different latitudes within one rung. MINSTORMLEN and MAXSTORMLEN are in timesteps, so they are a different duration at each rung too.

landmod.f90:406-410 and simba.f90:483 snow cover fraction dsnow/(dsnow+0.01), the canonical subgrid snow parameter, at a 1 cm scale.
rainmod.f90:92 rcrit = MAX(0.85, ...), critical relative humidity, which encodes an assumed within-cell humidity distribution. The by-level modifier at :105-107 normalises by NLEV; the horizontal assumption is untouched.
rainmod.f90:1904 convective cloud cover zcca = 0.245, zccb = 0.125, a fit to gridcell mean convective rain rate: the same simulated storm gives more cloud cover as the cell shrinks.
icemod.f90:213 and eleven more, land or sea at mask > 0.5.
glaciermod.f90:211 and :589, glacier flag at cell-mean snow depth > 30.0 and off below 0.1.
fluxmod.f90:26 zumin = 1., a gustiness floor standing in for unresolved wind variance. Documented in m/s and compared against a squared speed at :204.

Related and separately shaped: rainmod.f90:2238 and three siblings divide by deltsec2, so gamma is a fraction of the deficit per TIMESTEP rather than a rate. The T42 override at rainmod.f90:88 is a partial correction for exactly this, applied at one rung.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 7.
acceptance_criteria: Each threshold is either expressed in a rung-independent form, or declared as anchored to one rung with the anchoring rung named. SPAT-8's convergence protocol knows which of its differences come from these.
close_reason: Declared as anchored to T21 rather than re-keyed, because a per-rung table would be the same undeclared fit written more times. snowcovz is now one named key in landmod_nl at 0.01, replacing a bare literal at six sites in landmod and one in simba. rcrit's 0.85 floor, the zcca/zccb cloud-cover fit, glaciermod's 30 m flag on a cell-mean depth and hurricanemod's four grid-unit thresholds carry the statement in place. dls > 0.5 has no rung-independent form and is recorded as such. resolution-tuned-parameters.md section 4 is the list SPAT-8 attributes its cross-rung differences to. No numeric changed.

title: newsnow.f90 declares its own grid and is hardcoded to T21
description:
newsnow.f90:5-6 declares 'integer, parameter :: NLAT = 32' and 'NLON = 64', with NUGP = NLAT*NLON, and never references resmod. It is a standalone program, the offline snowpack accumulator driven by glaciermod.

It reads unformatted dsnow, lsm and persist records into 2048-element arrays with no dimension check. Run against any other rung's files it either reads a truncated field or hits an I/O error depending on record length, and it cannot know which.

Ask whether it should exist before fixing it: nothing in the current pipeline graph generates or consumes its output, so deleting it may be the fix.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 7.
acceptance_criteria: newsnow either takes its grid from resmod like every other compiled unit, or it is deleted and config/pipeline.yaml confirms nothing generated it.
close_reason: Fixed: newsnow.f90 and buildice.f90 both take NLAT from resmod's NLAT_ATM and derive NLON, instead of declaring T21. Not deleted, because clim-53 owns the open verdict on whether the offline glacier accelerator gets wired; no CMake target added, so nothing builds them yet and no build changes.

title: T31 has complete data and two tuning branches, and cannot be built
description:
lib/rungs.py declares eight rungs including T31 (48 latitudes). vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/CMakeLists.txt:57 lists allowed PLASIM_NLAT as 32 64 96 128 160 192 256 and OMITS 48, so build_model.py --res T31 resolves the geometry and then dies at CMake configure with a FATAL_ERROR.

T31 is the best-provisioned rung after T21 and T42: a complete 15-code set in plasim/dat/T31, an mpstep branch at plasim.f90:1531, and a radmod tuning branch at radmod.f90:977. vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/__init__.py:545-571 also refuses it, accepting seven rungs where the ladder declares eight.

The decision to make is whether T31 is on the ladder. If it is, the two tables need the row; if it is not, lib/rungs.py should not carry it.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md findings 9 and 10.
acceptance_criteria: One answer about T31 written in one place, and the ladder tables in CMakeLists.txt, __init__.py and lib/rungs.py agree with it.
close_reason: Decided and made consistent: T31 stays on the ladder (complete dat set, mpstep and radmod branches, NLON 96 in both FFT tables). CMakeLists.txt allows 48; __init__.py's chain became a RESOLUTIONS table including T31, with the t106 spelling fixed. lib/rungs.check_restatements makes the agreement checkable; nothing calls it yet -- offered to batch F for world-ltc.

title: The two FFT tables disagree with each other, with their own comments, and with the ladder
description:
fftmod.f90:7 accepts NLON 8,16,32,48,64,96,128,256,384,512,1024,2048,4096. fft991mod.f90:12 accepts 4,64,96,128,192,256,320,384. Neither covers the ladder:

T63 (192) and T106 (320) are absent from fftmod. T170 (512) is absent from fft991mod -- while fft991mod.f90:19 documents 'T170 - N512 : 8-4-4-4' and set99 factorises 512 without complaint. The refusal is the table, not the algorithm.

Separately, fftmod's table accepts NLON = 48, which its own radix loop cannot do. At fftmod.f90:45-61, la = 6 satisfies 'la >= 4', one dfft4 pass sets la = 6/4 = 1, and neither the radix-3 nor the radix-2 tail fires, so 32 of the required 48 is applied. The inverse at :80-90 overshoots instead: nf goes 6 to 1 with no tail, and la runs 1, 4, 16 past n/8 = 6. No error, wrong transform. The header comment 'T15 - N48 : 8-3-2' describes a factorisation the code does not implement.

Unreachable today: NLAT 24 is not a rung. It is a trap for anyone adding T15.

Also documentation drift: plasimmod.f90:48-49 lists allowed NLAT without 96 or 160, and plasimmod.f90:39 claims NPRO must be a power of two, which nothing enforces.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 6.
acceptance_criteria: Each table matches what its module can actually transform. NLON 48 is either implemented or refused, and fft991mod's T170 comment agrees with its table.
close_reason: Fixed: NLON 48 removed from fftmod (refused, since the radix loop cannot do it) and 512 added to fft991mod (set99 factorises it 8-4-4-4, and its own comment already claimed it). Mirrored into pyfft.f90 and pyfft991.f90. plasimmod.f90's NLAT comment list and NPRO power-of-two claim are batch A's file and are reported, not edited here.

title: builds.resolution_of accepts any T-digits tag and mints surface fields under it
description:
lib/builds.py:177-194 takes the tag after the last hyphen and returns it whenever it starts with T and the rest are digits. It never consults the ladder, so 'exoplasim-T99' returns 'T99'.

Three generators then write a surface-field family under it: build_surface_soil_water.py, build_surface_dust.py, and the albedo/roughness/boundary builders that take --grid. The result is inputs/t99/orogen_T99_surf_0129.sra, an artifact family under a rung that cannot exist.

grid_export in the same module, at :110, does call rungs.geometry(res) and refuses anything off the ladder. That is the pattern this function is missing, and the fix is one line.

Related, same file family: config/pipeline.yaml:85 declares the hydrography coupling as coupling_exoplasim-*.nc rather than by rung, so a stale coupling from another rung reads as present for --status and --purge will not name it. Every other ExoPlaSim row is parameterised through {res}.

Source: notes/audits/resolution-divergence.md finding 11.
acceptance_criteria: resolution_of refuses a tag outside lib/rungs.RUNGS. The pipeline coupling row names its rung so a stale one no longer satisfies --status.
close_reason: Fixed: builds.resolution_of now calls rungs.geometry on the parsed tag; pipeline.yaml's hydrography row gains the {res}-parameterised coupling entry beside the glob so --status answers for the configured rung while --purge still reaches all.

title: verify_shtns_model leaves the binary registry dirty: it overwrites the shipped executable and adds one nobody asked for
description:
Running exoplasim/scripts/verify_shtns_model.sh <bed> T21 4 leaves check_consistency red:

  [ FAIL ] binaries carry current patches
           most_plasim_t21_l10_p16_omp.x: sha differs from manifest
           most_plasim_t21_l10_p4_omp.x: not in manifest

The check builds its two arms -- the shipped one and the filter-dropped control -- through build_model.py, which always copies its result into plasim/run/ under the registry's own naming. So the check overwrites the registry's T21 executable with an arm, and when asked for a thread count outside MATRIX it adds an executable the registry has never heard of. Neither is cleaned up.

That is rule 4's failure mode reached from inside a verification: after running the gate, the binary a run would pick up has unknown provenance. Recovering means removing the stray and rebuilding, which is what was done.

The fix is for the check's arms to land in its own work directory only. build_model.py returns the path it wrote and the check already copies to $WORK/bin/$arm.x, so what is missing is either a build_model flag that suppresses the registry copy or a restore step in the check. The same applies to any other caller that builds an arm rather than a registry entry -- the flag sweep and bench_ab are the ones to look at beside it.

Source: exoplasim/scripts/verify_shtns_model.sh, exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py, CLAUDE.md rule 4
close_reason: build_model gains --no-publish and verify_shtns_model uses it; three runs of the gate left all five binaries matching the manifest

title: aanrho is divided by naccuout at output and reset nowhere, so its accumulation spans the whole run
description:
outmod.f90:508 divides aanrho by naccuout and writes it as code 411, exactly as it does for aammr on the line above. aammr is zeroed in outreset; aanrho is not, and it appears in no reset in the tree. So the accumulated aerosol number density sums over every step since the run began while being divided by one window's count, and the output falls as 1/n across the run instead of being a window mean.

Its neighbour is the evidence: aammr and aanrho are written together, read together (plasim.f90:1025-1026, 1289-1290), normalised together and only one of them is reset.

SEPARATE FROM asndch, which is also unreset but deliberately so, with the comment 'Let the net snow change keep accumulating' at outmod.f90:2459. Nothing marks aanrho that way.

Reaches an output rather than the model state, so no run is wrong because of it; code 411 is.

Source: vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/outmod.f90:508, outreset; exoplasim/scripts/restart_schema.py
close_reason: aanrho was never accumulated either, not just never reset; it now accumulates and resets beside aammr, and atsami's declaration/reset mismatch was found and fixed alongside it. Both are gated in smoke_test

title: Give each rank the number of latitudes its die's cache can hold
description:
Give each rank the number of latitudes its die's cache can hold, instead of the same number to all of them. A 16-rank run spans both CCDs and hands every rank an equal `NLPP`, while CCD0 has 96 MB of L3 and CCD1 has 32 MB

Source: `exoplasim/notes/rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md`, `exoplasim/notes/smt-rank-layout.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
wontfix 2026-08-21, refused on its own measurement. The imbalance is real and was confirmed per rank rather than inferred: ranks 0-7 on CCD0 wait 23.1% of samples at T127 and 30.6% at T170, ranks 8-15 on CCD1 wait 12.4% and 20.1%, a 10.5 point step at the die boundary against 3.5 points of variation inside a die, with CCD1 the critical path at both. The default binding was checked rather than assumed. **What refuses the task is the size of the prize once the pairing constraint is applied.** Perfect balance recovers `mean - min` = 5.74% of wall at T127 and 5.65% at T170, and that ceiling binds every balancing scheme equally. But the symmetric transforms need an EVEN latitude count per rank, so the granularity is two: at T127 the optimum split is 12.78 against the 12 each rank already holds and the next even step, 14/10, is 2.3% WORSE; at T170 the optimum is 17.12 and 18/14 is worth about 1.8% of wall. Making `NLPP` a per-rank variable turns every `(NHOR,...)` array into a maximum rather than an exact size and every loop bound over it into a runtime value, across the whole physics, and that cannot be worth 1.8% at one resolution and nothing at another. The same ceiling refuses OpenMP threading on its balance argument, which was the other reason to want it. **What replaces this is CLIM-48**, which removes the cause instead of balancing around it: the working set is eight Legendre weight matrices that are all P or Q times separable factors, and storing two fits CCD1's L3 at both resolutions
close_reason: wontfix 2026-08-21, refused on its own measurement.

title: Settle on the record what the production build initialises reals to. The flag line carries
description:
Settle on the record what the production build initialises reals to. The flag line carries `-ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow` and `-finit-real=zero` together, and the second makes the first unable to fire on the case it is least able to survive: zero is a valid operand, so an uninitialised read succeeds and is indistinguishable from a deliberate zero. `aocl-and-model-build-flags.md` keeps the trap on the argument that a NaN raises SIGFPE at the line that made it rather than reaching every spectral coefficient through the Legendre transform, and that argument does not reach an uninitialised read at all. The pairing is not a decision anyone recorded, and `-finit-real=zero` is meanwhile load-bearing for determinism in a way nothing states, so deleting it is not the move: dropping it leaves garbage rather than detection

Source: `notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
blocked, and PARKED until the optimisation worktree merges rather than blocked on effort. THE PREMISE THIS ROW WAS DECIDED ON IS CONTRADICTED: it was closed 2026-08-22 on the argument that zero fill is free, since gfortran folds a signalling NaN to a quiet one at -O1 and above so the alternative arms no trap, making the swap a loss on both sides rather than a trade. That argument holds only if the fill itself costs nothing, and the optimisation worktree reports `-finit-real=zero` costing on the order of 30 percent of runtime. If that survives review it is a real trade and the decision has to be retaken on it, so the comment written into `most_compiler_omp` has been REMOVED rather than left standing on a premise now in doubt. THE FILE IS ALSO THE WRONG PLACE NOW: that worktree reworked the build process, so where the flag line lives is itself unsettled. Retake this against the merged build, with the cost measured rather than reported, and do not re-derive it before then [step: rebuild_binaries]
close_reason:
Answered, and by exactly the procedure this row asked for: retaken against the merged build with the cost measured rather than reported. exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md carries it.

WHAT THE FLAG WAS WORTH: two T170 threaded binaries from the same source differing in that flag alone, paired and interleaved on the 300-step bed -- 70.55 s with -finit-real=zero against 51.97 s without, +26.03% [+22.76, +27.29], faster in 4 of 4 rounds, and the restart IDENTICAL. Visible statically too: 1193 memset call sites with the flag, 623 without. The cause of the 31% of T170 that shtns-viability.md had attributed to physics routines clearing their own work arrays was the compiler doing it, not the model.

WHETHER THE MODEL NEEDS IT: three gates, and it does not. The trapping gate (-finit-real=snan with -ffpe-trap=invalid) is clean on the legmod path at T21 and T170, at NLOWIO=0 and 1. The propagating gate, which answers what the trapping one cannot on the SHTns path, gives one restart hash across -finit-real=zero, -finit-real=snan with INVALID masked, and no init flag: bit identical, so nothing uninitialised reaches a stored value.

ADOPTED: config/planet.yaml no longer declares -finit-real=zero and the checked profile carries -finit-real=snan. The threaded build compiles byte for byte to c8b9c41046fd93ca, which IS the arm the 26.03% was measured on. Determinism, the one thing this could have cost, survives: verify_shtns_model.sh passes whole on the new build, both arms at rounding scale, the control rejected, four-run bit-identity giving one hash, fcf46ebbb1302d3a.

The row's premise text is also now false -- the flag line no longer carries -finit-real=zero at all.

title: Add a debug build configuration, -Og -finit-real=snan -fcheck=all
description:
Add a debug build configuration, `-Og -finit-real=snan -fcheck=all`, and register it in `rebuild_binaries.py` and `binary_manifest.json` so it is a known configuration rather than an unmanaged binary. `-Og` is not a convenience and not a compromise: at `-O1` and above gfortran folds the signalling NaN to a quiet one before any instruction runs, so the trap is never armed and the poison buys nothing, while `-Og` traps and is far cheaper than `-O0`. It adds a dimension to the (resolution, layers, ranks) triple that rule 4 counts binaries over, which is exactly why it goes in the manifest rather than beside it

Source: `notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
blocked, and PARKED with CLIM-49 until the optimisation worktree merges. This row adds a build CONFIGURATION and registers it in `rebuild_binaries.py` and `binary_manifest.json`, and that worktree reworked the build process, so both the registration point and the flag set it would carry are unsettled. Its argument is unaffected and stands: a debug build differs in optimisation level, so its numerics differ and a climatology off it is not comparable to one off the production binary, which is why it is a second binary rather than a flag. Build it against the merged build system [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: PARKED, and the row exists so the arithmetic is not redone. Running the model's spectral
description:
PARKED, and the row exists so the arithmetic is not redone. Running the model's spectral transform on the GPU is not attractive on this machine, and not for the usual reason: transfer is 128 MB a timestep at T170, which is 5.1 ms over PCIe 4.0 against a 48.9 ms transform, about a tenth. The blocker is that a consumer RTX 4090 throttles FP64 to a sixty-fourth of its FP32 rate, giving 1.29 TFLOP/s against this CPU's 1.28 with AVX-512 -- no advantage at all in the precision `config/planet.yaml` declares. `SHT_ALLOW_GPU` also documents that a plan cannot then be shared between threads, which breaks the chosen parallel design and forces the serial structure costing 140% of current runtime. And offloading the TRANSFORM alone is capped at 18.9% even at T170, because that is its whole share; a device that paid would need the physics on it too

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
parked, not wontfix, because two things would reopen it and neither is far-fetched: hardware with unthrottled FP64, or a decision to move the PHYSICS to the device, which is a different project decided on different evidence. FP32 on the GPU is the expensive rung of the precision ladder and CLIM-59 is the cheap one; do that first [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Decide whether the tendency ACCUMULATORS are worth not zeroing. The largest single per-step
description:
Decide whether the tendency ACCUMULATORS are worth not zeroing. The largest single per-step memset site in the model is the block of nine whole-array zeroings at the head of `gridpointd` -- gudt, gvdt, gtdt, gqdt, dudt, dvdt, dtdt, dqdt, mmrt -- at about 10.5% of the samples whose leaf is in a stripped library, which is roughly 2.7% of runtime at T170. The MPI-shim collectives (`mpgagp`, `mpgallsp`, `mpbci`, `mpsumbcr`) are another 9.5% between them. THE ONLY WAY TO REMOVE THE ZEROING IS TO MAKE THE FIRST WRITER OF EACH ARRAY ASSIGN RATHER THAN ACCUMULATE, across every physics routine that adds into them, which is wide and correctness-sensitive for a few percent

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
wontfix 2026-08-22, and the scoping that closes it is the point. With the model rebuilt for frame pointers -- DWARF fails on 94% of samples here, frame pointers on 0% and cost -1.17% with an identical restart sha -- the zeroing attributes fully: 300 steps, no lost samples, 88,661 stacks, 50.4% with their leaf in a stripped library. title: Decide whether the physics should work on CACHE-RESIDENT COLUMN BLOCKS instead of whole bands
description:
Decide whether the physics should work on CACHE-RESIDENT COLUMN BLOCKS instead of whole bands, which is the NPROMA/chunk shape IFS and CAM both use. THE PRIZE IS SMALLER THAN THIS ROW WAS OPENED ON. It was opened on 31% of T170 being `__memset_avx512_unaligned_erms`, read as every physics routine clearing its own `(NHOR,NLEV)` work arrays per step; that zeroing is `-finit-real=zero` and is worth 26% on its own, which is CLIM-81, and blocking's FIRST-ORDER claim was that it moves exactly that zeroing into L1. What survives is the second-order claim, which was always the larger one. At T170 NHOR is 8192, so one work array is 655 KB A THREAD and the nine at the head of `gridpointd` are 94 MB of zeroing a step across the team. BLOCKING DOES NOT ZERO FEWER BYTES; it moves the zeroing into L1, where the physics that overwrites those lines finds them already resident, so the same instruction count stops being a bandwidth operation. The second-order win is larger than the first: `radstep`, `rainstep`, `fluxstep`, `kuo` and `icestep` each stream the whole band independently today, and a block that stays resident fuses them. It also supplies the work queue that CLIM-79 wants without the locality loss that made band ownership worth keeping, because locality then comes from the BLOCK SIZE rather than from which thread owns the data

title: Sub-grid hypsometry is computed three times and persisted nowhere
description:
Sub-grid hypsometry is computed three times and persisted nowhere, and four threads are parked behind the machinery that would hold it. The quantity is the distribution of MESH elevations inside each model grid cell, 15.19 km regions under a T42 cell about 300 km across. `notes/glacier-rough-pass.md` integrated it inline and threw it away, `analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py` rebuilds it, and `maps/build_basemap.py` applies the same lapse correction against the render raster instead, so three implementations of one criterion sit on a field no artifact carries. It is measurable today and it is large: land peak excess `orog_max - orog_mean` averages 1.065 km and reaches 2.969 km at the 90th percentile, so the model evaluates its own high ground about 7.8 K too warm on average and 21.9 K in the top tenth, and land below freezing in the warmest month goes from 0.002% on the model's orography to 1.657% on the 15.19 km mesh. Those are `analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py`'s numbers, restated from the climatology product the pipeline consumes; an earlier draft of this row carried 1.355 km, 9.9 K and 1.395% from a raw run file. Waiting on it: PHYS-13's ice mask, the glacier mass balance that note says it cannot have without it, the saturated-area FRACTION that would replace SURF-7's all-or-nothing at-surface flag, and GRAV-6

Source: `notes/glacier-rough-pass.md`, `notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md`, `hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md`, `docs/src/reference/economic-minerals.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and what is missing is the GENERATOR rather than a stale artifact: no step in `config/pipeline.yaml` writes this field, so under the graph convention it does not exist, and the row that declares it belongs in the same commit as the script. SHAPE: one artifact per (build, grid), on the precedent of the coupling matrices the `hydrography` step already writes, which are the interface every mesh-to-grid consumer integrates over, with `lib/gridding.py` owning the region-to-cell mapping as it already does. Cheap, minutes, and no climate run: the export and a grid definition are the whole input. Rule 3 binds -- map by index or a shared coordinate source, never by longitude -- and land comes from `surface_class` per rule 1, or the closed-basin floors below sea level drop out of the very distribution this exists to hold. SCOPE, and one artifact must not be read as both halves. This delivers the MESH-UNDER-CELL half, which the export holds. The BELOW-MESH half is a different quantity and is not deliverable at any region count: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md` finds the generator designs nothing below about 20 km, so relief inside a mesh region has to be parameterised or come from external data, and GW-23's Earth measurement is its only calibration -- 14.8 m of within-cell standard deviation and 25.9 m from mean to minimum at 15.19 km, against a three-number target of 3.96 to 36.18 m of model spread with the observations at 28.19 m. That half stays GW-6's. Nor is this a decision to build the downscaling pass: discrete mineral deposits and glacial overdeepening are parked there too, and this row is only the one input all of them named [step: hydrography]. SEMI's `downscaling_mod`, and its sub-grid elevation, elevation standard deviation, slope and elevation-class inputs, are a worked CONSUMER design for the artifact this row would write, and are worth reading before its shape is fixed. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f. A WORKED ANSWER TO THE DEPTH QUESTION, AND A FILTERING TRAP, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/geo/hires_to_lowres.f90:476-478` hands the ocean model the 90th-PERCENTILE bed elevation of the ocean part of each coarse cell -- a quantile, not the mean, min or max. That is a worked answer to what depth a coarse ocean cell has. Its sub-grid surface statistics use the law of total variance, combining a read-in sub-grid variance with the variance of the hi-res means, and the expensive slope half is recomputed only every Nth update rather than every step. SEPARATELY, `topo_filter.f90` smooths topography at a stated length scale in km with cached per-latitude weights -- this project has no smoothing anywhere in the terrain-to-model path, only in rendering. THE TRAP IN IT: the filter width is computed in CELLS from a distance in KM via Earth's radius, so a 1.20-radius planet at the same degree spacing gets FEWER filter points for the same nominal length scale, silently changing effective resolution. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 47f

constant reads exactly like a live one to whoever throws it. The deletion half

(run_exoplasim.py:1886) routes solang to gen_orb_decl (radmod.f90:1855-1859),

(rainmod_bm.f90:414-415), the canonical two-hour deep and four-hour shallow
relaxation, fire on swapping RAINMOD in the build.

Hurricane diagnostics (hurricanemod.f90:62-74, :1355-1358) are Earth-empirical
end to end at nstormdiag = 0. Two are specifically broken off Earth rather than
merely unfitted: LAVTHRESH = 1.2e-5 per s absolute vorticity against a planetary
vorticity 0.8x Earth's at 30 hours, so 25 per cent too strict; and
SIZETHRESH = 30 cells against a T21 cell 1.44x Earth's area, so a 44 per cent
larger storm (world-khn covers the cell-size half). RD is correctly taken from
gascon at :181 while CPD = 1005.7 at :52 is hardcoded and not tied to acpd, and
CL = 2500.0 at :55 is an admitted fudge. The positive form: this diagnostic is
not meaningful on this world and should stay off; if it is ever wanted, the
thresholds are a re-derivation and not a namelist tweak.

carbonmod is dormant at NCARBON = 0, though carbonstep is still called every
timestep (plasim.f90:4088). carbonmod.f90:174 uses
localprecip = (dprc+dprl)*3.154e9, Earth's seconds per year, two lines from a
timeweight at :114 that correctly uses m_days_per_year, so the two disagree by a
factor of two here. :194 and :197 use exp(kact*(tsurf - 288.0)), Earth's global
mean as the activation reference. :213 divides by RAD_EARTHSQ*0.29, where the
radius is correctly the model's but 0.29 is Earth's land fraction against this
planet's 50 per cent, and :27 hardcodes RAD_EARTH = 6371220.0 beside a correct
plarad. tune1 = 5.41 and tune2 = 2.20 (:78-79) are commented as "tuning
adjustment to make global average match", so fitted to Earth by construction.

LSG and the coupler are not compiled -- CMakeLists.txt:182-183 links
src/lsgmod.f90, a four-line stub, and cpl_stub.f90. lsg/src/lsgmod.f90:3176-3199
and :3263-3265 carry g=9.80665, erdrad=6371000.00, erdrot=four*pi/86164. for
Coriolis, rhonul=1030., tfreez=-1.91, cp=4180. and entmel=80.*cp; the density
polynomial at :1771 is fitted to Earth's T and S range at sref=35., tref=2., and
the depth coordinate uses du(k)*rhonul/g. cpl.f90:3-5 is T21-only AND
Earth-radius-only via parameter(nxa=64,nya=32) and parameter(radea=6.371E6).
Additionally oceanmod.f90:335-344 aborts unless n_days_per_year == 360, which
this world's calendar can never satisfy, so LSG is unreachable as it stands.

icemod_template.f90:19 is a stale pre-fork copy still carrying
parameter(TFREEZE=271.25), the form the fork deliberately replaced with a
namelist key. It has no nseaice and no threadprivate directives and is in no
build. It is the file a grep for TFREEZE hits first and it gives the pre-CLIM-17
answer. plasim/bld/make_plasim likewise still names OCEAN=lsgmod against
lsg/src.
acceptance_criteria: Each item is removed, guarded, or has its trigger recorded where someone would read it before throwing the switch.
close_reason: Each item now states its trigger and its consequence at the code a person reads before throwing the switch: radmod's iyrbp remnant and orb_decl's Earth vernal equinox, rainmod_bm's Betts-Miller timescales, oceanmod's nlsg branch (LSG unreachable twice over -- the 360-day abort is a count of sidereal days per orbit, 146 here, and the module is not compiled), icemod_template.f90's not-in-any-build banner, and carbonmod's module head. One was a defect rather than a dormancy and is fixed: localprecip used Earth's seconds per year two lines from a timeweight using m_days_per_year, a factor of two apart. plasim/bld/make_plasim no longer exists.
